context.description: SGLang is a high-performance serving framework for large language models and multimodal models.

latestRelease.title: v0.5.17
latestRelease.notes:
# Highlights

*582 PRs from 194 contributors.*

**Kimi K3 day-0 support**: A 2.8T-parameter multimodal LatentMoE (896 experts, top-16, routed in a 3584-dim latent space) with a 1M-token context, 69 KDA linear-attention layers interleaved with 24 MLA layers, and a MoonViT3d vision tower, shipping as a native MXFP4 checkpoint. SGLang serves it from day 0 with DCP, DSpark speculative decoding, chunked-prefill PP with TP decode, KDA-aware prefix caching, HiCache L2 over DCP, LoRA on the quantized weights, and reasoning, tool-call and OpenAI-compatible serving, verified on NVIDIA GB300 and AMD MI35x ([#32541](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32541), [#32828](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32828), [#32890](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32890), [#33025](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33025), [#33112](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33112), [blog](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-07-27-kimi-k3-day0-support), [cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Moonshotai/Kimi-K3), [roadmap](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/32607)).

**MiniMax-H3 day-0 support**: MiniMax's video generation model that produces a video and a synchronized stereo audio track in one request, served natively on SGLang-Diffusion across all three public task profiles: text-to-video-and-audio (`t2va`), first/last-frame conditioning (`fl2va`), and image/video/audio reference conditioning (`ref2va`, which also covers video-to-video). Verified on B200 (TP2 + Ulysses4), H100 (TP2 + Ulysses2), AMD MI300X and MI355X (Ulysses1/2/4/8), and 2x RTX 5090 with layerwise offload ([#33275](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33275), [cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3)).

**Other new models added**: [EmbeddingGemma](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Google/EmbeddingGemma) and [LFM2.5](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/LiquidAI/LFM2.5) embedding models, nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4, plus cookbook recipes for Poolside's [Laguna-S-2.1](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Poolside/Laguna-S-2.1) family and [Inkling-Small](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/ThinkingMachines/Inkling-Small).

**Initial support for the Rust frontend**: Migrates the front half of the server, everything from network ingress up to the point a tokenized request is handed to the GPU scheduler, from Python to a multi-threaded Rust implementation ([#29799](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29799)).

**DCP communication backends and q-replicate (Helix)**: The DeepSeek-MLA decode context-parallel path gains pluggable comm backends. `a2a` exchanges packed attention output plus fp32 LSE in a single NCCL collective per layer, with fp8 KV carried as uint8 byte transport; `fi_a2a` delegates the cross-rank exchange to the FlashInfer MNNVL kernel on GB200. `--dcp-replicate-q-proj` projects full-head Q locally and skips the per-layer Q head-dim all-gather. Select with `--dcp-comm-backend {ag_rs, a2a, fi_a2a}` ([#21637](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21637)).

**DWDP for MoE prefill**: A new prefill parallelism strategy that prefetches peer expert weights over NVLink P2P and computes all experts locally, removing EP all-to-all token dispatch. On 4x B200 with gpt-oss-120b, prefill-only, DWDP4 reaches **1.92x over DEP4** at MNT 32K / ISL 32K, and **506K vs 329K tok/s (1.54x)** at saturation (CONC=128, ISL=8K). Enable with `--dwdp-size`; the authors mark it early-development ([#29778](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29778)).

**Session-reference-aware Unified Radix Cache**: For agentic and RL-rollout workloads, requests can carry a stable `session_id` so eviction knows which prefixes an active session still references, instead of evicting purely by cache policy. Release the references with `/close_session`. Opt in with `--enable-session-radix-cache` ([#29173](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29173)).

**SM90 FP8 MegaMoE for DeepSeek-V4**: Adds the DeepGEMM MegaMoE A2A path on SM90 for DeepSeek-V4-Flash/Pro FP8, including the pre-dispatch JIT kernel and FP8 expert weight preparation. Guarded behind `SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE=1` ([#29016](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29016)).

**Faster large-MoE model loading**: Oversized or non-contiguous CPU weight views were driving pathological H2D transfers, with DeepSeek-V4-Pro TP8 spending 27 to 32 minutes in H2D on some ranks. Copying those views into contiguous storage before H2D cuts full model loading from about **35 minutes to 6m20s (5.6x)**, and GPT-OSS-20B BF16 from **545s to 70s (7.8x)**, with Qwen3.5-397B measured at 1.93x to 2.3x. Opt in with `SGLANG_MOE_COPY_WEIGHT_VIEWS_BEFORE_H2D`, off by default ([#32315](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32315)).

**Lower DeepSeek-V4 memory on AMD**: Removing unnecessary expert padding drops MI355X FP4 MoE model weights from **159.07 GB to 112.36 GB**, and bringing the HIP compress-state pool into the memory_saver KV_CACHE region lets colocated RL reclaim it, cutting the measured training-phase footprint from about **143 GiB to 87 GiB per GPU** ([#31450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31450), [#31747](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31747)).

**Faster engine recovery**: Large-model restarts cost 3 to 6+ minutes today, about 6.5 minutes for Qwen3-235B FP8 on 4 GPUs, because weights reload from storage and CUDA graphs recapture. A weight-cache daemon holds weights per GPU so a restarting engine can recover from cache instead ([#27139](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27139)).

**Lower host overhead in hybrid-linear MTP decode**: Under spec-v2 overlap scheduling each decode step runs draft, verify and extend CUDA graphs, and the eager seams between them become GPU idle time at low concurrency. This trims that host work so the host stays off the critical path ([#32219](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32219)).

**Dependencies**: flashinfer 0.6.15.post1 ([#31927](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31927)), sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.5.post1 ([#32345](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32345), [#33143](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33143)), helion 1.4 ([#32562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32562)), mooncake 0.3.12.post1 ([#32302](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32302)), dynamo-tokenizers 1.7.0 ([#32981](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32981)). PyTorch stays at 2.11.0 and the CUDA base image at 13.0.1.

*Full release notes by category below; breaking changes and known issues are at the end.*

signals.title: [Feature] Load Balance Refactor for DP-Attention
signals.text: ### Motivation Current data parallel attention routing and load balance have the following problems: - Confusing naming: In PD mode, the `round_robin` balance method is not round robin. It should be called "follow_bootstrap_room" (see [code](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/88f3de25148d620f10eec3f9c8fdde7b4e695750/python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py#L530)), since it uses bootstrap_room to assign target ranks. - Limited load balancing methods: It leads to load imbalance in many cases. - In PD mode, it only supports "follow_bootstrap_room" method. - In non-PD model, the DataParallelController (DPC) only supports round robin or balancing by number of requests, but does not support balancing by the number of tokens. - Limited compatibility with external routing: we would like to use the the rust router (model gateway) to directly assign dp ranks but it is not supported. ### Tasks 1. Fix confusing names - Introduce a new load balancing method, "follow_bootstrap_room". Move the current [code](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b5d9fc873bf238ff1172b8050dfa1fbb665f0f4d/python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py#L517-L531) to this new method instead of incorrectly reusing "round_robin". - To make things backward compatible, we can change the default value of "--load-balance-method" to "auto" and set it in `ServerArgs:__post_init__` with the following rules: - If it is non-PD, set it to "round_robin". - If it is PD, set P workers to "follow_bootstrap_room" and set D workers to "round_robin". - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/16110 - Remove the balance method "decode_round_robin" and all its related code. It is not useful anymore. Basically revert this PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/15164. - Remove the argument `"--prefill-round-robin-balance"` and its related code. It is very confusing. If we want to do the check. We should let the router do the check. 2. Support methods other than "follow_bootstrap_room" in PD mode. We want to support the following two mode: a) The router directly add prefill and decode dp ranks in `GenerateReqInput`. In this case, DPC just follows the assignment. b) The router does not assign dp ranks and DPC assign prefill ranks. In this case, the decode worker needs an additional communication to know the prefill dp rank. See (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/14726). In this way, we can support flexible balance method in prefill worker. The old behavior falls in the category of (a), since router knows bootstrap_room, it will directly set prefill dp rank in `GenerateReqInput` as `bootstrap_room % dp_size`. 3. DP controller refactors - Unify the naming. Rename `shortest_queue` -> `total_requests`. Rename `minimum_tokens` -> `total_tokens`. These are the two basic methods that balance by the total number of requests or total number of tokens. - Implement both `total_requests` and `total_tokens` correctly in DPC with the piggyback load reporting. Simplify the implementation. For example, this function https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/88f3de25148d620f10eec3f9c8fdde7b4e695750/python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py#L98 is over complicated. We do not need to do ahead-of-time planning. We can simply do the following: a) when we get piggyback load report from a worker, we forcibly update the load of the worker. b). For each new request, we dispatch it to the worker with minimal load and increment the load of that worker by one. - Correctly set the default balance method with the guideline below: - For prefill, we typically use balance by total_tokens or cache aware - For decode, we look at the limiting resources. If KV cache is enough and latency requirement is tight, balance by total_requests (this is the normal case for online serving). If KV cache is very limited, balance by total_tokens. In the future, we might explore cache aware as well. 4. External Scheduling - [x] Support external assigned DP rank with router. - [ ] Support dp-rank aware load balancing with other instance-level load balance strategies, e.g., cache aware. Related Issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/13052

signals.title: [Roadmap] Unified Hybrid Radix Cache Refactor
signals.text: Blog: https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-08-11-unified-radix-cache/ ## Motivation The current radix cache implementations (RadixCache, MambaRadixCache, SWARadixCache, etc.) share a large amount of logic but are maintained as separate, diverged copies. This leads to code duplication, inconsistent behavior, and high maintenance burden when extending cache functionality to new model types (e.g., hybrid linear models, sliding window attention models). The goal of this refactor is to unify the hybrid radix cache hierarchy around a common base interface, making it easier to: - Add new cache variants without duplicating logic - Ensure consistency across all cache implementations - Enable future extensions (e.g., HiCache, PD disaggregation, new model architectures) @hzh0425 @yizhang2077 @pansicheng @ispobock ## Progress ### Stage 0: Unify Radix Tree Interface - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/17142 @hzh0425 - signals.title: [Feature] Improve Unit Test Coverage
signals.text: ## Motivation SGLang's test suite has **600+ test files**, but most are E2E tests that launch a full server. While these cover many code paths, core modules like `managers/`, `mem_cache/`, `entrypoints/`, `sampling/`, `parser/`, `function_call/`, and `utils/` still need better unit test coverage (tests that run without launching a server). **Why this matters:** - E2E tests launch a server and load model weights, taking minutes. Unit tests run in seconds with mocked dependencies. - When an E2E test fails, the root cause could be anywhere. Unit tests pinpoint the exact broken function. ## What's Already Done - **Unit test directory** [`test/registered/unit/`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/test/registered/unit) with READMEs ([`test/registered/README.md`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/test/registered/README.md), [`test/registered/unit/README.md`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/test/registered/unit/README.md)) documenting conventions - **32 unit tests migrated** across 12 subdirectories - **Coverage tooling** configured ([`.coveragerc`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.coveragerc), `pytest-cov`) - **CI coverage reporting** in [`ci-coverage-overview.yml`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci-coverage-overview.yml) (daily + manual trigger) — [example run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24032286387/attempts/1#summary-70083527423) - **Contribution guide** updated with [unit test section](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/developer_guide/contribution_guide.md#run-and-add-unit-tests) ## Directory Structure ``` test/registered/unit/ # mirrors python/sglang/srt/ ├── mem_cache/ (6 files) ├── function_call/ (5 files) ├── utils/ (4 files) ├── parser/ (3 files) ├── managers/ (3 files) ├── entrypoints/ (2 files) ├── layers/ (2 files) ├── observability/ (2 files) ├── model_loader/ (2 files) ├── server_args/ (1 file) ├── model_executor/ (1 file) ├── batch_invariant_ops/ (1 file) └── ... (new subdirs added as tests are written) ``` **Principle:** Source file at `srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py` → test at `unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache.py`. ## Open Tasks Below are some suggested starting points. Comment on this issue to claim one. You can check the latest UT coverage report run ([example](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24032286387/attempts/1#summary-70083527423)) or run coverage locally to find your own opportunities — modules with low coverage under core directories (`managers/`, `sampling/`, `parser/`, etc.) are good candidates: ```bash pytest test/registered/unit/ --cov --cov-config=.coveragerc --cov-report=term-missing -v ``` ### Easy (good first issue) - `srt/parser/` — conversation templates, reasoning parsers, code completion parser - `srt/sampling/` — parameter validation, normalization, logit processor serialization - `srt/entrypoints/openai/` — encoding/decoding, tool call formatting - `srt/function_call/` — extend existing detector tests, add new detector coverage ### Medium - `srt/utils/` — common util helpers - `srt/multimodal/` — media utils, processor base logic - `srt/constrained/` — grammar dispatch logic - `srt/managers/` — template manager, tokenizer utils, batch metadata helpers ## How to Contribute 1. **Pick a task** from above (or find your own via coverage), comment to claim it 2. **Look at existing examples:** - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_evict_policy.py` — pure logic, zero deps - `test/registered/unit/managers/test_prefill_adder.py` — mock factories for scheduler tests - `test/registered/unit/parser/test_reasoning_parser.py` — streaming parser tests 3. **Follow the conventions** in [`test/registered/unit/README.md`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/test/registered/unit/README.md) and the [contribution guide](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/developer_guide/contribution_guide.md#run-and-add-unit-tests) 4. **Run locally:** ```bash pytest test/registered/unit/ -v pytest test/registered/unit/ --cov --cov-config=.coveragerc -v # with coverage ``` 5. **Submit a PR** titled `[Test] Add unit tests for <module_name>`, referencing this issue ### PR Quality Bar **Note:** AI-assisted code is acceptable, but you are responsible for the quality — **understand every line you submit.** We will reject PRs that look auto-generated without understanding — e.g., tests that only check trivial cases, assert on mock return values, or don't actually exercise the real code logic. Read the source code first, then write tests that would catch real bugs. ### PR Requirements - [ ] Test is in `test/registered/unit/<module>/` (mirroring `srt/`) - [ ] Does NOT launch a server or load real model weights - [ ] Includes edge cases, not just happy paths - [ ] Use `CustomTestCase` instead of `unittest.TestCase`. - [ ] Registered with `register_cpu_ci()` or `register_cuda_ci()` - [ ] **Locally tested and passing.** Paste both the command and its output in your PR description: ```bash # command pytest test/registered/unit/<your_module>/test_xxx.py -v # output (copy-paste the full result) ```

signals.title: HiCache: HiMambaRadixCache crashes with 'Destination indices must be a CUDA tensor' on Qwen3.5/3.6
signals.text: ## Bug: HiCache crashes on hybrid Mamba+Attention models (Qwen3.5-397B, Qwen3.6-27B) ### Environment - SGLang version: latest main (as of 2026-04-29) - Hardware: RTX PRO 6000 (SM120 Blackwell) - Models: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (TP=4), Qwen3.6-27B (TP=1) - Both NVFP4 quantized, FP8 KV cache ### Reproduction Enable `--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 2.0 --hicache-io-backend kernel --hicache-write-policy write_through` on either Qwen3.5-397B or Qwen3.6-27B. The server starts, allocates host memory for both hierarchical KV cache and hierarchical Mamba cache: ``` [TP0] Allocating 14.06 GB host memory for hierarchical KV cache. [TP0] Allocating 12.63 GB host memory for hierarchical Mamba cache (layout=layer_first). ``` CUDA graphs capture successfully. On the first actual inference request, the scheduler crashes: ``` [TP0] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last): RuntimeError: Destination indices must be a CUDA tensor ``` All TP ranks hit the same error simultaneously. The server restarts and crash-loops. ### Root cause (hypothesis) `HiMambaRadixCache` (which is correctly selected for these hybrid models) appears to have an index tensor placement bug in its cache transfer path. During eviction or restore between L1 (GPU) and L2 (host), destination indices are on CPU when the CUDA kernel expects them on GPU. This is distinct from the `"HiRadixCache only supports MHA and MLA yet"` error (which we also hit on DeepSeek-V4-Flash due to its compressed attention, tracked in #23639). The Mamba path is reached correctly via `HiMambaRadixCache`, but the transfer kernel fails. ### Working model for comparison MiniMax-M2.7 (230B, Lightning Attention, no Mamba layers) works perfectly with HiCache. Same flags, same hardware. Cache hit rate climbs to 95% at 18K tokens. This confirms the bug is specific to the Mamba cache path, not HiCache in general. ### What we tested | Model | Attention Type | HiCache Result | |-------|---------------|----------------| | MiniMax-M2.7 (230B) | Lightning Attention | Works, 95% cache hit at 18K tokens | | Qwen3.5-397B | Hybrid Mamba+Attention | Crashes: "Destination indices must be a CUDA tensor" | | Qwen3.6-27B | Hybrid Mamba+Attention | Same crash | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Compressed MLA + SWA | "HiRadixCache only supports MHA and MLA yet" (tracked in #23639) | ### Workaround Disable HiCache (`--enable-hierarchical-cache` removed) for affected models.

signals.title: [Help] [Performance] PD disaggregation on H200 shows no throughput gain over single-node traditional deployment with 32k input / 512 output
signals.text: Title: [Help] PD disaggregation on H200 shows no throughput gain over single-node traditional deployment with 32k input / 512 output ## Question / Help wanted Hi SGLang team, I am testing PD disaggregation with SGLang on H200 GPUs using the Mooncake transfer backend. I have tried multiple deployment topologies, including 1P1D, 2P1D, and 1P2D, but the actual end-to-end performance is consistently close to only one traditional non-disaggregated single-node deployment. The workload is long-prefill oriented: - Input length: ~32k tokens - Output length: 512 tokens - Model: `ZhipuAI/GLM-5.1-FP8` - Hardware: H200 nodes - Transfer backend: Mooncake - Network: RoCE / `mlx5_0` - Router: `sglang_router.launch_router --pd-disaggregation` - Main baseline: traditional single-node SGLang deployment without PD disaggregation ## Expected behavior Since the workload has a large prefill part, I expected PD disaggregation to improve throughput or at least show clear scaling when adding more prefill or decode nodes. For example: - 1P1D should perform better than or comparable to one traditional node. - 2P1D should improve prefill capacity compared with 1P1D. - 1P2D should improve decode capacity if decode is the bottleneck. - At least one PD topology should outperform a single traditional deployment node meaningfully. ## Actual behavior In my tests, all PD configurations are only around the performance of one traditional non-disaggregated single-node deployment. Observed behavior: - 1P1D: roughly similar to one traditional node - 2P1D: no meaningful throughput improvement - 1P2D: no meaningful throughput improvement - Disabling speculative decoding does not change the conclusion - Passing explicit Mooncake bootstrap port does not change the conclusion - Binding `--host` to RoCE IP does not change the conclusion - Increasing `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE` and `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_THREAD_POOL_SIZE` does not bring obvious improvement - RoCE traffic exists, but adding more P/D nodes still does not improve end-to-end throughput This makes me suspect that the bottleneck may be KV transfer, Mooncake transfer concurrency, router scheduling, synchronization overhead, or some configuration limitation rather than pure GPU compute. ## Environment ```bash Docker image: sglang:v0.5.10 Model: ZhipuAI/GLM-5.1-FP8 GPU: H200 Main workload: input tokens: 32768 output tokens: 512 ``` ## Representative configurations tested ### 1. 1P1D, host network, TP=8 Prefill: ```bash nohup env \ SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=600 \ SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT=600 \ SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE=32 \ SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_THREAD_POOL_SIZE=64 \ SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_HEARTBEAT_MAX_FAILURE=6 \ SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=256 \ SGLANG_DEEPEP_LL_COMBINE_SEND_NUM_SMS=32 \ sglang serve \ --model-path /root/public/ZhipuAI/GLM-5.1-FP8 \ --tp 8 \ --reasoning-parser glm45 \ --tool-call-parser glm47 \ --moe-a2a-backend deepep \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_0 \ --disaggregation-mode prefill \ --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 \ --trust-remote-code \ --dist-init-addr 127.0.0.1:5000 \ --nnodes 1 \ --watchdog-timeout 1800 \ --soft-watchdog-timeout 300 \ --max-running-requests 32 \ > prefill.log 2>&1 & ``` Decode: ```bash nohup env \ SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=600 \ SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT=600 \ SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE=32 \ SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_THREAD_POOL_SIZE=64 \ SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_HEARTBEAT_MAX_FAILURE=6 \ SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=256 \ SGLANG_DEEPEP_LL_COMBINE_SEND_NUM_SMS=32 \ sglang serve \ --model-path /root/public/ZhipuAI/GLM-5.1-FP8 \ --tp 8 \ --reasoning-parser glm45 \ --tool-call-parser glm47 \ --moe-a2a-backend deepep \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_0 \ --disaggregation-mode decode \ --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30001 \ --trust-remote-code \ --dist-init-addr 127.0.0.1:5001 \ --nnodes 1 \ --node-rank 0 \ --watchdog-timeout 1800 \ --soft-watchdog-timeout 300 \ --max-running-requests 32 \ > decode.log 2>&1 & ``` Router: ```bash python -m sglang_router.launch_router \ --pd-disaggregation \ --prefill http://10.255.208.20:30000 \ --decode http://10.255.208.14:30001 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8000 \ --disable-circuit-breaker \ --health-check-interval-secs 999999 ``` ### 2. 2P1D, two independent prefill servers, one decode server Router: ```bash python -m sglang_router.launch_router \ --pd-disaggregation \ --prefill http://10.255.208.20:30000 \ --prefill http://10.255.208.15:30000 \ --decode http://10.255.208.14:30001 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8000 \ --disable-circuit-breaker \ --health-check-interval-secs 999999 ``` I also tried explicitly passing the Mooncake bootstrap port: ```bash python -m sglang_router.launch_router \ --pd-disaggregation \ --prefill http://10.255.208.20:30000 8998 \ --prefill http://10.255.208.15:30000 8998 \ --decode http://10.255.208.14:30001 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8000 \ --disable-circuit-breaker \ --health-check-interval-secs 30 ``` However, the throughput still did not improve meaningfully compared with 1P1D or one traditional node. ### 3. 2P1D, official-style --host 10.255.208.20 \ --port 30000 \ --trust-remote-code \ --dist-init-addr 10.255.208.20:5000 \ --nnodes 2 \ --node-rank 0 \ --tp 16 \ --dp 16 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --enable-dp-lm-head \ --watchdog-timeout 3600 \ --soft-watchdog-timeout 3600 \ --max-running-requests 32 \ > prefill.log 2>&1 & ``` Prefill node 1: ```bash nohup env \ SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=600 \ SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT=600 \ SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_HEARTBEAT_MAX_FAILURE=6 \ SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=256 \ SGLANG_DEEPEP_LL_COMBINE_SEND_NUM_SMS=32 \ --host 10.255.208.15 \ --port 30000 \ --trust-remote-code \ --dist-init-addr 10.255.208.20:5000 \ --nnodes 2 \ --node-rank 1 \ --tp 16 \ --dp 16 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --enable-dp-lm-head \ --watchdog-timeout 3600 \ --soft-watchdog-timeout 3600 \ --max-running-requests 32 \ > prefill.log 2>&1 & ``` Decode remained a single node with TP=8 / DP=8: ```bash nohup env \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_0 \ --disaggregation-mode decode \ --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake \ --host 10.255.208.14 \ --port 30001 \ --trust-remote-code \ --dist-init-addr 10.255.208.14:5001 \ --nnodes 1 \ --node-rank 0 \ --tp 8 \ --dp 8 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --enable-dp-lm-head \ --watchdog-timeout 3600 \ --soft-watchdog-timeout 3600 \ --max-running-requests 32 \ > decode.log 2>&1 & ``` This configuration also did not improve end-to-end throughput. ### 4. 1P2D, one prefill server, two decode servers Router: ```bash python -m sglang_router.launch_router \ --pd-disaggregation \ --prefill http://10.255.208.20:30000 8998 \ --decode http://10.255.208.14:30001 \ --decode http://10.255.208.15:30001 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8000 \ --disable-circuit-breaker \ --health-check-interval-secs 30 ``` This also did not improve throughput, even though I expected it to help if decode was the bottleneck. ### 5. With and without speculative decoding I tested both with speculative decoding: ```bash --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 ``` and without speculative decoding. The conclusion was the same: PD disaggregation did not scale beyond the single-node traditional baseline. ### 6. RoCE / host IP related tests I tried binding `--host` to RoCE IPs and setting: ```bash GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=enp25s0np0 NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=enp25s0np0 NCCL_IB_HCA=mlx5_0 NCCL_DEBUG=INFO --disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_0 ``` I also tested: ```bash --disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_0,mlx5_1 ``` on one decode node. The observed RoCE traffic on `mlx5_0` can reach around 60-80 Gbps during tests, but the overall throughput still does not improve with more prefill or decode nodes. ## Health checks The prefill and decode servers report healthy: ```bash curl -v http://10.255.208.20:30000/health curl -v http://10.255.208.15:30000/health curl -v http://10.255.208.14:30001/health curl -v http://localhost:8000/get_loads ``` ## Questions Could you help clarify the expected scaling behavior and the recommended topology for this case? 1. For a 32k input / 512 output workload on H200, should PD disaggregation be expected to outperform a single traditional deployment node? 2. Is it expected that 1P1D, 2P1D, and 1P2D all perform close to one traditional node because KV cache transfer overhead dominates? 3. For GLM-5.1-FP8 with MoE + DeepEP + Mooncake PD, are there recommended values for the following parameters? - `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE` - `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_THREAD_POOL_SIZE` - `SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` - `SGLANG_DEEPEP_LL_COMBINE_SEND_NUM_SMS` - `--max-running-requests` - `--mem-fraction-static` 4. For 2P1D, which topology is recommended? Option A: two independent prefill servers registered in the router: ```bash --prefill http://node0:30000 --prefill http://node1:30000 ``` with each prefill server using: ```bash --nnodes 1 --tp 8 ``` Option B: one distributed prefill group: ```bash --nnodes 2 --tp 16 --dp 16 ``` 5. For the router, is passing the bootstrap port required? ```bash --prefill http://host:30000 8998 ``` Or should the default `8998` be discovered automatically? 6. Is there any known limitation where adding more prefill or decode nodes does not improve throughput unless the cluster size is much larger? 7. What metrics should I collect to identify the bottleneck more precisely? - prefill GPU utilization - decode GPU utilization - RoCE bandwidth - Mooncake transfer latency - router scheduling/load - TTFT - TPOT - end-to-end throughput - per-rank KV transfer time 8. Is there a recommended benchmark script or profiling method for PD disaggregation to distinguish the following bottlenecks? - prefill compute bottleneck - decode compute bottleneck - KV transfer bottleneck - router scheduling bottleneck - Mooncake/RDMA connection bottleneck ## Additional observations In my experiments, decode GPUs are not always fully utilized, and RoCE traffic does not seem to saturate the 400Gbps link. Therefore, I am not sure whether the bottleneck is pure network bandwidth or synchronization / transfer / scheduling overhead. Any guidance on the correct deployment topology and recommended profiling method would be very helpful. Thanks!

signals.title: [Feature] dLLM performance optimization in prefill and batching
signals.text: ### Checklist - [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation Recently, we did a performance calibration of dLLM efficiency with speculative decoding. The majority of the work is done by Lingxiao Yang @eroship from ZLab@UCSD. In short, we found there is a huge gap of (long prefill) in dLLM and batching with speculative decoding, where the dLLM should be more efficient than speculative decoding because it does not need drafting. #### Why do we compare with the speculative decoding? 1. [similar usage] block dLLM and spec decoding are both accelerations for latency-sensitive tasks; 2. [same complexity] When we control the block size in dLLM and token candidate number in spec decoding, the verification/decode complexity is the same in both cases; 3. [refer to mature implementation] spec decoding is mature in SGLang, and we need to calibrate the long prefill and batching implementation of dLLM with spec decoding based on reason 1&2 above. #### Two optimization opportunities The two important performance optimizations to be done: - [ ] Longer/flexible prefill chunk size. Currently, all prefill and decode blocks share the same chunk size, like 32, which is inefficient in the long prefill case. - [ ] Fine-grained early exit of batching. Now the requests in a batch that end earlier cannot exit the decode chunk before all requests in the batch finish the decoding process of the entire chunk. We open-sourced the code for performance tracking. Lingxiao will share the code link below, as well as the performance gap analysis with evidence in two separate issues: 1. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24645 2. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24646 ### Related resources _No response_

signals.title: gRPC mode: --enable-metrics error message cites wrong servicer version (≥0.5.3 → should be ≥0.5.5); v0.5.13 image ships 0.5.4 and fails to boot
signals.text: ## Summary In gRPC mode, `--enable-metrics` requires `smg-grpc-servicer` to expose the `on_request_manager_ready` hook (that hook is what starts the HTTP sidecar serving `/metrics`). `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_server.py` guards this, but **the required version it reports is wrong**, and the **released `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.11`/`v0.5.13` images ship a servicer that lacks the hook**, so `--grpc-mode --enable-metrics` raises `RuntimeError` at startup out of the box. ## Bug A — wrong version in the error message + comment `serve_grpc()` in `grpc_server.py` says: ``` raise RuntimeError( "--enable-metrics requires smg-grpc-servicer ≥ 0.5.3 (the version " "that accepts 'on_request_manager_ready'); ..." ) ``` (and the comment above it: "Older smg-grpc-servicer releases (≤ 0.5.2) ... ≥ 0.5.3 ... accepts on_request_manager_ready") This is incorrect. Verified against `smg-grpc-servicer==0.5.4` (the version bundled in the `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.13` image): ```python import inspect from smg_grpc_servicer.sglang.server import serve_grpc print(list(inspect.signature(serve_grpc).parameters)) # -> ['server_args', 'model_info'] print("on_request_manager_ready" in inspect.signature(serve_grpc).parameters) # -> False ``` So 0.5.4 does **not** accept the hook. Empirically the first version that does is **0.5.5** (confirmed working: a `0.5.5` install starts the `:30001` sidecar). A user who follows the error's own advice and installs 0.5.3 or 0.5.4 will still crash. **Fix:** change `≥ 0.5.3` to `≥ 0.5.5` in both the `RuntimeError` message and the comment in `grpc_server.py`. ## Bug B — released images can't serve grpc-mode metrics out of the box `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.13` bundles `smg-grpc-servicer==0.5.4` + `smg-grpc-proto==0.4.9`, so `--grpc-mode --enable-metrics` hits the `RuntimeError` above and the server won't start. Root cause is release timing, not a code decision: - The image's pip layer was built **2026-06-11 ~10:05 UTC** (per `docker history`). - `smg-grpc-servicer 0.5.5` and `smg-grpc-proto 0.4.10` (which 0.5.5 requires, `proto>=0.4.10`) were published **2026-06-11 ~16:10 UTC** — ~6h later. - `pyproject.toml` pins `smg-grpc-servicer>=0.5.0` (newest-wins), so the layer resolved to the newest then-available: 0.5.4 + 0.4.9, which lacks the hook. **Suggested fix:** bump the pin to `smg-grpc-servicer>=0.5.5` (which transitively pulls `smg-grpc-proto>=0.4.10`) and/or rebuild the published image now that those packages exist, so `--grpc-mode --enable-metrics` works out of the box. ## Repro ```bash docker run --rm --entrypoint python3 lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.13 -c \ "import inspect; from smg_grpc_servicer.sglang.server import serve_grpc; \ print(list(inspect.signature(serve_grpc).parameters))" # ['server_args', 'model_info'] <- no on_request_manager_ready # => launch_server --grpc-mode --enable-metrics raises RuntimeError at startup ``` ## Environment - Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.13` (also affects `v0.5.11`) - `smg-grpc-servicer==0.5.4`, `smg-grpc-proto==0.4.9`, `grpcio==1.81.0` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: [Bug] NEXTN (MTP) + structured output (xgrammar) crashes scheduler on Mamba-hybrid model (Qwen3.5-397B) — TypeError 'NoneType' in prepare_mamba_track_for_verify (sm_100)
signals.text: ## Describe the bug With `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN` enabled on a Mamba-hybrid model (`Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8`), sending a request with **structured output** (`response_format` = `json_schema` or `json_object`) crashes **all TP scheduler ranks** and brings the server down (`/health` 200 → 000). Notably: - The structured output itself is **functionally correct** — for one request the server returns schema-valid JSON, then the scheduler dies immediately after. - Happens **regardless of `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`** (true or false). - **Without** speculative decoding, structured output works fine. **With** NEXTN but **without** structured output, chat / tool-calling / high-concurrency all work fine and stably. This looks adjacent to #26957 (NEXTN + hybrid-SWA + sm_100 crash, fixed 2026-06-09), but is triggered specifically by the **structured-output (grammar) + spec-verify + mamba-track** interaction rather than `trtllm_mha` attention. ## Reproduction Launch (8x B200, sm_100): ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 --tp 8 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --port 30000 ``` Request (crashes the server; `enable_thinking` true or false both crash): ```bash curl http://localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8", "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Extract: John Smith is 42 years old and lives in Seoul. Return JSON."}], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 256, "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}, "response_format": {"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":"person","schema":{ "type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"age":{"type":"integer"},"city":{"type":"string"}}, "required":["name","age","city"],"additionalProperties":false}}} }' ``` ## Observed - Response (when it returns): `{"name":"John Smith","age":42,"city":"Seoul"}` (schema-valid). - Immediately after, all TP ranks log: ``` [TP*] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last): ... File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py", line 1025, in forward_batch_generation File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py", line 1237, in verify File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py", line 318, in eagle_prepare_for_verify File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/spec_utils.py", line 550, in prepare_mamba_track_for_verify TypeError: 'NoneType' object cannot be interpreted as an integer ``` - Server dies; subsequent requests get connection refused. ## Expected Structured output (grammar-constrained decoding) should coexist with NEXTN speculative decoding on Mamba-hybrid models, or at minimum fail the request gracefully without killing the scheduler. ## Environment - SGLang: `0.5.13.post2.dev332+g486ec150d` (main, installed for Qwen3.5 support) - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` (Mamba-hybrid MoE), TP=8 - GPU: NVIDIA B200 (sm_100); torch 2.11+cu13, flashinfer 0.6.12, sgl-kernel 0.4.3 - attention_backend `triton`, moe_runner_backend `flashinfer_trtllm`, `--mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer` ## Workaround Route structured-output requests to a non-speculative endpoint (disable NEXTN for `response_format` json requests). Chat / tool / concurrency on NEXTN are unaffected.

signals.title: [Bug]
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug When launching a prefill server with --enable-prefill-cp (prefill context parallel) for a WNA16-quantized MoE model (e.g., Kimi K2.5), the server crashes during initialization with the following error: NotImplementedError: Runner backend MoeRunnerBackend.MARLIN requires a fused func for a2a backend deepep, but none is registered. Workaround Attempted (Not Working) Adding --moe-a2a-backend none to the launch command does not fix the issue. The flag is silently overridden. After tracing the code, the root cause is in server_args.py (~line 2134): when --enable-prefill-cp is used together with an MLA-based model (e.g., DeepSeek V3 / Kimi K2.5), moe_a2a_backend is unconditionally forced to "deepep", regardless of what the user explicitly sets: # server_args.py if self.enable_prefill_cp and self.use_mla_backend(): ... self.moe_a2a_backend = "deepep" # overrides user's --moe-a2a-backend none This means the user-provided --moe-a2a-backend none has no effect. Root Cause The conflict is between two components: Prefill CP + MLA forces moe_a2a_backend = "deepep" for correctness reasons (in server_args.py). WNA16 quantization (via Compressed Tensors) automatically selects CompressedTensorsWNA16MarlinMoEMethod, which creates MoeRunner(MoeRunnerBackend.MARLIN, ...). In FusedOpPool, the ("deepep", "marlin") combination has no registered fused function (only ("none", "marlin") exists in marlin.py), causing the NotImplementedError. Relevant call stack summary: server_args.py: moe_a2a_backend forced to "deepep" due to --enable-prefill-cp + MLA → compressed_tensors_wNa16_moe.py: creates MoeRunner(MoeRunnerBackend.MARLIN, ...) → runner.py: FusedOpPool.get_fused_func("deepep", "marlin") → None → raise NotImplementedError(...) Either: The ("deepep", "marlin") fused function is registered so that Marlin MoE works with DeepEP all-to-all, or A clear early error is raised stating that WNA16/Marlin quantization is not compatible with --enable-prefill-cp (which requires DeepEP), rather than failing with a cryptic internal error. Suggested Fix Register a @register_fused_func("deepep", "marlin") function in sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/marlin.py that handles DeepEPNormalDispatchOutput (used in prefill/high-throughput mode) and adapts it to call fused_marlin_moe with the pre-dispatched tokens. Alternatively, a short-term fix in server_args.py could detect the Marlin/WNA16 quantization and raise an informative error (or skip the deepep override) when --enable-prefill-cp is used with an incompatible quantization scheme. ### Reproduction NotImplementedError: MoeRunnerBackend.MARLIN requires a fused func for a2a backend deepep when using --enable-prefill-cp with WNA16-quantized MoE model When launching a prefill server with --enable-prefill-cp (prefill context parallel) for a WNA16-quantized MoE model (e.g., Kimi K2.5), --moe-a2a-backend none； --enable-prefill-context-parallel --attention-backend fa3 --attn-cp-size 8 ### Environment Model: Kimi K2.5 (uses DeepseekV3ForCausalLM as language model) Quantization: WNA16 via Compressed Tensors (CompressedTensorsWNA16MarlinMoEMethod) Launch args include: --enable-prefill-cp, --disaggregation-mode prefill SGLang version: (custom build from /sgl-workspace/sglang)

signals.title: Tool-call parsers lose or corrupt data at streaming chunk boundaries (multiple detectors)
signals.text: A sweep of `function_call/` found several streaming/parse bugs, all reproduced by feeding text to the real detector classes. Common root causes: (a) streaming state machines with no end-of-stream `_buffer` flush (`function_call_parser.parse_stream_chunk` never flushes, and `serving_chat._check_for_unstreamed_tool_args` only rescues the last tool's trailing args and bails when `prev_tool_call_arr` is empty); (b) hand-rolled brace/bracket/token counting that ignores string-literal context; (c) regex written for the happy path applied to the whole buffer / untrusted output. **Data loss (drops arguments or whole tool calls):** - `base_format_detector.parse_streaming_increment` (name-send branch, ~`:244-271`) emits the tool name and returns without emitting args, without populating `prev_tool_call_arr`, and without advancing `_buffer`. With coarse chunking (batched detok, `stream_interval>1`, speculative decode) 2 parallel tool calls lose data in **71% (Qwen25) / 91% (Hermes)** of random 1-4 chunk splits; a single tool call in one chunk streams `arguments: ""`. Affects Qwen25/Hermes/Mistral/Llama32/GLM4/DeepSeekV3. - `step3_detector.py:264,318`: `param_regex.finditer(invoke_part)` is not bounded by `</steptml:invoke>`, so with two calls the second is dropped and its params are grafted onto the first. - `kimik2_detector.py:394`: `_split_pending_start` range stops at 2, so a lone trailing `<` (prefix of both section/call begin tokens) is not held back -> the whole call is dropped and raw tokens leak to normal_text. **Corruption (emits invalid JSON / mangled text):** - `kimik2_detector.py:316-320`: when `<|tool_call_end|>` splits across a chunk, `args_full = buffer[args_start:]` includes the partial end-token prefix and streams it as argument content (never retracted) -> `json.loads` raises `Extra data`. - `deepseekv3_detector.py:114-118`: the greedy DOTALL streaming regex `...<sep>(.*)\n\`\`\`json...` spans two calls in one increment, so `tool_index 0` gets the second tool's name. - `llama32_detector.py:124-125`: `re.sub(r"'([^']*)':", ...)` over the whole buffer injects a `\"` inside JSON string values that contain `'x':` or `: 'x'`, truncating them (e.g. an arg echoing a dict literal). - `deepseekv3_detector.py:72-86` (+ v31): the per-call loop is in one `try`; a single malformed call jumps to `except`, discarding already-parsed valid calls and returning the raw markup as normal_text. **Prose corruption / off-by-one:** - `base_format_detector.py:160-161` / `mistral_detector.py:133-134`: `normal_text.replace(self.eot_token, "")` with Mistral `eot_token="]"` deletes every `]` in ordinary assistant text (`"item[0] done"` -> `"item[0 done"`). - `llama32_detector.py:72`: `idx += end + len(tool_call_separator)` assumes a `;` always follows a decoded object, so trailing normal text with no separator loses its first char. - `pythonic_detector._find_matching_bracket:113-133` counts `[`/`]` without respecting string literals, so a string arg containing `]` mis-slices the call and it is dropped in streaming. Each is individually reproducible against the real detector. Same family as the recently-fixed streaming-detok duplication -- streaming state that loses/corrupts data at chunk boundaries. Happy to send PRs for the self-contained ones (e.g. the Mistral `]` strip, the Llama32 first-char drop, the DeepSeek discard-all-on-error) if the direction is welcome. cc @JustinTong0323 @CatherineSue

signals.title: [RFC] PD disaggregation: single protocol layer, per-backend transport
signals.text: ## Summary The three PD transfer backends (mooncake, nixl, mori) each implement the full bootstrap + transfer control protocol independently: ZMQ socket loops, message dispatch, room/state lifecycle, staging glue, TP/DCP slice orchestration, timeouts, failure handling. They describe the same protocol but have drifted apart. This RFC proposes a **target end state** where the protocol exists once and a backend only implements data movement. It is an early proposal: the interface below is a sketch, and whether the end state is reachable exactly as drawn is open. ## Why The divergence is not cosmetic -- each copy is missing something the others have. Examples from comparing the three: - mori's decode manager never starts the heartbeat checker thread, so a dead prefill peer is never detected (mooncake and nixl both start it). - nixl's sender never enforces the bootstrap timeout, and prefill-side transfer failures are not propagated to decode -- requests hang until the generic waiting timeout instead of failing fast. - The transfer-info message swaps two frame positions between mooncake and nixl; both frames hold integers, so a mismatch would silently exchange two fields rather than fail cleanly. Every protocol fix or feature is currently written up to three times (staging exists in mooncake+nixl only, DCP relayout in mooncake+nixl only, session blacklisting in mooncake only), and the per-backend classes are dispatched through an enum-keyed `get_kv_class` table that erases static typing. ## Target end state (sketch, open to change) One concrete set of protocol classes -- `KVManager` / `KVSender` / `KVReceiver` / `KVBootstrapServer` -- with no backend subclasses. Socket loops, parsing/dispatch, room lifecycle, staging, chunking, TP/DCP slice math, timeouts, heartbeat, failure propagation live there, once. A backend provides only a transport object, injected at construction: ```python class BaseTransport(ABC): def init_engine(self): ... def register_memory(self, kv_args): ... def local_desc(self) -> bytes: ... # opaque, carried in the register message def open_peer(self, session_id, desc: bytes) -> Peer: ... def submit(self, peer, blocks) -> Handle: ... # blocks = [(src_ptr, dst_ptr, len)] def poll(self, handle) -> KVPoll: ... ``` Boundary: protocol decides which bytes go where and when; transport moves `(src_ptr, dst_ptr, len)` and names remote memory. Backend directories shrink to thin wrappers around their engines (today mooncake calls 5 engine methods, nixl 14, mori 8). `get_kv_class` / `KVClassType` are replaced by a typed `make_transport(backend)`. The `fake` backend becomes a null transport, which also makes the whole protocol layer testable in CPU-only CI. There is no big-bang refactor implied: the intended path is many small PRs -- behavior alignments (individually reviewable fixes) and mechanical hoists of already-identical code. Wire-format unification goes last and needs its own migration story, since there is no version negotiation today. ## Open questions - Completion signaling: mooncake/mori report status to decode over ZMQ; nixl uses in-band transport notifications with a passive decode side. Which model should the unified layer own? - Is the 6-method transport interface sufficient? (nixl's prepped descriptor lists need per-peer cached state; mixed VRAM/DRAM pools are nixl-only today.) - `is_dummy` / abort-ack / guard-frame semantics differ subtly across the three; each needs a call on which behavior is intended. - Wire migration: flag day vs a version frame with a dual-parse window. Feedback from the mooncake / nixl / mori owners is the main ask -- especially whether this target shape conflicts with anything planned for the backends.

signals.title: [Bug] [Diffusion] Attention backend fallback change introduced errors on most models
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Hi! Previously, if the desired attention backend was not part of any of the supported attention backends for the component, it defaulted to SDPA. PR #33707 changed the behavior so that it raises an error instead. Most text encoders (and some other components) have attention in them, but it's only supported via FAv3 or SDPA due to the input tensor dimensions. On ROCm, the default requested attention backend is AITER, so this now raises an error for pretty much all models. Most models don't outright crash entirely, they just revert to the diffusers version of the component instead of using the optimized sgl-d version, though MiniMax-H3 crashes fully (diffusers versions are not allowed). This is not limited to ROCm only - any desired backend that is not FA or SDPA will run into this issue (SageAttention, NPU etc). While it is possible to overcome this by adding `--component-attention-backends.text_encoder torch_sdpa`, this is not signaled to the user nor is it really that nice UX. I made this into a ticket instead of PR, as I'm not sure what's the best fix instead of just reverting it. It seems there's currently some attention backend related refactoring going on, maybe this is included in it. Thanks! @mickqian ### Reproduction ``` sglang generate --model-path black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev --height 1024 --width 1024 --ulysses-degree 8 --ring-degree 1 --num-gpus 8 --num-inference-steps 50 --guidance-scale 4.0 --prompt "Add a cool hat to the cat" --dit-cpu-offload False --dit-layerwise-offload False --text-encoder-cpu-offload False --image-encoder-cpu-offload False --offload-during-compile False --vae-cpu-offload False --warmup-mode request --warmup-steps 2 --vae-precision bf16 --image-encoder-precision bf16 --output-path /outputs/flux2.default --seed 42 --image-path /app/data/flux_cat.png --enable-torch-compile ``` ### Environment ``` Python: 3.12.3 (main, Mar 23 2026, 19:04:32) [GCC 13.3.0] ROCM available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: AMD Instinct MI355X GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 9.5 ROCM_HOME: /opt/rocm HIPCC: HIP version: 7.13.26183-444cadec35 ROCM Driver Version: 6.16.2 PyTorch: 2.9.1+gitff65f5b sglang: signals.title: [Bug] Kimi-K3 tool call parser fails ~8x/hour in production: TypeError 'string indices must be integers' and json 'unexpected character'
signals.text: ## Describe the bug Running Kimi-K3 with `--tool-call-parser kimi_k3` in production (agentic coding workload, Claude-Code-style tool loop), the tool call parser raises on a significant fraction of model outputs. Over a 24h window with moderate traffic we counted **~190 parser failures**: - 106x `Tool call parsing error: string indices must be integers` (TypeError — a parsed call is indexed like a dict but is a str) - 84x `Tool call parsing error: unexpected character: line 1 column 1 (char 0)` (json.loads on a non-JSON argument payload) - 1x `Tool call parsing error: Input is a zero-length, empty document` Logged from `serving_chat.py` ("Tool call parsing error") — the request then falls back to returning the raw text instead of a structured `tool_calls` entry, so the client sees a turn without tool calls and the agent loop degrades or retries. ## Environment - SGLang 0.5.17-tree, ROCm (8x MI350X, gfx950), `--tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --enable-strict-thinking`, grammar backend xgrammar - Failures occur both with streaming and non-streaming chat completions ## Analysis `function_call/kimik3_detector.py` extracts calls via `_CALL_RE`/`_ARG_RE` and then: - `json.loads(raw_value)` on each argument value — raises `unexpected character` when the model emits an unquoted/partial value (this is exactly the second error class), and - downstream consumers index `call["name"]`/`call["arguments"]` — the `string indices` TypeError suggests a code path where the parsed call is still a plain string (e.g. malformed/partial `<|open|>call ...` block that the regex only partially matches). ## Expected behavior Malformed tool-call blocks from the model should be handled defensively (skip the malformed call and/or return it as text with a warning), never raise inside the parser. Given Kimi-K3 is explicitly advertised for agentic workloads, hardening this parser has outsized impact — at our traffic every ~7-8 minutes an agent turn silently loses its tool call. ## Reproduction We do not yet have a captured raw failing sample (the error log does not include the payload). We are happy to add debug logging in production and attach concrete failing model outputs if that helps — please tell us the preferred capture point. ## Checklist - [x] Searched existing issues — found tool_call_id-related PRs for kimi-k3 but nothing covering these parser exceptions.
signals.author: stefanskiasan

signals.title: [Bug] Scheduler crashes with AttributeError ('list' object has no attribute 'tolist') on mixed batches with token_ids_logprob — prefill and decode paths, v0.5.14–v0.5.17
signals.text: ## Summary The scheduler process dies with ``` AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'tolist' ``` whenever a request using `token_ids_logprob` shares a batch with a request that does not. One scoring client can take the whole server down. This affects the released versions **v0.5.14, v0.5.16, and v0.5.17** (verified by reading each tag's source), in **both** the prefill and decode result paths of `scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py`. ## Mechanism `next_token_token_ids_logprobs_val` holds one entry per request in the batch. Requests that asked for token-ids logprobs contribute GPU tensors; co-batched requests that did not contribute plain `[]` entries (in decode, `get_token_ids_logprobs_raw` appends a bare `[]` for `token_ids is None`; the prefill delayed-D2H path produces plain lists as well). The consumer then calls `.tolist()` unconditionally on every entry: ```python # batch_result_processor.py, v0.5.17 — same in v0.5.14/v0.5.16 if logits_output.next_token_token_ids_logprobs_val: logits_output.next_token_token_ids_logprobs_val = [ v.tolist() for v in logits_output.next_token_token_ids_logprobs_val ] ``` The same unguarded pattern appears twice — in the prefill-path `move_logprobs_to_cpu` and in `_normalize_decode_outputs` — and `next_token_top_logprobs_val` / `next_token_top_logprobs_idx` carry the identical latent bug at both sites. Solo scoring requests survive (batch of one, all tensors), so light testing passes; the first *mixed* batch in production kills the scheduler. The HTTP server keeps answering `/health` with 503, so under Kubernetes the pod sits dead until a liveness probe restarts it, and the next such request kills it again — a crash loop. ## Reproduction Server: `sglang serve <any model> --port 8000` (observed on Qwen3.5-9B-based checkpoints, but the bug is model-independent). Send two concurrent requests so they co-batch, one scoring + decoding, one plain: ```bash curl -s localhost:8000/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "text": "The capital of France is", "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 8, "temperature": 0}, "return_logprob": true, "token_ids_logprob": [3837, 715]}' & curl -s localhost:8000/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "text": "Water boils at a temperature of", "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 8, "temperature": 0}}' & wait ``` Observed traceback (v0.5.14, overlap event loop, decode path): ``` File ".../managers/scheduler.py", line 1578, in event_loop_overlap pop_and_process() File ".../managers/scheduler.py", line 1544, in pop_and_process self.process_batch_result(tmp_batch, tmp_result) File ".../managers/scheduler.py", line 3375, in process_batch_result self.batch_result_processor.process_batch_result_decode(batch, result) File ".../scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py", line 657, in process_batch_result_decode next_token_ids, next_token_logprobs = self._normalize_decode_outputs( File ".../scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py", line 783, in _normalize_decode_outputs v.tolist() for v in logits_output.next_token_token_ids_logprobs_val AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'tolist' ``` The prefill-path twin of this crash (`move_logprobs_to_cpu` site) was hit the same way by prefill-only scoring traffic (`max_new_tokens=0`, `logprob_start_len=N-1`). ## History and related work - I fixed this once in #25183 (May 2026), but the refactor #25709 deleted `scheduler_output_processor_mixin.py` the next day, so I closed the PR; the refactored `batch_result_processor.py` reintroduced the unguarded pattern at both sites. - #34075 (opened today) fixes the **decode producer** by keeping `token_ids is None` entries tensor-typed under `no_copy_to_cpu` — it would fix the decode crash, but not the prefill-path variant, and the consumer sites stay fragile (`next_token_top_logprobs_val/_idx` included). - #30188 reports an adjacent but distinct mixed-batch crash in the prefill token-id logprob extraction (`torch.tensor(None)`). ## Suggested fix We run this consumer-side guard in production (as an image patch on v0.5.14 and v0.5.16); it is small and mirrors the producer-side precedent in `GenerationBatchResult.copy_to_cpu_async` (`v.to('cpu', non_blocking=True) if torch.is_tensor(v) else v`): ```python v.tolist() if torch.is_tensor(v) else v for v in logits_output.next_token_token_ids_logprobs_val ``` applied to all six comprehensions (`token_ids_logprobs_val`, `top_logprobs_val`, `top_logprobs_idx` × prefill/decode sites). Happy to submit this as a PR (a revival of #25183 against the current layout) — it composes with #34075 rather than conflicting with it. ## Environment - sglang v0.5.14 (`lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.14-cu130`) and v0.5.16 (`lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.16-cu130-runtime`), crash observed in production on both; v0.5.17 verified affected by source inspection. - Single B200, TP=1, dense Qwen3.5-9B fine-tune, `--attention-backend trtllm_mha`, overlap scheduling (default).

signals.title: [Bug] compressed-tensors FP8 lm_head weight_scale silently dropped → degenerate repetition with unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Serving [unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4) (compressed-tensors mixed-precision: NVFP4 W4A4 MLP layers 0–55, FP8 W8A8 per-channel linear_attn / layers 56–63 MLP / **lm_head**) with sglang produces severely degraded output: the model repeats a single phrase forever inside reasoning (e.g. ``"need analysis there need analysis there need analysis there ..."``) from the very first token, even for a short 67-token prompt, and finishes with empty content (`finish_reason=length`). The same checkpoint serves correctly with vLLM. ## Root cause `CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method()` only dispatches `LinearBase` and `FusedMoE`. `ParallelLMHead` (a `VocabParallelEmbedding` subclass) falls through to `return None` → `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`, so the FP8 `lm_head.weight_scale` is never loaded: ``` Parameter lm_head.weight_scale not found in params_dict ``` The raw FP8 `lm_head.weight` (values ~±448) is then consumed as if it were BF16. The per-channel scales (mean ≈ 1.55e-4, row-to-row spread up to 12×) are never applied, so logits ranking is badly corrupted (top-10 tokens overlap only 2/10 with the correct dequantized head) → garbage/looping generation. ## Related issues/PRs - **#28130** (PR, open): proposes exactly this `ParallelLMHead` dispatch, but only supports WNA16 (pack-quantized) heads and explicitly rejects W8A8-FP8. This model's FP8 lm_head needs the same dispatch without that restriction. - **vllm-project/vllm#37291** (merged): vLLM fixed the identical gap and routes **all** matching schemes (including W8A8-FP8) through `CompressedTensorsLinearMethod`. I verified the same approach works in sglang: `LogitsProcessor._compute_lm_head` already routes a quantized head through `quant_method.apply()` via `should_apply_lm_head_quant_method`, so FP8 W8A8 lm_head is computed correctly on the FP8 CUTLASS path. ### Reproduction ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --tp 2 --attention-backend flashinfer --kv-cache-dtype auto \ --chunked-prefill-size 2048 --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \ --max-running-requests 4 --cuda-graph-max-bs 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.78 ``` Request: `Which is larger, 9.11 or 9.9? Answer briefly.` ### Environment - sglang commit 41cd5a7 (2026-08-14), TP=2 - Hardware: 2× RTX 5090 (sm120), flashinfer 0.6.17

signals.title: [Feature] Bit-exact correctness coverage for Unified Radix Cache
signals.text: ## Motivation Cache correctness is difficult to verify from model output alone. A corrupted KV block or recurrent-state checkpoint can still produce fluent text, and the resulting numerical drift can remain far below the tolerance used by accuracy and KL tests. These failures have shipped because the existing signals are approximate. Bit-exact logprob consistency turns one of these approximate signals into a correctness oracle. `kl_test_utils` evaluates the same token through prefill and decode. If both paths are batch-invariant and compute the same function, they must produce identical logprobs. Once that baseline is established, the contract for every cache-reuse path becomes: > **Any nonzero KL is a KV/state reuse bug.** This is stronger than threshold-based testing. It does not ask whether the error is large enough to matter to a benchmark. It asks whether restoring cached state is exactly equivalent to recomputing it. Bugs that previously sat below a model-specific noise floor become unambiguous regressions. Examples: - Incorrect reused state: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34043, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34184, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29792 ## Foundation Bit-exactness depends on the model and execution path. Deterministic inference can remove batch-dependent kernel and communication behavior, but it cannot make two mathematically different algorithms identical. For example, Qwen3-Next uses different GDN kernels for prefill and decode, and retains a nonzero numerical floor. Inkling provides the combination needed for continuous gating. Its prefill and decode paths compute the same function, so under deterministic inference its prefill-versus-decode KL is exactly `0`. A shrunken checkpoint runs on one GPU. The model also contains `FULL`, `SWA`, and `MAMBA` cache components, so one test process exercises full KV, sliding-window, and recurrent-state reuse together. The resulting foundation has four layers: 1. deterministic execution makes repeated computation batch-invariant; 2. logprob consistency establishes an exact prefill/decode baseline; 3. cache tests apply that baseline to each state restoration path; 4. revert-then-red validation proves that each regression guard can detect the defect it claims to cover. Supporting work: - Inkling deterministic execution: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33417, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34159 - Workflow tools: [KL consistency test skill](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/.claude/skills/kl-consistency-test), https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34169 - Real-weight consistency coverage: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34168, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34356 - Per-commit guards: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34607 - Calibration and follow-up validation: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34405, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34653 ## Roadmap The remaining work is coverage, not a new testing method. Every feature that can save, move, or restore model state introduces a distinct correctness boundary and needs its own exact-KL test arm. - [x] Base cache path - [x] Mamba `extra_buffer` - [ ] Mamba `extra_buffer_lazy` - [x] HiCache multi-turn - [ ] Speculative decoding - [ ] MTP - [ ] DSpark / DFlash @alphabetc1 - Support return_logprob - [ ] Unified memory

signals.title: [diffusion] MiniMax-H3 resident serving stages a full DiT copy per rank through host RAM (114.3 GiB @ 2 ranks, 233.5 @ 4; silent SIGKILL below); only the RTX 5090 recipe documents a host-memory requirement
signals.text: ## Summary On the resident (non-FSDP) path, each rank stages the complete 61.7 GiB DiT checkpoint through host RAM during load. Measured at two scales, 3 s sampling, isolated to the DiT load: **114.3 GiB on 2 ranks, 233.5 GiB on 4** — 57.2 and 58.4 GiB per rank, i.e. linear in rank count. Container-wide usage peaked at **~377 GiB** during the 4-rank load (1024→647.5 GiB available), which is why a 384 GiB host dies: it misses by single-digit GiB. The death is an OOM kill mid-load with no sglang-level error — the last log line is `Loading safetensors with Run:ai Model Streamer to cpu`, then SIGKILL (exit 137). The docs state a host-memory requirement in exactly two places, both for the RTX 5090 recipe — *"validated on 2× RTX 5090 (32 GB each) and a 377 GiB host; use a 384 GiB-class machine"* (mdx §3, line 168) and *"with a 384 GiB-class host"* (picker jsx, rtx5090 cell warn, line 638). No datacenter recipe carries one, in either file, and every benchmark table reports Peak/GPU only. So the convention of stating host memory where it binds already exists; this asks for it to be applied to the recipes where the number is larger and the failure is silent. This is a docs request plus one optional loader-observability suggestion, not a report of a malfunction. *Doc citations below reference `docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3.mdx` (rev `a86edcdc`) and the picker config it imports at its line 74, `docs/src/snippets/configs/MiniMaxAI/minimax-h3.jsx` (rev `a25c330e`). Both files were read end to end; every citation carries the quoted phrase so it survives line drift.* ## Mechanism, from the streamer's own logs One full-checkpoint CPU stream **per rank** — four of them on the recommended 4-GPU recipe: ``` [08-15 03:30:47] [RunAI Streamer] Overall time to stream 61.7 GiB of all files to cpu: 26.78s, 2.3 GiB/s [08-15 03:30:47] [RunAI Streamer] Overall time to stream 61.7 GiB of all files to cpu: 26.92s, 2.3 GiB/s [08-15 03:30:47] [RunAI Streamer] Overall time to stream 61.7 GiB of all files to cpu: 26.97s, 2.3 GiB/s [08-15 03:30:47] [RunAI Streamer] Overall time to stream 61.7 GiB of all files to cpu: 26.94s, 2.3 GiB/s [08-15 03:32:20] Loaded transformer: MiniMaxH3DiTModel ... model size: 61.73 GB ``` (Timestamps UTC.) Ulysses shards the sequence, not the weights, so at `tp_size=1` each rank ends up holding — and first staging through CPU — a full DiT copy. The docs themselves name this property, in the RTX 5090 context: *"TP2 avoids the full per-rank DiT replication observed with Ulysses2 on PCIe"* (picker jsx, rtx5090 warn, line 638). That sentence speaks to the offload/PCIe recipe rather than the resident datacenter path, so I cite it only as evidence that per-rank replication under Ulysses is a known property — the host-staging consequence on the resident path is what goes unstated. The text encoder in the same load sequence streams straight to each device (`... to cuda:0`, `to cuda:1`) and is genuinely sharded: 25.26 GB resident on 2 ranks vs 13.91 GB on 4. ## Measurements | build | GPUs | topology | RAM limit | host RAM for the DiT load | outcome | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | nightly `c4271c3f` | 2 | `tp=1 u=2` | 1024 GiB | **114.3 GiB** (945.5→831.2 avail) | ✅ 67.6 s | | nightly `c4271c3f` | 4 | `tp=1 u=4` | 1024 GiB | **233.5 GiB** (881.0→647.5 avail) | ✅ 43.1 s | | nightly `c4271c3f` | 2 | `tp=1 u=2` + FSDP | 1024 GiB | **12.8 GiB**, no `to cpu` streams | ✅ 30.6 s | | 0.5.17 | 4 | `tp=1 u=4` | 384 GiB | — (353→22 avail, then froze) | died | | 0.5.17 | 4 | `tp=2 u=2` | 384 GiB | — (372→59 avail) | **SIGKILL, exit 137** | The nightly rows use 3 s sampling isolated to the DiT load. `MemAvailable` sampling bounds the peak from below. `tp_size=2` does not reduce the staging — the full checkpoint is read into CPU before sharding. `--pin-cpu-memory false` only changes the failure mode (with the default `true`, pinning a buffer this size under a sandboxed runtime stalled 16+ min without completing). ## Why the missing line bites 1. **Resident is the documented default and the picker's recommendation.** The mdx: *"For a four-card H200 host, keep the full BF16/FP32 model resident by default. The model fits without FSDP"* (lines 89–91) — "fits" meaning GPU memory. The picker's FSDP cells steer back: *"Prefer Resident when the full pipeline fits"* (jsx lines 502, 518). 2. **The resident-vs-FSDP trade is framed GPU-only everywhere.** *"FSDP reduces DiT weight residency at the cost of per-block parameter collectives"* (mdx lines 66–71; similarly line 760 and the jsx warns). The host-RAM axis — 114.3 vs 12.8 GiB at 2 ranks — appears nowhere, and on smaller hosts it is the deciding axis. 3. **Users of `quality: "high"` cannot take the FSDP escape.** Cache-DiT *"cannot be combined with FSDP inference"* (mdx lines 645–646), and the audited serve command pins `--use-fsdp-inference false` (mdx line 557). For them the per-rank staging path is mandatory. 4. **The failure is illegible.** No error, no warning; the container is killed by the OS mid-load. Diagnosing this from scratch cost three 4×H200 runs (~$11). For completeness, FSDP measured as a strictly better *loader* on every axis we checked: byte-identical MP4 to the resident path (same seed/prompt, sha256 equal), +0.5% inference latency, 57.8 vs 98.8 GB/card peak, faster startup, 12.8 vs 114.3 GiB host staging. ## Asks 1. **Add a host-memory line to the datacenter recipes**, following the existing RTX 5090 convention (mdx line 168 / jsx line 638). Suggested wording: *"host RAM during load scales with rank count — about 58 GiB per rank for the DiT alone (measured 114.3 GiB on 2 ranks, 233.5 GiB on 4), with container-wide usage peaking near 380 GiB on the 4-GPU resident recipe; use a 512 GiB-class host, or the FSDP profile, which removes the staging entirely."* 2. **Add the host-RAM axis to the FSDP framing** (mdx lines 66–71 and 760; jsx FSDP cell warns): FSDP does not only reduce GPU residency, it removes the per-rank CPU staging. 3. **Surface `--direct-gpu-weight-loading` in the recipes.** Nightly has grown exactly the escape this report would otherwise ask for: the DiT loader (`runtime/loader/component_loaders/transformer_loader.py:222`) passes `load_full_state_dict_on_device=direct_gpu_weight_loading` into its `WeightLoadPlan`, and the flag's tests show it is scoped to the unquantized, non-FSDP, non-offload, `tp=1` path — i.e. precisely the resident recipes above. It defaults to off and is mentioned nowhere in either cookbook file. (I have not yet measured it; the staging numbers above are with the default off.) 4. *Optional, code:* make the default path's failure legible. When the CPU staging path is chosen, log the expected staging size — the loader knows the checkpoint size and the runtime knows the rank count — or warn when it exceeds available RAM. Staging path: `safetensors_weights_iterator` (`runtime/loader/weight_utils.py:189`), whose `to_cpu` parameter defaults to `True` and whose CPU branch additionally clones each tensor; the DiT takes this default while the text encoder passes `to_cpu=False`. Happy to open the docs PR for (1)/(2)/(3) myself. ## Environment - `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260814-c4271c3f` (all measured rows), sglang 0.5.17 via pip (the two 384 GiB failure rows only); torch 2.11.0+cu130 - 2×/4× NVIDIA H200 (141 GB), CUDA 13.0.3, containerized (Modal), 16 vCPU; cgroup memory limits per table (`/proc/meminfo` inside the container reports the cgroup limit) - `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3`, FL2VA checkpoint, local volume ## Repro (cheap) 2 GPUs suffice; kill after the DiT finishes loading (no warmup or generation needed): ```bash sglang serve --model-path /path/to/MiniMax-H3 --model-type diffusion \ --model-variant fl2va --num-gpus 2 --tp-size 1 --ulysses-degree 2 \ --performance-mode speed --pin-cpu-memory false --port 30010 ``` Watch for two `Overall time to stream 61.7 GiB of all files to cpu` lines, or sample `MemAvailable` between `Loading transformer from` and `Loaded transformer`. To see the kill: cap the container below ~130 GiB (2 ranks) / ~350 GiB (4 ranks). ## Related - #19092 — lists *"Monitor Peak CPU memory usage when loading multiple state dicts into RAM simultaneously"* as a follow-up item and asks whether weights load through pageable memory. This is a measured instance of that concern (numbers above are with pageable memory, `--pin-cpu-memory false`). - #34772 — diffusion component-loading OOM, opposite direction (offload decisions dropped → GPU OOM on the fallback path). Distinct. - #33720 — the `quality="high"` deployment gate; context for "Why the missing line bites" item 3 (that tier pins the non-FSDP path).
