signals.title: [Bug] Kimi K3 decode crash: DSPARK target_verify + DCP → cumsum(extend_prefix_lens=None) in layers/dcp/planner.py
signals.text: ## Summary On Kimi K3, the **decode** side crashes deterministically when running **PD disaggregation + DCP (`--dcp-size 8`) + DSPARK speculative decoding** together. The first target-verify batch hits `dcp/planner.py` with `extend_prefix_lens=None` and all TP ranks die with `TypeError: cumsum(): argument 'input' (position 1) must be Tensor, not NoneType`. Each pair works on its own (DCP without DSPARK; DSPARK without DCP). Only the combination fails. ## Environment - Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260814-c4271c3f` (commit `c4271c3f`) - Model: Kimi K3 (hybrid: 69 KDA linear-attention layers + 24 MLA layers) - Topology: 1P1D PD disaggregation (Mooncake transfer backend), single node per side, 8 GPUs (B300) - Decode-side launch args (relevant): `--tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 7 --enable-linear-replayssm-spec --moe-a2a-backend megamoe --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --disaggregation-mode decode --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake` - Prefill side runs the same image with `--tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --speculative-dspark-block-size 7 --disaggregation-mode prefill` and stays alive; only the decode side crashes. ## Reproduction 1. Start prefill and decode with the args above. 2. Send any chat completion request through the router. 3. As soon as the decode side runs its first DSPARK target-verify batch, all ranks crash (in our case 26 minutes after process start, on first real traffic). ## Stack trace (all 8 TP ranks, identical) ``` Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last): File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 5058, in run_scheduler_process scheduler.run_event_loop() File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 4920, in dispatch_event_loop scheduler.event_loop_overlap_disagg_decode() File ".../sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py", line 2217, in event_loop_overlap_disagg_decode batch_result = self.run_batch(batch) File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 3691, in run_batch batch_result = self.model_worker.forward_batch_generation( File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py", line 424, in forward_batch_generation return self._forward_decode(batch, on_publish, grammar_barrier) File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py", line 673, in _forward_decode target_verify = self._verify_executor.run_non_compact( File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_verify.py", line 258, in run_non_compact result = self._forward_prepared_verify( File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_verify.py", line 288, in _forward_prepared_verify target_out = self.target_worker.forward_batch_generation( File ".../sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker.py", line 609, in forward_batch_generation out = self.model_runner.forward( File ".../sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 1742, in _forward_raw ret = self.eager_runner.execute( File ".../sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/eager_runner.py", line 282, in _execute_extend model_runner.model.prepare_context_parallel_metadata_for_dcp( File ".../sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py", line 3383, in prepare_context_parallel_metadata_for_dcp return self.language_model.prepare_context_parallel_metadata_for_dcp( File ".../sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py", line 2826, in prepare_context_parallel_metadata_for_dcp return prepare_decode_context_parallel_metadata( File ".../sglang/srt/layers/dcp/planner.py", line 63, in prepare_decode_context_parallel_metadata extend_cu_prefix_lens[1:] = torch.cumsum(extend_prefix_lens, dim=0) TypeError: cumsum(): argument 'input' (position 1) must be Tensor, not NoneType ``` ## Root cause analysis - `eager_runner._execute_extend` calls `prepare_context_parallel_metadata_for_dcp` unconditionally whenever `dcp_size > 1` and the batch needs forward-metadata init, passing `forward_batch.extend_prefix_lens` straight through. - The DSPARK **target-verify** batch built by `dspark_verify.run_non_compact` never populates `extend_prefix_lens` (verify tokens are not an "extend with prefix" in the usual sense), so the planner receives `None` and crashes on `torch.cumsum`. - The DCP+DSpark support merged in #32828/#33149 covered the tokenspeed MLA backend and draft-KV pool layout, but the non-compact verify path through the DCP planner has no `None` guard. Possible fixes: guard `extend_prefix_lens is None` in `prepare_decode_context_parallel_metadata` (e.g. treat verify batches as zero-prefix), or populate the field when the verify batch is constructed in `dspark_verify.run_non_compact`. ## Related work - #34343 (WIP) tracks **PD disaggregation + DCP + DSPARK**, but fixes a *different* failure point in that combination (draft KV geometry in `send_kvcache_dcp`). This issue is a second, independent bug in the same combination. - #33863 tracks PP + PD + DSpark.

signals.title: [Bug] [Responses API] input_image parts in function_call_output are not converted to image_url: 400 ChatCompletionRequest validation error (post-#25881 builds), silently dropped on current main
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug When calling `/v1/responses` with a vision model, an image placed inside a `function_call_output` item (i.e. a tool result carrying image content — e.g. the `view_image` tool output used by OpenAI Codex CLI) never reaches the model. Depending on the build: 1. **Builds containing PR #25881** ("Fix Responses API request handling"): the request fails with `400` and ~25 pydantic validation errors per image part against the internal `ChatCompletionRequest` (`Input should be 'image_url' ... input_value='input_image'`). Because every subsequent turn re-sends the same history, **the entire session becomes unusable** after the first image-bearing tool result (every turn fails with the same validation error). 2. **Current `main`** (verified in code as of commit `385903b`, 2026-08-12): the request now returns 200, but the tool message content is flattened to a text-only string, so **the image is silently dropped** and the model cannot see it (`usage` reports no image tokens). Images inside regular user/assistant messages work correctly (they are normalized by `_normalize_response_content_part_for_chat`, added in #25881). Only the `function_call_output` path is broken. ### Root cause In `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py`, `_normalize_response_message_for_chat` applies `_normalize_response_content_part_for_chat` only to `message`-type items. The `function_call_output` branch does not normalize its content parts: - #25881-era code (raw parts passed through unchanged → 400): ```python if msg_type == "function_call_output": return { "role": "tool", "tool_call_id": message.get("call_id"), "content": message.get("output", ""), } ``` - Current `main` (flatten to text only → images silently dropped): ```python if msg_type == "function_call_output": out = message.get("output", "") if isinstance(out, list): out = "".join(p.get("text", "") for p in out if isinstance(p, dict)) return {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": message.get("call_id"), "content": out} ``` ### Proposed fix Reuse the existing part normalizer for `function_call_output` content: ```python if msg_type == "function_call_output": out = message.get("output", "") if isinstance(out, list): out = [cls._normalize_response_content_part_for_chat(p) for p in out] return { "role": "tool", "tool_call_id": message.get("call_id"), "content": out, } ``` The target format was verified end-to-end against a running sglang server: a chat-completions `tool` message containing `{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": ..., "detail": "high"}}` parts passes `ChatCompletionRequest` validation and the model actually sees the image (`usage.image_tokens` is set). ### Real-world trigger OpenAI Codex CLI now uses the `/v1/responses` wire path and sends images inside tool results (e.g. `view_image`). With sglang as the backend, every turn after the first image-bearing tool result fails with `Turn error: N validation errors for ChatCompletionRequest`, rendering the session unusable. ### Related - #20644 (closed, not merged): fix `input_image` content parts for /v1/responses - #23766 (not merged): "Fix SGLang for Codex CLI switch to /v1/responses" - #29287 (open): Responses API overestimates max_output_tokens for multimodal requests, causing 400 (separate bug) ### Reproduction Command/script run and model used: ```bash # Any image-capable VLM; e.g. python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct --port 30000 ``` Reproduced with `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (Qwen3.5 family, `has_image_understanding: true`), sglang dev build containing #25881. ```bash curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/responses \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct", "input": [ {"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "input_text", "text": "Look at the image returned by the tool and tell me its color."} ]}, {"type": "function_call", "call_id": "call_1", "name": "view_image", "arguments": "{\"path\": \"test.png\"}"}, {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "call_1", "output": [ {"type": "input_image", "image_url": "https://example.com/test.png", "detail": "high"} ]} ], "max_output_tokens": 32 }' ``` (The image URL does not need to be fetchable — on affected builds the failure happens at request validation, before any image download.) **Actual behavior** - #25881-era builds: `{"error":{"message":"25 validation errors for ChatCompletionRequest ... Input should be 'image_url' [type=literal_error, input_value='input_image' ...]","type":"invalid_request_error"}}` - Current `main`: 200 OK, but the tool message content is flattened to `""` (text parts concatenated only), so no image data reaches the multimodal pipeline and the model has no image to describe. **Expected behavior** Per the OpenAI Responses API spec, `function_call_output.output` may be an array of content parts, including `input_image`. sglang should normalize these parts the same way it does for user/assistant messages (`input_image` → `{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":...,"detail":...}}`, `input_text` → `{"type":"text","text":...}`) so the image reaches the model. **Contrast (works on both builds):** the same image sent inside a `user` message content array is handled correctly. ### Environment sglang version: 0.0.0.dev0+qwen38.27b.g561c8f3 (dev build containing PR #25881; issue also present on main as of commit 385903b, 2026-08-12 — silent-drop form) model_path: RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 model_type: qwen3_5 architectures: Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration has_image_understanding: true max_model_len: 262144 dtype: auto kv_cache_dtype: fp8_e4m3 tp_size: 1 trust_remote_code: true server framework: uvicorn (sglang FastAPI entrypoint)

signals.title: [Bug] DSA sparse-MLA prefill silently computes no attention at all for a single extend > 65535 tokens (trtllm-gen gridDim.z limit is still unguarded on the non-DP path)
signals.text: ## TL;DR `gridDim.z` overflow in trtllm-gen sparse MLA (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3125) is still reachable from sglang, and still silent. On SM100, any **single unchunked extend of more than 65535 tokens** on the DSA `prefill=trtllm` path launches **zero** attention kernels, leaves the attention output tensor **uninitialized**, raises **no** Python exception, and returns garbage. `bench_one_batch` hits this by construction for `--input-len > 65535`. The onset is exact: **65535 tokens works, 65536 does not.** ### Relation to existing reports (please read before closing as duplicate) | prior art | state | why this report is not covered by it | |---|---|---| | flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3125 — "trtllm-gen attention error on large batch size" | closed 2026-04-21, **no fix commit** | Correctly diagnosed the root cause. Maintainer proposed "just raise an error"; that was never implemented. `fmhaKernels.cuh` still has a bare `int numCtasZ = params.mBatchSize;` and `cuErrCheck` still only `fprintf`s. | | sgl-project/sglang#29453 — GLM-5.2 NVFP4 DP4 long-context crash | closed 2026-06-27, **no code fix** | Same root cause, but reported via a *downstream* symptom (invalid sampling probabilities) under **DP attention**, and closed after the reporter worked around it with `--chunked-prefill-size`. No guard landed. | | sgl-project/sglang#29522 — "Guard Blackwell TRT-LLM prefill chunk size" | **closed, not merged** | The only guard attempt. It capped `chunked_prefill_size` / `get_max_chunk_capacity()` in `server_args.py` + `forward_batch_deepseek_mha_mixin.py` — i.e. **server config only**, gated on `enable_dp_attention`. It would not have covered the direct-ModelRunner path (`bench_one_batch`, `dp_size=1`) at all, and it never landed anyway. | | flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3238 — `cum_seq_lens_q` for trtllm-gen MLA | merged 2026-06-24 | This is the structural cure (stop flattening tokens into the batch dim), but sglang has **not adopted it**: `dsa_backend.py:3242` still does `q_all.view(batch_size, 1, num_heads, head_dim)`. | **New in this report:** (a) the fault is reachable with `dp_size=1` on the plain ModelRunner path, which no proposed guard covered; (b) an exact one-token onset bisection (65535 vs 65536); (c) direct proof of *silent corruption* — a sentinel-filled `out` tensor comes back untouched — rather than an inferred downstream symptom; (d) profiler proof that `0` of `num_layers` attention kernels run, so `bench_one_batch` silently reports **falsely fast** long-context prefill numbers. Also worth noting: sglang already guards this exact hardware limit elsewhere — `python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:298` gates a fused kernel on `query.shape[0] < 65535`, and `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/mamba_slot_fused.py:133` comments "gridDim.y/z cap at 65535". The DSA attention path has no such check. ## Environment | | | |---|---| | GPU | NVIDIA B200 (SM100), driver 590.48.01 | | sglang | `18107e38d266a98f59a8e3c766f8ddaf9b723ded` (main, 2026-08-14) | | flashinfer-python | 0.6.17 | | sglang-kernel | 0.4.6.post1 | | torch | 2.13.0 / Python 3.12.3 | | resolved backends | `Set DSA backends for fp8_e4m3 KV Cache: prefill=trtllm, decode=trtllm.` | `prefill=trtllm` here is the **auto-selected default** for fp8 KV on SM100 — no `--dsa-prefill-backend` flag was passed. (`enable_auto_select_prefill_impl` at `dsa_backend.py:350` is only true when the resolved impl is literally `flashmla_auto`, so the `flashmla_sparse`/`flashmla_kv` rewrite in `set_dsa_prefill_impl` does not apply here.) Reproduced on two models and two TP degrees: a 78-layer DSA MLA model at TP8, and a 47-layer `DeepseekV32ForCausalLM` fp8 checkpoint (`index_topk=2048`) at TP2. TP degree is irrelevant — the overflowing dimension is the token/pseudo-batch dimension, which TP does not shard. Note `SGLANG_DSA_PREFILL_DENSE_ATTN_KV_LEN_THRESHOLD` defaults to **2048** (`python/sglang/srt/environ.py:1375`), so both 32768 and 131072 take the same MLA path — the difference in behaviour is purely the 65535 overflow, not an MHA/MLA path switch. ## Minimal reproducer (no model, no sglang, ~30 s) Same FlashInfer entry point sglang calls, with a sentinel-filled `out` so "did the kernel run?" is directly observable: ```python import sys, torch, flashinfer B = int(sys.argv[1]) # pseudo-batch == number of query tokens NH, TOPK, KVL, ROPE, HD = 16, 2048, 512, 64, 576 PAGE, PAGES, SENT = 64, 8192, -31337.0 kv = torch.zeros(PAGES, 1, PAGE, HD, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device="cuda") ws = torch.empty(256 << 20, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda") q = torch.zeros(B, 1, NH, HD, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device="cuda") bt = torch.zeros(B, 1, TOPK, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") sl = torch.full((B,), TOPK, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") out = torch.full((B, 1, NH, KVL), SENT, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") flashinfer.decode.trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla( query=q, kv_cache=kv, workspace_buffer=ws, qk_nope_head_dim=KVL, kv_lora_rank=KVL, qk_rope_head_dim=ROPE, block_tables=bt, seq_lens=sl, max_seq_len=TOPK, sparse_mla_top_k=TOPK, out=out, bmm1_scale=1.0, backend="trtllm-gen", ) torch.cuda.synchronize() print(f"B={B} out_untouched={(out == SENT).all().item()}") ``` | pseudo-batch `B` (= `gridDim.z`) | output written? | stderr `CUDA Error` lines | Python exception | |---|---|---|---| | 1024 / 32768 / 65534 | yes | 0 | none | | **65535** | **yes** | 0 | none | | **65536** | **NO — 100 % of `out` still holds the sentinel** | 1 | **none** | | 65537 / 98304 / 131072 | NO | 1 | none | The only symptom is one stderr line per failed launch: ``` CUDA Error: CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE .../flashinfer/data/include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaKernels.cuh 388 ``` ## End-to-end reproducer ```bash python -m sglang.bench_one_batch \ --model-path <DeepSeek-V3.2-style DSA checkpoint> \ --tp-size 2 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --disable-cuda-graph \ --batch-size 1 --input-len 32768 65535 65536 --output-len 8 ``` `bench_one_batch` drives the ModelRunner directly, so each `--input-len` is **one unchunked extend** and `dp_size == 1`. Result on a 47-layer `DeepseekV32ForCausalLM` fp8 checkpoint at TP2: | `--input-len` | prefill latency | prefill throughput | swallowed launch errors | |---|---|---|---| | 32768 | 0.710 s | 46 167 tok/s | 0 | | **65535** | **2.195 s** | 29 853 tok/s | **0** | | **65536** | **1.222 s** | **53 614 tok/s** | **94 = 47 layers x 2 ranks** | One extra token makes the prefill **1.80x faster** (2.195 s -> 1.222 s), because 44 % of the work (all of attention) silently disappears. The error count is exactly `num_layers x tp_size`: one failed launch per layer per rank, and precisely zero below the threshold. **On this model the run did not crash at all** — it completed all 8 decode steps and printed benchmark numbers. On the 78-layer TP8 model the same condition instead ended in `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` at `model_runner.synchronize()`. So the observable outcome ranges from "wrong answers, no diagnostics" to "delayed IMA", depending on the model. Through the HTTP server the same thing happens with `--chunked-prefill-size -1` (documented at `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py:7225` as "keeps a request in a single forward") or any `--chunked-prefill-size > 65535`, plus a request longer than 65535 tokens. Auto-selected chunk sizes (2048-16384 by GPU class) keep default servers below the threshold. ## Observed vs expected torch-profiler GPU trace, rank 0, 78-layer model, single extend: | run | attention kernels | attention time | total kernel time | |---|---|---|---| | direct runner, extend 32768 | **78** `fmhaSm100fKernel_QkvE4m3O...TokenSparse...` (= `num_layers`) | 425.58 ms | 1192.20 ms | | direct runner, extend 131072 | **0** — the whole attention bucket is absent | 0 ms | 4079.30 ms | | HTTP server, 131072 chunked at 16384 | **624** (= 8 chunks x 78 layers) | 1755.94 ms | 5986.66 ms | Arithmetic check: the correct chunked run spends `5986.66 - 1755.94 = 4230.72 ms` outside attention; the broken unchunked run's **entire** runtime is 4079.30 ms — 3.6 % apart, leaving no room for any attention work. So `bench_one_batch` above 64K does not merely crash later, it reports a prefill that is ~30 % too fast. Everything *around* attention still runs at 131072 — the sparse indexer (`deep_gemm::sm100_mqa_logits`), top-k selection (`topk_transform_prefill_kernel`) and the KV write (`set_mla_kv_buffer_kernel`, 78 launches) are all present. Only the attention kernel is missing, so nothing upstream signals a problem. **Expected**: either `num_layers` attention kernels, or a loud failure. Never a normal return with an unwritten output tensor. ## Root cause Prefill reuses the *decode* kernel by turning every query token into its own batch entry. `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa_backend.py` @ `18107e38`: * `:1905` — extend with `dsa_impl == "trtllm" and not self.use_mha` -> `_forward_trtllm(..., is_prefill=True)` * `:3201` — `transform_index_page_table_prefill(..., output_num_tokens=q.shape[0])` -> one row **per query token** * `:3230` — `batch_size = page_table_1.shape[0]` -> number of extend tokens * `:3242` — `q = q_all.view(batch_size, 1, num_heads, head_dim)` * `:3256` — `flashinfer.decode.trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla(..., backend="trtllm-gen")` flashinfer 0.6.17, `include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaKernels.cuh`: * `:516` — `int numCtasZ = params.mBatchSize;` * `:640` — `ctaLaunchParams.mNumCtasZ = numCtasZ;` * `:413` — `launch_config.gridDimZ = ctaLaunchParams.mNumCtasZ;` * `:388` — `cuErrCheck(cuLaunchKernelEx(&launch_config, func, kernelParamsList, nullptr));` CUDA's maximum `gridDim.z` is 65535, so `batch_size >= 65536` makes `cuLaunchKernelEx` return `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE`. That return value is then discarded — `include/flashinfer/trtllm/common.h`: ```cpp :44 inline void cuErrCheck_(CUresult stat, char const* file, int line) { :45 if (stat != CUDA_SUCCESS) { :46 char const* msg = nullptr; :47 cuGetErrorName(stat, &msg); :48 fprintf(stderr, "CUDA Error: %s %s %d\n", msg, file, line); // prints, then returns :49 } :50 } ``` A launch-configuration error is also **not** a sticky context error, so nothing downstream notices either — until corrupted values eventually produce an out-of-range index and the IMA. ## Suggested fixes 1. **sglang, smallest useful change**: in `_forward_trtllm`'s `is_prefill` branch, split the call into `ceil(batch_size / 65535)` launches, or at minimum `raise` when `batch_size > 65535` so the failure is loud. This is the only fix that also protects `bench_one_batch` / `dp_size=1`. 2. **sglang, structural**: adopt `cum_seq_lens_q` (flashinfer#3238, merged) so prefill stops flattening tokens into the batch dimension. 3. **FlashInfer**: implement what was agreed in #3125 — `FLASHINFER_CHECK(numCtasZ <= 65535, ...)`, and make `cuErrCheck` raise rather than `fprintf`, so no trtllm-gen launch failure can ever be silent again. Happy to send the sglang-side PR (1) and a companion FlashInfer PR (3) if maintainers agree on the preferred shape. ## Note on the test environment The FlashInfer install carries one local, build-only deviation from the 0.6.17 release: in `fmhaKernels.cuh`, three `#if CUDA_VERSION >= 13030` guards (lines 134/150/167) were extended with `&& defined(FLASHINFER_ENABLE_RUBIN_OVERSIZED_SMEM)` so the file compiles against a CUDA header set lacking `CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_SHARED_MEMORY_MODE`. Those blocks only handle SM107 (Rubin) oversized shared memory and are dead code on SM100; they cannot affect grid configuration.

signals.title: --profile-by-stage with speculative decoding: profiler never stops on decode batches (TARGET_VERIFY counted as prefill); deferred stop + synchronous trace export freeze the server for ~25 s inside later unrelated requests
signals.text: **Environment** - sglang @ 18107e38 (main, 2026-08-14), TP8 on 8x B200, torch 2.13.0 - a DeepSeek-V3.2-style DSA model (MLA, fp8 KV cache; auto-selected DSA backends prefill=trtllm/decode=trtllm) + EAGLE/MTP draft (`--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`) **What happened** Benchmarking with `sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server --profile --profile-by-stage --profile-steps 50` on a bs=1 shape, then immediately running a *clean* (unprofiled) bs=32/32K measurement, the clean run's TTFT inflated from ~39.7 s to 65.4 s (+65%). Server log shows a 25 s gap mid-prefill bracketed by `Stop profiling-EXTEND...` → `Profiling done. Traces are saved to ...`; the 16384-token prefill batch spanning the gap reports ~623 tok/s (26 s). py-spy during the gap shows the TP0 scheduler MainThread in `run_batch -> _profile_batch_predicate -> _stop_profile -> torch.profiler.export_chrome_trace -> gzip write` with GPUs idle. The exported trace is 242 MB (8 ranks). **Root cause** 1. `ForwardMode.is_prefill()`/`is_extend()` include `TARGET_VERIFY` while `is_decode()` matches only `DECODE` (python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py). Under speculative decoding every decode-step batch is TARGET_VERIFY, so `_profile_batch_predicate` (python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/profiler_manager.py) counts verify batches on the *prefill* counter and the DECODE stage can never stop on decode batches. The armed session survives the profiling client and stops ~`num_steps` batches later — inside whichever request happens to be running (in our case, the next benchmark's prefill). 2. `_stop_profile` calls `torch_profiler.export_chrome_trace()` synchronously inside `run_batch` on the scheduler main thread, freezing all serving for the export duration (25 s here). 3. `sglang/profiler.py` documents that the `/start_profile` reply comes "when all steps are processed and files are generated", which is not true with `profile_by_stage` (arming only), so `one_batch_server` proceeds while tracing is still live. **Expected** (a) by-stage counters treat TARGET_VERIFY as decode (e.g. `is_decode() or is_target_verify()`), so stages terminate within the profiled request; (b) trace export moved off the scheduler event loop (or at least a warning that `/stop_profile` stalls serving for the export duration); (c) fix the profiler.py doc claim / actually await flush. **Repro** (deterministic, ~30 min): launch TP8 spec-decode server; run `one_batch_server --batch-size 1 --input-len 32768 --output-len 64 --skip-warmup --profile --profile-activities GPU --profile-steps 50 --profile-by-stage`; immediately run `one_batch_server --batch-size 32 --input-len 32768 --output-len 64` (clean). Clean run TTFT ~65 s vs ~40 s without the preceding profiled run. The stall lands at the same batch position every time (token usage 0.69, 22 running reqs in our shape).
signals.author: zkyue

signals.title: [Bug] Stopping the by-stage profiler under speculative decoding freezes the scheduler for ~25 s (synchronous trace export on the scheduler thread), and the stop condition leaks into later requests
signals.text: ## Summary Two coupled defects in `scheduler_components/profiler_manager.py` turn a routine `--profile-by-stage` run into a ~25 s full serving freeze that lands on *later, unrelated* requests when speculative decoding is enabled: 1. **Stage predicate misclassifies verify batches.** Under EAGLE/MTP, decode-step batches carry `forward_mode=TARGET_VERIFY`, which `ForwardMode.is_prefill()` accepts and `is_decode()` rejects. `_profile_batch_predicate` therefore counts verify batches as *prefill*, so a DECODE-stage window can only terminate on prefill batches of **later requests** — in our runs the stop fired 44 prefill chunks into the next (unprofiled) benchmark run. 2. **Trace export blocks the scheduler event loop.** When the stop finally fires, `_stop_profile()` executes `torch.profiler` stop + `export_chrome_trace()` (gzip) **synchronously on the TP0 scheduler main thread inside `run_batch`** (`profiler_manager.py:321/341/404` → `scheduler.py:3639` at 18107e38). Writing a 242 MB 8-rank gzip trace took 25.0 s while GPUs sat idle and all serving froze mid-prefill. ## Impact measured (B200 ×8, TP8, GLM-5.2 fp8, main @ 18107e38, MTP steps=3/topk=1/draft=4) Caliber: clean `bench_one_batch_server` wall clock, batch=32, ISL=32768, chunked prefill 16384. | run | sequence position | last TTFT | |---|---|---| | spec-on, clean | fresh server | 39.68 s | | spec-on, `--profile --profile-by-stage` bs=1 run | (profiled) | — | | spec-on, clean B32 **immediately after** | same server | **65.43 s (+65%)** | The +25.7 s is fully accounted for by the deferred trace export: server log brackets `Stop profiling-EXTEND... → Profiling done` span 25 s; the 16384-token chunk overlapping the stall reports 623 tok/s (≈26 s); py-spy over the stalled scheduler shows `run_batch → _profile_batch_predicate → _stop_profile → export_chrome_trace → gzip write`. The stall reproduces at the identical batch position across sessions (deterministic, not load noise). Steady-state spec-on prefill is unaffected (39.68 s vs spec-off 39.36 s). ## Repro 1. Launch with EAGLE/MTP enabled (any DSA model; observed on GLM-5.2 TP8). 2. Run a small profiled benchmark: `... bench_one_batch_server --profile --profile-by-stage --profile-steps 50` with a request whose prefill has <50 chunks. 3. Immediately run a clean larger benchmark against the same server: its TTFT absorbs the deferred export stall. ## Suggested fixes - Count `TARGET_VERIFY` (and draft modes) as decode in the by-stage predicate, or terminate stage windows on request completion rather than batch counts. - Move `export_chrome_trace` off the scheduler thread (background thread/process), or at minimum log a prominent warning that serving is paused for export. Happy to send a PR for either piece if maintainers agree on the direction.
signals.author: zkyue

signals.title: [Bug] DSA sparse-MLA prefill silently computes no attention at all for a single extend > 65535 tokens (trtllm-gen `gridDim.z` limit is still unguarded on the non-DP path)
signals.text: ## TL;DR `gridDim.z` overflow in trtllm-gen sparse MLA (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3125) is still reachable from sglang, and still silent. On SM100, any **single unchunked extend of more than 65535 tokens** on the DSA `prefill=trtllm` path launches **zero** attention kernels, leaves the attention output tensor **uninitialized**, raises **no** Python exception, and returns garbage. `bench_one_batch` hits this by construction for `--input-len > 65535`. The onset is exact: **65535 tokens works, 65536 does not.** ### Relation to existing reports (please read before closing as duplicate) | prior art | state | why this report is not covered by it | |---|---|---| | flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3125 — "trtllm-gen attention error on large batch size" | closed 2026-04-21, **no fix commit** | Correctly diagnosed the root cause. Maintainer proposed "just raise an error"; that was never implemented. `fmhaKernels.cuh` still has a bare `int numCtasZ = params.mBatchSize;` and `cuErrCheck` still only `fprintf`s. | | sgl-project/sglang#29453 — GLM-5.2 NVFP4 DP4 long-context crash | closed 2026-06-27, **no code fix** | Same root cause, but reported via a *downstream* symptom (invalid sampling probabilities) under **DP attention**, and closed after the reporter worked around it with `--chunked-prefill-size`. No guard landed. | | sgl-project/sglang#29522 — "Guard Blackwell TRT-LLM prefill chunk size" | **closed, not merged** | The only guard attempt. It capped `chunked_prefill_size` / `get_max_chunk_capacity()` in `server_args.py` + `forward_batch_deepseek_mha_mixin.py` — i.e. **server config only**, gated on `enable_dp_attention`. It would not have covered the direct-ModelRunner path (`bench_one_batch`, `dp_size=1`) at all, and it never landed anyway. | | flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3238 — `cum_seq_lens_q` for trtllm-gen MLA | merged 2026-06-24 | This is the structural cure (stop flattening tokens into the batch dim), but sglang has **not adopted it**: `dsa_backend.py:3242` still does `q_all.view(batch_size, 1, num_heads, head_dim)`. | **New in this report:** (a) the fault is reachable with `dp_size=1` on the plain ModelRunner path, which no proposed guard covered; (b) an exact one-token onset bisection (65535 vs 65536); (c) direct proof of *silent corruption* — a sentinel-filled `out` tensor comes back untouched — rather than an inferred downstream symptom; (d) profiler proof that `0` of `num_layers` attention kernels run, so `bench_one_batch` silently reports **falsely fast** long-context prefill numbers. Also worth noting: sglang already guards this exact hardware limit elsewhere — `python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:298` gates a fused kernel on `query.shape[0] < 65535`, and `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/mamba_slot_fused.py:133` comments "gridDim.y/z cap at 65535". The DSA attention path has no such check. ## Environment | | | |---|---| | GPU | NVIDIA B200 (SM100), driver 590.48.01 | | sglang | `18107e38d266a98f59a8e3c766f8ddaf9b723ded` (main, 2026-08-14) | | flashinfer-python | 0.6.17 | | sglang-kernel | 0.4.6.post1 | | torch | 2.13.0 / Python 3.12.3 | | resolved backends | `Set DSA backends for fp8_e4m3 KV Cache: prefill=trtllm, decode=trtllm.` | `prefill=trtllm` here is the **auto-selected default** for fp8 KV on SM100 — no `--dsa-prefill-backend` flag was passed. (`enable_auto_select_prefill_impl` at `dsa_backend.py:350` is only true when the resolved impl is literally `flashmla_auto`, so the `flashmla_sparse`/`flashmla_kv` rewrite in `set_dsa_prefill_impl` does not apply here.) Reproduced on two models and two TP degrees: a 78-layer DSA MLA model at TP8, and a 47-layer `DeepseekV32ForCausalLM` fp8 checkpoint (`index_topk=2048`) at TP2. TP degree is irrelevant — the overflowing dimension is the token/pseudo-batch dimension, which TP does not shard. Note `SGLANG_DSA_PREFILL_DENSE_ATTN_KV_LEN_THRESHOLD` defaults to **2048** (`python/sglang/srt/environ.py:1375`), so both 32768 and 131072 take the same MLA path — the difference in behaviour is purely the 65535 overflow, not an MHA/MLA path switch. ## Minimal reproducer (no model, no sglang, ~30 s) Same FlashInfer entry point sglang calls, with a sentinel-filled `out` so "did the kernel run?" is directly observable: ```python import sys, torch, flashinfer B = int(sys.argv[1]) # pseudo-batch == number of query tokens NH, TOPK, KVL, ROPE, HD = 16, 2048, 512, 64, 576 PAGE, PAGES, SENT = 64, 8192, -31337.0 kv = torch.zeros(PAGES, 1, PAGE, HD, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device="cuda") ws = torch.empty(256 << 20, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda") q = torch.zeros(B, 1, NH, HD, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device="cuda") bt = torch.zeros(B, 1, TOPK, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") sl = torch.full((B,), TOPK, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") out = torch.full((B, 1, NH, KVL), SENT, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") flashinfer.decode.trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla( query=q, kv_cache=kv, workspace_buffer=ws, qk_nope_head_dim=KVL, kv_lora_rank=KVL, qk_rope_head_dim=ROPE, block_tables=bt, seq_lens=sl, max_seq_len=TOPK, sparse_mla_top_k=TOPK, out=out, bmm1_scale=1.0, backend="trtllm-gen", ) torch.cuda.synchronize() print(f"B={B} out_untouched={(out == SENT).all().item()}") ``` | pseudo-batch `B` (= `gridDim.z`) | output written? | stderr `CUDA Error` lines | Python exception | |---|---|---|---| | 1024 / 32768 / 65534 | yes | 0 | none | | **65535** | **yes** | 0 | none | | **65536** | **NO — 100 % of `out` still holds the sentinel** | 1 | **none** | | 65537 / 98304 / 131072 | NO | 1 | none | The only symptom is one stderr line per failed launch: ``` CUDA Error: CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE .../flashinfer/data/include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaKernels.cuh 388 ``` ## End-to-end reproducer ```bash python -m sglang.bench_one_batch \ --model-path <DeepSeek-V3.2-style DSA checkpoint> \ --tp-size 2 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --disable-cuda-graph \ --batch-size 1 --input-len 32768 65535 65536 --output-len 8 ``` `bench_one_batch` drives the ModelRunner directly, so each `--input-len` is **one unchunked extend** and `dp_size == 1`. Result on a 47-layer `DeepseekV32ForCausalLM` fp8 checkpoint at TP2: | `--input-len` | prefill latency | prefill throughput | swallowed launch errors | |---|---|---|---| | 32768 | 0.710 s | 46 167 tok/s | 0 | | **65535** | **2.195 s** | 29 853 tok/s | **0** | | **65536** | **1.222 s** | **53 614 tok/s** | **47 layers x 2 ranks (87 intact stderr lines + 7 mangled by concurrent rank writes)** | One extra token makes the prefill **1.80x faster** (2.195 s -> 1.222 s), because 44 % of the work (all of attention) silently disappears. The failure count matches one launch per layer per rank (concurrent rank writes interleave a few stderr lines), and is precisely zero below the threshold. **On this model the run did not crash at all** — it completed all 8 decode steps and printed benchmark numbers. On the 78-layer TP8 model the same condition instead ended in `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` at `model_runner.synchronize()`. So the observable outcome ranges from "wrong answers, no diagnostics" to "delayed IMA", depending on the model. Through the HTTP server the same thing happens with `--chunked-prefill-size -1` (documented at `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py:7225` as "keeps a request in a single forward") or any `--chunked-prefill-size > 65535`, plus a request longer than 65535 tokens. Auto-selected chunk sizes (2048-16384 by GPU class) keep default servers below the threshold. ## Observed vs expected torch-profiler GPU trace, rank 0, 78-layer model, single extend: | run | attention kernels | attention time | total kernel time | |---|---|---|---| | direct runner, extend 32768 | **78** `fmhaSm100fKernel_QkvE4m3O...TokenSparse...` (= `num_layers`) | 425.58 ms | 1192.20 ms | | direct runner, extend 131072 | **0** — the whole attention bucket is absent | 0 ms | 4079.30 ms | | HTTP server, 131072 chunked at 16384 | **624** (= 8 chunks x 78 layers) | 1755.94 ms | 5986.66 ms | Arithmetic check: the correct chunked run spends `5986.66 - 1755.94 = 4230.72 ms` outside attention; the broken unchunked run's **entire** runtime is 4079.30 ms — 3.6 % apart, leaving no room for any attention work. So `bench_one_batch` above 64K does not merely crash later, it reports a prefill that is ~30 % too fast. Everything *around* attention still runs at 131072 — the sparse indexer (`deep_gemm::sm100_mqa_logits`), top-k selection (`topk_transform_prefill_kernel`) and the KV write (`set_mla_kv_buffer_kernel`, 78 launches) are all present. Only the attention kernel is missing, so nothing upstream signals a problem. **Expected**: either `num_layers` attention kernels, or a loud failure. Never a normal return with an unwritten output tensor. ## Root cause Prefill reuses the *decode* kernel by turning every query token into its own batch entry. `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa_backend.py` @ `18107e38`: * `:1905` — extend with `dsa_impl == "trtllm" and not self.use_mha` -> `_forward_trtllm(..., is_prefill=True)` * `:3201` — `transform_index_page_table_prefill(..., output_num_tokens=q.shape[0])` -> one row **per query token** * `:3230` — `batch_size = page_table_1.shape[0]` -> number of extend tokens * `:3242` — `q = q_all.view(batch_size, 1, num_heads, head_dim)` * `:3256` — `flashinfer.decode.trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla(..., backend="trtllm-gen")` flashinfer 0.6.17, `include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaKernels.cuh`: * `:516` — `int numCtasZ = params.mBatchSize;` * `:640` — `ctaLaunchParams.mNumCtasZ = numCtasZ;` * `:413` — `launch_config.gridDimZ = ctaLaunchParams.mNumCtasZ;` * `:388` — `cuErrCheck(cuLaunchKernelEx(&launch_config, func, kernelParamsList, nullptr));` CUDA's maximum `gridDim.z` is 65535, so `batch_size >= 65536` makes `cuLaunchKernelEx` return `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE`. That return value is then discarded — `include/flashinfer/trtllm/common.h`: ```cpp :44 inline void cuErrCheck_(CUresult stat, char const* file, int line) { :45 if (stat != CUDA_SUCCESS) { :46 char const* msg = nullptr; :47 cuGetErrorName(stat, &msg); :48 fprintf(stderr, "CUDA Error: %s %s %d\n", msg, file, line); // prints, then returns :49 } :50 } ``` A launch-configuration error is also **not** a sticky context error, so nothing downstream notices either — until corrupted values eventually produce an out-of-range index and the IMA. ## Suggested fixes 1. **sglang, smallest useful change**: in `_forward_trtllm`'s `is_prefill` branch, split the call into `ceil(batch_size / 65535)` launches, or at minimum `raise` when `batch_size > 65535` so the failure is loud. This is the only fix that also protects `bench_one_batch` / `dp_size=1`. 2. **sglang, structural**: adopt `cum_seq_lens_q` (flashinfer#3238, merged) so prefill stops flattening tokens into the batch dimension. 3. **FlashInfer**: implement what was agreed in #3125 — `FLASHINFER_CHECK(numCtasZ <= 65535, ...)`, and make `cuErrCheck` raise rather than `fprintf`, so no trtllm-gen launch failure can ever be silent again. Two minimal fail-loud PRs accompany this issue: an sglang-side guard implementing the `raise` from (1), and a FlashInfer-side pre-launch check implementing (3)'s `FLASHINFER_CHECK` (links in the first comment below). The chunk-split from (1) and the `cum_seq_lens_q` adoption (2) remain open as the actual capability fix. ## Note on the test environment The FlashInfer install carries one local, build-only deviation from the 0.6.17 release: in `fmhaKernels.cuh`, three `#if CUDA_VERSION >= 13030` guards (lines 134/150/167) were extended with `&& defined(FLASHINFER_ENABLE_RUBIN_OVERSIZED_SMEM)` so the file compiles against a CUDA header set lacking `CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_SHARED_MEMORY_MODE`. Those blocks only handle SM107 (Rubin) oversized shared memory and are dead code on SM100; they cannot affect grid configuration.
signals.author: zkyue

signals.title: [diffusion] MiniMax-H3 quality="high" runs on Turbo-LoRA-merged weights — the audit gate has no adapter field
signals.text: The LoRA recipes section of the MiniMax-H3 cookbook says not to stack a distilled adapter with `quality: "high"`: "both alter denoising, and that combination has not been quality-validated". Nothing enforces that. A server launched with the cookbook's own recommended Turbo-LoRA recipe, on the exact audited 4×H200 deployment, accepts and completes `quality: "high"` requests. Measured on `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260814-c4271c3f`, 4×H200, with `larryvrh/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora` (`minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600_ema.safetensors`, scale 1.0, `--lora-merge-mode auto`): | request | result | |---|---| | `quality: "high"`, 50 steps, 124 frames (the audited shape) | completed, `inference_time_s` 42.98 s | | `quality: "high"`, 9 steps (the adapter's documented schedule) | task failed after ~3 s: request signature wants `num_inference_steps: 50` | | `quality: "lossless"`, 9 steps | completed, 13.46 s | The second row shows the gate firing on this very server; the first row is the combination it cannot see. And it is genuinely the accelerated path, not a silent fallback: lossless at this shape measures 75.93 s, while 42.98 s with the adapter merged matches the 43.28 s the tier does without it (merge mode adds no per-step cost, so timing offers no hint that anything is different). `validate_quality_deployment` (`configs/pipeline_configs/minimax_h3.py`) fails closed on sixteen server-arg fields plus the device, and the request gate pins the exact workload, but none of it covers adapter state. So the response still carries `quality: "high"`, whose documentation promises "Quality is guaranteed (the audited Cache-DiT configuration measures SSIM 0.931 / PSNR 28.16 dB against lossless)" — a guarantee measured on base weights. I didn't measure whether the merged output is actually degraded; per the docs nobody has, which is what a fail-closed gate is for. Repro: ```bash sglang serve --model-path /path/to/MiniMax-H3 --model-type diffusion \ --model-variant fl2va --num-gpus 4 --tp-size 1 --ulysses-degree 4 \ --performance-mode speed \ --lora-path larryvrh/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora \ --lora-weight-name minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600_ema.safetensors \ --lora-scale 1.0 --lora-merge-mode auto --port 30010 ``` ```bash curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30010/v1/videos -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "task": "t2va", "prompt": "<any>", "quality": "high", "seed": 0, "num_inference_steps": 50, "target": {"short_edge": 768, "aspect_ratio": "16:9", "duration_seconds": 5.1667}}' ``` Suggested fix: include adapter state in the expected signature — `server_args` already carries `lora_path` / `lora_weight_name` / `lora_merge_mode`, so a `"lora_path": None` entry matches the existing one-line-per-field shape. Happy to send a PR. If the combination is instead meant to be allowed, the LoRA-recipes warning and the quality guarantee need reconciling. Related: #33720 (same validator, topology axis), and #34841, which widens the same expected dict to B300 and also carries no adapter field — the gap carries over as the gate grows.
signals.author: Raymondlol

signals.title: [Bug] DSPARK silently corrupts identifiers on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, making speculative decoding unsafe
signals.text:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug

Summary

On DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, SGLang’s DSPARK speculative decoding silently introduces single-character corruptions into identifiers supplied verbatim in the prompt:

kimi-k3 → kimi-kw nova-x7 → nova-7 apollo-n9 → apollo-n11

The same server, weights, prompts, and launch configuration—with only speculative decoding disabled—produces zero such corruptions across thousands of grounded identifier tokens.

The corruption rate increases with the DSPARK verify-window width:

--speculative-dspark-block-size | speculative_num_draft_tokens | Temp 0 | Temp 1 -- | -- | -- | -- 6 | 7 | 1.03% | 0.82% 5 | 6 | 0.32% | 0.77% 1 | 2 | 0.00% | 0.00% Speculation disabled | — | 0.00% | 0.00%

Aggregated across both block_size=1 runs:

  • Temperature 0: 0 / 4561
  • Temperature 1: 0 / 3701

Using the rule of three, the corresponding approximate 95% upper bounds are:

  • Temperature 0: <0.066%
  • Temperature 1: <0.081%

This contrasts with the 1.03% observed rate at block_size=6, temperature 0.

Examples of corrupted identifiers

Malformed forms observed at block_size=6, temperature 0:

kimi-kw -> kimi-k3 (x5) kimi-k2 -> kimi-k3 (x3) kimi-k7 -> kimi-k3 (x2) apollo-n11 -> apollo-n9 (x2) nova-12 -> nova-x7 (x2) wq-7f2e -> wq-7f2b (x2) kimi-kw2 -> kimi-k3 kimi-v2 -> kimi-k3 kimi-k11 -> kimi-k3 apollo-n12 -> apollo-n9 nova-7 -> nova-x7 nova-v7 -> nova-x7 wq-7f2e2 -> wq-7f2b

These are not malformed responses or obvious decoding failures. They are plausible-looking, single-character-wrong identifiers embedded in otherwise normal output.

Expected behavior

At temperature 0, DSPARK should emit the same greedy token sequence as the target model without speculative decoding.

A draft token should only be committed if it matches the corresponding target prediction. On mismatch, DSPARK should emit the target prediction instead.

Therefore, enabling DSPARK should not change grounded identifiers from:

kimi-k3

to:

kimi-kw

when the non-speculative target forward selects the correct token.

Actual behavior

With multi-position DSPARK verification enabled:

  • Grounded identifiers are silently corrupted.
  • The issue reproduces at temperature 0.
  • The issue requires or is strongly amplified by heterogeneous concurrent batching.
  • The rate increases with verify-window width.
  • No request error or warning is produced.
  • The finish reason remains normal.
  • Disabling speculation eliminates the corruption.
  • Reducing DSPARK to block_size=1 eliminates the corruption.

Hypotheses investigated and ruled out

1. Lossy accept/verify rule

This does not appear to be the cause.

Both accept_greedy and accept_greedy_triton in:

sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/dspark/dspark_accept.py

delegate to compute_dflash_correct_drafts_and_bonus in:

sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py

The relevant logic is:

matches = candidates[:, 1:] == target_predict[:, :-1] correct_len = matches.to(torch.int32).cumprod(dim=1).sum(dim=1) bonus = target_predict[torch.arange(bs, ...), correct_len]

Every committed token should therefore be either:

  1. An accepted draft token that compared equal to target_predict; or
  2. The bonus token, which is taken directly from target_predict.

A mismatching draft token should not be able to leak into the output.

This implies that the corrupted emitted tokens are likely themselves present in target_predict. In other words, the target verify forward appears to be producing incorrect logits or incorrect token alignment.

2. Ragged verify-window misalignment

accept_greedy performs:

torch.argmax(target_logits, dim=-1).view( bs, verify_num_draft_tokens )

A dense reshape could misalign tokens if requests had different verify lengths.

However, SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE defaults to static. In static mode, resolve_ragged_verify_layout returns None, and verify lengths are uniform.

Therefore, the rectangular reshape is expected to be valid for this reproduction.

3. Numerical noise or batch-shape-dependent reductions

We tested three separate interventions. Each was verified to engage, and none removed the corruption.

FP32 LM head

Enabled:

--enable-fp32-lm-head

Engagement was confirmed empirically:

  • Before the change, 65.5% of recorded margins fell on the 0.25 BF16 grid.
  • After the change, 0% did.
  • There were zero exact ties across 34,420 records.

The typo rate did not improve.

Deterministic FP32 MoE reduction

We forced:

use_atomic_add = False

so the already-passed:

use_fp32_reduce = True

would engage.

In:

sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_wna16_marlin.py

the FP32 temporary buffer is allocated only under:

if use_fp32_reduce and not use_atomic_add:

This provides a structural confirmation that the path was active.

The observed rates remained approximately:

  • Temperature 0: 1.03%
  • Temperature 1: 0.82%

Tie epsilon on sampled accept path

Adding a tie epsilon to the sampled acceptance path had no effect.

More generally, an identifier repeated verbatim several times in the prompt should usually be a high-margin prediction. Low-order numerical noise would not be expected to repeatedly transform such identifiers into plausible alternatives.

The non-speculative control also varies in free-form prose between temperature-0 runs—likely due to prefix-cache or chunked-prefill effects—but it never corrupts a grounded identifier.

4. Draft/target gamma mismatch

The CLI can override the draft checkpoint’s declared gamma with only a warning:

DSpark gamma mismatch: using gamma=6 (from speculative_num_draft_tokens=7) but draft config block_size=5.

This occurs in:

sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_config.py

The draft module itself obtains gamma from the checkpoint:

self.gamma = int(dspark_config.resolve_gamma(...))

in:

sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_dspark.py

This means the draft module and worker may disagree about the verify-window width.

However, running with block_size=5:

  • Makes the configured values agree
  • Removes the warning
  • Still reproduces the bug

Observed rates at block_size=5 were:

  • Temperature 0: 0.32%
  • Temperature 1: 0.77%

Therefore, the gamma mismatch is not the root cause of this corruption, although the silent override may be worth hardening as a separate issue.

5. Draft-side kernels

SGLANG_DSPARK_FAST_KERNEL only gates the draft forward.

Under a correct speculative verification rule, draft quality may affect acceptance and performance, but it should not affect temperature-0 correctness. Incorrect draft tokens should be rejected in favor of the target prediction.

Therefore, a draft-only kernel failure does not explain committed token corruption unless there is also a target-verification or alignment bug.

Suspected fault area

The following is a hypothesis, not yet a verified root cause.

Given that:

  1. The accept rule appears to emit only target_predict;
  2. The corruption reproduces at temperature 0;
  3. The corruption disappears at a two-position verify window;
  4. The rate generally increases with verify-window width;
  5. Multiple numerical-determinism interventions had no effect; and
  6. The issue depends on concurrent heterogeneous batching,

the likely fault is in the target verify forward for multi-position DSPARK verification, especially for in-block positions t >= 1.

Potential areas include:

  • Intra-block causal masking
  • Position-ID construction or indexing
  • KV-cache placement for draft positions
  • Request-to-token mapping under heterogeneous batching
  • CUDA graph replay metadata for TARGET_VERIFY
  • Batch-slot reuse or stale per-request metadata
  • dsv4 attention behavior during multi-token verification

The current evidence suggests the target verification pass is computing incorrect logits or associating correct logits with the wrong request/position.

We have not yet isolated the specific kernel or metadata transition.

Suggested next diagnostics

A useful first datapoint would be:

--speculative-dspark-block-size 2

This would help distinguish between:

  • Failure beginning at the first genuinely multi-position verify step; and
  • Error probability accumulating with larger verify windows.

Other useful comparisons may include:

  1. DSPARK with CUDA graphs disabled.
  2. DSPARK with the hierarchical cache disabled.
  3. DSPARK with radix cache and chunked prefill disabled.
  4. An alternate attention backend, if DeepSeek-V4-Flash supports one.
  5. Capturing target_predict before acceptance and comparing it against independent one-token target forwards.
  6. Logging request IDs, verify positions, position IDs, and KV locations for the first divergent token.

Workaround

Both of the following avoid the observed corruption:

Option 1: Disable speculative decoding

This is the safest workaround.

Option 2: Use block_size=1

--speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 1

This produced zero true typos across:

  • 4,561 grounded identifiers at temperature 0
  • 3,701 grounded identifiers at temperature 1

However, this sacrifices most of the speculative speedup, so it is a mitigation rather than a practical fix.

Until the multi-position verification issue is resolved, DSPARK should not be used with DeepSeek-V4-Flash for workloads where exact token reproduction matters.

Reproduction notes

DeepGEMM JIT warmup

Changing:

--speculative-dspark-block-size

changes num_tokens_per_req and invalidates the DeepGEMM JIT shape cache.

The first launch after changing this value may compile approximately 16,000 shapes and exceed a 3,600-second readiness budget. If the process is killed during warmup, it may look like an unrelated startup failure.

Please allow additional warmup time when changing the block size.

Log probabilities unavailable

DSPARK currently rejects:

"return_logprob": true

with:

DFLASH speculative decoding does not support return_logprob yet

Therefore, per-token target margins cannot currently be collected over HTTP on the affected speculative arm.

Severity

This is a silent data-corruption issue, not only a quality or performance regression.

The generated response is well-formed, and the corrupted identifier often looks plausible. Downstream systems therefore have no reliable way to distinguish the incorrect value from an intended value.

For DeepSeek-V4-Flash, this makes multi-position DSPARK speculative decoding unsafe for exact-identifier and tool-use workloads.

### Reproduction

Reproduction

The corruption usually requires concurrent, heterogeneous batching. A single request in isolation may not reproduce it. The script below sends four byte-identical target requests and four variable-length distractor requests per round.

1. Launch the affected DSPARK configuration

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <deepseek-v4-flash-0731> \ --tp 4 \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 6 \ --max-running-requests 16 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16

2. Save the reproduction script

Save the following code as dspark_typo_repro.py:

#!/usr/bin/env python3 """Concurrency typo probe for one model and temperature.""" import collections import concurrent.futures import json import os import re import time import urllib.error import urllib.request MODEL = os.environ["TEST_MODEL"] TEMP = float(os.environ.get("TEST_TEMP", "0")) ROUNDS = int(os.environ.get("TEST_ROUNDS", "30")) BASE = os.environ.get("TEST_BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:30000") URL = f"{BASE}/v1/chat/completions" IDS = [ "kimi-k3", "nova-x7", "atlas-j9", "wq-7f2b", "zeta-r1", "apollo-n9", ] CTX = " ".join( f"event{i}=ok latency={i % 37}ms owner=team{i % 9}" for i in range(350) ) PROMPT = ( f"Analyze this deployment history and write a 6-section operational report. " f"{CTX}\n" f"Canonical identifiers: {', '.join(IDS)}. " "Include a table and prose recap. " "Use every identifier at least four times, always verbatim; " "do not invent or normalize identifiers." ) RX = re.compile(r"[a-z][a-z0-9]*-[a-z0-9]+", re.I) def lev(a, b): prev = list(range(len(b) + 1)) for i, x in enumerate(a, 1): cur = [i] for j, y in enumerate(b, 1): cur.append( min( cur[-1] + 1, prev[j] + 1, prev[j - 1] + (x != y), ) ) prev = cur return prev[-1] def ask(prompt=PROMPT, max_tokens=700, retries=5): body = json.dumps( { "model": MODEL, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], "max_tokens": max_tokens, "temperature": TEMP, "top_p": 1.0, } ).encode() for n in range(retries): request = urllib.request.Request( URL, data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, ) try: with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=300) as response: result = json.load(response) return result["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] or "" except urllib.error.HTTPError as error: if error.code not in (429, 503) or n + 1 == retries: raise time.sleep(0.3 * (n + 1)) raise RuntimeError("retries exhausted") wrong = collections.Counter() truncations = collections.Counter() error_types = collections.Counter() exact = 0 grounded = 0 responses = 0 errors = 0 typo_responses = 0 started = time.time() with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool: for rnd in range(ROUNDS): futures = [pool.submit(ask) for _ in range(4)] # Variable-length distractors perturb server-side batch composition. for j in range(4): length = 50 + ((rnd * 67 + j * 97) % 500) distractor = "Summarize: " + " ".join( f"word{k}" for k in range(length) ) futures.append(pool.submit(ask, distractor, 128)) for future in futures[:4]: try: text = future.result() responses += 1 except Exception as error: errors += 1 error_types[type(error).__name__] += 1 continue response_has_typo = False for token in ( match.lower().rstrip(".,;:") for match in RX.findall(text) ): if token in IDS: exact += 1 grounded += 1 continue distance, target = min( (lev(token, identifier), identifier) for identifier in IDS ) if distance <= 2: grounded += 1 if any(identifier.startswith(token) for identifier in IDS): # Prefixes are output-limit truncations, not typos. truncations[(token, target, distance)] += 1 else: wrong[(token, target, distance)] += 1 response_has_typo = True typo_responses += response_has_typo for future in futures[4:]: try: future.result() except Exception: pass print( f"MODEL={MODEL} TEMP={TEMP} rounds={ROUNDS} " f"responses={responses} errors={errors} " f"errtypes={dict(error_types)} " f"elapsed={time.time() - started:.1f}s" ) print( f"grounded_ids={grounded} exact={exact} " f"true_typos={sum(wrong.values())} " f"typo_responses={typo_responses} " f"rate={(sum(wrong.values()) / grounded if grounded else 0):.4%} " f"truncations={sum(truncations.values())}" ) print("typo_forms:", dict(wrong.most_common(20)) or "NONE")

A true typo is a token with Levenshtein distance 1–2 from a canonical identifier that is not a prefix of one. Prefixes are counted separately as output-limit truncations.

3. Run the reproduction at temperature 0

TEST_MODEL=<served-model-name> \ TEST_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:30000 \ TEST_TEMP=0 \ TEST_ROUNDS=30 \ python3 -u dspark_typo_repro.py

4. Repeat at temperature 1

TEST_MODEL=<served-model-name> \ TEST_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:30000 \ TEST_TEMP=1 \ TEST_ROUNDS=30 \ python3 -u dspark_typo_repro.py

5. Run the non-speculative control

Relaunch the server with all --speculative-* flags removed while leaving every other launch argument unchanged. Repeat both commands above. This control produced zero true typos.

6. Test the block-size workaround

Relaunch DSPARK with a block size of 1: 

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <deepseek-v4-flash-0731> \ --tp 4 \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 1 \ --max-running-requests 16 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16

Repeat the temperature-0 and temperature-1 tests. This configuration also produced zero true typos.

Expected result

At temperature 0, DSPARK should produce the same greedy token sequence as non-speculative decoding. All identifiers supplied verbatim in the prompt should be emitted without modification.

Observed result

With --speculative-dspark-block-size 6, the output silently contains plausible single-character corruptions such as: 

kimi-k3 -> kimi-kw nova-x7 -> nova-7 apollo-n9 -> apollo-n11 wq-7f2b -> wq-7f2e

In one temperature-0 run, 23 of 2,224 grounded identifiers were corrupted (1.0342%), affecting 15 of 120 target responses. The same test produced zero corruptions with speculative decoding disabled and with DSPARK block size 1.

Reproduction note

Changing --speculative-dspark-block-size changes num_tokens_per_req and may invalidate the DeepGEMM JIT shape cache. The first launch after changing the block size can require a long recompilation warmup. Allow enough startup time to prevent the server from being killed before it becomes ready.

### Environment Run this **inside the same Python environment/container used to launch the affected SGLang server**: ```bash python3 -m sglang.check_env 2>&1 | tee sglang_check_env.txt ``` Then paste the **complete command output verbatim** into that field, preferably wrapped as: ```text ``` Do not substitute the manually listed environment details; the maintainers explicitly require the actual `check_env` output.

signals.title: [Bug] HF3FS HiCache hits ZeroDivisionError with DeepSeek-V4 logical KV anchor
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ### Symptom DeepSeek-V4 HiCache uses a LogicalHostPool as the primary KV anchor. This pool only manages logical token indices and does not contain physical KV data. When hf3fs is selected as the HiCache storage backend, the backend calculates bytes_per_page=0 from this logical pool and later divides by it during initialization. Therefore, DeepSeek-V4 cannot start with HF3FS L3 storage. Starting sglang with DSV4 and HF3FS will encounter: ``` File "/path/to/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/hf3fs/storage_hf3fs.py", line 220, in __init__ self.num_pages = self.file_size // self.bytes_per_page ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ZeroDivisionError: integer division or modulo by zero ``` The DeepSeek-V4 cookbook currently lists hf3fs as an available L3 backend, but I could not find a DSV4-specific HF3FS test or existing issue covering this problem. ### root cause DeepSeek-V4 creates a LogicalHostPool whose storage-related properties are: ``` self.kv_buffer = None self.size_per_token = 0 def get_ksize_per_token(self): return 0 ``` The storage factory calculates: ``` bytes_per_page = ( mem_pool_host.get_ksize_per_token() * mem_pool_host.page_size ) ``` Therefore, bytes_per_page is zero. `HiCacheHF3FS.__init__()` subsequently executes: ``` self.num_pages = self.file_size // self.bytes_per_page ``` This should result in: ZeroDivisionError: integer division or modulo by zero ### Reproduction Setup HF3FS config json file according to doc https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/hf3fs/docs/deploy_sglang_3fs_multinode.md Start SGLang server like: ``` export SGLANG_HICACHE_HF3FS_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/hf3fs_config.json sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --tp 2 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.92 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32 \ --served-model-name local-dsv4-flash \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-ratio 2 \ --hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct \ --hicache-io-backend direct \ --hicache-storage-backend hf3fs \ --hicache-storage-prefetch-policy wait_complete ``` You will see ``` File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py", line 527, in build_deepseek_v4_hicache_stack cache_controller = HybridCacheController( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py", line 205, in __init__ self.attach_storage_backend( File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py", line 225, in attach_storage_backend super().attach_storage_backend( File "/path/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py", line 475, in attach_storage_backend self.storage_backend = StorageBackendFactory.create_backend( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/backend_factory.py", line 94, in create_backend return cls._create_builtin_backend( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/backend_factory.py", line 183, in _create_builtin_backend return backend_class.from_env_config(bytes_per_page, dtype, storage_config) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/hf3fs/storage_hf3fs.py", line 362, in from_env_config return HiCacheHF3FS( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/hf3fs/storage_hf3fs.py", line 220, in __init__ self.num_pages = self.file_size // self.bytes_per_page ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ZeroDivisionError: integer division or modulo by zero ``` ### Environment Python: 3.12.3 (main, Mar 23 2026, 19:04:32) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU 0,1 Compute Capability: 12.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.3, V13.3.33 CUDA Driver Version: 610.43.02 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.17 signals.title: [Bug] HiCache host-pool memory check (psutil.virtual_memory().available) does not account for reserved HugePages, causing false "Not enough host memory" failures
signals.text: [Bug] HiCache host-pool memory check (`psutil.virtual_memory().available`) does not account for reserved HugePages, causing false "Not enough host memory" failures ## Checklist - [x] I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version (reproduced against a recent `main` checkout). - [x] Environment info and a minimal reproduction are included below. ## Describe the bug When `vm.nr_hugepages` is configured on the host and `--enable-hierarchical-cache` is used, `HostKVCache.__init__` (in `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/base.py`) can fail to start with: ``` ValueError: Not enough host memory available. Requesting 7.05 GB but only have 2.04 GB free. Please reduce the size of the hierarchical cache. ``` even though the reserved HugePages pool is *completely free* at that moment (`HugePages_Free` == `HugePages_Total`), and even though the very allocation this check is gating will, if it succeeds, be satisfied via a hugetlbfs-backed `mmap` from that same pool — not from general system RAM. The check in question: ```python # python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/base.py (~line 135-146) # Verify there is enough available host memory. host_mem = psutil.virtual_memory() requested_bytes = self.size * self.size_per_token available_bytes = host_mem.available - HICACHE_HOST_MEMORY_RESERVE_BYTES if requested_bytes > available_bytes: raise ValueError( f"Not enough host memory available. Requesting " f"{requested_bytes / 1e9:.2f} GB but only have " f"{available_bytes / 1e9:.2f} GB free. Please reduce the " f"size of the hierarchical cache." ) ``` `psutil.virtual_memory().available` mirrors the kernel's `MemAvailable` in `/proc/meminfo`, which **excludes reserved HugePages by design** (they are not reclaimable general-purpose memory, regardless of whether they're currently allocated). So reserving `N` GB of HugePages reduces `available` by roughly `N` GB, and this check then uses that already-reduced `available` to decide whether there's room for... an allocation that is actually going to be satisfied from the (still fully free) HugePages pool. Net effect: the more HugePages you reserve to make the host KV pool fast, the more likely this pre-flight check is to fail, independent of whether the HugePages pool itself has enough room. ## Root cause confirmation Immediately after this check would pass, the actual allocation path confirms it targets hugetlbfs specifically. When no HugePages are reserved (`vm.nr_hugepages=0`), the same code path logs: ``` Hugepage mmap via libc failed ([Errno 12] Cannot allocate memory); falling back to plain mmap. SGLANG_HUGEPAGE_SIZE=2MB will be ignored. ``` This proves the intended allocation always attempts `MAP_HUGETLB` first, and only falls back to plain pages when hugetlbfs allocation fails — i.e., the code is fully hugepage-aware downstream of the check, just not *in* the check itself. ## Reproduction Hardware: Ryzen 7 9700X, 32 GB DDR5, RTX 5060 Ti 16GB, single node, `--tp 1`. Model launched with `--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 2.0` and varying `--hicache-size`. **1) Baseline, no HugePages reserved:** ``` $ free -h Mem: 30Gi 1.3Gi 16Gi ... 29Gi available HugePages_Total: 0 ``` **2) Reserve HugePages sized to match `--hicache-size 8`, start server — succeeds:** ``` $ sudo sysctl -w vm.nr_hugepages=4096 # 8 GiB $ free -h Mem: 30Gi 9.3Gi 8.4Gi ... 21Gi available HugePages_Total: 4096 HugePages_Free: 4096 ``` Server starts fine with `--hicache-size 8`. After startup: `HugePages_Free: 280` (pool nearly fully consumed, ~7.45 GB used out of 8 GB reserved) — i.e. it *does* use the HugePages successfully when the check passes. **3) Reserve HugePages sized to match `--hicache-size 12`, start server — fails:** ``` $ sudo sysctl -w vm.nr_hugepages=6144 # 12 GiB $ free -h Mem: 30Gi 13Gi 3.8Gi ... 17Gi available HugePages_Total: 6144 HugePages_Free: 6144 # 100% free ``` Server startup fails: ``` Allocating full hierarchical KV host pool: 246016 tokens, 7.05 GB host memory. ValueError: Not enough host memory available. Requesting 7.05 GB but only have 2.04 GB free. ``` Note: `HugePages_Free` was 6144 (fully free, 12 GB available in the hugetlb pool) immediately before this. The "2.04 GB free" clearly does not come from the hugepage pool. **4) Remove the HugePages reservation entirely, same `--hicache-size 12` — succeeds:** ``` $ sudo sysctl -w vm.nr_hugepages=0 $ free -h Mem: 30Gi 1.3Gi 17Gi ... 29Gi available ``` ``` Allocating full hierarchical KV host pool: 246016 tokens, 7.05 GB host memory. Hugepage mmap via libc failed ([Errno 12] Cannot allocate memory); falling back to plain mmap. Allocating swa hierarchical KV host pool: 69056 tokens, 4.95 GB host memory. Hugepage mmap via libc failed ([Errno 12] Cannot allocate memory); falling back to plain mmap. ... The server is fired up and ready to roll! ``` Same total request (12 GB), same machine, same free RAM budget minus the HugePages reservation — succeeds without HugePages, fails with them. ## Expected behavior The pre-flight check should not treat HugePages capacity as unavailable when the allocator is actually going to (attempt to) draw from the HugePages pool. At minimum, when `HugePages_Total > 0`, the check should also consider `HugePages_Free * Hugepagesize` (from `/proc/meminfo`) as usable capacity for this request, e.g. something like: ```python available_bytes = host_mem.available - HICACHE_HOST_MEMORY_RESERVE_BYTES if hugepages_are_configured(): available_bytes += free_hugepage_bytes() # HugePages_Free * Hugepagesize ``` (or equivalently, only apply the `psutil`-based check when the allocation is *not* going to attempt hugetlbfs, and check `HugePages_Free` instead when it is). ## Environment (sglang-env) mario@mario-ia:~$ python3 -m sglang.check_env Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti GPU 0 Compute Capability: 12.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.3, V13.3.73 CUDA Driver Version: 595.71.05 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.17 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5 flashinfer_python: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_cubin: Module Not Found flashinfer_jit_cache: Module Not Found triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0 numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.141.1 huggingface_hub: 1.27.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.39.1 orjson: 3.11.9 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.52.3 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.1 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.13.0 anthropic: 0.122.0 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: 0.11.1 NVIDIA Topology: GPU0 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID GPU0 X 0-15 0 N/A Legend: X = Self SYS = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the SMP interconnect between NUMA nodes (e.g., QPI/UPI) NODE = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the interconnect between PCIe Host Bridges within a NUMA node PHB = Connection traversing PCIe as well as a PCIe Host Bridge (typically the CPU) PXB = Connection traversing multiple PCIe bridges (without traversing the PCIe Host Bridge) PIX = Connection traversing at most a single PCIe bridge NV# = Connection traversing a bonded set of # NVLinks ulimit soft: 1024 ## Additional context This is consistent with documented Linux kernel behavior: `MemAvailable` (and by extension `psutil.virtual_memory().available`) intentionally excludes HugePages, reserved or not, since they are a separate, non-reclaimable memory pool. So this isn't a kernel quirk — it's specifically that the SGLang check doesn't compensate for it when HugePages are configured and about to be used.

signals.title: [Bug] --enable-eplb + --speculative-algorithm DSPARK crashes during draft CUDA graph capture: on_select_experts scatter_add_ dimension mismatch (layer_idx=None)
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Enabling EPLB together with DSPARK speculative decoding on DeepSeek-V4-Flash crashes all 8 TP ranks simultaneously during **draft-model decode CUDA graph capture**, then crash-loops on restart (container restart policy).
