signals.title: [diffusion][model] Support LingBot-Video MoE: image-to-video, text-to-image, refiner, and prompt rewriting
signals.text:
# Support LingBot-Video MoE: image-to-video, text-to-image, refiner, and prompt rewriting ## Motivation The initial LingBot-Video MoE 30B-A3B port covered text-to-video. The released checkpoint also ships refiner weights and supports image-to-video and text-to-image, so a deployment today exercises only part of what the model can do. This PR closes that gap. Related issue: #32336 Upstream PR: #32341 ## Design One pipeline serves every task. `task_type` becomes `TI2V`, which makes the input image optional, so the request decides: `image_path` gives image-to-video, omitting it gives text-to-video, `num_frames=1` gives a still. The checkpoint leaves little choice here — `model_index.json` declares a single pipeline class and the registry resolves a single config, so a second class would be unreachable without an extra CLI flag on every image-to-video request. Conditioning uses the frame twice: as visual context for the Qwen3-VL encoder, and as a clean latent pinned to the head of the diffusion latent and rewritten after every scheduler step. The DiT forward signature is untouched. The refiner is the one part behind an explicit `--pipeline-class-name LingBotVideoRefinerPipeline`, since doubling resident DiT weights is a deployment decision rather than a per-request one. It loads from the checkpoint's `refiner/` subfolder by redirecting only the weight path, so the component keeps its `transformer_2` identity and still resolves the transformer loader. Its second pass rebuilds text conditioning without vision tokens because the refiner DiT has no image-conditioning path, drives both posterior samples and the noise draw from one seeded generator, and rejects single-frame requests. Prompt rewriting runs as a stage against an externally served vision language model over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, rather than pulling another 27B model into the diffusion worker. Set `rewriter_url` and free-text prompts get expanded and mapped to JSON in two turns; structured captions pass through untouched, and leaving the URL unset skips the stage. ## Verification Checked against the reference diffusers implementation on the same hardware, checkpoint, seed, and parameters. Cross-GPU comparison is not meaningful for this model — identical code and seed on an H100 and a 5090 produce visibly different motion — so every comparison below is same-hardware. ### Prompts and inputs The DiT consumes a structured JSON caption rather than a plain sentence, so the prompt below is the caption itself. Every run in this section uses seed 42 and the same caption for its task, so a reviewer can reproduce any clip from the served model. ```bash sglang serve --model-path robbyant/lingbot-video-moe-30b-a3b --num-gpus 1 ```
Caption used for T2V, TI2V, and the refiner runs ```json { "caption": { "comprehensive_description": { "scene_content_description": "A dynamic, high-fidelity sequence of a fit young man and a sleek white humanoid robot running side-by-side along a paved promenade lined with blooming cherry blossom trees. The man is dressed in black athletic wear, while the robot features a glossy white chassis with black mechanical joints. They are running towards the camera, which tracks backward to maintain their position in the frame. The background features a blurred cityscape and a bridge over a river, creating a sense of depth and urban vitality. The atmosphere is energetic and futuristic, blending organic nature with advanced technology.", "camera_movement_description": "The camera executes a smooth, continuous backward tracking shot, moving parallel to the subjects' forward motion to keep them centered in the frame. There is a subtle, rhythmic vertical bobbing motion synchronized with the cadence of the runners' footsteps, adding a visceral sense of speed and physical exertion. The camera maintains a steady focus on the two runners, allowing the background elements to exhibit motion blur." }, "camera_info": { "color": "Natural", "frame_size": "Wide", "shot_type_angle": "Eye level", "lens_size": "Telephoto", "composition": "Symmetrical", "lighting": "Bright sunlight", "lighting_type": "Daylight" }, "world_knowledge": [], "prominent_elements": [ { "name": "fit young man", "description": "A muscular male with short dark hair, wearing a tight black t-shirt and black running shorts.", "actions": [ { "timestamp": "[0.0s - signals.title: [MoE] Fuse swiglu moe up gemm epilogue
signals.text: ## Motivation **What the MoE activation costs today.** The triton fused-MoE path runs three steps per layer: an up-GEMM that writes `intermediate_cache1` at the full gate+up width `N`, a standalone `silu_and_mul` that reads that buffer and writes `intermediate_cache2` at width `N/2`, and a down-GEMM. The middle step is pure data movement dressed as compute — it round-trips the entire intermediate tensor through HBM to apply an elementwise function whose inputs the up-GEMM already had sitting in registers. **Why that is worth removing at small batch.** At batch 1 a MoE layer's GEMMs degenerate into `M=4..8` slivers, so the step is bound by weight bandwidth and by the intrinsic latency floor of several hundred tiny kernels rather than by arithmetic. In that regime an extra launch plus a full round trip of the intermediate buffer, paid once per MoE layer per decode step, is a visible fraction of the step. It is also a link in the dependency chain — `GEMM1 -> act -> GEMM2` — that no amount of overlap can shorten while the activation stands between the two GEMMs. **Why it cannot simply be folded in.** The activation needs `gate[i]` and `up[i]` together, but the checkpoint stores W13 as two contiguous halves, so those two values come out of output columns `i` and `i + N/2` — different tiles of the up-GEMM. A tile holding `gate[i]` does not hold `up[i]`, and vice versa. **The fix.** Permute the rows of W13 once at load so gate and up of the same intermediate channel become adjacent columns. Each GEMM output column is an independent dot product of the input with one row of W13, so reordering rows can only reorder columns — the permute is value-neutral. After it, every `(gate[i], up[i])` pair lands in the *same* output tile as an even/odd column pair, the epilogue applies `silu(gate) * up` in-register, and only the half-width result is stored. `intermediate_cache1` and the standalone activation launch disappear, and the chain shortens to `GEMM1 -> GEMM2`. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py`: `FUSE_SWIGLU` constexpr on `fused_moe_kernel`, plus the epilogue that splits the accumulator into even/odd column pairs, applies the activation, and stores the half-width result. `invoke_fused_moe_kernel` gains a `fuse_swiglu` argument and asserts the output flavors it is incompatible with. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py`: allocates the half-width buffer as the up-GEMM destination, skips the standalone activation, and threads the flag through `fused_experts` / `fused_experts_impl` / `_fused_moe_kernel_sequence`. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton.py`: `TritonMoeQuantInfo.fuse_swiglu_interleaved` carries the layout fact from the weight owner to both `fused_experts` entry points. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py`: `_maybe_interleave_w13_for_fused_swiglu` performs the load-time permute, per expert so the gather temporary stays at one expert's slice. - `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_SWIGLU_INTERLEAVED`, default off. ### Bit parity is instruction-level, not approximate The kernel being replaced is compiled with `-use_fast_math`, so matching it means matching the instructions it emits. The epilogue uses `tl.inline_asm_elementwise` to do exactly that: `mul + ex2.approx.ftz` for `__expf`, `div.approx.ftz` for the division, and `mul.ftz.f32` for the product, with a single final rounding to bf16. The accumulator is already `compute_type` at that point, which matches the reference's bf16 store to `intermediate_cache1` followed by a reload. One detail is easy to get wrong and invisible from the call site: the reference instantiates its activation functor at `float`, so silu never lands in bf16 before the multiply. An implementation that rounds silu to bf16 first double-rounds and diverges on a large fraction of inputs. The first version of this change did exactly that, and only an element-wise bit comparison caught it. ### Why this is opt-in The permuted layout is understood by the fused epilogue and by nothing else, so every consumer that reads W13 — or the pre-activation buffer — in the checkpoint's halves layout has to be excluded at load rather than trapped later. The gate requires CUDA, the plain triton runner, standard a2a, no bias, bf16, and gated silu without `alpha` / `clamp_limit` / `swiglu_limit`, and additionally excludes: - **LoRA.** `_add_lora_gate_up_delta` adds its delta into the full-width pre-activation buffer this path eliminates, and indexes gate/up as contiguous halves of it — both assumptions break. Excluding it at load matters more than asserting at run time: permuting first and asserting later would turn `--enable-lora` into a crash after warmup instead of a clean fallback. The virtual-experts LoRA path is unaffected, since it consumes `lora_a` / `lora_b` and never the base W13. - **EPLB**, which rearranges experts by copying checkpoint-layout weights into the parameter. - Runtime weight updates, for the same reason; this one is documented on the env var rather than detected. Two further guards fail loudly rather than silently: `_fused_moe_kernel_sequence` asserts the call carries no hooks and no quantization, and `invoke_fused_moe_kernel` asserts that none of `fuse_add_to_output` / `mask_output` / `fuse_sum_all_reduce` / `lora_preserve_base` are set — those address `C` at the full width `N` and would write past the row end of the half-width buffer. Filtered (`-1`) expert blocks skip the store entirely for the same reason. Under the unfused path those rows are zero-filled at full width; here the row is only `N/2` wide, so an `N`-wide zero store would run into the next token's data. The rows are never read, because the down-GEMM CTA for such a block early-exits before loading its input. ## Accuracy Tests New: `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_fused_swiglu_epilogue.py`, registered `base-b-kernel-unit` / `1-gpu-large`. Both cases assert **bitwise** equality; a tolerance would defeat their purpose, since the failure mode this change risks is a plausible-looking few-ULP drift that no `assert_close` would flag. - `test_fused_matches_unfused_bitwise` drives the real `fused_experts` entry point twice — halves layout with the standalone activation, then interleaved layout with the epilogue — and requires the final MoE output to be bit-identical. Shapes cover a bs=1 decode row and a ragged token count that forces the `BLOCK_SIZE_M` tail. It also covers the filtered-expert claim: if those unwritten rows were ever read, the comparison would fail immediately. - `test_epilogue_matches_silu_and_mul_bitwise` isolates the epilogue arithmetic against `silu_and_mul` over random values plus the saturating tails and signed zeros. This is the guard against a future "simplification" to `tl.sigmoid` or an early bf16 cast. All three pass on H20-3e (sm90). End-to-end on `Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct` (256 experts, `moe_intermediate_size` 1024, bf16, TP4, H20-3e): six greedy prompts at 128 new tokens each, served once with the flag off and once with it on. The two output sets are **byte-identical** (equal md5). The fused run logs `Interleaved w13 gate/up: ...` on all four TP ranks and the baseline run logs it zero times, so the comparison is not vacuously passing on an inactive fast path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Removed, per MoE layer per forward: | | before | after | |---|---|---| | kernel launches | up-GEMM, activation, down-GEMM | up-GEMM, down-GEMM | | intermediate traffic | `intermediate_cache1` written at width `N`, read back at width `N` | none | | dependency chain | `GEMM1 -> act -> GEMM2` | `GEMM1 -> GEMM2` | Measured on `Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct`, TP4 on H20-3e (sm90), `bench_serving --dataset-name random --num-prompts 24 --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 256 --max-concurrency 1`, four runs per configuration: | | mean TPOT (4 runs) | output throughput | |---|---|---| | baseline | 2.49 / 2.49 / 2.49 / 2.49 ms | 362.2 - 368.6 tok/s | | fused | **2.46 / 2.46 / 2.46 / 2.46 ms** | 364.5 - 372.4 tok/s | **-1.2% mean TPOT**, with the two sets fully separated — no overlap across four runs each. Throughput moves the same way but its run-to-run spread (~1.8%) is wider than the effect, so only the TPOT column supports a conclusion here. The win scales with how launch-bound the step is, so it is largest at small batch and shrinks toward zero once the GEMMs grow big enough to dominate. sm90 with a 27-layer model at 512/256 is a conservative setting for it; the shape this was originally built for is batch-1 decode on Blackwell with a deeper MoE stack, which is not measured here. That asymmetry is the other reason this ships opt-in rather than on by default. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #31776581047](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31776581047) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #31776580851](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31776580851)

signals.text: The server-arguments reference documents `--optimistic-prefill-retries`, but no such flag exists. `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py:2989` defines the field: ```python optimistic_prefill_attempts: A[int, "Number of optimistic prefill forward passes that skip the bootstrap wait.", NS("disagg")] = 0 ``` which auto-derives the CLI flag **`--optimistic-prefill-attempts`** (used at `server_args.py:7846+` and `disaggregation/prefill.py`). There is no `optimistic_prefill_retries` anywhere in the code — a repo-wide search returns only this one doc line — so passing `--optimistic-prefill-retries` errors as an unrecognized argument. Same int type, same default `0`, same feature: just a misnamed doc row. This renames it to `--optimistic-prefill-attempts`. signals.title: SGLang scale-down number of processes.
signals.text: ## Motivation SGLang's upstream elastic-EP supports **scale-up** (adding ranks) and **fault recovery** (recovering a rank that crashed), but not runtime **scale-down** (retiring live ranks from a serving deployment). This PR adds a Mooncake-native scale-down path, layered on top of upstream's existing elastic-EP infrastructure, and stabilizes end-to-end shrink + grow flows against Mooncake C++'s runtime constraints. The design principle is simple: at launch, allocate `--max-ep-size` ranks and immediately **pre-shrink** to the operator's desired starting size. Every subsequent scale-up is then treated as a *grow-into-retired-slot* operation via upstream's v1 recovery path, and every scale-down is a retirement of a contiguous suffix of live ranks. This unifies scale-up and scale-down under one contract (the `active_ranks` bitmask), keeps the mask size stable across the lifetime of the deployment, and lets us reuse upstream's `maybe_recover_ep_ranks` machinery unchanged. ## What this PR adds ### 1. Scale-down finite state machine (new) `ElasticEPStateManager` gains a scale-down phase graph: ``` serving ──POST /scale_elastic_ep(target<current)──▶ waiting_for_retire │ ▼ drain (admission gate; drain in-flight batches) │ ▼ flip_mask (survivors clear active_ranks[retiree]; retirees run local Mooncake quiesce + os._exit(0)) │ ▼ reconfig (Mooncake update_ep_member; broadcast_global_expert_location_metadata) │ ▼ local_cleanup (rearm EPLB, reset expert distribution recorder) │ ▼ serving_shrunk ``` Driver lives in `python/sglang/srt/elastic_ep/scale_down_state.py` (new) with per-tick callbacks (`on_prepare` / `on_flip_mask` / `on_reconfig` / `on_exit`) implemented on `ModelRunner`. The scheduler + tokenizer manager gate new admissions on the phase. ### 2. NIXL retire barrier (new) A TCPStore-backed elected-leader epoch derivation coordinates the `flip_mask` transition across the surviving cohort. Handles rank-drift, arrival-counter rollback, catch-up busy-polling, and the same-tick DRAIN fold. Full implementation in `python/sglang/srt/elastic_ep/elastic_ep.py::nixl_retire_barrier_{post,check,consume}`. ### 3. Two-cycle Mooncake retire primitive (new) `try_retire_ranks(retirees)` fences via `cuda.synchronize()`, clears `active_ranks[retiree]=0` on every launch-time PG, calls `mooncake_ep.update_ep_member(WORLD, active_ranks)`, and awaits a completion barrier. Retirees separately execute `_retire_and_exit(...)` which quiesces Mooncake buffers and calls `os._exit(0)` — deliberately *not* `sys.exit(0)`, so we avoid pytest atexit hooks that would re-enter the Mooncake destructor and hang. ### 4. Grow-into-retired-slot via v1 recovery (new integration) When the operator POSTs `/scale_elastic_ep` with `target > effective_ep_size`, the scheduler now populates `ElasticEPStateManager.pending_recover_ranks` from `active_ranks == 0` slots, and `maybe_join_ep_ranks` routes through upstream's `try_recover_ranks` + `_finalize_scale_recover` instead of `try_admit_scale_ranks`. Retired slots stay in the Mooncake peer table for exactly this reason, so no new joiner subprocess needs to negotiate a wider WORLD. The joiner subprocess (`server_args.ep_join_mode="recover"` + non-zero `ep_join_rank_offset`) initializes elastic-EP state via `ModelRunner.__init__` before `initialize()`, gets its `active_ranks` mask flipped ON, and syncs the random seed from the survivor cohort via TCPStore (paired write in `_finalize_scale_recover`, `is_source=True`). ### 5. Runtime stabilization - **`retire_barrier_consume` skips `Work.wait()` when the TCPStore counter confirms all ranks posted** — Mooncake's async collective can hang here asymmetrically after retiree exit; the counter is the authoritative signal. - **Same-tick DRAIN fold**: `scale_down_state.py` no longer returns to the scheduler between DRAIN-posted and DRAIN-consumed on the same tick, avoiding a 30s stall in the NIXL a2a barrier. - **TCPStore initialization for Mooncake WORLD**: `_create_global_tcp_store` runs unconditionally when elastic-EP is enabled (previously NIXL-only), so the elected-leader epoch works uniformly. - **`_finalize_scale_up` writes `self.dp_size = target_size`**: `update_dp_attention_post_scale` only updates module globals; downstream consumers reading `ModelRunner.dp_size` (DP-attention-aware kernels, DPC-side elasticity accounting) would otherwise see the stale launch value. - **`maybe_join_ep_ranks` silent-skips on `has_scaled` when `pending_size is None`**: upstream's original called `fail_recovery` which sets `scale_phase="recovery_unsupported"` and blocks every subsequent scale request. Our design needs scale-up and scale-down to remain requestable after any prior scale, so we return silently. - **Local timeout check** (per-rank `time.monotonic()` on `pending_since`) instead of upstream's `dist.all_reduce(WORLD, MAX)`: our WORLD may include `os._exit(0)`'d retirees whose Mooncake slot has not yet reconnected, and NCCL/Gloo would deadlock waiting for peers that will never respond. ### 6. Test coverage (new) - **Manual end-to-end** (`test/manual/ep/test_mooncake_scale_down.py`, 3.7k lines): MC01–MC14 cover single-node + multi-node scale-down and grow-back on both NIXL and Mooncake a2a backends. MC06 uses deterministic inference (`--enable-deterministic-inference` + fixed seed + serial GSM8K + KV-cache flush between rounds) and asserts byte-identical scores across three post-shrink rounds. MC11 is intentionally skipped (Mooncake C++ `join_group(WORLD)` deadlock on join-then-shrink is a separate upstream issue). MC13 (shrink-below-primary after append) is env-gated behind `SGLANG_MC13_FORCE_RUN` as a compatibility valve for older container images; on the default nightly (Mooncake 0.3.12+) MC13 passes. - **Unit tests** (`test/srt/unit/elastic_ep/`, new): FSM transitions, boot-guard rejections (max-ep-size / initial-size / recover-only-with-mooncake), wiring between `ElasticEPStateManager` ↔ scheduler ↔ tokenizer manager. ### 7. Runtime environment - Default container in sweep scripts: nightly ≥ 2026-07-29 (bakes Mooncake 0.3.12.post1, which resizes P2PProxy peer arrays dynamically). Older containers still work for MC01–MC12/MC14 but need `SGLANG_MC13_FORCE_RUN=0` (the default) to skip MC13. ## Design constraints worth calling out for reviewers **Mooncake P2PProxy peer arrays.** In Mooncake versions before 0.3.12 the peer arrays were fixed-width at construction time. Our pre-shrink pattern (allocate at `--max-ep-size`, immediately retire down to the operator's desired starting size, grow back into retired slots) neatly sidestepped that constraint. Mooncake 0.3.12+ resizes these arrays dynamically (kvcache-ai/Mooncake#2623), so the constraint no longer applies at runtime — but we keep the pre-shrink design because it also gives us a stable `active_ranks` mask size, keeps every scale-up on the same code path (upstream's recovery path), and lets us keep retired slots addressable in the Mooncake peer table for future refill. **Asymmetric `Work.wait()` on Mooncake WORLD backend.** Some ranks return instantly from `handle.wait()`, others hang for 30s+. On NIXL this doesn't matter (all ranks tick at the same rate), but on Mooncake a2a it corrupts subsequent C++ collectives (`EPBuffer.update_ep_member` hangs). We ship a NIXL-first design; Mooncake a2a scale-down carries this documented limitation and is out of scope for this PR. **Fault recovery + scale coexistence.** Upstream's original `maybe_join_ep_ranks` calls `fail_recovery` when a runtime recovery attempt is detected on a scaled cohort, permanently blocking every subsequent scales. Our design supports iterative shrink/grow cycles, so we return silently on that path and preserve the ability to request future scales. ## Test plan - [x] Unit tests (`test/srt/unit/elastic_ep/`): FSM transitions, boot-guard rejections, and admission-gate wiring. - [x] Full MC01–MC14 × 5 baseline sweep on NIXL a2a: **PASS**. - [x] MC01 smoke on the layered-port rebase: **PASS** (GSM8K parity 62.50% → 61.72%, within 10% tol). - [x] MC06 deterministic smoke: byte-identical scores across all three post-shrink rounds. - [x] All 11 commits pass `python3 -m py_compile` at every snapshot. ## Commit-by-commit walkthrough (11 commits) Rebased on top of `sgl-project/sglang:main` as of 2026-07-31. Each commit passes tests standalone. | # | Commit | Summary | |---|---|---| | 1 | `e38192f08e` | **Layer scale-down on top of upstream elastic-EP.** New `scale_down_state.py`, `try_retire_ranks`, retire barrier, FSM entry points on `ModelRunner`, scheduler + tokenizer-manager admission gates, `pending_recover_ranks` plumbing, `is_ep_offset_joiner` predicate. | | 2 | `b2197ff6d1` | Unit + manual test coverage (MC01–MC12, unit tests). | | 3 | `f9e7d340b6` | Stabilize scale-down on NIXL a2a: retire barrier busy-poll, TCPStore epoch derivation, arrival-counter rollback handling. | | 4 | `9d55cf89e8` | Fix recover-mode joiner MoE storage sizing (joiner slot count from `ep_join_rank_offset + tp_size`, not `elastic_ep_initial_size`, to support partial regrow). | | 5 | `4085745e18` | Wire scale-down FSM + partial-recovery grow-back through `maybe_join_ep_ranks`. | | 6 | `3f74440ec6` | MC14 (`4→3→5` shrink-recover-then-append) + skipped MC13 regression trigger. | | 7 | `6f7c2cd19d` | Env-gate MC13 on Mooncake ≥ 0.3.12 P2PProxy fix. | | 8 | `19b9fa11e2` | Harden scale-down FSM: same-tick DRAIN fold, backend-conditional `Work.wait()` skip, TCPStore for Mooncake WORLD, `_finalize_scale_up::dp_size`, local timeout in `maybe_join_ep_ranks`. | | 9 | `078bf87c26` | Pre-PR cleanup: barrier arrival-counter leak, dedup, doc drift. | | 10 | `0c12260b21` | Dedup `ModelRunner` methods after layered port; **reorder methods to match upstream order** (reviewer-friendly diff shape, drops 603 lines of `git diff` phantom-move noise). | | 11 | `8ec48f0cae` | Make MC06 deterministic: exact-equality across post-shrink rounds via `--enable-deterministic-inference` + `--random-seed 42` + serial GSM8K + KV-cache flush between rounds. | ## Diff shape 29 files changed; net `+9,731 / -236`. Two files carry most of the surface: - `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py`: `+1507 / -123` after the reorder in commit 10. All upstream methods stay at their upstream line numbers; new scale-down/retire methods append at the class tail as a clean additive block. - `python/sglang/srt/elastic_ep/elastic_ep.py`: `+1559 / -33`. Mostly honest additions (NIXL retire barrier, retire primitives, FSM state). Other notable: - `python/sglang/srt/elastic_ep/scale_down_state.py`: new file, 677 lines (FSM driver). - `test/manual/ep/test_mooncake_scale_down.py`: new file, 3,716 lines (MC01–MC14). - `test/srt/unit/elastic_ep/*.py`: 3 new unit test files. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [x] Provide test results (5-round baseline sweep + smoke tests, itemized above). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31890380942](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890380942)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31890380863](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890380863)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Model] Add Boogu-Image base T2I support
signals.text:
## Motivation Add sglang inference support for **Boogu-Image** ([boogu-project/Boogu-Image](https://github.com/boogu-project/Boogu-Image)). The base model is a 10 B DiT (40 layers = 8 double-stream + 32 single-stream, plus 3 refiner groups), conditioned on Qwen3-VL-8B instruction features, decoded via the FLUX.1-dev `AutoencoderKL`. It ships with a bespoke ascending-time flow-match Euler scheduler that has no direct diffusers equivalent, so this PR wires everything needed to run it end-to-end. Scope of this PR: **base T2I only**. Edit / reference-image, Turbo, and the instruct-reasoner variants are intentionally out of scope and will follow separately. ## Modifications - `runtime/models/dits/boogu_image.py` — DiT: `BooguRMSNormZero` / `BooguLayerNormContinuous`, double-stream + single-stream blocks, 3-axis 3D RoPE (`text / ref-image / noise`) with per-sample windows via `BooguRopeBundle` (msgspec.Struct). Batch is folded into the token dim before rotary so sglang's Triton kernel receives 2D `[num_tokens, head_dim//2]` cos/sin; padded rows use the identity rotation (`cos=1, sin=0`) to match upstream `position_ids=0` semantics. 4D↔5D squeeze at the `ImagePipelineConfig` boundary since Boogu is image-only. - `runtime/models/schedulers/scheduling_boogu_flow_match.py` — flow-match Euler on an **ascending** time axis (`t: 0 → 1`, `prev = sample + (t_next − t) · v`), fundamentally different from `FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler`. Ports the upstream v1 logistic shift (`mu = lin(seq_len)` with `x1=256, y1=0.5, x2=4096, y2=1.15`) and v2 shift (`t / (m − mt + t)` with `m = sqrt(seq_len)/120`). - `configs/pipeline_configs/boogu_image.py` — `BooguImagePipelineConfig`. Chat template routes empty instruction → `SYSTEM_PROMPT_DROP`, non-empty → `SYSTEM_PROMPT_4_T2I` (upstream `system_prompt_follows_task_type=False`, no images). Postprocess reads `.last_hidden_state` (norm-applied); `BooguTextEncodingStage` overrides `_forward_text_encoder` to call `text_encoder.model(...)` because the outer `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration.forward` returns a causal-LM output without `last_hidden_state`. `BooguQwen3VLArchConfig` mirrors the `PretrainedConfig` defaults (`output_attentions=False` etc.) that the HF Qwen3-VL `config.json` doesn't ship. - `runtime/pipelines/boogu_image_pipeline.py` — `_load_config` remaps the on-disk `mllm` / `processor` slots to `text_encoder` / `tokenizer` (via `component_paths` redirect) and relabels the non-diffusers `transformer_boogu` / `scheduling_flow_match_euler_discrete_time_shifting` module strings so the loader library-string assertions pass (`ModelRegistry.resolve_model_cls` keys on the class name). - `configs/models/vaes/boogu_image.py` — subclass of `StableDiffusion3VAEArchConfig` (the SD3 arch config *is* the diffusers `AutoencoderKL`), with FLUX.1-dev's `scaling_factor=0.3611`, `shift_factor=0.1159`. - `configs/models/dits/boogu_image.py`, `configs/sample/boogu_image.py` — DiT and sampling defaults (50 steps, guidance 4.0, 1024²). - `configs/models/fsdp.py`, `registry.py` — `is_boogu_image_layer` FSDP predicate; register `BooguImagePipelineConfig` / `BooguImageSamplingParams` behind a `"boogu-image"` path detector. - `runtime/pipelines_core/stages/text_encoding.py` — **the only shared-path change in this PR.** `align_negative_batch_dim` was applied to both negative embeddings and negative masks, but its 2-D branch is only valid for embeddings: a 2-D *embedding* is `(seq, dim)` with no batch axis, so it must gain one (`unsqueeze(0).repeat(B, 1, 1)` — the Z-Image single-prompt case the branch was written for), whereas a 2-D *mask* is already `(batch, seq)` and must be broadcast in place. Conflating them turned a `[1, S_neg]` mask into `[B, 1, S_neg]`, so any consumer reducing over the sequence dim gets a list of lists instead of one length per request — for Boogu that is an HTTP 500 out of the RoPE builder for every dynamically-batched request (`TypeError: can only concatenate list (not "int") to list`). At batch 1 the broadcast is a no-op (`target_batch == 1` returns the tensor unchanged), which is why the one-shot `generate` path never surfaced it. The helper now takes a kw-only `batchless_2d` flag; both mask call sites pass `batchless_2d=False`. - `runtime/models/dits/boogu_image.py` — `@torch.compiler.disable` on `BooguRopeEmbedder.forward`, which is what makes `--enable-torch-compile` usable for this model. Dynamo's polyfill calls `cls.__new__(cls, *args)` and msgspec's C-level `__new__` rejects it, so compiling the DiT raised from the RoPE embedder's `BooguRopeBundle` return value. Position ids depend only on sequence lengths and image sizes, never on the latents, and the call is ~0.5 ms, so keeping it out of the graph costs nothing and lets the remaining 40 layers compile. - `test/unit/test_text_encoding_negative_batch.py` — new. A shared `[1, seq]` negative mask stays 2-D when broadcast to a batch (and still reduces to one length per request); a 2-D `(seq, dim)` embedding still gains a batch axis; batch 1 is unchanged. Follows [`no-getattr-defensive`](.claude/rules/no-getattr-defensive.md), [`no-dataclasses`](.claude/rules/no-dataclasses.md) (new containers are `msgspec.Struct`; config classes are grandfathered `@dataclass`), [`general-code-style`](.claude/rules/general-code-style.md). ## Accuracy Tests - Scheduler: bit-identical to upstream across `static-v1` / `dynamic-v1` / `dynamic-v2` / `do_shift=False` × steps ∈ {50, 40, 28}, and `step()` integration over 40 steps (max delta `0.0`). - Weight loading: 942 checkpoint keys → 888 model params, 0 missing / 0 unexpected / 0 shape mismatch. - Single-GPU T2I end-to-end (1024×1024, guidance 4.0, seed 0): output image aligns with the reference `inference_simple.py` prompt (elderly scavenger + trash can + red traffic light + Leica street-photography aesthetic). - Unit tests: `pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_text_encoding_negative_batch.py -q` → **3 passed**. Shared negative-conditioning / CFG paths re-run to confirm no other model regressed (`test_text_encoding_cache.py`, `test_cfg_gating.py`, `test_sampling_params.py`, plus the new file) → **36 passed, 8 subtests passed**. - Server end-to-end: the benchmark below produced 10 images (1 warmup + 3 sequential + 2 concurrent + 4 concurrent) with zero exceptions in the server log, at scheduler-reported batch sizes 1 / 2 / 4. - The `text_encoding.py` fix is shape-only and a no-op at batch 1, so single-request output is unchanged by construction; the batched shapes are locked by the new unit tests. `@torch.compiler.disable` keeps the RoPE builder in eager rather than altering it, so it does not move numerics either. - 50-step parity vs the upstream diffusers reference (same `seed=42`, cyberpunk prompt / gallery row 1): injecting byte-identical initial noise **and** conditioning into both stacks leaves the initial latent bit-identical (max abs diff `0.0`) and the step-1 latent within **0.53%** rel-L2 (cosine `0.99997`) — a single denoise step is numerically equivalent across backends. Over 50 CFG steps at guidance 4.0 this compounds to step-50 latent rel-L2 ≈ 72% and final-image PSNR 12.3 dB / SSIM 0.40 (see the Qualitative Comparison section), i.e. benign last-bit bf16 kernel drift (FlashInfer/fused vs SDPA), not a structural difference. ## Qualitative Comparison (upstream diffusers vs sglang native) Same weights, `seed=42`, 1024×1024, 50 steps, `guidance_scale=4.0`. Images are width-limited to 320px; click any cell to view full 1024×1024. | Prompt | diffusers (upstream) | sglang (native) | |---|---|---| | A futuristic cyberpunk city at night, neon reflections on wet streets | | | | A cute orange tabby kitten sitting in a field of sunflowers, golden hour lighting, photorealistic | | | | A serene Japanese garden with a red maple tree, koi pond and stone lantern in autumn | | | | A steaming bowl of ramen with a soft-boiled egg and chopsticks, close-up food photography | | | | An astronaut riding a horse on Mars, dramatic cinematic lighting | | |
Parity note (same-seed divergence is expected, not a bug) Feeding byte-identical initial noise **and** identical conditioning embeddings into both stacks: step-1 latent rel-L2 = 0.53% (cosine 0.99997), step-50 = 72%, final image PSNR 12.3 dB / SSIM 0.40. A single denoise step is numerically equivalent between the two backends; the divergence is compounding bf16 kernel drift amplified over 50 CFG steps at guidance 4.0 — a different-but-valid sample from the same distribution, not a structural difference.
## Speed Tests and Profiling H20 (95.6 GiB), bf16, `Boogu-Image-0.1-Base` (10.29B DiT, 40 layers), `guidance_scale=4.0`, `seed=42`, fixed prompt set. Sections 1–3 are 1024²/50 steps with the upstream diffusers pipeline as reference (identical weights, sglang on GPU 2, diffusers on GPU 0); section 4 uses vllm-omni's published 512²/28-step config. The native-backend gate was verified on every sglang run (no `diffusers backend` / `Loaded diffusers pipeline` in any log). Shared env: `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`.
Commands sglang one-shot and server. `serve` opens its HTTP port *before* warmup runs (`/health` answers 200 while the GPU is still warming), so readiness is gated on the `fired up and ready to roll` log line: ```bash python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.entrypoints.cli.main generate \ --backend=sglang --model-path $MODEL --prompt "$PROMPT" \ --width 1024 --height 1024 --num-inference-steps 50 --guidance-scale 4.0 \ --seed 42 --save-output --warmup --dit-cpu-offload false \ --perf-dump-path outputs/diffusion_benchmarks/$LABEL.json \ [--enable-torch-compile] [--enable-cfg-parallel] python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.entrypoints.cli.main serve \ --model-path $MODEL --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31000 \ --batching-max-size 4 --batching-delay-ms 100 \ --enable-batching-metrics --dit-cpu-offload false curl -x '' -s http://127.0.0.1:31000/v1/images/generations \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"prompt":"'"$PROMPT"'","width":1024,"height":1024, "num_inference_steps":50,"guidance_scale":4.0,"seed":42,"n":1}' ``` Upstream diffusers reference. `device=cuda:0` must be exported *before* importing `boogu` — it gates upstream's own fused RMSNorm and fused SwiGLU, so leaving it unset understates the reference. One 50-step warmup pass is discarded: ```python import os; os.environ["device"] = "cuda:0" # before the boogu import import torch from boogu.pipelines.boogu.pipeline_boogu import BooguImagePipeline pipe = BooguImagePipeline.from_pretrained(MODEL, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, trust_remote_code=True).to("cuda:0") # str -> batch 1; list -> batch_size = len(list) (pipeline_boogu.py:2743) pipe(instruction=PROMPT, negative_instruction="", height=1024, width=1024, max_input_image_pixels=1024 * 1024, max_input_image_side_length=2048, num_inference_steps=50, text_guidance_scale=4.0, generator=torch.Generator("cuda:0").manual_seed(42)) ``` Section 4, sglang side — the in-tree benchmark client, one server lifetime per config. With `--enable-torch-compile` *and* `--batching-max-size > 1` the sweep runs twice and only the second, compile-warm pass is reported; see the section 4 caveats for why `--warmup-requests` cannot cover it: ```bash python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.entrypoints.cli.main serve \ --model-path $MODEL --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31011 \ --batching-max-size {1,4} --batching-delay-ms 100 \ --enable-batching-metrics --dit-cpu-offload false --enable-torch-compile true for conc in 1 2 4; do python python/sglang/multimodal_gen/benchmarks/bench_serving.py \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31011 --dataset random --task text-to-image \ --width 512 --height 512 --num-inference-steps 28 \ --num-prompts 10 --max-concurrency $conc --warmup-requests 4 \ --disable-tqdm --output-file c$conc.json done ``` vllm-omni side (their own harness and config, model repointed at our local checkpoint, baseline assertion replaced by `skip-performance-assertion`): ```bash python -m pytest tests/dfx/perf/scripts/run_diffusion_benchmark.py \ --test-config-file tests/dfx/perf/tests/test_boogu_image_h20_local.json -s -v ```
### 1. Optimization stack vs upstream diffusers, one-shot latency The diffusers reference is repeated per row so each sglang config is compared to the closest diffusers configuration — 68.65 s eager (its own fused RMSNorm / SwiGLU / FA on) for the non-compile rows, 66.51 s (+ `torch.compile`) for the compile rows. Head-dim padding and CFG parallel have no equivalent there. | config | diffusers (upstream) | sglang (native) | sglang speedup | sglang vs diffusers | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | eager, 1 GPU | 68.65 | 69.49 | 1.00× | 0.99× | | + `--enable-torch-compile` | 66.51 | 59.87 | **1.16×** | **1.11×** | | + head-dim padded to FA bucket, eager | 68.65 | 64.67 | **1.07×** | **1.06×** | | + head-dim padded + `--enable-torch-compile` | 66.51 | **54.54** | **1.27×** | **1.22×** | | + `--enable-cfg-parallel`, 2 GPU | 68.65 | 34.79 | **2.00×** | **1.97×** | | + CFG parallel ×2 + compile | 66.51 | **29.93** | **2.32×** | **2.22×** | - Eager baselines agree within 1.2%, so the ports are at parity before any lever. - `torch.compile` buys diffusers only 3.1% (68.65 → 66.51, fast paths already on) but 1.16× here — and is reachable only via the `@torch.compiler.disable` change in this PR. Compile × CFG-parallel stacks cleanly: 2.01 × 1.16 = 2.33 predicted vs 2.336× measured. - Best single-GPU 54.54 s is **1.22×** diffusers' own best; CFG-parallel ×2 + compile 29.93 s is **2.22×**. - Head-dim padding routes Boogu's head_dim=120 through FlashAttention by zero-padding Q/K/V to 128 (softmax_scale pinned to 1/√120) and slicing back — the trick `sana_wm_components._sana_wm_sdpa` already uses for head_dim=112. Kernel test matches SDPA within bf16 noise (rel-L2 = 3.9 × 10⁻⁵). The two padding rows were re-measured as a four-cell A/B on one commit, the only variable being `_padded_head_dim` (128 vs `self.head_dim`, which makes the selector reject FA at head size 120 and fall back to `torch_sdpa` — confirmed per cell from the `Attention backends for transformer` log line); all four cells reproduce the table within 0.21%. The gain is resolution-dependent: attention is 22.5% of DiT GPU time at 1024²'s 4352 joint tokens but roughly a third of that at 512²'s 1280, since attention FLOPs grow as S² and the linear layers as S, so the same A/B at 512² returns only +0.27% (section 4). ### 2. Server mode with dynamic batching Warmup is `server warmup req (1024x1024, 2/50 steps)` = 6.12 s, then `fired up and ready to roll` — 210 s from launch. Batch sizes are the scheduler's own `Dynamic batch dispatch` metric, not the request count. Compile rows are compile-warm (first request at a new batch dim recompiles: 315 s at batch 2). SDPA eager (= section 1's `eager, 1 GPU`): | concurrency | scheduler dispatch | per-request latency (s) | wall (s) | img/s | vs 1 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | `size=1/4 delay` | 70.48 / 70.00 / 70.77 → median **70.48** | 70.48 | 0.0142 | 1.000× | | 2 | `size=2/4 delay` | 137.01 / 137.01 | 137.02 | 0.0146 | 1.03× | | 4 | `size=4/4 config_cap:4` | 271.18 ×4 | 271.19 | 0.0148 | 1.04× | Padded FA + `--enable-torch-compile` (= section 1's best single-GPU row): | concurrency | scheduler dispatch | per-request latency (s) | wall (s) | img/s | vs 1 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | `size=1/4 delay` | 55.44 / 55.15 / 55.15 → median **55.15** | 55.44 | 0.0181 | 1.000× | | 2 | `size=2/4 delay` | 110.51 / 110.51 | 110.52 | 0.0181 | 1.00× | | 4 | `size=4/4 config_cap:4` | 218.16 ×4 | 218.17 | 0.0183 | 1.01× | Serving overhead is small — 70.48 s through HTTP + ZMQ + scheduler vs 69.49 s one-shot, **+1.4%**. Padded FA + compile is **1.28× / 1.24× / 1.24×** faster per request at concurrency 1 / 2 / 4, matching section 1's 1.27×. ### 3. Batching headroom at this resolution, vs diffusers | batch | diffusers ms/forward | diffusers img/s | vs 1 | sglang (SDPA) img/s | vs 1 | sglang (padded FA + compile) img/s | vs 1 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 683.3 | 0.0146 | 1.000× | 0.0142 | 1.000× | 0.0181 | 1.000× | | 2 | 1331.9 (1.95×) | 0.0150 | 1.027× | 0.0146 | 1.03× | 0.0181 | 1.00× | | 4 | 2617.5 (3.83×) | 0.0152 | 1.046× | 0.0148 | 1.04× | 0.0183 | 1.01× | diffusers' per-forward scales 1.00 / 1.95 / 3.83 — essentially linear — so one 1024² image (4096 image + 256 instruction = 4352 joint tokens) already saturates the H20 and batching is worth ~1–4% for any implementation. All three curves agreeing on the flat shape is the result: this PR makes batching *correct*, and section 1's multi-GPU path is where throughput comes from. Peak memory, per engine: sglang 29 950 / 34 558 / 44 794 MB (server's own `Peak memory usage`), diffusers 36.91 / 38.54 / 42.54 GiB (`torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated`). ### 4. Cross-engine check against vllm-omni, on the same GPU vllm-omni [PR #4995](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/4995) ports the same model, but on different hardware, so its published numbers support no claim about either implementation. Their stack was installed (own uv venv, `vllm 0.26.0` + vllm-omni at upstream main `67c54777`, torch 2.11.0+cu130) and **their harness and their published config were run on the same H20, GPU 1** — the card our own sweep used. That config is `tests/dfx/perf/tests/test_boogu_image_vllm_omni.json` (512×512, 28 steps, 10 prompts, `max-concurrency` 1/2/4, 4 warmup requests at concurrency 4, negative prompt on, guidance 4.0 with CFG on), **not** the 1024² command in their PR body. Their pipeline profiler costs 0.5–1.0%, so their profiler-off numbers are quoted. 30/30 requests succeeded per run. Medians are used throughout: at 10 prompts / concurrency 4 the run is only 2.5 waves, so the partly-empty first wave biases every mean, while medians match Little's Law within 0.15%. Each engine at its own best. Both harnesses share a client lineage and emit the same fields (`throughput_qps`, `latency_median`), so the rows line up directly: latency is the median of 10 requests at concurrency 1, throughput the best over concurrency 1 / 2 / 4. | engine | best config | per-image latency (s) | throughput (img/s) | |---|---|---:|---:| | vllm-omni | compile on by default; request batching unavailable | 8.502 | 0.1192 | | sglang (this PR) | padded FA + `--enable-torch-compile` | **8.259** | **0.1341** | | ratio (sglang / vllm-omni) | | **1.029×** | **1.125×** | The two sglang figures come from different `--batching-max-size` values — 8.259 s at `maxb 1`, 0.1341 img/s at `maxb 4` — because batching trades 0.115 s of single-image latency (the `--batching-delay-ms 100` window, with nothing to merge at concurrency 1) for +10.7% throughput at concurrency 4. Run `maxb 4` when loaded, `maxb 1` when latency-bound. - **They compile the DiT by default** (`Regional compilation applied to 42 module(s) for repeated blocks [...]`, no flag); our defaults are eager and `batching_max_size = 1` (`server_args.py:355`). Default vs default **we lose 11.6%**, and only this PR unblocks the flip — worth 1.16× here, the same as section 1's 1024² figure. Compile vs compile with batching off the two engines are within 1.6%: the denoising loops are at parity, and the gap above comes from the levers around them. - **Their concurrency curve is flat for a structural reason, not a batching result.** `pipeline_boogu_image.py:201` sets `supports_request_batch = False`; `diffusion_engine.py:205` raises `ValueError` for any `max_num_seqs > 1`; the alternative `--step-execution` path needs `prepare_encode()` / `denoise_step()` / `step_scheduler()` / `post_decode()`, none of which their pipeline implements. Their log confirms `max_num_seqs=1 max_wait_ms=0.0`, `batch_size=1`. Per-pipeline gap, not an engine limit: `qwen_image`, `sd3`, `flux`, `ltx2` all set `supports_request_batch = True`. - **Head-dim padding is nearly free at this resolution** — +0.27% against +7.5% / +9.7% at 1024² in section 1. A 1280-token joint sequence spends far less of its time in attention than a 4352-token one. | lever | sglang (this PR) | vllm-omni Boogu | upstream diffusers | |---|---|---|---| | `torch.compile` on the DiT | 1.16× at both resolutions, unblocked here | on by default | 1.03× | | request batching | +10.7% qps at concurrency 4 | unavailable | +4.6% at batch 4 | | CFG parallel, 2 GPU | **2.00×** | unavailable | unavailable | | stacked | **2.32×** | — | — | Caveats: single run per point. For the `maxb 4` figure the sweep was run twice against one server and the second, compile-warm pass reported — with `--enable-torch-compile` the first request at a previously unseen batch dim recompiles inside the measured window, so cold pass 1 at concurrency 2 reads qps 0.0560 with p99 116.4 s against a 15.51 s median. Their harness posts t2i to `/v1/chat/completions` while `bench_serving.py` posts `/v1/images/generations` (each engine's documented path). All four GPUs carried an external tenant at ~80% utilization throughout, applying to both engines equally — the point of measuring on one box. ## Follow-up work (not in this PR) Called out so reviewers know the current boundary; these will land separately: - **Sequence parallelism (Ulysses/SP).** `--ulysses-degree 2` does not yet work for this model — the latent `rearrange` is over 5 dims and the 7 KV heads do not divide by the SP degree, so it needs a `shard_latents_for_sp` override in `base.py` and a fix to the head-count assert at `usp.py:263`. CFG parallelism in section 1 is unaffected and is the multi-GPU path that works today. - **Cache-DiT (step-layer caching, ~1.5–2× lossy).** Boogu is not yet registered in `_CUSTOM_BLOCK_ADAPTER_SPECS`; the adapter carries a single block-list attribute while Boogu has two (`double_stream_layers` = 8, `single_stream_layers` = 32), so registration has to handle both. Gated on a PSNR/SSIM check since it is lossy. - **Warm up serving benchmarks at the real step count.** `bench_serving.py:591` pins warmup requests to `num_inference_steps=1` because the server overrides them anyway (`warmup_request_builder.py:394` → `Req.set_as_warmup`), and issues them serially — so warmup pre-warms neither the real denoise shape nor a batch dim, and under `--enable-torch-compile` with `--batching-max-size > 1` the first request at each new batch dim recompiles inside the measured window. vllm-omni's harness avoids this by warming at `warmup-num-inference-steps=28, warmup-concurrency=4`. Section 4 works around it by reporting the second of two passes; the fix is to let warmup requests carry the benchmark's step count and concurrency. - **I2I / edit and reference-image** (and Turbo / instruct-reasoner), per the scope note in Motivation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #30752695530](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30752695530) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #30752695446](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30752695446) --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #31592879159](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31592879159) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #31592878948](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31592878948)

signals.title: feat(dsv4): support --dsa-topk-backend flashinfer with fused top-k
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation @humansand **Scope: DeepSeek V4 FlashInfer backend support.** This PR makes `--dsa-topk-backend flashinfer` usable for the DeepSeek V4 indexer and implements that path with FlashInfer's fused compact-page top-k transform; the packed PAGED DSA prerequisite lives in #33006. This PR is the DeepSeek V4 layer of a two-PR stack: 1. [#33006](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33006) restores FlashInfer fused top-k for packed PAGED rows using independent score and page-table starts. 2. This PR uses the same fused transform for DeepSeek V4's compact page table, where one page-table entry represents 64 score positions. The child commit `fd150ca930e3391e58b70c760963e5e54a64e364` is directly based on #33006 head `e074a275de1290cc5f284ee16a90644d5119cd74`. Until #33006 merges, GitHub's diff against `main` includes both layers; the changes unique to this PR are the DeepSeek V4 integration described below. DeepSeek V4 score rows can be padded, and CUDA graph capture supplies caller-owned translated and raw-index output buffers. The old FlashInfer path therefore cloned and masked scores, ran `top_k`, re-gathered scores, translated indices through the compact table, handled short rows, and copied the outputs. [FlashInfer #4315](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4315) extends `top_k_page_table_transform` to support this layout in one fused call. > **Draft dependencies:** #33006 must merge first. FlashInfer #4315 is merged, but every currently published stable, RC, and nightly artifact predates that merge. Once a containing release is available, SGLang must run `python scripts/release/bump_flashinfer_version.py <first-containing-release>` so its dependency pins and runtime minimum enforce both required APIs. ## Modifications - Replace DeepSeek V4's unfused FlashInfer helper with one `top_k_page_table_transform` call that accepts: - padded-stride score rows without materializing a contiguous copy; - the compact page table with `page_size=64`; - graph-safe deterministic and tie-break settings; - caller-owned translated and optional raw-index output buffers. - Remove the generic `topk_op` plumbing that existed only for the unfused workaround; keep the vectorized PyTorch fallback on `torch.topk`. - Build and dispatch SGL top-k-v2 metadata only when the SGL backend is selected, so the FlashInfer path does not create or copy an unused SGL plan. - Apply the FlashInfer version check when `--dsa-topk-backend flashinfer` is selected, even if the attention backend is not FlashInfer. The minimum is intentionally unchanged until a containing release exists. - Update the top-k benchmark to measure compact page-size-64 translation with a preallocated output instead of materializing a page-size-1 table. - Add mocked API-wiring coverage and real compact-page CUDA-graph coverage for K=512/K=1024, padded score strides, optional raw output, replayed inputs, short rows, and raw/translated alignment. ## Accuracy Tests Rebase/static validation at `fd150ca930e3391e58b70c760963e5e54a64e364`: ```text git diff --check origin/agent/integrate-flashinfer-topk-fix..HEAD python3 -m compileall -q <changed Python files> ``` Both passed. The child commit replayed without conflicts; `git range-diff` retained the patch with only the expected shared-test import context from #33006. SGLang runtime tests were not rerun after the rebase. The repository still pins `flashinfer_python==0.6.15.post1`, which does not provide #4315's compact-page and caller-owned-output contract. The underlying FlashInfer implementation was separately validated in #4315 on an NVIDIA B200 with CUDA 13.2.78 and PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132. Its focused compact-page tests passed 18 cases, related preallocated-output tests passed 6 cases, trace tests passed 6 cases with 1 skipped, and the full `tests/utils/test_topk.py` file passed 1,495 tests. Those are FlashInfer results, not SGLang runtime validation. Before this PR leaves draft, run the focused SGLang unit/GPU tests against the first containing FlashInfer release, then exercise the DeepSeek V4 B200 model path with `--dsa-topk-backend flashinfer`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No SGLang performance benchmark has been run. `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_topk.py` now measures the actual compact-page, preallocated-output path. Report K=512 and K=1024 before merge, plus a DeepSeek V4 serving comparison if the operator change is material at model level. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No CLI or public SGLang API change.) - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: fix(router): preserve upstream response headers
signals.text: ## Motivation The experimental router currently rebuilds worker responses with only the status and `Content-Type`. All other upstream response headers are dropped on both buffered and streaming paths. This removes headers that clients rely on, including `Retry-After` for backoff and upstream request IDs for correlating worker logs. It also differs from normal reverse-proxy behavior and from the response-header handling in the existing model gateway. ## Modifications - Preserve end-to-end worker response headers for buffered JSON and streaming responses. - Strip connection-specific and framing headers, including fields named by `Connection`, before constructing the downstream response. - Preserve repeated header values such as multiple `Set-Cookie` fields. - Add unit coverage for header filtering and integration coverage for both proxy response paths. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This change does not alter request routing or model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The change performs one bounded copy over the small upstream response header map and does not affect inference execution. ## Validation - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` - `cargo test --release -- --skip parity_matrix` (431 library, 3 binary, 40 component, and 67 proxy tests passed) The regression test fails before this change because `Retry-After` is absent from the downstream response, and passes after the fix for both buffered and streaming responses. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Documentation is not required because this does not change configuration or public API usage. - [x] Accuracy and speed benchmarks are not applicable because this does not affect model execution. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [NPU] [Diffusion] Support MiniMax H3 on Ascend NPU's
signals.text: ## Motivation Extend the native MiniMax-H3 pipeline introduced in [#33275](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33275) to Ascend NPU. MiniMax-H3 packs real multimodal tokens together with sequence-parallel alignment padding. Its attention path is therefore variable-length even when request batch size is one: the real-token segment and the alignment-padding segment must remain isolated. ## Scope and related work - [#33275](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33275) provides the upstream MiniMax-H3 model and pipeline implementation that this PR extends. - [#33366](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33366) is the related XPU enablement PR. This PR does not include XPU backend code; shared paths use `current_platform` so the Ascend changes remain isolated and existing CUDA/ROCm behavior is preserved. - Experimental NPU RoPE, SwiGLU, and gate kernel paths were removed after benchmarking (since they did not improve performance). The final PR keeps the attention and platform-integration changes required for MiniMax-H3 on Ascend. ## Modifications ### Ascend Flash Attention - Add `forward_varlen` using `torch.ops.npu.npu_fused_infer_attention_score` with the `TND` layout and actual packed-sequence lengths. - Preserve independent packed-sequence boundaries. - Repack strided Ulysses Q/K/V views with one allocation instead of three independent contiguous copies. - Preserve the segmented fallback for causal attention. ### Laser Attention - Enable `laser_attn` for MiniMax-H3. - Add variable-length handling so real tokens cannot attend alignment padding. - Run attention only for the real-token segment, retain padding rows for sequence-parallel shape alignment, and zero-fill their output instead of computing attention for them. - Preserve BF16 activation range when the FP16 Laser kernel is used by compensating the Q/K softmax scale and restoring the value/output scale. - Limit this BF16 compensation to MiniMax-H3's packed variable-length path; the existing dense Laser path keeps its previous behavior. ### NPU dependencies and media output - Install `attentions*.whl` alongside the `deep_ep` and `sgl_kernel_npu` wheels from the pinned `sgl-kernel-npu` release archive in both the NPU Docker image and NPU CI. - Scope the missing-`attentions` layer-normalization warning to NPU. Layer normalization falls back to its native implementation; explicitly selecting Laser Attention without the package raises an actionable import error. - Install `ffmpeg` in the NPU Docker and CI environments and fail MiniMax-H3 startup early when required media tools are absent, preventing the late output loss reported in [#33927](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33927). - Keep these dependency checks and warnings isolated from CUDA, ROCm, XPU, MUSA, and CPU. ### Ascend platform integration - Use `current_platform` for shared memory residency, RNG, autocast, and denoising dispatch. - Add NPU support to component offload/cache-release handling while preserving CUDA/ROCm behavior. - Keep Qwen3-VL position IDs and rotary embeddings on the execution device only on NPU. - Avoid enabling Ascend-specific behavior on XPU, MUSA, or CPU. - Add the validated eight-NPU TP2 + SP4 launch command and a four-NPU TP2 + SP2 variant to the MiniMax-H3 cookbook. Both commands list the benchmarked Cache-DiT configuration and pass `--dit-cpu-offload false` to keep the DiT resident; the cookbook records 55.07 s and 103.57 s end-to-end latency respectively. ### FL2VA keyframe encoding - Register `MiniMaxH3Qwen3VLEncoder.encode_ids` as an FSDP2 forward method when text-encoder CPU offload is active. - Ensure the root FSDP hooks materialize non-layer parameters, including the Qwen3-VL vision `Conv3d` patch embedding, before image-conditioned encoding. - Prevent the `aten.convolution` mixed `torch.Tensor`/`DTensor` failure observed by FL2VA requests. - Keep the change platform-independent and limited to FSDP-wrapped encoders that expose `encode_ids`; non-FSDP execution is unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Validated end-to-end 5-second MiniMax-H3 T2VA generation with both Ascend Flash Attention and Laser Attention on 8 Ascend NPUs. Image-conditioned FL2VA was also validated with Laser Attention after the FSDP2 custom-forward fix. Server startup: ```bash SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_FN=2 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_BN=1 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_WARMUP=4 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_RDT=0.4 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_MC=4 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TAYLORSEER=true \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TS_ORDER=2 \ HCCL_BUFFSIZE=256 sglang serve \ --model-path ./weights/MiniMax-H3/ \ --model-type diffusion \ --model-variant fl2va \ --dit-cpu-offload false \ --num-gpus 8 \ --tp-size 2 \ --sp-degree 4 \ --attention-backend laser_attn \ --port 30088 ``` For a four-NPU host, use TP2 + SP2: ```bash SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_FN=2 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_BN=1 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_WARMUP=4 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_RDT=0.4 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_MC=4 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TAYLORSEER=true \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TS_ORDER=2 \ HCCL_BUFFSIZE=256 sglang serve \ --model-path ./weights/MiniMax-H3/ \ --model-type diffusion \ --model-variant fl2va \ --dit-cpu-offload false \ --num-gpus 4 \ --tp-size 2 \ --sp-degree 2 \ --attention-backend laser_attn \ --port 30088 ``` Use `--attention-backend fa` to validate the Ascend Flash Attention path. T2VA request: ```bash curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30088/v1/videos \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3", "prompt": "At night, while their owner sleeps in a bedroom, three cats march in loudly playing tiny brass instruments, then abruptly file out.", "seconds": 5, "task": "t2va", "conditions": [], "target": { "short_edge": 768, "aspect_ratio": "16:9", "duration_seconds": 5.0 }, "num_outputs_per_prompt": 1, "num_inference_steps": 50, "flow_shift": 12.0, "audio_flow_shift": 3.0, "seed": 1101 }' ``` Result: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6fd97552-b6ce-446c-b8d2-c26f61f7c91f FL2VA request: ```bash curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30088/v1/videos \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3", "prompt": "The supplied frame continues with calm, natural motion and synchronized ambient sound.", "seconds": 5, "task": "fl2va", "conditions": [ { "type": "image", "uri": "./Forest.jpg", "role": "keyframe", "frame_index": 0 } ], "target": { "short_edge": 768, "aspect_ratio": "auto", "duration_seconds": 5.0 }, "num_outputs_per_prompt": 1, "num_inference_steps": 50, "flow_shift": 12.0, "audio_flow_shift": 3.0, "seed": 2101 }' ``` Forest.jpg Result: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0cad1f72-86f4-45c2-bc70-5f8d4831ef97 ## Speed Tests and Profiling The Ascend FA path performs one packed `TND` attention operation using actual sequence lengths. For strided Ulysses tensors, Q/K/V are repacked through one allocation. Laser Attention computes only the real-token segment and zero-fills alignment-padding outputs, avoiding the previous short-segment fallback calculation. FA vs Laser Attention on T2VA: | Attention backend | Topology | End-to-end generation time | Speedup vs. 8-NPU FA | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | Ascend Flash Attention | 8 NPUs, TP2 + SP4 | 69.51 s | 1.00× | | Laser Attention | 8 NPUs, TP2 + SP4 | 55.07 s | 1.26× | | Laser Attention | 4 NPUs, TP2 + SP2 | 103.57 s | — | On the same eight-NPU topology, Laser Attention reduced end-to-end generation time by 20.8% compared with Ascend Flash Attention. The attention measurements use the same 5-second T2VA request at 1344×768, 124 frames, 24 FPS, 50 inference steps, and seed 1101. The launch commands list the measured Cache-DiT configuration explicitly: `FN=2`, `BN=1`, `WARMUP=4`, `RDT=0.4`, `MC=4`, TaylorSeer enabled, and TaylorSeer order 2. They also pass `--dit-cpu-offload false` so the transformer remains resident on the NPUs; allowing the automatic CPU-offload policy reduces peak device memory but adds transfer latency. Experimental NPU RoPE, SwiGLU, and gate kernels were disabled; they are not present in the final PR. signals.title: [AMD] Add Work-Centric (Lean) Attention: a persistent-CTA decode kernel for long-context serving
signals.text: ## Motivation The standard flash-decode ("SplitK") attention kernel parallelizes decode by splitting each sequence's KV cache into chunks and assigning chunks to GPU compute units (CUs). While effective at short context, it leaves performance on the table in two common serving regimes: - **Long-context, low-batch** — std's grid is `batch × head-tiles × num_splits` with a fixed split count, so a single (or few) long sequence cannot generate enough KV-split work to fill all CUs: many CUs sit idle while the few launched programs each grind through a long serial KV loop, and decode-step latency grows **roughly linearly** with context, making the workload occupancy-starved, not bandwidth-bound. As context windows reach 64K–128K+, attention dominates the decode step here. - **Ragged batches** — with mixed sequence lengths, SplitK cannot rebalance a long request's work onto the CUs freed by short requests, so a few stragglers set the step latency. **Work-Centric Attention (WCA / "Lean")** launches a fixed persistent grid sized to the device CU count and derives its KV-tile schedule on-device from `kv_indptr`, cooperatively splitting long sequences across CTAs (work-stealing) so no CU idles. Decode-attention latency stays **nearly flat** as context grows (1.06–1.30× E2E throughput even on uniform batches) and absorbs raggedness for free (up to 1.52× throughput, 3.62× lower ITL). Lean is numerically identical to the standard kernel and ships behind a conservative auto-gate that enables it only where it wins — including by default under CUDA graphs — so existing workloads are unaffected. Validated on **AMD MI355X (gfx950)** across GQA (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B) and MLA (DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4, TP=4, fp8 KV). Also re-validated on **AMD MI300X (gfx942)** at the same 1×CU grid across GQA (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B) and MLA (proxied with DeepSeek-V2-Lite, fp8 KV, since fp4/MXFP4 GEMM is gfx950-only). ## Modifications A minimal, mostly-additive change (6 files, ~+1540 lines) on the ROCm/Triton backend. Almost all of it is new code; the only edits to existing paths are the `forward_decode` dispatch hook and the `decode_attention_fwd` signature. The standard decode path is untouched when Lean is inactive. | File | Change | |------|--------| | `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/decode_attention.py` (+822) | The Lean kernel (`_lean_attention_decode_kernel`) and its launch/dispatch helpers. `decode_attention_fwd` gains an `enable_lean` parameter and early dispatch to Lean. Supports bf16/fp16 and **fp8** KV (fold `k_scale` into `sm_scale`, cast `q → K.dtype` for the fp8×fp8 MMA, dequantize rope-split `kpe`, apply `v_scale`), and both contiguous and **paged** KV (`kv_loc // page_size` / `% page_size` addressing). Auto-gate: `lean_decode_seqlen_gate` (eager) and `lean_capture_policy` (CUDA-graph capture). | | `test/registered/kernels/test_lean_attention.py` (+440) | CI gating test on the MI35x AMD per-commit suite (`stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`): parity vs standard SplitK for bf16 (cos > 0.999), fp8 (cos > 0.99), and paged KV (cos > 0.999), plus gate/policy logic. | | `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_backend.py` (+119) | Resolve `enable_lean_attention` in `forward_decode` (explicit override → auto-gate → kill-switch); allocate the Lean scratch buffers (Mp/Lp/Op/locks) for the eager and CUDA-graph paths. | | `benchmark/lean_kernel_sweep.py` (+150) | Kernel-level Lean-vs-standard (SplitK) sweep: both GQA head configs × full batch/context grid, per-call latency, speedup, cosine parity, and eager-gate decision; writes a CSV. | | `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py` (+4) | `--enable-lean-attention` flag (`Optional[bool]`, default `None` = auto-gate). | | `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` (+11) | Two env vars: `SGLANG_DISABLE_LEAN_ATTENTION` kill-switch (force the standard kernel) and `SGLANG_FORCE_LEAN_GRID_CU_MULT` (persistent-grid size multiplier, default `1.0` = one CTA per CU; a knob for grid A/B without a rebuild). | **Design:** - **Persistent grid.** Launches `total_programs = device CU count` CTAs — one CTA per CU (rounded to whole XCDs under the ROCm XCD remap). One CTA per CU maximizes the KV work-tiles handled per CTA, so each CTA's cross-CTA combine/atomic reduction amortizes more useful work; oversubscribing (e.g. 2 CTAs/CU) halves tiles-per-CTA and inflates that reduction, regressing high-batch decode (measured on MI300X/gfx942 and confirmed on MI355X/gfx950). The grid is independent of batch×heads×splits, so it is CUDA-graph capturable and a single captured grid replays across batch sizes. - **On-device work-stealing.** Each CTA computes its slice of the global KV-tile work list from `kv_indptr`; long sequences are cooperatively split across CTAs. The schedule is derived from `kv_indptr` **at replay**, so a captured graph adapts to the real per-step sequence lengths and raggedness — no host sync, no per-step relaunch. - **Auto-gate.** The default (`None`) resolves to a concrete decision before launch; explicit `True`/`False` overrides it. Because Lean is a win only in specific regimes, the gate operates in two modes: - *Eager decode*, where real `seq_lens` are known: `lean_decode_seqlen_gate` keys a length threshold on query-head parallelism (`tiles = ceil(num_q_heads / min(16, kv_group))`, i.e. how well the standard kernel already fills the CUs), relaxed as batch grows. - *CUDA-graph capture*, where per-step lengths are not yet known: `lean_capture_policy` makes the bake decision from capture-time-known signals (`batch`, `tiles`, `is_mla`) — bake GQA/MHA at `batch ≥ 16`, MLA at `batch ≥ 8`, and never for heavy TP shards (`tiles < 4`). Lean's fixed grid then adapts to the actual lengths at replay. - **Shape/dtype coverage.** MHA, GQA, and MLA (rope-split `qk_head_dim != v_head_dim`); bf16/fp16/fp8 KV; contiguous and paged KV. Falls back to the standard kernel for unimplemented features (logit capping, attention sinks, xAI temperature, score modification), so results are never silently wrong. **Usage:** - Default (`None`): auto-gate — Lean turns on automatically where it wins (including by default under CUDA graphs). No flag needed. - Force on: `--enable-lean-attention` (with `--attention-backend triton`). - Force off: `--enable-lean-attention=False`, or `SGLANG_DISABLE_LEAN_ATTENTION=1`. ## Accuracy Tests **Test configuration:** | | | |---|---| | **Hardware** | 1× AMD Instinct MI355X (256 CUs, gfx950, 288 GB HBM3E) | | **Software** | ROCm 7.2.0, PyTorch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.0, Triton 3.7.0 (AMD wheel) | | **Models (head shapes)** | Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (GQA 28Q/4KV, D=128) · Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (GQA 32Q/8KV, D=128) | | **Method** | Isolated decode-attention call; compare Lean vs standard SplitK output over three KV formats — bf16, fp8 (e4m3, per-tensor scales), and paged (4-D buffer, scattered slots) | | **Metric** | Cosine similarity of the two output tensors | **Command** (the registered CI gating test): ```bash python3 -m pytest test/registered/kernels/test_lean_attention.py -v # Per shape: standard = decode_attention_fwd(..., enable_lean=False) # lean = decode_attention_fwd(..., enable_lean=True, lean_Mp/Lp/Op/locks=...) # cos = F.cosine_similarity(o_lean.flatten().float(), o_std.flatten().float(), dim=0) ``` **Results.** Lean matches the standard kernel across every tested configuration: | KV format | Configs | Result | |-----------|:-------:|:-------| | bf16/fp16 | 59 cells (2 models × 6 batches × 5 contexts, less Llama b32×128K) | **cosine = 1.0000** (bit-identical) | | fp8 e4m3 (per-tensor scale) | 2 models × {b1,b8} × {8K,32K} | **cosine > 0.99** (fp8 quantization noise only) | | paged (4-D, scattered slots) | 2 models × page_size {16, 64} | **cosine > 0.999** | Every measured configuration is bit-identical in bf16 (the one unmeasured cell, Llama batch-32 × 128K, exceeds the microbenchmark's single contiguous KV tensor — it is a harness limit, not a kernel result). The committed CI gating test (`test_lean_attention.py`) reproduces the bf16, fp8, and paged parity checks on the MI35x per-commit suite. Because output is numerically equivalent, downstream generation quality is unchanged. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Unless noted otherwise, the tables below are on **1× MI355X** (gfx950); the dedicated **MI300X (gfx942)** subsection re-runs the same suites on that arch. Both: ROCm 7.2.0, PyTorch2.9.1+rocm7.2.0, **Triton 3.7.0** (AMD wheel; the production ROCm wheel — the stock rocm7.2 image's Triton 3.5.1 inverts the crossover and must not be used for Lean benchmarking). The **baseline is the Triton backend's own standard decode kernel, not AITER**: both arms use `--attention-backend triton` and dispatch through the same `decode_attention_fwd`, differing only in the `enable_lean` branch, so this is a clean Lean-vs-standard A/B. ### Kernel-level (isolated decode attention, speedup = standard ÷ lean) Direct kernel call, fp16, random Q/K/V, `page_size=1`; batch ∈ {1,2,4,8,16,32} × context ∈ {8K,16K,32K,64K,128K}. **Command:** `SGLANG_FORCE_LEAN_GRID_CU_MULT=1.0 python3 benchmark/lean_kernel_sweep.py` **Qwen2.5-7B (28Q/4KV):** | batch | 8K | 16K | 32K | 64K | 128K | |------:|---:|----:|----:|----:|-----:| | 1 | 0.46× | 0.92× | **1.86×** | **3.30×** | **5.33×** | | 8 | 0.59× | **1.04×** | **1.28×** | **1.59×** | **1.95×** | | 32 | **1.78×** | **1.99×** | **2.21×** | **1.74×** | **1.77×** | **Llama-3.1-8B (32Q/8KV):** | batch | 8K | 16K | 32K | 64K | 128K | |------:|---:|----:|----:|----:|-----:| | 1 | 0.79× | **1.47×** | **2.41×** | **3.56×** | **5.92×** | | 8 | **1.46×** | **1.82×** | **1.97×** | **2.18×** | **1.71×** | | 32 | **2.13×** | **2.29×** | **1.74×** | **1.73×** | — | **Bold** = Lean is faster at the kernel level (speedup ≥ 1×). Peak **5.33× (Qwen) / 5.92× (Llama)** at batch=1 / 128K; speedup grows superlinearly with context (SplitK's idle-CU penalty scales with length, Lean's stays flat) and the crossover falls with batch. The production auto-gate turns Lean on around the **end-to-end** break-even (later than the isolated-kernel crossover), so it enables the long-context / larger-batch cells and keeps the standard kernel for short-context low-batch. (The batch-32 × 128K Llama cell exceeds the microbenchmark's single contiguous KV tensor and is not measured; real serving uses a paged KV pool and is unaffected — see the E2E tables.) ### End-to-end serving — GQA Full-model serving, closed-loop / fixed-batch (`num-prompts == max-concurrency == reqs`, `--request-rate inf`), CUDA graphs on (`--cuda-graph-bs 1 2 4 8 16 32`), `--seed 42` (both arms see the identical batch). `--random-range-ratio r` samples per-request prompt **and** output lengths in `[r·ctx, ctx]`, so `ratio < 1` = ragged. Rows include batch 1 to show the low-batch long-context win and the auto-gate's enabled region (GQA `batch ≥ 16`); below b16 the standard kernel runs by default. Columns: **reqs** = concurrent requests; **KV mean / KV range** = mean and min–max prompt (KV) length across the batch; **dec/req** = mean decode (output) tokens per request; **dec iters** = total decode tokens measured; **tps×** = Lean ÷ baseline output throughput; **ITL× / p99×** = baseline ÷ Lean median / p99 inter-token latency (>1 = Lean faster). | model | B | ratio | reqs | KV mean | KV
