signals.title: [KV Cache] Use exact page demand for paged prefill eviction
signals.text: ## Motivation `alloc_paged_token_slots_extend()` currently estimates its eviction target as the total number of extend tokens plus one full page per request. This ignores free slots in each request's existing partial tail page and can evict reusable prefixes even when the pending allocation already fits. For example, with `page_size=64`, `prefix_len=63`, and `seq_len=64`, the allocator consumes no new page. The current estimate requests 65 tokens of capacity, while the exact requirement is zero. The allocator already uses `get_num_new_pages()` to validate the actual page consumption. This PR uses the same page accounting for the preceding tree-cache eviction decision. This is a narrow extraction of the exact extend-eviction portion previously included in #25500. It is also complementary to #33091: this PR fixes the requested allocation capacity, while #33091 changes when unified-memory eviction can stop after shared capacity becomes available. ## Modifications - Compute the exact number of new pages from the existing CPU prefix and sequence-length tensors before paged prefill eviction. - Convert that count to allocator capacity with `num_new_pages * page_size`. - Keep every allocator interface unchanged. Allocators continue to recompute their page count defensively before consuming pages. - Add CPU regression coverage for: - a page-boundary matrix over page sizes 16, 64, and 128; - a simulated `RadixCache` case that verifies a cached prefix survives a zero-new-page extend; - a mixed batch whose exact allocation requires only one new page and only evicts its capacity shortfall. This does not change paged decode accounting, scheduler admission budgeting, the eviction policy, or allocation kernels. ### Open design question The caller now computes the page count for eviction, while allocators recompute it defensively for allocation safety. On the local CPU benchmark below this costs about 9-10 us per paged extend call and avoids changing the allocator API, including out-of-tree implementations. Would maintainers prefer to keep this compatibility-first duplication, or standardize an optional precomputed page-count argument across every allocator? I intentionally did not add allocator capability flags in this draft. ## Accuracy Tests Target regression: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_paged_alloc_extend_eviction.py ``` ```text 3 passed, 15 subtests passed ``` The 15 page-boundary subtests cover page sizes 16, 64, and 128, with cases for reuse within a partial page, exact free capacity, one- and multi-page crossings, and a reused request with no new tokens. The `RadixCache` regression inserts a 64-token evictable prefix as an unrelated reusable victim before running the `prefix_len=63`, `seq_len=64` extend. It verifies that the cache size stays at 64, `free_segment()` is not called, and the full cached prefix still matches after allocation. Adjacent allocator regression: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_paged_alloc_extend_eviction.py \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_swa_alloc_extend_page_estimation.py \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_multi_ended_allocator.py \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hisparse_allocator.py \ -k 'not TestO3FusedAllocBind' ``` ```text 70 passed, 11 deselected, 15 subtests passed ``` `TestO3FusedAllocBind` was excluded locally because its unrelated Triton JIT tests require Python development headers that are not installed on the test host. The changed path is CPU-only and will also run in the registered `base-a-test-cpu` suite. The change does not alter model math or allocator output. The tests assert that the output is preserved and that no new keyword argument is forwarded to the allocator. ## Speed Tests and Profiling `get_num_new_pages()` was measured on an Intel Core Ultra 7 265K with PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, using 9 repeats of 1,000 calls (`page_size=64`): | Batch size | Median per call | | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 9.31 us | | 8 | 9.67 us | | 32 | 9.91 us | | 128 | 10.05 us | The deterministic regression cases show the eviction difference directly: | Case | Previous shortfall | Exact shortfall | | --- | ---: | ---: | | `prefix=63`, `seq=64`, no free capacity | 65 tokens | 0 tokens | | Mixed batch, 32 free tokens | 353 tokens | 32 tokens | No general throughput improvement is claimed. The expected benefit is retaining reusable prefixes under page-level cache pressure. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing API or configuration change.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31891562985](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31891562985)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31891562818](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31891562818)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Native SANA-WM stage-2 refiner stack
signals.text: ## Summary - replace the SANA-WM stage-2 Diffusers/HF runtime modules with native SGLang refiner, connector, and text-only Gemma-3 implementations - route nested refiner components through the unified component loaders and support layerwise offload for `transformer_2`, `text_encoder_2`, and `connectors` - remove duplicate batch/streaming Diffusers forward paths, preserve streaming KV behavior behind explicit model APIs, and document the native runtime/residency behavior ## Details - loads the released audiovisual LTX-2 checkpoint into a video-only 48-layer refiner while treating only the known audio/AV branches as intentionally unused - avoids materializing the unused 416M-parameter Gemma-3 vision tower - keeps Diffusers/Transformers checkpoint compatibility and the existing tokenizer path - fixes the packed/5D refiner output contract and keeps timestep scaling owned by the native model - removes the low-signal warning listing 2295 expected unused audio/AV checkpoint keys while preserving warnings for unknown keys ## Validation - `pre-commit run --files ...` - remote H100: `103 passed` for SANA-WM native/config tests and FSDP loader tests - released SANA-WM checkpoint, BF16 math SDPA: - Gemma-3: all 49 hidden states bitwise identical to HF on the runtime-valid 128-token path; signals.title: [Quantization] Fix GPTQ scheme attachment broken by LinearBase.scheme default
signals.text: ## Summary #29328 added a class-level `scheme = None` to `LinearBase`, which turned GPTQ's `if not hasattr(layer, "scheme")` guard into a no-op — the scheme never gets built and weight creation dies with `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'create_weights'`. Every GPTQ checkpoint fails to load; `test_gptqmodel_dynamic.py` is the only e2e test covering it. Probe becomes `layer.scheme is None`, per the repo's no-defensive-probe rule. That makes the default load-bearing, so it's declared on the other two bases a GPTQ method can be handed (`VocabParallelEmbedding` for a quantized `ParallelLMHead`, `FusedMoE` for gptq_marlin MoE), and `FusedMoE`'s two `hasattr` weight-loader reads flip with it — leaving those would set `method = None` for every unquantized and fp8 MoE layer on reload. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31894414468](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31894414468)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31894414374](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31894414374)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Fix dsv4 kl test timeout
signals.text: ## Motivation `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dsv4.py` is killed at 1200s on every scheduled run, most recently https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31849115802. The stage sets no `timeout_per_file`, so `run_suite.py` falls back to its flat 1200s default, which sits below the file's own registered `est_time` of 1500. It is the only registered CUDA test with an `est_time` above that default. Measured with no harness timeout on 4 GPUs and a warm cache: 16 tests pass in 2055s. `est_time` moves to 2400 as well because `compute_partitions.py` packs shards by it, so raising only the per-file timeout would trade the file timeout for a job timeout. Left alone: `--timeout-from-est-time` would have derived 3300s here, but it is gated on the `scheduled` input that `pr-test.yml` and `pr-test-extra.yml` never pass, and passing it would also flip `max-parallel` to 1 for every scheduled stage. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31895383698](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31895383698)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #31895383613](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31895383613)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(sgl-kernel): preload CUDA runtime before loading common ops
signals.text: ## Motivation `common_ops.so` resolves its shared-library dependencies while it is dynamically loaded. Preloading `libcudart` afterward cannot prevent an earlier `libcudart.so.*` resolution failure. ## Modifications Preload the CUDA runtime with `RTLD_GLOBAL` before loading the architecture-specific `common_ops` extension. ## Tests - `python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/kernels/aot/python/sgl_kernel/__init__.py` - `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` - `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/kernels/aot/python/sgl_kernel/__init__.py` - Manual smoke test on an NVIDIA A100 CUDA host: applied the same loader-order change to the installed `sgl_kernel` package under `site-packages` and successfully started SGLang. The original `libcudart.so.*` lookup failure was not reproducible on the test host. The change is based on the loader ordering: `common_ops.so` dependency resolution occurs before a subsequent CUDA runtime preload could run. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->pending<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->pending<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Support compressed-tensors NVFP4 Marlin with BF16 and DSpark
signals.text: ## Motivation Compressed-tensors NVFP4 checkpoints currently require the native SM100+ FP4 runner. On SM80-SM90 GPUs, the existing Marlin NVFP4 path is available for ModelOpt checkpoints but is not wired into the compressed-tensors scheme. BF16 models expose a second issue: small E4M3 block scales can underflow when Marlin encodes them through FP16 bit manipulation. In addition, compressed-tensors quantization is not attached to `ParallelLMHead`, and DSpark computes logits through the raw weight tensor, so a quantized `lm_head` is loaded or executed incorrectly. Together these issues prevent checkpoints such as `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` from running correctly with `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark` on RTX 4090/SM89. ## Modifications - Add a Marlin fallback for compressed-tensors W4A4 NVFP4 on SM80-SM90. - Convert compressed-tensors global scale divisors to Marlin multipliers. - Rescale tiny BF16 NVFP4 block scales by an exact power of two and compensate the global scale, following the approach in vLLM PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/34577. - Apply compressed-tensors quantization to `ParallelLMHead`. - Route DSpark logits through the quantized `lm_head` method and size folded-sampling buffers from the original output dtype. ## Accuracy Tests - `pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_gptq_marlin.py -k nvfp4_marlin_dense_matches_dequant_reference`: **2 passed** (FP16 and BF16). - Synthetic tiny-scale BF16 Marlin comparison: relative MAE `0.001704`, cosine similarity `0.999996`. - Real checkpoint NVFP4 MLP comparison: relative MAE `0.001906`, cosine similarity `0.999995`. - Real checkpoint FP8 linear-attention comparison: relative MAE `0.02650`, cosine similarity `0.999638`. - End-to-end smoke test with the checkpoints above: `6 * 7 -> 42`; two concurrent requests returned `42` and `81` correctly. ## Speed Tests and Profiling RTX 4090, BF16 activations, Marlin FP4 GEMM, FP8 target/draft KV cache, DSpark block size 7, CUDA graphs enabled: - 512 input / 256 output, concurrency 1: `82.30` output tok/s, mean TPOT `11.47 ms`. - 8192 input / 64 output, concurrency 1: `3229.87` input tok/s, mean TPOT `7.88 ms`. - 8192 input / 256 output live request: approximately `3330` prefill tok/s and `72` decode tok/s. The server starts with a 262144-token context and two running request slots on one 48 GB RTX 4090. Validation launch command: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --served-model-name unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8081 \ --tp-size 1 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --context-length 262144 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.88 \ --max-running-requests 2 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --fp4-gemm-backend marlin \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --image-processor-backend pil \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \ --enable-cache-report \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-draft-model-path RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 7 \ --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \ --speculative-draft-attention-backend flashinfer \ --speculative-draft-kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \ --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer ``` ## Checklist - [x] Formatted with pre-commit; all hooks for the touched files pass. - [x] Added and ran the relevant NVFP4 Marlin unit test. - [x] Documentation update is not required; this extends an existing backend selection. - [x] Included accuracy and speed results above. - [x] Followed the existing compressed-tensors and Marlin code paths without adding a new backend abstraction. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31896134248](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31896134248)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31896134111](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31896134111)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [MoE] Add FlashInfer SM90 MXFP4 W4A8 MoE
signals.text: ## Motivation SGLang currently supports FlashInfer's SM90 MXFP4 W4A16 CUTLASS MoE path, which was introduced in SGLang #24816 on top of FlashInfer [#3084](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3084). FlashInfer [#3738](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738) adds a different Hopper path that dynamically quantizes activations to FP8 and runs MXFP4-weight x FP8-activation MoE GEMMs using Humming-style pre-MMA E8M0 scale fusion. This PR wires that path into SGLang as an explicit opt-in: ```bash --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 ``` The existing `default` and `bf16` behavior is unchanged. Related work: - SGLang https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24816 - FlashInfer https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738 ### FlashInfer version requirement This integration intentionally targets the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431, where the FC1 and FC2 residual scales are FP32 tensors in local-expert order with shape `[num_local_experts]`. FlashInfer reuses its internal expert permutation to map those scales to routed rows, including global-to-local expert mapping under EP. The original #3738 ABI briefly shipped before being reverted from FlashInfer 0.6.17 by #4411. It required downstream runtimes to construct routed-row residual tensors during every forward. SGLang does not support that older ABI. The new option therefore requires both: - `flashinfer-python >= 0.6.18` - `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` SGLang currently pins FlashInfer 0.6.17. This PR does not change that global pin. With 0.6.17, selecting `fp8` fails immediately with an actionable error, while all existing FlashInfer paths remain compatible. The dependency, cubin, and JIT-cache pins should be upgraded together in a follow-up change. GPU validation for this PR used FlashInfer 0.6.18 built from commit `8044d94bf9acc5369857baf88d28906bb32bf264`, which contains the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431. ## Modifications ### Runtime selection and compatibility - Add `fp8` to `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision`. - Select the new path only for `flashinfer_mxfp4` on SM90. - Keep W4A16 as the default SM90 behavior. - Reject the SM90-specific `fp8` option on SM100 and SM120 to avoid confusing it with their existing MXFP8 activation paths. - Require the corrected FlashInfer 0.6.18+ API instead of accepting the older routed-row residual ABI. - Pass `use_wfp4afp8_humming=True` only when the new path is selected. The keyword is omitted completely for FlashInfer 0.6.17 compatibility. ### Weight preprocessing - Use `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` for both FC1 and FC2 during post-load processing. - Store the folded interleaved weight scales produced by FlashInfer. - Store `residual * 64` as one FP32 value per local expert for FC1 and FC2. - Preserve GPT-OSS gate/up layout conversion and its existing padding rules. - Fill synthetic E8M0 scale padding from an existing scale in the same expert, preventing padding from changing that expert's min/max exponent range. - Support both the GPT-OSS MXFP4 quantization path and the DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 expert path. ### Kernel invocation Construct the five Humming quant-scale slots expected by the corrected FlashInfer API: 1. FC1 folded weight block scales 2. FC1 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation 3. Reserved scalar FC2 activation scale 4. FC2 folded weight block scales 5. FC2 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation The existing TP/EP topology is forwarded to FlashInfer so it can map global expert IDs to the corresponding local residual scale. ### Tests and benchmark - Extend the registered SM90 MXFP4 test suite with: - GPT-OSS preprocessing checks against the FlashInfer helper - five-scale kernel invocation and direct FlashInfer comparison - aligned and non-aligned hidden/intermediate dimensions - padding invariance for per-expert residual scales - EP rank with global expert IDs - DeepSeek-V4 preprocessing - fail-fast behavior on FlashInfer versions before 0.6.18 - Extend the manual SM90 benchmark to compare: - SGLang Marlin W4A16 - FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A16 - FlashInfer Humming W4A8 - Update the server-argument documentation. ## Accuracy Tests GPU correctness and end-to-end smoke testing completed in the following environment: | Component | Version / configuration | | --- | --- | | GPU | 4 x NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), TP=4 | | NVIDIA driver | 590.48.01 | | CUDA toolchain | CUDA 13.0, NVCC 13.0.88 | | Host compiler | GCC 13.3.1 | | PyTorch | 2.13.0+cu130 | | FlashInfer | 0.6.18 (`8044d94bf9acc5369857baf88d28906bb32bf264`) | | sglang-kernel | 0.4.6.post1 | | Model | `/home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` | The registered SM90 MXFP4 suite passed: ```bash python -m pytest \ test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp4_sm90_cutlass.py -v ``` ```text 18 passed, 1 skipped ``` The DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 checkpoint was launched with: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 4 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 \ --enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` All 43 MoE layers completed the FlashInfer SM90 CUTLASS W4A8 weight preprocessing path. SGLang Custom AllReduce remained enabled during startup and inference. The server passed both health and generation checks: ```text GET /health -> HTTP 200 POST /generate -> HTTP 200 Prompt: "The capital of France is" Output: " Paris..." Completion tokens: 16 End-to-end latency: 0.251 s ``` No CUDA error, runtime error, or traceback was observed during model loading, CUDA graph capture, or the generation request. Broader accuracy evaluation and GPT-OSS end-to-end coverage are still required before enabling this path by default. ## Speed Tests and Profiling FlashInfer #3738 reports broad fused-MoE kernel gains on H200, while results on H20 depend more heavily on token count and topology. Those upstream numbers are not sufficient to establish SGLang end-to-end gains. The updated downstream benchmark can be run on H100/H200 with FlashInfer 0.6.18+: ```bash FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \ python test/manual/layers/moe/bench_mxfp4_sm90_kernels.py ``` Results should be collected for decode and prefill token counts and reported as W4A16/W4A8 latency and speedup. End-to-end serving throughput and latency should also be measured before changing the default precision. | GPU | Model shape | Token range | W4A16 | Humming W4A8 | Speedup | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | H100/H200 | GPT-OSS-like | 4-8192 | TODO | TODO | TODO | | H100/H200 | DeepSeek-V4 | decode/prefill | TODO | TODO | TODO | ## Scope and Limitations - The implementation is SM90-only. - It is opt-in and does not change the default W4A16 path. - It targets the corrected per-local-expert API from FlashInfer #4431. - The current `flashinfer_mxfp4` runner is registered for the standard/no-A2A dispatcher. This PR does not add Humming support to DeepEP dispatchers. - A coordinated FlashInfer 0.6.18 dependency update and broader H100/H200 and GPT-OSS validation are required before production enablement. ## Checklist - [ ] Format the code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the repository test conventions. - [x] Update server-argument documentation. - [x] Run the registered tests on an SM90 GPU with FlashInfer 0.6.18. - [x] Add a DeepSeek-V4 end-to-end smoke-test result. - [ ] Add broader accuracy results for GPT-OSS and DeepSeek-V4. - [ ] Add downstream kernel and end-to-end performance results. - [ ] Upgrade the FlashInfer Python, cubin, and JIT-cache pins together in a coordinated follow-up change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31897611111](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31897611111)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31897749451](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31897749451)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD][DI][CI] 9/N Add Qwen3.5-397B-A17B MXFP4 1P1D DI/CI recipes (base + MTP + DP8/EP8) — conflict resolved
signals.text:
## Motivation Conflict-resolved rebasing of #33919, which went `CONFLICTING` / `DIRTY` against `main`. The original PR is authored by @Lzy17 on a fork branch (`Lzy17:qwen35-recipes`); its commits are preserved here verbatim, with one added merge commit that resolves the conflict. Content and intent are unchanged from #33919 — see that PR for the motivation and the MI355X validation numbers. ### What conflicted Exactly one file: `scripts/ci/slurm/nightly-configs.yaml`. Both sides appended new MI355X entries at the end of the file: - `main` gained the GLM-5.2 wide-EP16 2P1D pair (`glm52-fp4-mi355x-ep16-sglang`, `glm52-fp4-mi355x-ep16-mtp-sglang`) from #34476, which landed after this branch's merge base. - This branch appends the four Qwen3.5 entries (`qwen35-fp4-mi355x-{,mtp-,dp8ep8-,dp8ep8-mtp-}sglang`). Git could not pick a side because the two additions overlap at the same end-of-file anchor. There is no semantic disagreement between them. ## Modifications Resolved as a pure union, GLM-5.2 EP16 first (preserving `main`'s ordering), then the Qwen3.5 block. No other file conflicted: `main` touched only `nightly-configs.yaml` and the two new `glm52/1k1k/2p1d-ep16*.yaml` recipes under `scripts/ci/slurm/` since the merge base, and did not touch `launch_mi355x.sh`. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — CI recipe configuration only, no runtime or model code. The accuracy numbers backing the four recipes are in #33919 (GSM8K `run_eval` on MI355X 2-node 1P1D: 0.976 / 0.973 / 0.971 / 0.973). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. ### Verification of the resolution The resolution was checked mechanically rather than by eye: - **Union is exact.** `diff(resolved, PR-head version)` is precisely `main`'s 32 added lines, and `diff(resolved, main version)` is precisely the PR's 64 added lines — neither side lost or gained anything else. - **Nothing else drifted.** `git diff main HEAD` is the same 6 files / +376 / -5 that GitHub reports for #33919. - **Generated CI matrix is the union.** `generate_matrix.py --runner mi355x` yields 38 entries: 34 from `main` plus the 4 new `qwen35-fp4-1k1k-1p1d*` entries, equivalently 36 from the PR plus the 2 new `glm52-fp4-1k1k-2p1d-ep16*` entries. Nothing lost from either side, and no duplicate matrix names. - **Workflow grouping still succeeds.** `nightly-amd-mi355x-disagg.yml` hard-fails its `setup` job on any entry that matches neither the `-1p1d` (2-node) nor `-2p1d-ep16` (4-node) group. Simulating that step over the merged config leaves zero unmatched entries: 26 in `matrix-2n` (including the four Qwen3.5 recipes) and 12 in `matrix-4n` (including the two new GLM-5.2 EP16 recipes). - **The new launcher knob is inert for existing recipes.** Running the launcher's recipe parser over all 22 `mi355x-fp4` recipes shows every pre-existing one — including `main`'s new `glm52/1k1k/2p1d-ep16*.yaml`, which this branch never saw — resolving to the `few_shot` / 512 defaults, so their behavior is byte-identical. signals.title: [Diffusion] Add native GLM-Image AR encoder
signals.text: ## Summary - replace the in-process Transformers GLM-Image AR model with SGLang-owned vision, VQ, and text decoder modules - expose text and vision blocks to component layerwise offload while preserving component CPU offload and the external SRT path - route single-token CUDA decode through SDPA, keep the configured backend for prefill and vision, and update the public AR documentation ## Why The default in-process GLM-Image path instantiated Transformers' full weighted model. This prevented the diffusion runtime from managing every AR layer consistently and from applying native attention and layerwise offload across the full component. FlashAttention also has higher dispatch overhead than SDPA for the single-token decode shape. The native model therefore uses SDPA for CUDA decode while retaining the configured attention backend for prefill and vision workloads. The causal SDPA adjustment is identical to #34951 and is included so this PR can be tested independently. It becomes an empty overlap after that change lands. ## Validation - pre-commit - 66 focused GLM-Image, multi-output, and disaggregation tests - real `zai-org/GLM-Image` checkpoint parity: sampled weights, all 40 text layers, prefill and decode logits, vision features, VQ tokens, and greedy generation were exact - loader and layerwise smoke with 40 text layers and 40 vision blocks - H100 median: 256-token prefill 20.63 to 20.14 ms; 576-token vision 10.37 to 8.73 ms; 32-token generation 617.79 to 591.37 ms <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31900486307](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31900486307)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #31900493342](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31900493342)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] DSv4: fuse the qk-norm-rope pair on the MTP target-verify path
signals.text: ## Summary On the DeepSeek-V4 unified-KV path, the fused qk-norm-rope kernel is wired to decode only. MTP **target-verify** falls back to running the same work as two separate launches per layer — `sglang::fused_q_norm_rope` for q and `sglang::fused_norm_rope` for kv — which is 122 launches per verify step across the 61 target layers. This PR routes target-verify through the same fused kernel, **with the cache store left off**. The store half deliberately does not move. Decode is a 1-source consumer: the ring holds everything, so writing it before attention is required. Target-verify is **2-source** — attention reads history from the ring and takes the current chunk as `k`/`v` so the draft tokens stay causally masked against one another. Writing the current chunk into the ring ahead of attention makes those tokens indistinguishable from history, and every draft position then attends to all of them regardless of order. Fusing the store as well drops GSM8K from 0.950 to 0.027 while looking like a ~7% throughput win, because it skips exactly the work correctness depends on. Only the norm+RoPE half is sound, and that is what this PR fuses. ## Modifications - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`** (`MQALayer._forward_prepare`) - `do_fused_store` now also admits `is_target_verify()` when the new gate is on. The kernel is token-indexed (`q`, `kv` and `positions` are all length M), so a verify batch carrying several draft tokens per request is a shape it already handles. - On that path the kernel is called with `swa_cache`/`swa_loc` left as `None`, so it performs q-norm+RoPE and kv-norm+RoPE and stores nothing. `get_unified_swa_loc` is not called at all — it exists solely to address a store this path no longer performs. - `kv` is returned instead of being set to `None`, so the caller's existing contract drives the rest unchanged: `attn_k = kv` gives attention the real current-chunk source, and `save_kv_cache = kv is not None` makes the backend write the ring after attention, exactly as the unfused path did. - `kv` is materialised with `.contiguous()` first: it is a strided slice of `qkv_a`, and the ring store requires a contiguous buffer. The unfused path pays the identical copy inside `_compute_kv_bf16`, so this is parity, not added overhead. - **`python/sglang/srt/environ.py`** — new `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY` (default on). Set to 0 to fall back to the unfused chain on the verify path. Decode, prefill and the non-unified paths are untouched. ### Kernel-level evidence Per target-verify forward, from graphs-off traces segmented by the 61 `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` frames (TP8, 8k/1k, conc 16, rank 0). `fused_q_norm_rope` and `fused_norm_rope` both go to zero and one `_fused_qk_norm_rope_store_kernel` replaces them; no other kernel is added. | layer type | launches/fwd (base → patched) | GPU us/fwd excl. collective | |---|---|---| | CSA (30 layers) | 1920.0 → 1800.0 | 15779 → 15488 (−1.8%) | | HCA (31 layers) | 1526.8 → 1410.5 | 12385 → 12014 (−3.0%) | "excl. collective" is the number to read: `cross_device_reduce` blocks until the slowest rank arrives, so its duration tracks inter-rank skew rather than work this change moves. ## Accuracy Model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`, MI355X (gfx950), TP8. GSM8K, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy. | run | accuracy | invalid | |---|---|---| | baseline (gate 0) | 0.950 | 0.000 | | patched (gate 1) | 0.949 | 0.000 | | patched (gate 1, repeat) | 0.945 | 0.000 | Note this is measured **without** `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`. The throughput harness pins acceptance to the golden AL, which fabricates which draft tokens are accepted — fine for speed, but it would bypass the accept/reject path this change touches. Acceptance here is whatever the draft model earns. ```bash export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton export SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1 export SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1 export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=high # flip this between 0 (baseline) and 1 (patched) export SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 31710 --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --page-size 256 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --max-running-requests 32 --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --backend srt --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 31710 \ --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 \ --max-new-tokens 1024 --temperature 0.0 --parallel 32 ``` ## Performance Same model and hardware. 8k input / 1k output, TP8, steady state (10 waves through a `--max-concurrency` gate). Each cell is the mean of 2 repeats run in `off, on, on, off` order per concurrency, so a monotonic drift over the block shifts both arms equally instead of being credited to the patch. Repeated all-gates-off runs on this node put the noise floor at 0.25% (1σ). | concurrency | output tok/s (base → patched) | uplift | mean TPOT ms | accept len | |---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 332.43 → 341.07 | **+2.60%** | 11.37 → 11.06 | 2.499 → 2.498 | | 8 | 543.73 → 555.57 | **+2.18%** | 13.75 → 13.46 | 2.499 → 2.469 | | 16 | 839.00 → 857.32 | **+2.18%** | 17.98 → 17.57 | 2.499 → 2.507 | | 32 | 1167.14 → 1186.66 | **+1.67%** | 25.79 → 25.34 | 2.482 → 2.508 | Acceptance length is flat across arms, so the uplift is kernel time and not a shift in speculation behaviour. ```bash # same server launch as above, with SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY # flipped 0/1 between arms, plus the throughput harness env: export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=2.49 export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token # CONC in {4, 8, 16, 32}; --max-running-requests/--cuda-graph-max-bs = 2*CONC # capped at 32 on both arms (this image cannot capture a decode graph at bs 48). CONC=16 python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31710 --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 0.8 --num-prompts $((CONC * 10)) \ --max-concurrency $CONC ``` `bench_serving` ignores EOS by default here (it only offers `--disable-ignore-eos`), so every request runs to exactly 1024 output tokens and neither arm can win by generating less. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31901655398](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31901655398)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31901655847](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31901655847)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(unified-cache): allow multiple concurrent load-back pins per node
signals.text: ## Motivation Under heavy device-eviction↔load-back cycling (small-VRAM GPUs with `--enable-hierarchical-cache`, hybrid GDN/mamba models), the scheduler crashes with: ``` AssertionError: node 2498 pinned by load-back 2563, new anchor 2498 ``` at `UnifiedTreeCore.commit_load_back` (`unified_tree_core.py`). Hit repeatedly serving `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` + EAGLE + hicache ratio-12 on RTX 5090 (32GB) under a production-trace replay; 96GB GPUs never trip it (no deep evicted chains → no overlap). ## Root cause `UnifiedTreeNode.load_back_pending_id` is single-valued, but two live load-backs can legitimately pin the same node: 1. Request A load-backs anchored at a **descendant**; its Full-KV chain covers the evicted **ancestor** and pins it (`load_back_pending_id = A`). 2. Before A's ack, request B anchors **at that ancestor** to restore its **independently-evicted mamba state** (`mamba_component.build_hicache_transfers` pins `[node.id]`). 3. The single pin slot can't represent both live pins → assertion (`new anchor` == the node itself, matching the production message shape exactly). The overlap is semantically safe: both in-flight DMAs only **read** the shared host slots, and their writes target disjoint destinations (Full-KV pool vs mamba pool). Only the bookkeeping cannot represent it. ## Modifications - `load_back_pending_id: Optional[int]` → `load_back_pending_ids: set[int]`. - `commit_load_back` adds the anchor id (idempotent for a node sitting in both the Full and an aux transfer list of one anchor). - `finish_load_back` discards its anchor id along the root path; duplicate tracking updates once the last pin drains. - Reclaim guards (`_is_settled_full_host_duplicate`, `_can_reclaim_full_host_duplicate`) and the sanity check test set-emptiness; split inheritance copies the set. ## Test / repro `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_loadback_multipin.py` — a deterministic CPU repro built on the existing `UnifiedRadixCacheSuite` fixtures (FULL+MAMBA): backup → full evict → load-back anchored at the leaf (ack withheld) → load-back anchored at the pinned ancestor. - **Unpatched**: fails in 0.3s with the exact production assertion. - **Patched**: passes; pins drain to empty after both acks; `sanity_check` clean. - Full inherited FULL+MAMBA suite under the new class: 107 tests green. - Serving-level: the patched server sustains 400-span production-trace replays at hicache ratio-12 on RTX 5090 with zero assertions (previously crashed mid-run). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings as needed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31902335393](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31902335393)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31902335225](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31902335225)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Expose selected worker ID in SMG responses
signals.text: ## Why is this change needed? Clients can provide a stable `x-smg-routing-key`, but today they cannot verify which backend worker served each response. This makes it difficult to diagnose whether multi-request agent sessions actually preserve worker affinity. The HTTP regular router now returns an opaque, deterministic `x-smg-worker-id` derived from the selected worker URL (including its data-parallel rank, when present). The identifier is added to both streaming and non-streaming responses after worker selection, including the final response after gateway retries, without exposing the worker IP or URL. For example, two requests routed to the same worker can now be correlated directly from their response headers: ```text request 1 -> x-smg-worker-id: 0f3a...c912 request 2 -> x-smg-worker-id: 0f3a...c912 ``` ## Test Plan - `cargo fmt --check` - `cargo test --lib test_insert_worker_id_is_stable_and_opaque` - `cargo test --test routing_tests test_worker_id_is_stable_for_streaming_and_non_streaming_responses` The integration test verifies that both streaming and non-streaming chat-completion responses expose the same worker ID when routed to the same backend. -Robot <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31902512993](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31902512993)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31902512922](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31902512922)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Fail MiniMax-H3 quality="high" closed on substituted DiT weights
signals.text: ## Motivation Closes #34954. `validate_quality_deployment` pins sixteen server args and the device, but none of them observes which DiT weights are resident, so `quality: "high"` keeps its audited SSIM/PSNR promise attached to weights it was never measured on. Two CLI args substitute those weights: - `--lora-path` — on the audited 4×H200 deployment, with the cookbook's own Turbo-LoRA recipe merged, `quality: "high"` completes at the audited shape in 42.98 s against the 43.28 s the same tier takes on base weights. The LoRA recipes section says that combination "has not been quality-validated". Repro in #34954. - `--transformer-weights-path` — `quantization: None` does not cover this. That field carries only the explicit `--quantization` override, whose help states the method is otherwise auto-detected from the checkpoint, and nothing writes the detected method back onto `server_args`. `resolve_transformer_safetensors_to_load` substitutes the entire transformer weight set whenever the path is set; when no quant config resolves, `TransformerLoader` warns and proceeds. ## Modifications Add both args to the `actual`/`expected` pair, following the existing one-line-per-field shape, so the gate fails closed on a substituted DiT. Extend `_quality_server_args()` and add a parametrized test per arg. This affects only `quality: "high"`. `MiniMaxH3PartitionAdmissionStage.forward` calls the validator under `if high_quality and not batch.is_warmup`, so lossless serving with a LoRA and the warmup path are unchanged. The docs warning names distilled adapters, while `lora_path: None` also rejects style adapters like the Realism-People LoRA that keep the 50-step schedule. That is deliberate. The audited figure was measured on base weights and the Cache-DiT policy keys on residual drift, so any merged adapter moves what was measured, and the server cannot tell the two kinds apart from the path. Allowing non-distilled adapters would want an explicit allowlist rather than an unchecked field. `model_path` is deliberately out of scope. It has no single expected value the way the other fields do: the cookbook gives a root model ID per hub (`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3` on Hugging Face, `MiniMax/MiniMax-H3` on ModelScope), and a repo ID on its own does not fix the content without a pinned revision. Base-model identity needs that revision pin or a weight digest, which is a separate decision. `component_transformer_weights_paths` is left alone as well: it has no CLI flag and I did not find an H3 path that populates it. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — admission-time validation only; no model output or kernel path changes. `test_minimax_h3_admission.py` passes 16/16 with this change. Reverting only the config change and keeping the new test fails exactly the two new parametrizations (`DID NOT RAISE ValueError`) with the other 14 still passing, so the test covers the gap rather than restating the fix. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A — one dict comparison per `quality: "high"` batch admission. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). Docs are left out on purpose: the cookbook wording that this now enforces sits in the same `.mdx` that #34841 and #34909 are both editing. Happy to follow up separately once those land. --- This touches the same function as #34841, which moves the topology fields into per-profile updates. Both fields here are topology-independent and stay in the shared literal, so the two changes are disjoint; happy to rebase whichever merges second. I don't have permission to add the `run-ci` label, so `pr-gate` will be red until someone applies it — grateful if a maintainer can. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31905631519](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31905631519)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31905631412](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31905631412)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Delegate shared-read-ends declarations in wrapper attention backends
signals.text: Follow-up to #34916. Three things: name the read-end concept after what it is, make wrapper backends answer for the child that actually reads, and cut the fence tests down to what they guard. ### `SharedReadBoundary` -> `SharedReadEnds` The values now say where they sit relative to the two init hooks, instead of leaving the reader to infer it: ```python PRE_REPLAY = auto() # After the init_forward_metadata_out_graph IN_REPLAY = auto() # After the init_forward_metadata_in_graph POST_REPLAY = auto() # Metadata snapshot not implemented UNKNOWN = auto() # not audited -> coarse whole-forward fence ``` `POST_REPLAY` is worth calling out: it is not a design state, it marks a backend whose metadata snapshot is incomplete. Naming it that way is what makes the remaining users of it auditable. Also `shared_read_boundary()` -> `shared_read_ends()`, `_resolve_shared_read_boundary` -> `_resolve_shared_read_ends`, and the local in the resolver -> `declared` (the backend's declaration, as distinct from the resolved point the function returns). ### Wrapper backends now delegate the declaration A wrapper drives one or more child backends but inherited the base declaration and answered for itself. Fixed for all four, via a new `SharedReadEnds.max_of` (the record must cover every child, so the latest end wins): | wrapper | | |---|---| | `HybridAttnBackend` | delegates to `_select_backend(mode)` | | `TboAttnBackend` | max over primary + children | | `HybridLinearAttnBackend` | max over `attn_backend_list` | | `MiniMaxHybridAttnBackend` | max over sparse + dense | This is a real fence bug wherever a wrapped child overrides the default. Concretely, `TboAttnBackend` wrapping `DeepseekV4AttnBackend`: the child declares `POST_REPLAY` for non-DSPARK target verify, the wrapper reported `IN_REPLAY`, so the scheduler was released while the child was still reading across graph segments. Behavior is otherwise unchanged -- children that inherit the default all report `IN_REPLAY`, so the aggregate matches what the wrapper returned before. ### Fence tests: 136 -> 80 lines Dropped the `execute()` harness (fake backend, `ShapeKey`, `PPProxyTensors`, `load_batch`, `device_module`) and the three cases built on it -- ~60 lines guarding six lines of `if` wiring. What is left tests the two methods directly: a five-row table over the resolver, and both branches of `_publish_read_done`. The backend stub is now `create_autospec(AttentionBackend, instance=True)` rather than a `SimpleNamespace`. A hand-rolled stub supplies whatever name the caller asks for, so a renamed method leaves a stale call site in the runner green in CI and broken at runtime; spec'd against the real ABC it fails in the test. Not covered anymore: that the pre-replay record lands before `backend.replay()`. That ordering assertion was the only thing needing the full harness. ### Not in this PR - The default stays `IN_REPLAY`. Moving a backend to `PRE_REPLAY` is a per-backend optimization worth one audit each, not a global flip. - `_resolve_shared_read_ends` still answers two questions (does this phase own the publish, and where do the reads end). Splitting the ownership predicate out is the next step. - The `IN_REPLAY -> PRE_REPLAY` fallback demotes to a point earlier than the declared end; `POST_REPLAY` is the sound direction. Left as a TODO in code -- it is only reachable under `--debug-cuda-graph` and on platforms without external-event support, where the barrier is off anyway. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31915127758](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31915127758)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31915127678](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31915127678)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Refactor: Deprecate Prefill CP V1
signals.text: ## Motivation Prefill context parallelism still carried both the v1 and v2 implementations behind `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2`. This duplicated server-argument compatibility handling, coupled model implementations to CP internals, and left legacy paths in attention backends and DSA. This PR makes the current v2 implementation the only prefill CP implementation and removes the version distinction. It is intentionally stacked on `clean-dsv4`. ## Modifications - Remove `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2` and the legacy CP server-argument aliases and compatibility rewrites. - Delete the legacy `python/sglang/srt/layers/utils/cp_utils.py` implementation. - Remove prefill CP branches from model files, including DeepSeek and Qwen MoE implementations, so modeling code no longer owns CP data movement. - Remove CP v1 branches from CUDA, NPU, and MUSA attention backends and delete stale DSA v1 helpers. - Rename versioned APIs and fields, for example `is_cp_v2_active` to `is_cp_active`. - Delete v1-only and old parity tests while retaining the canonical CP test coverage. - Handle DSA CP warmup batches without speculative metadata and add regression coverage for that case. - Update documentation and examples to use `--enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy ...`. ## Accuracy Tests Passed: - `test/registered/cp/test_cp_strategy_unit.py`: 26/26 tests. - `test/registered/cp/test_dsa_prefill_cp.py`: 1/1 test on H200; GSM8K score 0.946. - `test/registered/cp/test_gpt_oss_4gpu_mxfp4_cp.py`: 1/1 test on B200; GPQA score 0.6566 (threshold 0.58). - Two compatible configurations in `test_gqa_prefill_cp.py`: GSM8K score 0.98 each. Environment-blocked configurations: - GQA CP4: FA3 architecture restriction on B200; the H100 retry was blocked during backend initialization. - DeepSeek V3: JIT CUDA `silu_and_mul_masked_post_quant` / NVSHMEM initialization failure before CP evaluation. - DeepSeek V4: the B200 image lacked `aiter` for two configurations; the final configuration timed out during weight validation/prewarm before serving requests. Additional validation: - Full changed-file pre-commit suite. - Python `compileall` for `python/sglang/srt` and `test/registered/cp`. - Registered-test registry validation. - Diff whitespace validation and scans confirming removal of the legacy flag, aliases, and versioned CP API names. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not run. This is a legacy-path removal and API cleanup; no performance claim is made. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with pre-commit. - [x] Add/update unit tests. - [x] Update documentation. - [x] Provide available accuracy results and document environment-blocked runs. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [AMD] Make the Kimi-K3 MI35x nightly accuracy-only, and fix the lint blocker
signals.text:
Targets `amd/mi355x-kimi-k3-nightly`, the branch behind #32568. Merging this leaves that PR as accuracy only and lint-clean. The perf sweep moves to a follow-up, which adds it as a step inside the accuracy job rather than as a separate gated job. ## Why **The lint failure is one word, and it is what makes the whole PR red.** codespell flags `unparseable ==> unparsable` in `test_kimi_k3_eval_mi35x.py:15`. `.github/actions/check-pr-test-health` fast-fails every PR-test job as soon as the `lint` check is red, so that single word aborted all 21 `base-b-*` jobs in ~10 s each without any of them running a test. Roughly 30 of #32568's failing checks are cascade noise from it. `unparsable` is the spelling used everywhere else in the tree, so the word is fixed rather than allow-listed in `.codespellrc`. **The perf job has never been green.** It was dispatched exactly once, in run [31853704954](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31853704954), and died in `setUpClass` after 23 s: ``` AttributeError: 'NightlyBenchmarkRunner' object has no attribute 'setup_profile_directory'. Did you mean: 'setup_result_directory'? Ran 0 tests in 0.001s ``` Not a typo — the test was written against the pre-#33832 `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` API. #33832 ("[CI] Remove profiling from nightly tests") renamed `profile_dir` → `result_dir`, `setup_profile_directory()` → `setup_result_directory()`, `generate_profile_filename()` → `generate_result_filename()` and deleted the `enable_profile` kwarg. The K3 perf test still used the old three, so there was a second `TypeError` on `enable_profile=False` waiting behind the first failure. `Ran 0 tests` means the sweep body has never executed and this test has never produced a throughput number. The accuracy job in that same run passed, so nothing about accuracy depends on any of this. ## What changes - `test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_kimi_k3_eval_mi35x.py` — `unparseable` → `unparsable`. - Removes `test/registered/amd/perf/mi35x/test_kimi_k3_perf_mi35x.py`. - Removes the `nightly-perf-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3` suite from `test/run_suite.py`. - Removes the `nightly-perf-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3-rocm720` job from `nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`, plus its `job_select` option and `check-all-jobs` entry. The accuracy job, its suite registration, and the Kimi-K2.6 retirement are untouched. ## Accuracy is already validated twice | | Head `61a52a9`, standard image | Earlier, pinned image | | --- | --- | --- | | Run | [31853704954](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31853704954) | [30386408970](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30386408970) | | GSM8K accuracy | **0.956** (threshold 0.92) | **0.956** | | Unparsable | 0.1% | 0.2% | | Eval latency | 270.8 s | 276 s | | Output throughput | 497.9 tok/s | 488 tok/s | | Job wall time | ~62 min | ~74 min | Plus [31849574590](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31849574590) on `d35e7ed`, which is what retires the image pin: the standard `rocm720-mi35x` nightly image imports `kimi_k3` and the server launches. ## Test plan - [x] `codespell --config .codespellrc` clean repo-wide (was 1 error, now 0) - [x] `black --check` and `isort --check-only` clean on touched files - [x] Workflow YAML parses; every `job_select` option, every `needs:` target and every `check-all-jobs` entry names a real job. `job_select` options go 47 → 46 and `check-all-jobs` 46 → 45, exactly the perf job. (`nightly-test-1-gpu-kernel-rocm720` is absent from `check-all-jobs` both before and after, and on `main` too — pre-existing, untouched here.) - [x] No dangling `nightly-perf-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3` or `test_kimi_k3_perf` references anywhere in the tree - [x] The K3 accuracy suite is still registered and still wired into `job_select` and `check-all-jobs` ## Not addressed here `test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen35_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py` has the identical stale-API breakage on `main` today — `runner.setup_profile_directory()` at line 146 and `enable_profile=False` at line 162, both left behind by #33832. Its `test_b_perf` will hit the same `AttributeError`, and it is CI-registered as `nightly-amd-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen35-mxfp4`. That is a separate pre-existing bug against `main`, so it is deliberately out of scope; happy to send a one-line fix for it separately.

signals.title: [AMD] Add the Kimi-K3 MI35x perf sweep inside the accuracy job
signals.text:
Follow-up to #32568 that adds the Kimi-K3 perf sweep as a step inside the existing accuracy job, rather than as a separate gated job. Based on `amd/mi355x-kimi-k3-nightly` so the diff is purely the perf delta on top of #32568. Retarget to `main` once #32568 lands. ## Why inside the accuracy job This is not a new pattern — it is the dominant one in `nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`. Twenty jobs there already pair an "Accuracy Test" step with a "Performance Test" step in the same job (Grok1-INT4, Grok2, DeepSeek-V3.1/V3.2/V3.2-MTP, Qwen3.5, GLM-5.1, GLM-5-MXFP4, MiniMax-M2.7, …). Only four perf steps invoke a test file directly; twenty-two go through `run_suite.py`, which is what this does. For K3 specifically the shared job is strictly better than a separate one: - **The checkpoint is already cached.** The 1.56 TB MXFP4 weights dominate wall time — the eval job runs ~62 min, of which the sweep itself is a small tail. A separate job pays the download and load a second time from cold. - **One 8-GPU MI35x slot instead of two.** That runner is contended enough that a redundant slot costs real wall time for everyone else in the queue. - **Step ordering is the accuracy gate, for free.** The eval step ends with `exit ${TEST_EXIT_CODE:-0}`, so a failed eval fails the job and the perf step never runs. That is the same guarantee a separate job would buy with `needs:`. - **It avoids the wart `needs:` brings.** With a separate gated job, perf cannot be dispatched on its own: selecting only the perf job skips accuracy, which skips perf. Sharing the job means there is nothing to document. `continue-on-error: true` on the perf step follows the same sibling jobs. `check-all-jobs` gates on the job, so without it a flaky sweep would turn a green accuracy result red. ## The test needed fixing, not just moving An earlier revision of this test lived in #32568 and had never run a single line of its benchmark body. Its one dispatch, in run [31853704954](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31853704954), died in `setUpClass` after 23 s with `Ran 0 tests in 0.001s`. It was written against the pre-#33832 `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` API — #33832 ("[CI] Remove profiling from nightly tests") renamed the profile API to result and deleted the profiling kwarg. Three fixes: | Before | After | Why | | --- | --- | --- | | `setup_profile_directory()` | `setup_result_directory()` | The method #33832 renamed. This is the `AttributeError` that killed the run. | | `PROFILE_DIR = "performance_profiles_kimi_k3_mi35x"` | `RESULT_DIR = "performance_results_kimi_k3_mi35x"` | Matches all fifteen sibling MI35x perf tests, and the directory holds the `results_*.json` that `scripts/ci/utils/save_metrics.py` collects. | | `enable_profile=False` | removed | #33832 removed this kwarg from `run_benchmark_for_model`; it has no `**kwargs`, so this was a `TypeError` waiting directly behind the first failure. | That second latent failure is why this is worth more than a one-line rename: fixing only the `AttributeError` would have burned another MI35x hour to surface the `TypeError`. ## Test plan Verified with a harness that loads the real `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` with only its torch-backed leaf imports stubbed, so the class under test is the one from the tree: - [x] `setUpClass()` runs to completion and creates `performance_results_kimi_k3_mi35x` - [x] Every `runner.*` attribute the test touches exists on `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` - [x] The `run_benchmark_for_model(...)` call binds against the real signature - [x] **The same harness fails on the pre-fix file**, reproducing the CI error verbatim (`AttributeError: ... has no attribute 'setup_profile_directory'`) plus the latent `got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_profile'` — so these checks are load-bearing, not vacuous - [x] Workflow YAML parses; job count, `job_select` options and `check-all-jobs` entries are all unchanged from the base, confirming no new job was introduced - [x] The K3 job's steps are, in order, `Accuracy Test …` then `Performance Test …`, running `nightly-amd-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3` then `nightly-perf-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3` - [x] `codespell --config .codespellrc` clean repo-wide; `black --check` and `isort --check-only` clean Not yet verified on hardware: the sweep has still never produced a throughput number, so this needs one MI35x dispatch of `job_select=nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3-rocm720` before merge. Reference numbers to compare against are in #32548 — 102.5 tok/s/GPU at concurrency 2 rising to 612.3 at 32, non-speculative — and the eval's own decode logs on the green accuracy run showed ~619 tok/s aggregate at batch 11. ## Note on a neighbouring bug `test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen35_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py` on `main` has the identical stale-API breakage that #33832 left behind — `runner.setup_profile_directory()` at line 146 and `enable_profile=False` at line 162 — so its `test_b_perf` will hit the same `AttributeError`. It is CI-registered as `nightly-amd-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen35-mxfp4`. Left out of scope here since it is a pre-existing bug against `main`; happy to send it separately.

signals.title: [diffusion] feat: support MiniMax-H3 text encoder FP8 quantization
signals.text: ## Summary - add text-encoder-specific quantization controls without changing the DiT `--quantization` contract - auto-detect serialized text-encoder quantization metadata and run native post-load weight processing - opt MiniMax-H3's native Qwen3-VL language stack into FP8 while keeping embeddings, normalization, and the vision tower in BF16 - document online and serialized FP8 recipes, including startup-memory behavior and the strict `quality="high"` exclusion ## Why MiniMax-H3 uses a large Qwen3-VL prompt encoder. The native linear layers already support SGLang quantization methods, but the encoder loader did not resolve checkpoint quantization metadata, pass the quantization config into the model, or run post-load processing. Reusing the transformer flag would also couple prompt conditioning precision to DiT precision. This change introduces an explicit text-encoder boundary and keeps unsupported native encoders fail-closed. ## Validation - H100 online FP8 load and real prompt encoding - H100 serialized `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct-FP8` load through the normal `sglang serve` download path - complete 5-second 1344×768 T2VA requests with online and serialized FP8 plus layerwise offload - serialized FP8 TP1/TP2 load and forward comparison - focused unit tests and changed-files pre-commit checks <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31921261879](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921261879)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31921261716](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921261716)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [multimodal] Bound tokenizer-side GPU memory in Kimi GPU image preprocessing
signals.text: ## Motivation `_gpu_preprocess_images` (shared by Kimi K2.5 and K3) keeps every image's fp32 patch tensor live in `all_patches` and finishes with a request-wide `torch.cat`, so peak tokenizer-side GPU memory is **≥ 2× the request's total patch bytes** — unbounded in image count and resolution. The allocations land on `base_gpu_id`, the same device the TP0 scheduler sizes itself against `--mem-fraction-static`, and the caching allocator retains the peak permanently. On a production K3 deployment (TP8, mem-fraction 0.915) this converged every warm replica to ~1.3 GiB free on GPU 0; a ~15-image request (2.36 GiB of patches) then OOMed **every time** — surfaced as sustained per-request 500s on 2026-08-15 while `/health` stayed 200, so load balancing never ejected the replica. Scheduler-side ~1.3 GiB prefill workspace allocations on GPU 0 also began failing once the ratchet saturated. ## Modifications Three coupled pieces, all in the multimodal processor layer (scheduler, ViT, transport wire format, and the CPU path untouched): 1. **`_gpu_preprocess_images`** processes size-groups in sub-batches capped at `SGLANG_MM_GPU_PREPROCESS_CHUNK_BYTES` (new env, default 512 MB) of fp32 pixels, emits per-image contiguous tensors instead of a request-wide concat, and hands each image to an optional `per_image_sink` as it is produced. Per-image entries are `.clone()`d out of sub-batch views so no entry pins sub-batch storage. 2. **`MMFeatureStreamSink`** (wired into the K2.5 and K3 processors via a `sglang_feature_sink` kwarg): per image — `hash_feature` → `_wrap_tensor_for_cuda_ipc` into the bounded IPC pool (pool-full falls back to `.cpu()`, exactly like the per-item wrap it replaces; non-IPC transports go straight to host) → the GPU copy is dropped before the next image. Peak = one sub-batch + one image, independent of request shape. 3. **`get_new_expanded_mm_items`** splits list-shaped bundled features by element (grid boundaries still shape model-specific data) and preserves the production-time hashes via `PRECOMPUTED_FEATURE_HASHES_KEY` instead of re-hashing an already-wrapped feature. `mimo_v2` has its own copy of the accumulate-and-concat pattern; happy to port it in a follow-up once this shape is agreed on. ## Accuracy Tests Model inputs are **bit-exact**: `test_parity_mixed_size_groups`, `test_parity_single_group_chunked`, and `test_parity_k3_rgba_compositing` assert `torch.equal` between the new per-image outputs and the legacy request-wide pipeline across size-groups, forced chunking, and the K3 RGBA compositing hook. Radix-cache keys are unchanged: `test_stream_sink_hashes_match_legacy_split` asserts the production-time hashes equal `hash_feature` of the legacy post-split slices (same bytes, same algorithm). ## Speed Tests and Profiling `test_peak_memory_bounded_vs_legacy` (H100): 8×1344px single-group request — legacy peak ≥ 2× total patch bytes; bounded peak ≤ 4× chunk bytes and >4× below legacy. Latency: per-image resize/normalize kernels are unchanged; chunking only splits one batched launch into ceil(group_bytes / 512 MB) launches, and per-image hashing replaces the identical post-split hashing — happy to attach preprocessing latency numbers if desired. ## Tests to run - `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_kimi_mm_preprocess_bounded.py` (new; `register_cuda_ci`, stage `base-b`, `1-gpu-small`) — 8 tests, all passing on H100 - `test/registered/unit/managers/test_mm_utils_split.py` (extended with `TestPerItemFeatureListSplit`; `base-a-test-cpu`) — 12 tests, all passing - Neighboring regression: `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_kimi_k3_gpu_preprocess.py`, `test_cuda_ipc_transport.py`, `test_base_processor_image_decode.py` — all passing against this branch ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31921674513](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921674513)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31921674461](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921674461)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Implement distributed batch weight updates in both engine and server
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. --> ## Motivation <!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. --> In the current version, updating weights using `update_weights_from_distributed` requires sending a separate HTTP request for each parameter update, even though each request only contains minimal information (name, dtype, shape). By allowing multiple parameters to be updated in a single HTTP request (as a list of parameters), the communication overhead would be reduced, enhancing performance, especially when updating many or all parameters simultaneously. Closes #3646 ## Modifications <!-- Describe the changes made in this PR. --> - **New Batch Parameter Update Functionality** - Added `BatchUpdateWeightsFromDistributedReqInput` class in `io_struct.py` to represent batch parameter updates. - Implemented `batch_update_weights_from_distributed` methods in: - `Engine` class (`engine.py`) - `TokenizerManager` class (`tokenizer_manager.py`) - **New HTTP Endpoint** - Introduced `/batch_update_weights_from_distributed` endpoint in `http_server.py` to expose batch updates via API. - **Testing Enhancements** - Updated tests (`test_update_weights_from_distributed.py`) to randomly execute either batch or individual parameter updates, ensuring comprehensive test coverage. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [ ] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci). - [ ] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/accuracy_evaluation.html). - [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [ ] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR.

signal.title: [AMD] [GLM5] Add opt-in PTPC FP8 projections on gfx950
signal.text: ## Motivation The GLM-5.2 MXFP4 checkpoint keeps four attention projections in BF16: - fused `q_a + kv_a` - `q_b_proj` - `o_proj` This PR adds an opt-in FP8 path for those projections on gfx950. PTPC means per-token activation scaling and per-channel weight scaling. BF16 remains the default and fallback path. ## Modifications - Cache bpreshuffled FP8 projection weights while retaining the original BF16 parameters. - Use one flag, `SGLANG_DSA_FP8_PROJ_GEMM`, to switch all four projections between BF16 and PTPC FP8. - Reuse fused quantized inputs for `q_b_proj` and `o_proj` where available. - Keep fused `q_a + kv_a` on tuned Aiter BF16 for M≤512; use PTPC FP8 for M>512. - Limit the path to GLM-5.2 on gfx950 with Aiter enabled. ## Accuracy Tests GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4 MI355X: | Validation | Result | | --- | ---: | | PTPC GSM8K, 1319 examples | 0.933 | ## Speed Benchmarks GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4 MI355X, 8k input / 1k output.
