signal.title: [AMD] Add Kimi-K3 8-GPU MI35x nightly accuracy CI
signal.text: ## Motivation The [Kimi-K3 cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Moonshotai/Kimi-K3) publishes an `MI350X/MI355X 1×8` deployment cell — one of only two single-node topologies for K3, alongside `B300 1×8`. The AMD Day-0 tracking issue (#32548) reports throughput for that recipe on MI355 TP8, up to 612 tok/s/GPU non-speculative. What neither provides is **accuracy**. The cookbook cell is still `verified: false` with no `benchmarks` entry, #32548 measures speed only, and there is no end-to-end K3 accuracy nightly on any backend — every existing K3 test is a unit or kernel test. So the ROCm path is known to run, and to run fast; nothing tells us it emits *correct* tokens. ## Result Verified on hardware, `linux-mi35x-gpu-8`, run [30386408970](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30386408970): | Metric | Value | | --- | --- | | GSM8K accuracy | **0.956** (threshold 0.92) | | Unparseable | 0.2% | | Eval latency | 276 s | | Output throughput | 488 tok/s | | Job wall time | ~74 min | ## Changes - **`test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_kimi_k3_eval_mi35x.py`** — GSM8K few-shot accuracy at TP8, threshold `0.92` (matching the K2/K2.5/K2.6 AMD family). Server args track the non-speculative recipe from #32548, so a green run is evidence for that exact published recipe: - `--attention-backend triton`, `--dtype bfloat16`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.85`, `--disable-radix-cache` - `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1 AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1 AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1` - **`test/registered/amd/perf/mi35x/test_kimi_k3_perf_mi35x.py`** — TP8 batch-size sweep (`[1, 8, 16, 64]`) on the *same* recipe as the accuracy test, so a perf regression cannot be confused with a config difference. Reference numbers to compare against are in #32548: 102.5 tok/s/GPU at concurrency 2 rising to 612.3 at 32. - **`test/run_suite.py`** — register `nightly-amd-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3` and `nightly-perf-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3` in `NIGHTLY_SUITES[AMD]`. - **`.github/workflows/nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`** — new `nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3-rocm720` and `nightly-perf-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3-rocm720` jobs, plus their `job_select` options and `check-all-jobs` entries. - **Retires the four Kimi-K2.6 accuracy jobs** across both AMD nightly lanes — `nightly-8-gpu-kimi-k26` and `nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k26` in `nightly-test-amd.yml`, and their `-rocm720` counterparts. See below. ## Decisions worth reviewing **ROCm 7.2 lane only for K3.** K3's native MXFP4 weights need `gfx95x` and `mxfp4` does not register on `gfx942`, so MI300/MI325 is out and no K3 job is added to `nightly-test-amd.yml`. That file is still touched here, but only to retire the K2.6 jobs. **Completion harness, not the chat API.** K3 has thinking permanently enabled and routes its answer through `reasoning_content`. On the chat path `message.content` comes back empty and the eval scores 0 — the same failure mode `run_eval.py` already documents for Qwen3.5. The measured 0.2% unparseable rate confirms scoring raw completions works. This also matches every sibling Kimi MI35x test. **No image pin.** An earlier revision pinned `--custom-image lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:rocm720-mi35x-k3-20260727`, because the generic nightly image then shipped an AITER without `aiter.ops.triton.conv.conv2d`, which made `sglang.srt.models.kimi_k3` fail to import so the architecture never registered and the server could not launch. That is fixed: the standard `rocm720-mi35x` nightly image now carries the module and imports `kimi_k3`, `kimi_k3_vl` and the K3 processor cleanly (verified on the `20260809`, `20260810` and `20260814` builds). The pin is dropped for `--rocm-version rocm720`, which is the right basis for a nightly — the `k3-*` image line stopped at `20260803` once K3 landed on main, so pinning that dated tag would only rot. **Perf gated on accuracy.** The perf job carries `needs: nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3-rocm720`, so it is skipped whenever accuracy fails or is skipped. Measuring throughput on a checkpoint that spends most of an hour loading is not worth an 8-GPU MI35x slot until the kernels are known to emit correct tokens, and that runner is contended enough that a wasted slot costs real wall time. One consequence worth knowing: perf cannot be dispatched alone, since selecting only it skips accuracy and therefore skips perf. Use `job_filter` with both names comma-separated — `job_select` is single-choice. This is noted in a comment above the job. **Retiring the K2.6 jobs.** K3 supersedes K2.6 on this hardware and the two would otherwise contend for the same scarce MI35x and MI325 runners. Only the scheduled jobs and their `job_select` / `check-all-jobs` entries are removed; `test_kimi_k26_eval_amd.py` and `test_kimi_k26_eval_mi35x.py` stay in tree and remain runnable via `run_suite.py`, which mirrors the state the K2.6 *perf* tests were already in. Say the word if you would rather keep one lane on K2.6 for continuity and I will restore it. **Concurrency capped at 64.** `--max-running-requests 64` with `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` matched. This is the one deviation from the published recipe: the eval submits all 1319 questions at once where the perf runs used bounded concurrency, and capturing decode graphs above the concurrency ceiling only burns capture time across K3's 93 attention + 92 MoE layers. ## Test plan - [x] Workflow YAML parses; job present, `runs-on: linux-mi35x-gpu-8`, wired into `job_select` and `check-all-jobs` - [x] `run_suite.py --hw amd --suite nightly-amd-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3 --nightly` discovers exactly this test at `est_time=9000` - [x] `run_suite.py` resolves `nightly-perf-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3` to exactly the new perf test; both workflows parse, no dangling `kimi-k26` references, and every `needs:` / `job_select` target maps to a real job - [x] Server args parse through `prepare_server_args` (`disable_radix_cache=True`, `cuda_graph_max_bs_decode=64`, `mamba_full_memory_ratio=0.9`) - [x] `black` clean - [x] **Hardware run green: 0.956 GSM8K** — [30386408970](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30386408970) (produced on the pinned image) - [ ] **Confirming run on the un-pinned standard image: [31849574590](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31849574590)** — in progress, started 23:24Z. `Setup docker (ROCm 7.2)` and `Install dependencies` are green and the eval is already well past the 52s mark where the pre-fix run died, so the model is importing and loading weights. This is the run that validates the revision actually being merged. `--max-running-requests`, `GSM8K_NUM_QUESTIONS`, `GSM8K_MAX_NEW_TOKENS` and `KIMI_K3_MODEL_PATH` are env-tunable so the first runs can be adjusted without a code change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31922097505](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31922097505)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31922097442](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31922097442)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] [GLM5] Enable dense-MHA short-context prefill fallback on gfx950
signal.text: ## Motivation On gfx950 (MI355X), GLM-5.2 DSA prefill always ran the triton sparse-MLA path, even at short context where the sparse indexer top-k + gather + mask overhead exceeds the KV it prunes. The dense-MHA prefill fallback — already used on NVIDIA SM90/SM100 and gated by `SGLANG_DSA_PREFILL_DENSE_ATTN_KV_LEN_THRESHOLD` (default = model `index_topk`) — was hard-gated to NVIDIA and never taken on ROCm, despite the dense kernel (aiter `flash_attn_varlen_func`) already being available. ## Modifications - Add gfx950 detection (`gcnArchName`) and include it in the `use_mha` prefill device gate in `dsa_backend.py` (previously `device_sm == 90 or 100 <= device_sm < 110`, NVIDIA only). - Guard `_forward_standard_mha` so ROCm routes through aiter `flash_attn_varlen_func`, never the flashinfer/trtllm (Blackwell) path. - NVIDIA behavior unchanged. On gfx950 the dense path triggers only when `max_kv_len <= SGLANG_DSA_PREFILL_DENSE_ATTN_KV_LEN_THRESHOLD` (GLM-5.2: index_topk = 2048); longer context stays on sparse-MLA. Off switch: set the threshold to 0. ## Accuracy Tests GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X TP4, GSM8K (200 questions): dense fallback = 0.955. ## Speed Benchmarks GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X TP4, graphs-on, random 1024/1024, `sglang.bench_serving`, median. A. Baseline (dense fallback off)*: | concurrency | TTFT (ms) | ITL (ms) | E2EL (ms) | output tok/s | |---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 277.3 | 11.33 | 11860 | 342.0 | | 8 | 467.6 | 12.98 | 13790 | 592.7 | | 16 | 872.9 | 16.48 | 17767 | 915.8 | | 32 | 1371.1 | 20.25 | 22655 | 1443.9 | | 64 | 1920.5 | 26.05 | 30112 | 2174.0 | B. Dense fallback on (Δ vs baseline): | concurrency | TTFT (ms) | Δ | ITL (ms) | Δ | E2EL (ms) | Δ | output tok/s | Δ | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 196.9 | −29.0% | 11.31 | −0.2% | 11775 | −0.7% | 346.9 | +1.4% | | 8 | 366.8 | −21.6% | 13.00 | +0.2% | 13660 | −0.9% | 582.1 | −1.8% | | 16 | 526.6 | −39.7% | 16.46 | −0.1% | 17432| −1.9% | 935.0 | +2.1% | | 32 | 783.2 | −42.9% | 20.48 | +1.1% | 21895| −3.4% | 1498.13 | +3.8% | | 64 | 1125.6 | −41.4% | 26.10 | +0.2% | 29352 | −2.5% | 2227.3 | +2.5% | Aside from the consistent TTFT decreases (−22% to −43%), the ITL, E2EL, and output throughput deltas are within run-to-run noise (dense fallback is prefill-only, so decode is unaffected). *Baseline and Feature both measured with #30519, #30715 and aiter tuned MoE configs for GLM5.2; we expect those will be merged first and aiter version updated in recent images. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [ ] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Diffusion] Unify component residency controls
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang-Diffusion currently exposes overlapping CPU-offload and layerwise-offload flags with different scopes. In particular, an explicit `--dit-layerwise-offload false` can still inherit automatic DiT component offload, even though callers use that spelling to request a resident DiT. The DiT/VAE booleans also implicitly control model-specific helper components, making placement difficult to reason about as pipelines add dynamic modules. ## Modifications - Add `--component-residency COMPONENT=MODE` with `resident`, `component-offload`, and `layerwise-offload`. Exact component keys override the `dit`, `text_encoder`, `image_encoder`, `vae`, and `all` groups. Omitted components retain their legacy or model defaults. - Map those mode names directly to runtime strategy classes; there is no duplicate policy/mode enum beside the strategy implementation. - Keep all legacy controls supported: `--dit-cpu-offload`, `--text-encoder-cpu-offload`, `--image-encoder-cpu-offload`, `--vae-cpu-offload`, `--cpu-offload-components`, and the existing layerwise flags. Legacy and canonical controls may be mixed; a canonical selector overrides only the components it matches. - Fix explicit `--dit-layerwise-offload false` to keep the DiT resident unless another explicit DiT offload control is selected. - Route loaders, stage lifecycle management, dynamic components, Diffusers pipeline-wide placement, quantization overrides, FSDP validation, disaggregation argument copies, and CI helpers through the resolved strategy. - Prepare and release single-component stages through the shared executor lifecycle. Multi-component stages declare their actual component-use intervals, and replacing or deleting a dynamic module clears stale active/cache/prefetch state. - Require explicitly selected components to implement layerwise offload. Explicit unsupported or FSDP-managed selections fail clearly; automatic selection warns and retains the component's previous placement instead of silently changing its mode. - Keep DiT/VAE groups limited to actual denoisers/VAEs. Model-specific helpers such as connectors, sound tokenizers, upsamplers, and vocoders remain independently addressable by exact component key. - Add focused coverage for precedence, every legacy flag, mixed controls, dynamic components, lifecycle behavior, strict layerwise validation, FSDP/quantization/LTX constraints, CPU platform behavior, disaggregation reconstruction, and Diffusers effective placement. - Update the multimodal-gen README and public SGLang-Diffusion CLI/deployment documentation. Deprecated `docs/diffusion` remains untouched. ## Accuracy Tests No model math, weights, scheduler behavior, or output contracts are intentionally changed. Existing diffusion CI exercises model execution and consistency paths. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No optimization claim. The selector chooses the existing resident, component-offload, or layerwise-offload execution behavior. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #31921994130](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921994130)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31921994040](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921994040)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [KDA] Route Kimi-Linear through native Cake kernels
signal.text: Depends on #34299 for the checkpoint-capable KDA serving surface and on FlashInfer [#4535](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4535) for the native `lower_bound=None` kernels. The incremental commits after #34299's head will narrow automatically when the dependency lands. ## Summary - Auto-select BF16 recurrent state and native Cake prefill/decode for TP-local H32/D128 Kimi-Linear-48B. - Read prefill selection from the runner-scoped linear-attention dispatcher, preserving current server configuration ownership after the upstream backend refactor. - Feed packed projection Q/K/V, raw gate, and beta views directly to FlashInfer without `contiguous()` staging or state gather/scatter copies. - Preserve the native prefill route under breakable CUDA Graph padding by slicing only the live token prefix as storage-sharing row views; unpadded calls preserve exact tensor identity. - Keep admission fail-closed and emit structured per-layer route telemetry proving eligibility, native success, zero fallback/fatal outcomes, graph phase, and static zero-copy ownership. ## Validation - B200 and B300 each pass 80 focused unit tests, nine GPU decode integration tests, and four GPU prefill integration tests, including bounded rows, native H32 unbounded checkpoints, packed rows, graph padding, and exact-identity inputs. - The exact-stack FlashInfer matrix passes 93 source/API/JIT contracts, three unbounded prefill GPU rows, and 20 decode/export tests on both architectures. - The final source passes current Black, Ruff, isort, Python compilation, and the repository lint workflow. ## Kimi-Linear-48B serving The reference arm uses SGLang's Flash Linear Attention-derived `TritonKDAKernel` (FLA Triton). The single post-optimization B200 audit used 32 workload-shaped warmup requests followed by 64 measured requests at nominal 2,048 input / 256 output tokens, concurrency 32, seed 20260814, and cache flush for both arms. Cake/FLA-Triton completed 64/64 requests at 13,540.86/12,621.88 token/s. Median TTFT was 188.191/374.956 ms, mean TTFT was 279.591/500.729 ms, median TPOT was 15.564/14.999 ms, and mean TPOT was 15.188/14.123 ms. Peak device memory was 153,769/157,287 MiB. Cake/FLA-Triton scored 0.890/0.905 on the same 200-example five-shot GSM8K evaluation with temperature zero, 512 maximum tokens, 128 request threads, and explicit stop token 163586; both strictly exceed the declared 0.88 gate. Route telemetry recorded 2,560 prefill and 23,840 decode successes with zero FLA-Triton fallback, zero fatal outcomes, and zero copied inputs. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31921885032](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921885032)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31921885044](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921885044)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [VLM] Cache Kimi-K3 per-image processor artifacts
signal.text: ## Summary Stacked on #34398. - adds a model-independent per-media artifact coordinator for strict identity, option-aware keys, trusted/untrusted hashes, partial hits, batching, single-flight, cancellation, flush generations, and CPU-only retention - reduces Kimi-K3 to a typed adapter: the wrapped processor owns one `KimiK3PreprocessConfig`, K3 implements only miss materialization and per-turn prompt composition - removes the K3 private-field fingerprint block and moves fingerprint discovery into the common processor contract - preserves arbitrary per-media preprocessing options through normal/EPD dispatch; unknown future options conservatively change the artifact key instead of risking a false hit - replaces K3 checks in the new EPD loading path with typed model capability resolvers; the new cache path does not probe optional fields with `getattr` - keeps CUDA IPC/VMM proxies request-local; the preprocess cache adds no fixed HBM allocation ## Extension contract A new model supplies: 1. a typed artifact implementing `content_digest`, `artifact_key`, full `feature_identity`, compact `feature_hash`, `has_feature`, and `cache_value()` 2. its modality and artifact-producing processor fingerprint 3. `prepare_artifact_batch(misses)` 4. per-turn request/prompt composition The shared coordinator owns identity validation, source snapshots, partial-hit ordering, duplicate/concurrent miss coalescing, and lifecycle. Image snapshot/decode is provided by default; video/audio models override those two modality hooks without copying the cache algorithm. ## Correctness coverage - content identity comes from actual media bytes/snapshots, never path, URL, mtime, or object address - processor fingerprint and every non-envelope per-media option are namespaced into the artifact key - unknown future model options cause safe misses - adapter outputs cannot change the validated content digest or artifact key, and feature hashes must be non-negative integers - compatible cache lookup plus reservation is atomic, including metadata-only versus feature-required entries - trusted hot hit skips media reads; untrusted caller hashes are verified - mutable path contents miss by actual bytes - same artifact composes distinct prompts and offsets per turn - multi-image partial hits and deduplicated misses preserve order - feature-hash drift for one artifact identity is rejected - EPD content identity and per-media options remain aligned through dispatch and are verified before decode - non-image adapters are covered through overridable identity/decode hooks K3 embedding/prefix identity remains `hash(artifact_key, processor_output_hash)`; a raw content hash never replaces the existing processor-output hash. ## Validation - changed-file pre-commit suite: pass - Python compile check for all changed modules/tests: pass - generic contract tests added for future options, video hook extension, partial/duplicate hits, trusted reads, adapter identity validation, and atomic compatible reservation - previous final stacked Linux suite on both GB300 nodes: 170 passed + 5 subtests per node - previous normal-serving K3 cold/hot, changed-media, and two-image partial-hit checks: pass on 2-node GB300 with full real weights - previous 32-conversation x 8-turn run preserved input/output lengths with zero request errors; end-to-end performance is reported in #34411, where scheduler leases make artifact reuse fully effective ## Stack 1. #34398 — identity, API, bounded LRU/single-flight infrastructure 2. this PR — generic per-media artifact contract plus K3 ordinary/EPD adapter 3. #34411 — scheduler leases, early EPD reuse, metrics, documentation, and benchmark <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #31921817146](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921817146)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #31921817020](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921817020)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [multimodal] Bound tokenizer-side GPU memory in Kimi GPU image preprocessing
signal.text: ## Motivation `_gpu_preprocess_images` (shared by Kimi K2.5 and K3) keeps every image's fp32 patch tensor live in `all_patches` and finishes with a request-wide `torch.cat`, so peak tokenizer-side GPU memory is **≥ 2× the request's total patch bytes** — unbounded in image count and resolution. The allocations land on `base_gpu_id`, the same device the TP0 scheduler sizes itself against `--mem-fraction-static`, and the caching allocator retains the peak permanently. On a production K3 deployment (TP8, mem-fraction 0.915) this converged every warm replica to ~1.3 GiB free on GPU 0; a ~15-image request (2.36 GiB of patches) then OOMed **every time** — surfaced as sustained per-request 500s on 2026-08-15 while `/health` stayed 200, so load balancing never ejected the replica. Scheduler-side ~1.3 GiB prefill workspace allocations on GPU 0 also began failing once the ratchet saturated. ## Modifications Three coupled pieces, all in the multimodal processor layer (scheduler, ViT, transport wire format, and the CPU path untouched): 1. **`_gpu_preprocess_images`** processes size-groups in sub-batches capped at `SGLANG_MM_GPU_PREPROCESS_CHUNK_BYTES` (new env, default 512 MB) of fp32 pixels, emits per-image contiguous tensors instead of a request-wide concat, and hands each image to an optional `per_image_sink` as it is produced. Per-image entries are `.clone()`d out of sub-batch views so no entry pins sub-batch storage. 2. **`MMFeatureStreamSink`** (wired into the K2.5 and K3 processors via a `sglang_feature_sink` kwarg): per image — `hash_feature` → `_wrap_tensor_for_cuda_ipc` into the bounded IPC pool (pool-full falls back to `.cpu()`, exactly like the per-item wrap it replaces; non-IPC transports go straight to host) → the GPU copy is dropped before the next image. Peak = one sub-batch + one image, independent of request shape. 3. **`get_new_expanded_mm_items`** splits list-shaped bundled features by element (grid boundaries still shape model-specific data) and preserves the production-time hashes via `PRECOMPUTED_FEATURE_HASHES_KEY` instead of re-hashing an already-wrapped feature. `mimo_v2` has its own copy of the accumulate-and-concat pattern; happy to port it in a follow-up once this shape is agreed on. ## Accuracy Tests Model inputs are **bit-exact**: `test_parity_mixed_size_groups`, `test_parity_single_group_chunked`, and `test_parity_k3_rgba_compositing` assert `torch.equal` between the new per-image outputs and the legacy request-wide pipeline across size-groups, forced chunking, and the K3 RGBA compositing hook. Radix-cache keys are unchanged: `test_stream_sink_hashes_match_legacy_split` asserts the production-time hashes equal `hash_feature` of the legacy post-split slices (same bytes, same algorithm). ## Speed Tests and Profiling `test_peak_memory_bounded_vs_legacy` (H100): 8×1344px single-group request — legacy peak ≥ 2× total patch bytes; bounded peak ≤ 4× chunk bytes and >4× below legacy. Latency: per-image resize/normalize kernels are unchanged; chunking only splits one batched launch into ceil(group_bytes / 512 MB) launches, and per-image hashing replaces the identical post-split hashing — happy to attach preprocessing latency numbers if desired. ## Tests to run - `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_kimi_mm_preprocess_bounded.py` (new; `register_cuda_ci`, stage `base-b`, `1-gpu-small`) — 8 tests, all passing on H100 - `test/registered/unit/managers/test_mm_utils_split.py` (extended with `TestPerItemFeatureListSplit`; `base-a-test-cpu`) — 12 tests, all passing - Neighboring regression: `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_kimi_k3_gpu_preprocess.py`, `test_cuda_ipc_transport.py`, `test_base_processor_image_decode.py` — all passing against this branch ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31921674513](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921674513)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31921674461](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921674461)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Apple Silicon] [MLX] Fuse MoE combine multiply-reduce into one Metal kernel
signal.text: <!-- PR body rewritten to .github/pull_request_template.md, fetched fresh from sgl-project/sglang main and followed verbatim (Motivation / Modifications / Accuracy Tests / Speed Tests and Profiling / Checklist / Review and Merge Process). Current head numbers only. Figures this run confirmed on hardware are marked [hardware verified, this run]; figures carried over from the original author's server level benchmark and not remeasured end to end are marked [author reported, not reverified end to end]; figures carried over from the prior founder review without a rerun this session are marked [prior review, not rerun this session]. --> ## Motivation The reference MoE combine, `(y * scores[..., None]).sum(axis=-2)`, runs a broadcast multiply and a reduction with a transient materialized between them. Fusing both into one Metal kernel saves a full read of `y`, the transient round trip, and one dispatch per MoE layer. This PR began as the kernel plus its verification suite. Review exposed a real coverage bug in the eligibility guard (rank 3 assumption against a rank 4 production call site), which the fix generalized. The performance question required measured serving numbers, which required an integration path. The abstraction ask captured the JIT declaration pattern this kernel now shares with `fused_swiglu.py`. A founder-level review of the abstraction and its test suite followed; this revision applies that review's fixes. ## Modifications **Guard generalization and bf16 scores** - SGLang never flattens batch and sequence upstream, so every real combine call site is rank 4 `y` with rank 3 `scores` (prefill `[1, L, 4, 2048]`, batched decode `[R, 1, 4, 2048]`). The original rank 3 guard would have fallen back on every real forward pass; caught in review. Both target models run bf16 activations, and the original `_SCORES_DTYPES` rejected bf16 scores. - The contract is now `scores.shape == y.shape[:-1]` with rank at least 3. Leading dims flatten into the kernel's row dimension before dispatch and the output reshapes back. bf16 scores are accepted. **Default off integration** - `SGLANG_MLX_FUSE_MOE_COMBINE = EnvBool(False)` in `environ.py`, plus `patch_moe_combine_with_fused`, a subclass swap on `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock` and `Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock`, gated in `_load_model` beside the existing SwiGLU patch. Per call eligibility stays inside `fused_combine`, which falls back inline, so patching never changes results. Merging changes nothing for any user; the flag flip is a separate, evidence backed decision. **`metal_jit` abstraction** - `hardware_backend/mlx/metal_jit.py`: kernel files declare source once via the `@metal_jit.kernel(...)` decorator on a `MetalJitOp` subclass. The base class owns a `can_fuse` to `dispatch_fused` or `dispatch_fallback` template with typed `NotFusable` routing. Compile failures degrade via a memoized guard mirroring `jit_kernel/moe_fused_gate.py`'s `can_use_moe_fused_gate` pattern (catch, log once, memoize, fall back) instead of crashing the forward pass. - `MetalJitKernel` still owns the per dtype key compile cache and warm dedupe underneath, unchanged in behavior. - Both kernels migrate as the first consumers. Name templates keep kernel names byte identical, so profiler labels and shader cache keys do not change; the SwiGLU warm set folds into `warm_once`. - Patch registration stays in `model_runner`. The env flags' one reader should remain the load path, and the patch functions encode `mlx_lm` model class knowledge, not Metal JIT knowledge. **`can_fuse` is now abstract, per review** - A founder-level review found `FusedGateQmvSiluMulKernel` was a live example of the risk in an optimistic base default: it inherited `can_fuse` returning `True` unconditionally instead of declaring its own eligibility, relying entirely on `dispatch_fused` raising `NotFusable` before any observable effect to stay safe. `MetalJitOp.can_fuse` now raises `NotImplementedError` (`metal_jit.py:123-125`, matching this codebase's existing abstract-method idiom of a bare `raise NotImplementedError`, used already by `dispatch_fused`/`dispatch_fallback` on the same class; no `abc.ABC` is used anywhere in this tree). The class docstring states the rule directly: every op declares its own predicate, the base declares none. - `FusedMoeCombineKernel.can_fuse` already had a real structural predicate (`fused_combine.py:100-112`); unchanged. - `FusedGateQmvSiluMulKernel.can_fuse` (new, `fused_swiglu.py:246-263`) delegates to the same `_check_eligibility` regime check `dispatch_fused`/`dispatch_fallback` already share, so all three stay in sync by construction. This does not change the op's observable behavior: for structurally ineligible inputs, `dispatch()` now short-circuits straight to `dispatch_fallback` instead of first attempting `dispatch_fused` (which raised the identical diagnostic anyway); for eligible inputs whose Metal compile fails, `can_fuse` cannot see that and the routing is unchanged. SwiGLU's asymmetry is preserved exactly: `dispatch_fallback` still always raises the diagnostic chain rather than computing, since its real fallback needs wrapper layer context the op does not receive; only its predicate became explicit. - Three `test_metal_jit.py` stub classes that exercised `dispatch_fused`/`dispatch_fallback` routing without overriding `can_fuse` (relying on the removed default) now declare an explicit `can_fuse` returning `True`, so they keep testing what they were written to test. **Tolerance test fix, per review** - The same review found the bf16 1 ULP, zero headroom bound in `test_fused_combine.py` could reach tens of thousands of "ULP" at production scale. Root cause, found this session: the huge values are a metric artifact, not a kernel regression. Near zero, fp16/bf16 use absolute (subnormal-adjacent) steps far finer than the ULP ceiling's relative-error assumption, and the two paths can even land on opposite sides of zero (e.g. `0.0` vs `-1e-7`), where the bit-pattern-distance metric's own documented same-sign assumption breaks down. `allclose(atol=tol)` already bounds these elements correctly. - Fix: the integer-ULP ceiling is now checked only on elements at or above a `1e-3` ground-truth-magnitude floor (`_ULP_FLOOR`, `test_fused_combine.py`), where the bit-pattern-distance metric is meaningful. A live 100-seed-per-shape sweep across every shape in `_SHAPES` plus the real production prefill shape `(1, 268, 4, 2048)` found max ULP at or above the floor was 0-1 in every case, for both dtypes; the ceilings (`_ROUNDED_MAX_ULP`) are now 3 for both fp16 and bf16, roughly 3x headroom over that observed max. The check is not deleted or loosened past what the evidence supports. ## Accuracy Tests - `test_fused_combine.py`: 102 of 102 matrix cases fire the fused path. fp16 and bf16 scores are bit exact against the fp32 reference; fp32 scores are asserted within narrowing tolerance and a floor-masked integer-ULP ceiling (see Modifications). **[hardware verified, this run]** the updated bound was demonstrated seed robust: `test_scores_fp32_correctly_rounded` and the production-shape case in `test_leading_dims_match_reference` were run across 7 shifted seed offsets (0 through 60000) on this hardware, all passing, with observed ULP at or above the floor staying in {0, 1} throughout. Patch idempotency on real, small dimension `mlx_lm` blocks is a no op with bit identical outputs. - `test_metal_jit.py`: cache identity, name formatting, warm dedupe, decorator validation, and the dispatch template's routing contract (fused, fallback, `NotFusable` propagation, now including `can_fuse` as a required override), including the compile failure memoization guard. - `test_fused_swiglu.py`: regime diagnostics through the wrapper, dtype membership fallback (not just dtype agreement), warm skip logging, warmup enumeration, and (new) the explicit `can_fuse` predicate. - **47 tests across the three files at head** (17 + 10 + 20, `pytest --collect-only`) **[hardware verified, this run]**. Unchanged from before this revision: the fixes changed test bodies and one helper signature, not test count. - **[hardware verified, this run]** Full suite: 45 passed, 2 skipped (opt-in, HF-checkpoint-gated, not a hardware skip), 0 failed, both before and after this revision's changes. - **[hardware verified, this run]** The three `NotFusable` safety sub claims from the prior review (forced Metal compile failure on an eligible input: no raise to caller, bit exact output, no partial/corrupted cache state) were re-run against the real `fused_combine()` entry point after the `can_fuse` change and still hold; the equivalent check on `FusedGateQmvSiluMulKernel`'s own compile-failure path (now gated by its own `can_fuse`) also holds. ## Speed Tests and Profiling **Original end to end measurement** [author reported, not reverified end to end], `mlx-community/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat-4bit` on a 24 GB Apple Silicon machine, interleaved on/off server launches, warmup discarded, temperature 0, medians with min and max: | config | decode bs=1 tok/s | per step ms | decode bs=4 tok/s | prefill L=268 tok/s | |---|---|---|---|---| | unfused | 131.02 [130.61, 131.67] | 7.632 | 201.20 [199.13, 203.11] | 758.4 [756.0, 815.8]\* | | fused | 131.80 [131.64, 132.11] | 7.587 | 203.56 [201.82, 205.55] | 818.2 [809.8, 820.1] | \* One unfused launch at 9.7 GB free excluded as memory pressure (732.7 tok/s). Decode bs=1 is +0.6 percent, decode bs=4 is +1.2 percent, prefill is +0.0 to +1.5 percent depending on which launches are compared. **Isolated op measurement, decode bs=1** [hardware verified, this run]: re-ran the fused-vs-fallback dispatch check on this hardware after the `can_fuse` change. `dispatch()` still routes through exactly one `metal_jit.get("fused_moe_combine", ...)` call on the fused path, output still bit exact against an independent reference, and the fused path still measures faster than the fallback (paired timing this run: +2.4%, a simpler protocol than the prior review's bootstrapped interleaved A/B, so not a direct comparison to the fuller table below). **Prior isolated op measurement** [prior review, not rerun this session], Apple M4 Pro, 24 GB, bootstrap 95 percent confidence interval: | shape | fused (us) | fallback (us) | speedup | 95% CI excludes zero | |---|---|---|---|---| | decode bs=1 | 17.87 | 18.80 | +9.6% | yes | | decode bs=4 | 18.39 | 19.54 | +7.4% | yes | | prefill L=268 | 34.83 | 190.94 | +82.2% | yes | The two end-to-end/isolated tables are not directly comparable: the isolated measurement strips out every other per token cost (attention, routing, the expert GEMMs, sampling, KV bookkeeping), so it upper bounds what the combine op itself could contribute, while the end-to-end measurement is what actually reaches a user after dilution by the rest of the forward pass. The `metal_jit` registry promotion and the `can_fuse` abstraction change are both same-process refactors with no dispatch-count or numerics change on the fused path, confirmed this run; neither table's numbers are affected by them. ## Known Limitations - `warmup_specs` declares each op's supported variant set and has no consumer yet. The working warm path (SwiGLU only; combine pays its first dispatch JIT cost today) warms instantiated shapes derived from the live model. `aot.py` reconciles the two in a follow up PR. - The patch time `can_fuse(switch_mlp)` free function in `fused_swiglu.py` is unrelated to `MetalJitOp.can_fuse`; a rename is follow up material. This is a naming collision only; both `FusedMoeCombineKernel` and `FusedGateQmvSiluMulKernel` now declare their own `MetalJitOp.can_fuse` explicitly (see Modifications), so the base class no longer has an optimistic default for a future op to silently inherit. - SwiGLU's `dispatch_fallback` intentionally raises rather than computes, since its real fallback needs wrapper layer context the op does not receive. Unifying that is follow up scope. - Nothing counts fallback occurrences on either op (no logging on `FusedMoeCombineKernel`'s fallback path, a once-per-process warning on SwiGLU's). This was flagged by review as a real but lower-leverage gap for this pass and is not addressed here. - The `register_mlx_ci` addition to `ci_register.py` this branch carries is now byte identical to what #30121 independently merged to `main`; a real merge auto-resolves it with no manual edit, confirmed this run (`git hash-object` matches on both sides). signal.title: [Diffusion] Add MiniMax H3 cube sparse attention
signal.text: ## Summary - add a FlexAttention-based cube sparse attention backend for MiniMax H3's 3D visual streams - wire H3 packed-sequence metadata and denoise-step sparsity schedules into the native pipeline - keep text, audio, standalone reference images, and the text-only token refiner on dense attention - document the component-scoped command and add numerical, CUDA, admission, and parallelism coverage ## Behavior Select the backend only for the H3 transformer: ```bash --component-attention-backends transformer=cube_sparse_attn \ --attention-backend-config '{"local_cube_size":[4,4,4],"topk_ratio_list":[1.0,1.0,0.8,0.7,0.6,0.5,0.5]}' ``` A ratio of `1.0` uses H3's native FlashAttention path. Ratios below `1.0` use approximate cube sparsity. Ring parallelism is rejected because its attention exchange does not compose with this backend; Ulysses remains supported. ## Recommended `attention-backend-config` For `num_inference_steps=50` (49 denoise updates), use: ```json { "local_cube_size": [4, 4, 4], "topk_ratio_list": [ 1.0, 1.0, 0.55, 0.45, 0.35, 0.35, 0.30, 0.25, 0.25, 0.20, 0.20, 0.20, 0.15, 0.15, 0.15, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05 ] } ``` Pass this JSON through `--attention-backend-config` alongside the component-scoped backend selection above. ## Implementation Note The Cube sparse attention backend in this PR is a reference implementation built with PyTorch FlexAttention. For higher performance on supported NVIDIA hardware, future work may explore replacing it with cuDNN Frontend's Block Sparse Attention ([cudnn-frontend/python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention at main · NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/tree/main/python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention)) operator. Broader hardware support and backend-specific optimizations are left to future community contributions. ## Performance On 2×H100 with the 1344×768, 4-second, 8-step TP2 workload: - dense FlashAttention denoise: 16.51s - aggressive all-`0.05` sparse schedule: 13.32s (19.3% faster) - mixed `[1.0, 1.0, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.5]` schedule: 19.67s The mixed schedule is slower on this short sequence because FlexAttention routing overhead outweighs the sparse-kernel savings, so the feature remains opt-in and the cookbook calls out the tradeoff. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31856755676](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31856755676)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31856755577](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31856755577)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion] feat: support MiniMax-H3 text encoder FP8 quantization
signal.text: ## Summary - add text-encoder-specific quantization controls without changing the DiT `--quantization` contract - auto-detect serialized text-encoder quantization metadata and run native post-load weight processing - opt MiniMax-H3's native Qwen3-VL language stack into FP8 while keeping embeddings, normalization, and the vision tower in BF16 - document online and serialized FP8 recipes, including startup-memory behavior and the strict `quality="high"` exclusion ## Why MiniMax-H3 uses a large Qwen3-VL prompt encoder. The native linear layers already support SGLang quantization methods, but the encoder loader did not resolve checkpoint quantization metadata, pass the quantization config into the model, or run post-load processing. Reusing the transformer flag would also couple prompt conditioning precision to DiT precision. This change introduces an explicit text-encoder boundary and keeps unsupported native encoders fail-closed. ## Validation - H100 online FP8 load and real prompt encoding - H100 serialized `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct-FP8` load through the normal `sglang serve` download path - complete 5-second 1344×768 T2VA requests with online and serialized FP8 plus layerwise offload - serialized FP8 TP1/TP2 load and forward comparison - focused unit tests and changed-files pre-commit checks <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31921261879](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921261879)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31921261716](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921261716)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Route MiniMax H3 VAE attention through native backends
signal.text: ## Summary - route both MiniMax H3 VAE attention modules through `USPAttention`, so they use SGLang's native component/backend selection - keep VAE attention tile-local with `skip_sequence_parallel=True`; H3 decode distributes complete independent tiles, so applying global Ulysses/Ring collectives here would mix unrelated sequences - keep the audio VAE on FP32 causal Torch SDPA by default while allowing an explicit `audio_vae=fa` component override; only explicit fused backends cast QKV compute precision - preserve the explicit FP32, MPS, and ROCm correctness fallbacks - remove the local 190-line `flash_attn` wrapper and unreachable causal/mask/varlen plumbing from the released non-causal decoder - establish the standard forward context required by native attention during VAE decode ## Root cause The H3 video VAE exposed a helper named `flash_attn`, but its dense path always called PyTorch SDPA and bypassed SGLang's attention backend machinery. On H100, PyTorch SDPA did select its own fused Flash kernel, so this was not math SDPA; the issue was the parallel backend abstraction and component overrides being bypassed. The released H3 video decoder is non-causal (`causal_decoder=False`). Its block-causal mask, varlen, valid-padding, and associated `pack_info` branches had no runtime caller, which made the actual behavior harder to see. The H3 DiT/token refiner already uses native packed-varlen backend dispatch, and the Qwen text path already uses `LocalAttention`. The audio VAE still defaults to its released FP32 causal SDPA contract, but now participates in component backend selection; `skip_sequence_parallel=True` keeps reference-audio encoding rank-local. ## Validation - pre-commit passed on all changed files - targeted remote tests: `12 passed` - exact commit tested on an isolated 2xH100 80 GB devbox: `9401d6db495894cb356771ba4b8274ba946203b7` - standard `sglang serve --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3` downloaded and loaded the public snapshot through the normal Hub path - server log confirmed `Attention backends for video_vae: fa` - standard 1344x768x124-frame warmup completed successfully in 27.43 s - fixed-seed 4-second T2VA E2E completed in 22.582 s with a valid 1344x768/24-fps H.264 video and 32-kHz stereo AAC audio - component override `video_vae=torch_sdpa` also completed the same request successfully - the audio VAE follow-up adds a focused contract check for SDPA default selection, FA admission, QKV casting, and FP32 output restoration H100 attention microbenchmarks at H3 VAE geometry: | Sequence | Torch SDPA | SGLang FA3 | Kernel speedup | Max abs diff | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1,285 | 0.1024 ms | 0.0585 ms | 1.75x | 1.22e-4 | | 4,101 | 0.4996 ms | 0.3181 ms | 1.57x | 1.22e-4 | The isolated kernel win is below full-pipeline timing noise: FA3 and Torch SDPA decoded the E2E request in 14.800 s and 14.801 s respectively. This PR therefore does not claim an E2E speedup. For the paired E2E outputs, decoded audio was bit-exact. Both videos had 107 frames and identical stream geometry; decoded-frame comparison measured 45.05 dB PSNR and 0.9814 SSIM, with no visible structural difference in side-by-side inspection. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31889115740](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31889115740)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31889144009](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31889144009)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bugfix] Preserve MXFP4 Triton weights in sharded state
signal.text: ## Summary - keep Triton-swizzled MXFP4 expert weights and scales registered on the layer - serialize non-contiguous postprocessed tensors through contiguous CPU snapshots - keep wrapper-backed runtime tensors out of CPU/offload-group parameter remapping - add CPU regressions for a fresh-layer sharded round trip and the offloader guard ## Root cause The Triton MXFP4 post-load path moved the swizzled `w13` and `w2` weight wrappers onto the quantization method and deleted the registered layer parameters. `ShardedStateLoader.save_model` only exports `model.state_dict()`, so those runtime weights were omitted. On reload, SGLang postprocesses freshly initialized placeholders before it builds the expected state dict. The missing weights therefore disappeared from both the checkpoint and the expected-key set, and loading silently succeeded with placeholder runtime weights. The swizzled scales held by `PrecisionConfig` had the same stale-storage problem even though the original scale parameters remained registered. This change rebinds all four Triton runtime tensors (two weights and two scales) to their existing registered `Parameter` objects. The module state and kernel wrappers then share the same backing storage, so sharded-load copies update the tensors actually consumed by the kernels. Parameter identity and weight-loader attributes are preserved. The Hopper swizzle can produce non-contiguous runtime tensors. Safetensors rejects those tensors, so the exporter materializes contiguous CPU snapshots at the save boundary without changing the live runtime layout. ## CPU offload compatibility Triton wrappers live outside the module parameter mapping temporarily installed by `functional_call`. The four wrapper-backed Parameters are therefore marked to remain on device, and both offloader implementations honor that marker. This preserves the previous effective behavior of the hidden Triton tensors while allowing them to remain registered for serialization. Fixes #34448 ## Validation - focused CPU regression with import-only stubs for unavailable GPU dependencies: `2 tests`, `OK` - creates source and zero-initialized destination layers through the real MXFP4 `create_weights` - runs the real MXFP4 post-load method with only the Triton layout conversion mocked - saves through the real `ShardedStateLoader`, reloads every safetensors entry into the fresh destination state, and verifies both weights and scales consumed by the runtime wrappers - verifies wrapper-backed Parameters are excluded from CPU offload - the same sharded round-trip regression against current `upstream/main@b3bffef70a` fails as expected because `w13_weight` is absent after postprocessing - `python3 scripts/ci/check_registered_tests.py` - Black (`--check`) on all four changed files - isort (`--check-only`) on the new test - Ruff (`F401`, `F821`, `UP037`) on all four changed files - `git diff --check` - `python3 -m py_compile test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_mxfp4_sharded_state.py` The CPU tests are registered in `base-a-test-cpu`. - reporter validation on the original GH200, TP=2 reproduction: the sharded export increased from the broken `4.0G` result to `14G`, resolving the reported missing-weight export symptom ([result](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34558#issuecomment-5293077326)) A full save-reload logits comparison has not yet been reported. Project CI is still pending. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31921029831](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921029831)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31921029709](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31921029709)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Add the Kimi-K3 MI35x perf sweep inside the accuracy job
signal.text:
Follow-up to #32568 that adds the Kimi-K3 perf sweep as a step inside the existing accuracy job, rather than as a separate gated job. Based on `amd/mi355x-kimi-k3-nightly` so the diff is purely the perf delta on top of #32568. Retarget to `main` once #32568 lands. ## Why inside the accuracy job This is not a new pattern — it is the dominant one in `nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`. Twenty jobs there already pair an "Accuracy Test" step with a "Performance Test" step in the same job (Grok1-INT4, Grok2, DeepSeek-V3.1/V3.2/V3.2-MTP, Qwen3.5, GLM-5.1, GLM-5-MXFP4, MiniMax-M2.7, …). Only four perf steps invoke a test file directly; twenty-two go through `run_suite.py`, which is what this does. For K3 specifically the shared job is strictly better than a separate one: - **The checkpoint is already cached.** The 1.56 TB MXFP4 weights dominate wall time — the eval job runs ~62 min, of which the sweep itself is a small tail. A separate job pays the download and load a second time from cold. - **One 8-GPU MI35x slot instead of two.** That runner is contended enough that a redundant slot costs real wall time for everyone else in the queue. - **Step ordering is the accuracy gate, for free.** The eval step ends with `exit ${TEST_EXIT_CODE:-0}`, so a failed eval fails the job and the perf step never runs. That is the same guarantee a separate job would buy with `needs:`. - **It avoids the wart `needs:` brings.** With a separate gated job, perf cannot be dispatched on its own: selecting only the perf job skips accuracy, which skips perf. Sharing the job means there is nothing to document. `continue-on-error: true` on the perf step follows the same sibling jobs. `check-all-jobs` gates on the job, so without it a flaky sweep would turn a green accuracy result red. ## The test needed fixing, not just moving An earlier revision of this test lived in #32568 and had never run a single line of its benchmark body. Its one dispatch, in run [31853704954](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31853704954), died in `setUpClass` after 23 s with `Ran 0 tests in 0.001s`. It was written against the pre-#33832 `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` API — #33832 ("[CI] Remove profiling from nightly tests") renamed the profile API to result and deleted the profiling kwarg. Three fixes: | Before | After | Why | | --- | --- | --- | | `setup_profile_directory()` | `setup_result_directory()` | The method #33832 renamed. This is the `AttributeError` that killed the run. | | `PROFILE_DIR = "performance_profiles_kimi_k3_mi35x"` | `RESULT_DIR = "performance_results_kimi_k3_mi35x"` | Matches all fifteen sibling MI35x perf tests, and the directory holds the `results_*.json` that `scripts/ci/utils/save_metrics.py` collects. | | `enable_profile=False` | removed | #33832 removed this kwarg from `run_benchmark_for_model`; it has no `**kwargs`, so this was a `TypeError` waiting directly behind the first failure. | That second latent failure is why this is worth more than a one-line rename: fixing only the `AttributeError` would have burned another MI35x hour to surface the `TypeError`. ## Test plan Verified with a harness that loads the real `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` with only its torch-backed leaf imports stubbed, so the class under test is the one from the tree: - [x] `setUpClass()` runs to completion and creates `performance_results_kimi_k3_mi35x` - [x] Every `runner.*` attribute the test touches exists on `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` - [x] The `run_benchmark_for_model(...)` call binds against the real signature - [x] **The same harness fails on the pre-fix file**, reproducing the CI error verbatim (`AttributeError: ... has no attribute 'setup_profile_directory'`) plus the latent `got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_profile'` — so these checks are load-bearing, not vacuous - [x] Workflow YAML parses; job count, `job_select` options and `check-all-jobs` entries are all unchanged from the base, confirming no new job was introduced - [x] The K3 job's steps are, in order, `Accuracy Test …` then `Performance Test …`, running `nightly-amd-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3` then `nightly-perf-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3` - [x] `codespell --config .codespellrc` clean repo-wide; `black --check` and `isort --check-only` clean Not yet verified on hardware: the sweep has still never produced a throughput number, so this needs one MI35x dispatch of `job_select=nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3-rocm720` before merge. Reference numbers to compare against are in #32548 — 102.5 tok/s/GPU at concurrency 2 rising to 612.3 at 32, non-speculative — and the eval's own decode logs on the green accuracy run showed ~619 tok/s aggregate at batch 11. ## Note on a neighbouring bug `test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen35_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py` on `main` has the identical stale-API breakage that #33832 left behind — `runner.setup_profile_directory()` at line 146 and `enable_profile=False` at line 162 — so its `test_b_perf` will hit the same `AttributeError`. It is CI-registered as `nightly-amd-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen35-mxfp4`. Left out of scope here since it is a pre-existing bug against `main`; happy to send it separately.

signal.title: [AMD] Make the Kimi-K3 MI35x nightly accuracy-only, and fix the lint blocker
signal.text:
Targets `amd/mi355x-kimi-k3-nightly`, the branch behind #32568. Merging this leaves that PR as accuracy only and lint-clean. The perf sweep moves to a follow-up, which adds it as a step inside the accuracy job rather than as a separate gated job. ## Why **The lint failure is one word, and it is what makes the whole PR red.** codespell flags `unparseable ==> unparsable` in `test_kimi_k3_eval_mi35x.py:15`. `.github/actions/check-pr-test-health` fast-fails every PR-test job as soon as the `lint` check is red, so that single word aborted all 21 `base-b-*` jobs in ~10 s each without any of them running a test. Roughly 30 of #32568's failing checks are cascade noise from it. `unparsable` is the spelling used everywhere else in the tree, so the word is fixed rather than allow-listed in `.codespellrc`. **The perf job has never been green.** It was dispatched exactly once, in run [31853704954](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31853704954), and died in `setUpClass` after 23 s: ``` AttributeError: 'NightlyBenchmarkRunner' object has no attribute 'setup_profile_directory'. Did you mean: 'setup_result_directory'? Ran 0 tests in 0.001s ``` Not a typo — the test was written against the pre-#33832 `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` API. #33832 ("[CI] Remove profiling from nightly tests") renamed `profile_dir` → `result_dir`, `setup_profile_directory()` → `setup_result_directory()`, `generate_profile_filename()` → `generate_result_filename()` and deleted the `enable_profile` kwarg. The K3 perf test still used the old three, so there was a second `TypeError` on `enable_profile=False` waiting behind the first failure. `Ran 0 tests` means the sweep body has never executed and this test has never produced a throughput number. The accuracy job in that same run passed, so nothing about accuracy depends on any of this. ## What changes - `test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_kimi_k3_eval_mi35x.py` — `unparseable` → `unparsable`. - Removes `test/registered/amd/perf/mi35x/test_kimi_k3_perf_mi35x.py`. - Removes the `nightly-perf-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3` suite from `test/run_suite.py`. - Removes the `nightly-perf-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3-rocm720` job from `nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`, plus its `job_select` option and `check-all-jobs` entry. The accuracy job, its suite registration, and the Kimi-K2.6 retirement are untouched. ## Accuracy is already validated twice | | Head `61a52a9`, standard image | Earlier, pinned image | | --- | --- | --- | | Run | [31853704954](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31853704954) | [30386408970](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30386408970) | | GSM8K accuracy | **0.956** (threshold 0.92) | **0.956** | | Unparsable | 0.1% | 0.2% | | Eval latency | 270.8 s | 276 s | | Output throughput | 497.9 tok/s | 488 tok/s | | Job wall time | ~62 min | ~74 min | Plus [31849574590](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31849574590) on `d35e7ed`, which is what retires the image pin: the standard `rocm720-mi35x` nightly image imports `kimi_k3` and the server launches. ## Test plan - [x] `codespell --config .codespellrc` clean repo-wide (was 1 error, now 0) - [x] `black --check` and `isort --check-only` clean on touched files - [x] Workflow YAML parses; every `job_select` option, every `needs:` target and every `check-all-jobs` entry names a real job. `job_select` options go 47 → 46 and `check-all-jobs` 46 → 45, exactly the perf job. (`nightly-test-1-gpu-kernel-rocm720` is absent from `check-all-jobs` both before and after, and on `main` too — pre-existing, untouched here.) - [x] No dangling `nightly-perf-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k3` or `test_kimi_k3_perf` references anywhere in the tree - [x] The K3 accuracy suite is still registered and still wired into `job_select` and `check-all-jobs` ## Not addressed here `test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen35_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py` has the identical stale-API breakage on `main` today — `runner.setup_profile_directory()` at line 146 and `enable_profile=False` at line 162, both left behind by #33832. Its `test_b_perf` will hit the same `AttributeError`, and it is CI-registered as `nightly-amd-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen35-mxfp4`. That is a separate pre-existing bug against `main`, so it is deliberately out of scope; happy to send a one-line fix for it separately.

signal.title: [Diffusion] Add native GLM-Image AR encoder
signal.text: ## Summary - replace the in-process Transformers GLM-Image AR model with SGLang-owned vision, VQ, and text decoder modules - expose text and vision blocks to component layerwise offload while preserving component CPU offload and the external SRT path - route single-token CUDA decode through SDPA, keep the configured backend for prefill and vision, and update the public AR documentation ## Why The default in-process GLM-Image path instantiated Transformers' full weighted model. This prevented the diffusion runtime from managing every AR layer consistently and from applying native attention and layerwise offload across the full component. FlashAttention also has higher dispatch overhead than SDPA for the single-token decode shape. The native model therefore uses SDPA for CUDA decode while retaining the configured attention backend for prefill and vision workloads. The causal SDPA adjustment is identical to #34951 and is included so this PR can be tested independently. It becomes an empty overlap after that change lands. ## Validation - pre-commit - 66 focused GLM-Image, multi-output, and disaggregation tests - real `zai-org/GLM-Image` checkpoint parity: sampled weights, all 40 text layers, prefill and decode logits, vision features, VQ tokens, and greedy generation were exact - loader and layerwise smoke with 40 text layers and 40 vision blocks - H100 median: 256-token prefill 20.63 to 20.14 ms; 576-token vision 10.37 to 8.73 ms; 32-token generation 617.79 to 591.37 ms <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31900486307](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31900486307)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #31900493342](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31900493342)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Native ERNIE prompt enhancer
signal.text: ## Summary - replace the in-process ERNIE prompt enhancer HF causal LM with the native Ministral3 decoder - align cached causal SDPA with FlashAttention lower-right semantics and expose PE decoder layers to component layerwise offload - update the ERNIE PE docs and add native/HF generation and offload contract tests ## Validation - pre-commit on all changed files - remote H100: `test_ministral3_generation.py` (6 passed) - remote H100, real `baidu/ERNIE-Image/pe`: all 26 layers, KV cache, cached decode logits, sampled IDs, and greedy IDs exactly match HF (`max_abs=0`) - remote H100: actual `PELoader` generation with all 26 decoder layers under layerwise offload <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31886314478](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31886314478)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31886314342](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31886314342)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Native Qwen3-VL vision encoder
signal.text: ## Summary - replace the Transformers-owned Qwen3-VL vision model with a native SGLang-Diffusion implementation - preserve checkpoint parameter names and exact BF16 numerics, including FP32 position interpolation - include vision blocks in layerwise offload and FSDP sharding - add focused unit coverage for layout, dtype, checkpoint keys, and offload registration ## Validation - pre-commit hooks: passed - remote H100 unit test: `4 passed` - real MiniMax-H3 27-layer checkpoint parity against Transformers 5.12.1: exact for all blocks, deepstack outputs, and pooler (`max_abs=0`) - remote 2xH100 server test: `minimax_h3_t2va_2gpu_h100` passed; E2E 46.97s vs 47.54s baseline <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31883602373](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31883602373)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31883602312](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31883602312)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Use native Qwen2.5-VL generation
signal.text: ## Summary - load Qwen Image Layered and LongCat-Image's Qwen2.5-VL encoder through the native component loader instead of stage-local Transformers models - add native Qwen2.5-VL vision execution and KV-cache autoregressive generation, including checkpoint generation settings and packed attention - unify text-encoder ownership under the existing residency, layerwise offload, FSDP, and legacy CPU-offload paths - document the in-process native AR path and add LongCat-Image to the compatibility inventory ## Compatibility This does not change the image API or CLI. Existing component flags, including `--text-encoder-cpu-offload` and explicit layerwise offload, remain supported. ## Validation - pre-commit passed - focused Qwen/LongCat/residency unit tests: 61 passed; final generation-focused selection: 20 passed - full unit suite: 1555 passed, 105 skipped; 4 failures reproduced unchanged on the base commit - native/HF vision checkpoint alignment: max absolute difference 0, cosine similarity 1.0 - Qwen Image Layered consistency: CLIP 0.9993, SSIM 0.9909, PSNR 42.9456 - verified resident, explicit layerwise, and 2-GPU FSDP with legacy text-encoder CPU offload - verified LongCat prompt rewriting and Qwen visual-caption generation - visual-caption preprocessing improved from 2.172 s to 2.042 s in same-machine HF/native comparison; the full request improved from 6.087 s to 5.449 s <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31880165562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31880165562)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31880165417](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31880165417)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation In RL async mode, multiple communication groups are often required for coordination between actors and rollout workers. However, Ray's collective communication interfaces currently do not support the HCCL backend. To address this, pynccl (and its counterpart pyhccl) are used to support the creation of new communication groups. Furthermore, pyhccl will be utilized for KV Cache communication, ensuring efficient data exchange across NPUs. While vLLM already supports both([[Core] Add pyhccl](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/503)), sglang currently only supports pynccl. This PR aims to bridge that gap by supporting pyhccl to sglang. <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications add two files: python/sglang/srt/distributed/device_communicators/pyhccl.py python/sglang/srt/distributed/device_communicators/pyhccl_wrapper.py Within these two files, we wrap collective communication algorithms—including All-Reduce, Broadcast, All-Gather, Reduce-Scatter, and Barrier using `hccl_library`. <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> ## Accuracy Tests We have verified the correctness of the provided collective communication library: ``` [CI Test Method] TestAscendPyhccl.test_pyhccl [Gloo] Rank 0 is connected to 1 peer ranks. signal.title: [diffusion] lora: Fix/qkv fuse lora breakage
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Some diffusion pipelines/models use **fused projections** (e.g., `attn.to_qkv` / `attn.to_added_qkv`, and fused SwiGLU `ffn.w13`). However, many public LoRAs (including Qwen-Image / Z-Image / Lightning-style LoRAs) are authored for **split projections** (e.g., `to_q/to_k/to_v`, `add_q_proj/add_k_proj/add_v_proj`, `w1/w3`). When the target model expects fused modules but the LoRA provides split keys, plain name-format normalization is not enough: LoRA keys may not match the target layers (becoming ineffective), or weight injection can fail with **rank/shape mismatches** (especially when exact fusions expand effective rank). This PR adds **target-aware LoRA preparation + exact fusing** and a **dynamic-rank injection fallback** so split-projection LoRAs can be reliably applied to fused targets without breaking inference. ## Modifications ### 1) `lora_format_adapter.py` - **Target-aware LoRA preparation** via `prepare_lora_state_dict_for_target(...)`: - Normalize external LoRA formats into canonical `.lora_A/.lora_B`. - Detect fused targets (QKV/add_qkv, SwiGLU) from target layer names. - Perform **exact fusion** when the target is fused but the LoRA is split: - QKV/add_qkv: `q/k/v → to_qkv / to_added_qkv` - FFN: `w1/w3 → w13` - Shared `A`: concatenate `B`; different `A`: block-diagonal exact fusion. - **Robust injection** via `set_lora_weights_dynamic_rank(...)`: - Try `set_lora_weights(...)` first; on rank/shape mismatch, dynamically replace `lora_A/B` (inference-safe). - **Correct scaling**: - Bake `(alpha / rank)` into `lora_B` and drop `.alpha`. ### 2) `lora_pipeline.py` - **Load-time preparation**: - Collect target LoRA layers across components and call `prepare_lora_state_dict_for_target(...)`. - **Application path**: - Use `set_lora_weights_dynamic_rank(...)` instead of direct setting to handle fused targets and rank mismatches. ## Compatibility notes - If the target does not use fused modules (or the LoRA already matches fused keys), no fusing is performed and behavior remains unchanged. - If the canonical `layer.set_lora_weights(...)` accepts the provided shapes, the dynamic-rank fallback is not triggered. ## Accuracy Tests This PR affects LoRA weight mapping/injection logic. I ran local functional tests focusing on: - no crashes / no shape assertion failures - LoRA effectively applied (qualitative output changes as expected) - logs indicate target-aware fuse behavior where applicable ### ✅ Local tests executed 1. **Qwen-Image + `lightx2v/Qwen-Image-Lightning-4` & `8steps-V2.0-bf16`** 2. **Z-Image + `Z-Image-Turbo-DeJPEG-Lora/dejpeg_v3`** 3. **Qwen-Edit + `lightx2v/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Lightning/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Lightning-4steps-V1.0-fp32`** ## Benchmarking and Profiling This PR does not affect runtime inference performance. Normalization occurs only once at LoRA load time and has negligible overhead. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to the [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). - [x] Work with maintainers to merge your PR. signal.title: [WIP][diffusion] new model: support Wan Animate with Data preprocessing
signal.text: ## Motivation Supporting Wan Animate (https://huggingface.co/Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-14B-Diffusers) See issue https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/13867 Based on PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/15419 ## Modifications This PR introduces a customized orchestration pipeline for the Wan Animate model. By implementing a Segment Loop mechanism, it overcomes VRAM limitations for long video generation. Additionally, it integrates a Data Preprocessing stage that supports direct extraction of pose and face features from raw videos, significantly lowering the barrier to entry for end-users. ### Pipeline Design #### `WanAnimatePipeline`: ```shell Preprocessing -> Validation -> Text/Image Encoding -> VAE Encoding -> Video Processing -> Condition Construction -> Segment Loop ``` #### SegmentLoopStage - The SegmentLoopStage manages the cur_segment index and orchestrates a sub-pipeline consisting of five stages: Conditioning → Timestep → Latent → Denoising → Decoding - The WanAnimateConditioningStage dynamically slices the Pose/Face conditions for the current segment. - The DecodingStage triggers postprocess_decoded_frames for incremental frame stitching and returns a Req object to drive the next iteration or returns OutputBatch to terminate. #### Data Preprocessing Stage We provide a Data Preprocessing Stage, if users provide the onnx model path of the preprocess model, we can directly process the original video passed in by the user instead of the user passing in the preprocessed pose video and face video. With `preprocess_model_path`: ```shell sglang generate --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-14B-Diffusers \ --prompt='People in the video are doing actions.' --image-path [ref image path] --video-path [video path] --preprocess-model-path [process model path] --width 1280 --height 720 --save-output ``` Without `preprocess_model_path`: ```shell sglang generate --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-14B-Diffusers\\n --prompt='People in the video are doing actions.' --image-path [ref image path] --pose-video-path [processed pose video path] --face-video-path [processed face video path] --width 1280 --height 720 --save-output ``` ## TODO - replace mode for wan animate - retarget and use flux for data preprocess ## Accuracy Tests Replicate.com wan animate animation: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f02381bf-6d8a-44bf-a026-492a6e0764e9 Our results: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/891e7f4b-cbab-4e38-ab98-558c22ff3c9e ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). - [ ] Work with maintainers to merge your PR. signal.title: feat: add SchedulerRecvSkipper support for dp attention
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Add SchedulerRecvSkipper support for dp attention. Previously, `SchedulerRecvSkipper` was explicitly blocked from being used with dp_attention mode (via an assertion). This PR removes that limitation and implements proper support for dp_attention, ensuring all DP ranks make consistent skip/recv decisions. The key challenge with dp_attention is that all DP ranks must make the **same decision** about whether to receive new requests, otherwise they would diverge. This PR solves this by: 1. Computing a `global_forward_mode` that is synchronized across all DP ranks after the sync point 2. Updating the counter based on this global mode to ensure consistency ## Modifications 1. **`scheduler_recv_skipper.py`**: - Removed the assertion that blocked dp_attention mode - Added `update_counter_dp()` method that updates the counter based on `global_forward_mode` after the sync point - Modified `handle()` to separate the check-and-update logic: - For dp_attention: only checks if counter >= threshold (counter update is done separately via `update_counter_dp()`) - For non-dp_attention: check and update counter in one call (original behavior) - Changed initial counter value from `0` to `self._threshold` to ensure first iteration triggers recv 2. **`scheduler_dp_attn_mixin.py`**: - Added `_get_global_forward_mode()` helper function to compute the global forward mode from all DP ranks (excluding IDLE modes) - Integrated `global_forward_mode` computation into `prepare_mlp_sync_batch_raw()` - Called `recv_skipper.update_counter_dp()` in `prepare_dp_attn_batch()` after the sync point to ensure all DP ranks have the same counter value ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Benchmarking and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist -
