signal.title: [model-gateway] Support MCP Namespaces
signal.text: ## Motivation Currently when multiple MCP servers registered, the tool name collisions will cause an overwrite in inventory (Insert into Dashmap with duplicated keys). For example both postgres and DuckDB has tool `query`. ## Modifications - Introduced `Namespace` Module and `ServerIdentity` Struct - `key` - An internal, unique ID for a server connection (e.g., a URL) - Used by connection pooling for dynamic mcp, from `server_key` - Same as `label` for static mcp - `label ` - For inventory and user-facing (e.g. `duckdb`) - Will be used to construct qualified names for tools and prompts - From `server_name` and fall back to `server_key` if `server_name` not provided for dynamic mcp - `ToolInventory` Storage - All tools and prompts are now stored in the ToolInventory using a qualified name, following `[server_label]_[tool/prompt_name]` - The `McpManager` public API (call_tool, get_prompt) now operates on these qualified names for lookup and routing - Actual request to MCP servers will strip the prefix and contain only the original name - Associated unit tests updated. ## Accuracy Tests ### Both Tools in Response With Qualified Names - Example Request ``` "tools": [ { "type": "mcp", "server_label": "duckdb", "server_url": "http://localhost:8003/sse" }, { "type": "mcp", "server_label": "postgres", "server_url": "http://localhost:8001/sse" } ] ``` - Example Response ``` "tools": [ { "name": "postgres_query", "description": "Run a read-only SQL query", "input_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "sql": { "type": "string" } } }, "annotations": { "read_only": false } }, { "name": "duckdb_query", "description": "Execute a query on the DuckDB database", "input_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "query": { "type": "string", "description": "SQL query to execute" } }, "required": [ "query" ] }, "annotations": { "read_only": false } } ] ``` ### Originally Only 1 Stored into Inventory with Collision ### Now Both Stored with Prefix ### Correct Tool Calling ## Checklist - signal.title: [diffusion] Controlnet
signal.text: Hello this is a implementation of controlnet for QwenImage. I am opening this PR to invite discussions and some review if I am going the right direction. ## Summary This PR adds ControlNet support to the QwenImage diffusion pipeline, enabling precise spatial control over image generation through conditioning signals like edge maps, depth maps, poses, and inpainting masks. **Supported Models:** - `InstantX/Qwen-Image-ControlNet-Union` (canny, depth, pose, soft edge, etc.) - `InstantX/Qwen-Image-ControlNet-Inpainting` (image inpainting with masks) - Multiple ControlNets simultaneously (multi-control mode) Closes #13790 ## Changes ### New Components | File | Description | |------|-------------| | `runtime/models/controlnets/qwen_image_controlnet.py` | `QwenImageControlNetModel` and `QwenImageMultiControlNetModel` implementations with FSDP support | | `runtime/pipelines_core/stages/control_encoding.py` | Pipeline stage for loading, resizing, VAE-encoding, and patchifying control images | | `runtime/loader/component_loader.py` | `ControlNetLoader` class for loading ControlNet weights from HuggingFace | ### API Additions **Server Arguments** (`server_args.py`): - `controlnet_path`: Path to single ControlNet model - `controlnet_paths`: List of paths for multi-ControlNet setups **Sampling Parameters** (`sampling_params.py`): - `control_image_path`: Path/URL to pre-processed control image - `control_mask_path`: Path/URL to inpainting mask (white=inpaint, black=keep) - `controlnet_conditioning_scale`: Strength of ControlNet guidance (0.0-2.0) - `control_image_paths` / `controlnet_conditioning_scales`: For multi-control mode **OpenAI-compatible API** (`protocol.py`, `image_api.py`): - Added `control_image_path` and `controlnet_conditioning_scale` to `ImageGenerationsRequest` ### Pipeline Integration - **`qwen_image.py`**: Added `ControlEncodingStage` and passes `controlnet` to `DenoisingStage` - **`denoising.py`**: Computes ControlNet block residuals and passes them to the transformer during denoising - **`composed_pipeline_base.py`**: Added `has_module()` helper and ControlNet loading logic with HuggingFace Hub download support ## Architecture ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ QwenImage Pipeline │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ 1. ControlEncodingStage │ │ - Load control image(s) from path/URL │ │ - Resize to match generation dimensions │ │ - VAE encode → latent space │ │ - Patchify (2x2 patches → sequence) │ │ - For inpainting: concatenate mask channels │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ 2. DenoisingStage │ │ - At each timestep: │ │ a) Run ControlNet(latents, control_cond) → residuals │ │ b) Run Transformer(latents, residuals) → noise pred │ │ c) Scheduler step │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ## Usage ### Basic Usage (Union ControlNet) ```python from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.entrypoints.diffusion_generator import DiffGenerator gen = DiffGenerator.from_pretrained( model_path='Qwen/Qwen-Image', controlnet_path='InstantX/Qwen-Image-ControlNet-Union', ) result = gen.generate( sampling_params_kwargs={ "prompt": "a beautiful sunset over mountains", "width": 1024, "height": 1024, "control_image_path": "path/to/canny_edges.png", "controlnet_conditioning_scale": 0.8, } ) Inpainting gen = DiffGenerator.from_pretrained( model_path='Qwen/Qwen-Image', controlnet_path='InstantX/Qwen-Image-ControlNet-Inpainting', ) result = gen.generate( sampling_params_kwargs={ "prompt": "a green taxi on the road", "control_image_path": "path/to/source_image.png", "control_mask_path": "path/to/mask.png", # white=inpaint, black=keep "controlnet_conditioning_scale": 1.0, } ) Multi-ControlNet (Multiple Conditions) gen = DiffGenerator.from_pretrained( model_path='Qwen/Qwen-Image', controlnet_path='InstantX/Qwen-Image-ControlNet-Union', ) result = gen.generate( sampling_params_kwargs={ "prompt": "a rabbit on a beach", "control_image_paths": ["canny.png", "depth.png"], "controlnet_conditioning_scales": [0.5, 0.5], } )''' Happy to share test scripts I ran on modal to verify the outputs too. On A100/80 GPU.

signal.title: [Metric] add output throughput per request in Prometheus.
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation When monitoring LLM inference performance, per-request output throughput is a critical metric for understanding individual request performance. Currently, **vLLM** exposes `vllm:request_time_per_output_token_seconds` as a per-request histogram in Prometheus, allowing users to calculate metrics like: - Average per-request throughput over the last N minutes - P50/P90/P99 percentiles of per-request throughput **SGLang** only provides `decode_throughput` in the API response's `meta_info` field, but does not expose it as a Prometheus metric. This makes it impossible to: 1. Calculate the average per-request output throughput over a time window using PromQL 2. Monitor per-request throughput percentiles in Grafana dashboards 3. Set up alerts based on per-request throughput degradation This PR adds a new Prometheus histogram metric `sglang:request_output_throughput_tokens_per_second` to address this gap. ## Modifications 1. **`python/sglang/srt/metrics/collector.py`** - Added `histogram_request_output_throughput` Histogram in `TokenizerMetricsCollector` - Modified `observe_one_finished_request()` to accept optional `output_throughput` parameter and record it 2. **`python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py`** - Calculate per-request output throughput (`completion_tokens / decode_time`) in `collect_metrics()` - Pass `output_throughput` to `observe_one_finished_request()` 3. **`docs/references/production_metrics.md`** - Added documentation and example output for the new metric ## Tests 1. **`test/srt/test_metrics.py`** - Added `sglang:request_output_throughput_tokens_per_second` to essential metrics verification list

signal.title: Add validation for missing model weights during checkpoint loading
signal.text: # Add validation for missing model weights during checkpoint loading ## Overview This PR fixes a critical silent bug where model parameters that exist in the model architecture but are missing from checkpoint files retain random initialization values, causing incorrect model outputs without any error or warning. ## The Problem ### What Happens When `load_weights()` iterates through checkpoint weights, it only processes weights that exist in the checkpoint. If a model parameter is missing from the checkpoint, the iteration never encounters it, so it keeps its random initialization value. ```python # Current behavior (BEFORE this PR): params_dict = dict(self.named_parameters()) # Model has layers 0-24 for name, weight in checkpoint_weights: # Checkpoint has layers 0-23 param = params_dict[name] load_weight(param, weight) # Layer 24 is never loaded → keeps random values → broken model! # No error raised ❌ ``` ### Real-World Scenarios This bug can occur when: 1. **Config mismatch**: `config.json` says 25 layers, checkpoint has 24 2. **Architecture evolution**: New model version adds layers, loaded with old checkpoint 3. **Custom models**: Training team adds parameters not in standard HuggingFace format 4. **Incomplete checkpoints**: Checkpoint save interrupted or corrupted ### Impact - **Severity**: Critical - produces wrong outputs silently - **Scope**: Affects all 130+ model architectures in SGLang - **Duration**: Present since initial codebase (Jan 2024) ## The Solution ### Approach Add centralized validation in `loader.py` that: 1. **Tracks** which parameters are loaded during weight loading 2. **Validates** all required parameters were loaded 3. **Excludes** parameters that are legitimately missing: - Computed parameters (`rotary_emb.inv_freq`, `cos_sin_cache`) - Tied weights (`lm_head.weight` when tied to `embed_tokens.weight`) - Pipeline parallelism placeholders (`PPMissingLayer`) - Fused parameters (`qkv_proj` loaded from separate `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj`) 4. **Reports** missing weights with actionable error message ### Key Features - ✅ **Centralized**: Single validation point in `load_weights_and_postprocess()` - ✅ **Comprehensive**: Handles all known edge cases (tied weights, fused params, PP, etc.) - ✅ **Opt-in**: Controlled via `SGLANG_STRICT_WEIGHT_LOADING=1` environment variable - ✅ **Backward compatible**: Default behavior is warn-only (no breaking changes) - ✅ **Well-tested**: Unit tests cover all edge cases ## Implementation Details ### Files Changed #### 1. `python/sglang/srt/model_loader/weight_utils.py` Added `validate_loaded_weights()` function: ```python def validate_loaded_weights( model: torch.nn.Module, loaded_param_names: set, logger: logging.Logger, strict: bool = False, ) -> None: """Validate that all model parameters were loaded from checkpoint.""" # Get all params and exclude expected missing ones # (tied weights, computed params, PP layers, etc.) # Raise/warn if any required params weren't loaded ``` Handles these edge cases: - **Tied embeddings**: Skip `lm_head.weight` when `config.tie_word_embeddings=True` - **Computed params**: Skip `rotary_emb.*`, `projector` patterns - **Non-persistent buffers**: Skip buffers registered with `persistent=False` - **Pipeline parallelism**: Skip `PPMissingLayer` parameters #### 2. `python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py` Modified `load_weights_and_postprocess()`: ```python def load_weights_and_postprocess(model, weights, target_device): # Track which params are loaded by wrapping the iterator loaded_param_names = set() def tracking_iterator(weights_iter): for name, tensor in weights_iter: # Track this weight + handle fused param mapping loaded_param_names.add(name) yield name, tensor model.load_weights(tracking_iterator(weights)) # Validate completeness strict_mode = os.getenv("SGLANG_STRICT_WEIGHT_LOADING", "0") == "1" validate_loaded_weights(model, loaded_param_names, logger, strict=strict_mode) # ... rest of postprocessing ``` #### 3. `test/srt/test_missing_weights_validation.py` New unit tests: - ✅ All weights loaded (should pass) - ✅ Missing weights in non-strict mode (should warn) - ✅ Missing weights in strict mode (should raise) - ✅ Tied weights excluded (should pass) - ✅ Computed params excluded (should pass) - ✅ Partial loading detected (should raise) ## Usage ### Default Behavior (Non-Strict) ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /path/to/model ``` If weights are missing, you'll see: ``` WARNING: Weight loading validation failed! 2 parameters exist in the model but were not loaded from checkpoint. These parameters will have random values and cause incorrect outputs: ['model.layers.24.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight', 'model.layers.24.mlp.gate_up_proj.weight'] This usually indicates: 1. Model architecture doesn't match checkpoint (config.json mismatch) 2. Checkpoint is incomplete or from different model version 3. Custom model class has parameters not in HuggingFace format ``` ### Strict Mode (Recommended for Production) ```bash export SGLANG_STRICT_WEIGHT_LOADING=1 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /path/to/model ``` If weights are missing, server startup will **fail** with the above error message. ## Testing ### Unit Tests ```bash python -m pytest test/srt/test_missing_weights_validation.py -v ``` All tests pass, covering: - Normal loading (all weights present) - Missing weights detection - Edge case exclusions (tied weights, computed params) - Strict vs non-strict modes ### Integration Testing The validation automatically runs for all models loaded through SGLang. To test with a real model: ```bash # Non-strict (default) python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct # Strict mode SGLANG_STRICT_WEIGHT_LOADING=1 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct ``` ## Historical Context ### Git History Analysis - **Jan 2024** (commit `6b0af2853`): Original implementation had no validation - **Feb 2025** (commit `a3339d8ca`): Fixed bug with tied weights - symptom of missing validation - **May 2025** (commit `11553c1a3`): Added warning for *extra* weights in checkpoint - **Present**: Still no validation for *missing* weights (this PR fixes it) ### Why This Wasn't Caught Earlier 1. **Silent failure**: Random weights don't crash, just produce wrong outputs 2. **Edge case complexity**: Fused weights, tied embeddings, PP made validation tricky 3. **No user reports**: Most users load official checkpoints that match architectures 4. **vLLM heritage**: Inherited from vLLM codebase which also lacks this validation ## Migration Guide ### For Users No action needed! Validation defaults to warn-only mode. **Recommended**: Enable strict mode for production deployments: ```bash export SGLANG_STRICT_WEIGHT_LOADING=1 ``` ### For Developers If you maintain custom model classes, ensure your `load_weights()` method: 1. Loads all required parameters from the checkpoint 2. Properly handles fused parameters (qkv_proj, gate_up_proj) 3. Skips computed parameters (rotary embeddings) The validation will catch any issues during development! ## Performance Impact - **Negligible**: Validation runs once at model load time (not per inference) - **Memory**: Tracking set of parameter names (~few KB) - **Time**: O(num_parameters) iteration (~milliseconds for typical models) ## Future Work Potential enhancements (out of scope for this PR): - [ ] Validate parameter shapes match config.json - [ ] Check for NaN/Inf values in loaded weights - [ ] Verify checkpoint dtype matches config dtype - [ ] Detect quantization mismatches ## Related Issues This PR addresses the root cause of several potential issues: - Models loading with wrong layer counts - Custom architectures failing silently - Checkpoint version mismatches ## Checklist - [x] Code implements centralized validation - [x] All edge cases handled (tied weights, computed params, PP, fused weights) - [x] Unit tests added and passing - [x] Backward compatible (opt-in strict mode) - [x] Documentation in code comments - [x] Commit message explains context - [x] PR description comprehensive ## References - HuggingFace Transformers: Uses `strict=True` by default in `load_state_dict()` - PyTorch: `load_state_dict()` returns `(missing_keys, unexpected_keys)` - vLLM: Also lacks this validation (as of v0.6.3) --- **Ready for review!** 🎯 This is a minimal, focused change that fixes a critical silent bug while maintaining backward compatibility.

signal.title: [Feature] Realtime ASR: segment snapshots for bounded long-audio transcription
signal.text: <!-- Suggested PR title: [Feature] Realtime ASR: segment snapshots for bounded long-audio transcription --> ## Summary This PR adds an experimental, opt-in long-audio mode to the realtime ASR WebSocket endpoint. The new mode divides one long outer audio item into independent causal segments. While a segment is active, the server publishes replaceable transcript snapshots. At a confirmed acoustic boundary, the server transcribes the complete segment once without a transcript prefix and publishes that result as the authoritative final revision. PCM belonging to that segment is released only after this final request succeeds. ```text causal independent segments + replaceable active-segment previews + unprefixed authoritative segment finals + immutable completed segments ``` The existing cumulative, append-only realtime path remains the default. The new behavior requires both a server flag and an explicit client protocol opt-in. This PR does not add encoder-window reuse, a new multimodal cache, scheduler policy, cross-segment decoder prefixes, timestamps, forced alignment, or fuzzy text deduplication. ## Why The existing cumulative implementation resubmits all audio accumulated in the current item every two seconds. This preserves full acoustic context, but the per-request work and resident PCM grow with the session. Qwen3-ASR also has a 60-second default item limit, so a single long realtime item cannot continue indefinitely. The earlier rolling encoder-window prototype bounded this work, but it had a correctness ambiguity at every hard window transition: without audio-text alignment, the runtime cannot distinguish text repeated by newly received audio from text replayed by overlapping historical audio. A decoder prefix can therefore suppress a legitimate repetition, while text overlap removal can delete real speech. This PR uses a different correctness boundary: 1. Each acoustic segment owns a disjoint PCM range. 2. No transcript prefix crosses a completed segment boundary. 3. No text deduplication runs across segments. 4. The authoritative result always comes from the complete segment PCM and the adapter's base prompt. 5. Only authoritative segment text contributes to the outer completed transcript. This keeps long-session memory bounded without asking text heuristics to infer audio ownership. ## Protocol negotiation The server exposes the capability with: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B \ --asr-long-audio-strategy segment \ --asr-max-buffer-seconds 1800 \ --asr-max-resident-buffer-seconds 62 ``` The client selects snapshot semantics in `session.update`: ```json { "type": "session.update", "session": { "audio": { "input": { "format": {"type": "audio/pcm", "rate": 16000}, "transcription": { "model": "qwen3-asr", "language": "en", "partial_result_mode": "segment_snapshot_v1" }, "noise_reduction": null, "turn_detection": null } } } } ``` Both sides must opt in: | Server | Client | Result | |---|---|---| | `cumulative` | default | Existing append-only cumulative path | | `cumulative` | `segment_snapshot_v1` | Request rejected as unsupported | | `segment` | default | Existing cumulative path, still capped at 60 seconds | | `segment` | `segment_snapshot_v1`, supported language | Segment-snapshot path | | `segment` | `segment_snapshot_v1`, unsupported/unknown language | Request rejected before audio is accepted | Qwen3-ASR currently declares this capability only for English. The adapter owns the model-specific policy; the endpoint owns the generic protocol and lifecycle. ## Snapshot events An intermediate request publishes the complete visible text for the active segment: ```json { "type": "conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.segment_snapshot", "item_id": "item_123", "content_index": 0, "segment_id": 7, "revision": 14, "text": "complete provisional text for this segment", "is_final": false } ``` The client replaces the previous text for the same `(item_id, segment_id)` when it receives a newer revision. It must not append snapshot text as a delta. At an internal boundary or outer commit, the same event type closes the segment: ```json { "type": "conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.segment_snapshot", "item_id": "item_123", "content_index": 0, "segment_id": 7, "revision": 15, "text": "authoritative final text for this segment", "is_final": true } ``` The existing `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed` event is still emitted exactly once after the outer item is committed. Its transcript is the ordered join of authoritative segment finals. The default session response omits `partial_result_mode`, so existing clients do not see a wire-schema change unless they request this mode. ## Processing flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[PCM append] --> B[Resample to model rate] B --> C[Absolute-offset AudioBuffer] C --> D[Causal segmenter observes new frames] D --> E{Boundary ready?} E -- No --> F[Decode visible active-segment PCM] F --> G[Apply current segment decoder prefix] G --> H[Publish complete provisional snapshot] E -- Yes --> I[Clamp request to exclusive segment boundary] I --> J[Decode complete segment with base prompt only] J --> K{Final succeeded?} K -- No --> L[Keep PCM and fail the request] K -- Yes --> M[Publish authoritative final snapshot] M --> N[Discard completed PCM] N --> O[Start next segment with empty transcript state] ``` ### Boundary policy for Qwen3-ASR - Preview cadence: 2 seconds. - Earliest silence boundary search: 52 seconds into the active segment. - Minimum qualifying silence: 500 ms. - Analysis frame: 30 ms. - Hard maximum segment duration: 60 seconds. - Silence detection: adaptive RMS derived from the segment's early quiet level; no new runtime dependency is introduced. A possible silence tail is withheld from preview requests until speech resumes. If the pause is long enough, resumed speech confirms an exclusive boundary. A short pause is released back into the current segment. If no qualifying pause appears, the 60-second hard maximum closes the segment. Exact digital silence is finalized without invoking the model, avoiding empty audio-feature requests and silence hallucinations. ## State and failure invariants - Segment boundaries are expressed on one absolute PCM byte timeline. - Audio after a confirmed boundary is never visible to the previous segment. - A provisional snapshot never enters the authoritative transcript. - Repeated provisional text is suppressed without incrementing the revision. - A final snapshot permanently closes its segment id. - PCM is compacted only after the authoritative final is available. - `None`, an exception, or `finish_reason=length` on a final request does not retire PCM, advance the segment id, or emit outer completion. - Commit-time failure emits the existing transcription failure event. - Append-time failure closes the socket because the outer item is not yet client-visible. - Clear and item rollover reset PCM, segment detector state, revisions, and transcript state together. - Total accepted duration and resident PCM are independent limits. ## Qwen ragged-audio batching fix While testing heterogeneous realtime sessions, a separate pre-existing Qwen3-ASR issue became reproducible on `origin/main`: concurrent requests whose Whisper features had different padded time widths failed at `torch.cat([item.feature ...])` and terminated the scheduler. This PR fixes that at the audio-tower input boundary. A generic `pack_audio_features()` helper uses each item's attention mask to concatenate only valid mel frames and returns the corresponding per-item lengths. The Qwen model calls this helper before invoking its existing audio tower. This scoped fix: - keeps mixed-width audio requests in one encoder call; - preserves the existing equal-width fallback when masks are absent; - does not add model-specific scheduler behavior; - does not change vision batching; - does not introduce encoder-window cache items. Four heterogeneous native HTTP requests that previously completed `0/4` on a fresh main server completed `4/4` with the packed-frame path, and the server remained healthy. ## Request identity Server-built ASR requests now provide an `mm_hashes` value derived from the raw WAV bytes. Whisper padding can map different short waveforms to the same padded feature shape, so raw-audio identity prevents an unrelated cached embedding from being reused. This is a request-identity correction for ASR. It is not an encoder-window cache and does not add cache lifecycle or scheduler policy. ## Results ### Long-form quality and protocol Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B` GPU: NVIDIA RTX 4090 Transport: realtime WebSocket, 2-second PCM appends, one outer commit | Case | Duration | Result | Final segments | Snapshots | Flood wall | |---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:| | Earnings22 EXCOF | 1686.7s | WER 0.1081 on the final packed-frame run | 31 | 856 | 97.990s | | repeat120 | 119.4s | WER 0, 189/189 words, all 9/9 repetitions | 3 | 60 | 6.121s | | LongLibriHeavy | 59.8s | WER 0.12778, no terminal-silence segment | 1 | 30 | 4.035s | | LongLibriHeavy | 93.4s | WER 0.05851 | 2 | 47 | 5.851s | | Qwen English demo | 15.05s | Completed cleanly | 1 | 8 | 1.020s latest smoke | | Digital silence | 125.0s | Empty transcript, zero backend ASR requests | 3 | 3 | 0.059s | The four fresh Earnings22 architecture runs had WER values from 0.11143 to 0.11546, with median 0.11321. The final packed-frame run produced WER 0.1081. Near-greedy Qwen output is not byte-deterministic across fresh servers, so the distribution and missing/repetition checks are the acceptance evidence rather than one exact long-form string. All snapshot runs satisfied: - monotonic revisions per segment; - no snapshot after a segment final; - no append-only delta events in snapshot mode; - outer completed text equals the ordered authoritative finals; - full opening and closing coverage; - server health after every request. The latest post-refactor GPU smoke also checked the wire contents directly. All seven provisional Qwen-demo revisions contained the complete active-segment text, had no duplicated boundary whitespace, and the authoritative final was byte-identical to the pre-refactor result. ### Existing path compared with main Fresh current and main servers were compared before enabling snapshot mode: | Transport | Case | Output comparison | Current | Main | |---|---|---|---:|---:| | HTTP JSON | 15s Qwen | Byte-identical | 0.337s | 0.352s | | HTTP JSON | 30s LLH | Byte-identical | 0.506s | 0.453s | | HTTP SSE | 15s Qwen | Byte-identical | 0.832s | 0.930s | | HTTP SSE | 30s LLH | Pairwise WER 0.0122 | 1.671s | 1.618s | | WebSocket | 15s Qwen | Byte-identical | 0.818s | 0.809s | | WebSocket | 30s LLH | Pairwise WER 0.0120 | 1.651s | 1.579s | The 30-second streaming differences were one occurrence of `that` and dash versus comma formatting, in opposite directions across transports. This is consistent with fresh-run model variation rather than a fixed branch omission. ### Heterogeneous paced sessions The final packed implementation was tested with different native clips rather than repeated copies of one audio file: | Workload | Result | |---|---| | 4 heterogeneous HTTP requests | 4/4 completed in 1.663s; server healthy | | 4 heterogeneous paced realtime sessions | 4/4 completed in 94.477s | | 8 heterogeneous paced realtime sessions, 15s to 291s | 8/8 completed in 292.844s; no duplicate runs | Seven of eight paced outputs were normalized-exact against the preceding pad-based implementation. Brian Cox varied only at `they` versus `they're` and `50` versus `fifty`; both runs had the same dataset WER, 0.07966. ### Encoder-cache A/B A separate POC tested completed encoder-window reuse only for provisional previews, while keeping the same unprefixed authoritative finals. | Workload | Cache-off representation | Cache on | Cache-only change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Earnings22 median, 3 fresh runs | 95.142s | 94.911s | 0.24% faster | | 4 heterogeneous realtime sessions | 94.351s | 94.600s | 0.26% slower | | 8 heterogeneous flood sessions | 29.620s | 31.055s | 4.84% slower | The cache-only result did not meet the proposed 5% single-stream or 10% to 15% concurrency acceptance bar. The POC is therefore not included in this PR. ## Implementation scope | Area | Change | |---|---| | `realtime/protocol.py` | Adds explicit snapshot negotiation and event schema | | `realtime/session.py` | Owns WS negotiation, item lifecycle, revisions, and wire events | | `realtime/asr_processor.py` | Builds, executes, and commits cumulative or segment transcription steps | | `realtime/audio_buffer.py` | Keeps resident PCM on an absolute byte timeline and compacts finalized audio | | `realtime/audio_segmentation.py` | Implements causal held-tail silence boundaries and hard limits | | `streaming_asr.py` | Shares stateless generation and existing cumulative reconciliation helpers | | transcription adapters | Declares model sample rate, chunk cadence, language capability, and segment policy | | `multimodal/mm_utils.py` | Adds generic masked audio-feature packing | | `models/qwen3_asr.py` | Calls the generic packer at the Qwen audio-tower boundary | | `server_args.py` | Adds the long-audio strategy and independent resident-buffer limit | There are no net changes relative to main in `mm_schedule.py`, `schedule_batch.py`, `tokenizer_manager.py`, multimodal processors, or Radix/MM cache internals. ## Validation Latest local checks on commit `843f02b828`: ```text 23 focused CPU tests passed 7 parameterized subtests passed py_compile passed git diff --check passed PR-file pre-commit passed: AST, isort, Ruff, Black, codespell, runtime ratchets, and CI registry validation ``` GPU checks used native audio from the Qwen3-ASR demo, LongLibriHeavy, Earnings22, and TED-LIUM long-form sources. The latest focused smoke covered the post-refactor snapshot wire output; the broader long-form and concurrency matrices are reported above. ## Limits and follow-ups - Snapshot mode is experimental, server opt-in, client opt-in, and currently English-only for Qwen3-ASR. - Clients requesting this mode must implement replacement by segment revision. - The default item cap remains 60 seconds. Operators must raise `--asr-max-buffer-seconds` for a longer single outer item. - Each authoritative segment requires one complete unprefixed decode. This is the correctness mechanism and may create a boundary-time decode burst. - Adaptive RMS is deliberately conservative and is not a general VAD model. - There are no timestamps, forced alignment, cross-segment language-model state, or model-native streaming encoder/decoder state. - Validation is currently bounded to Qwen3-ASR-0.6B on one RTX 4090; it does not establish universal boundaries or capacity for every model, language, or GPU. - Encoder reuse can be revisited separately if future heterogeneous production traces show encoder work dominates, but the measured cache-only POC does not justify adding that complexity here. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31919055177](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31919055177)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31919053885](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31919053885)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [KV Cache] Use exact page demand for paged prefill eviction
signal.text: ## Motivation `alloc_paged_token_slots_extend()` currently estimates its eviction target as the total number of extend tokens plus one full page per request. This ignores free slots in each request's existing partial tail page and can evict reusable prefixes even when the pending allocation already fits. For example, with `page_size=64`, `prefix_len=63`, and `seq_len=64`, the allocator consumes no new page. The current estimate requests 65 tokens of capacity, while the exact requirement is zero. The allocator already uses `get_num_new_pages()` to validate the actual page consumption. This PR uses the same page accounting for the preceding tree-cache eviction decision. This is a narrow extraction of the exact extend-eviction portion previously included in #25500. It is also complementary to #33091: this PR fixes the requested allocation capacity, while #33091 changes when unified-memory eviction can stop after shared capacity becomes available. ## Modifications - Compute the exact number of new pages from the existing CPU prefix and sequence-length tensors before paged prefill eviction. - Convert that count to allocator capacity with `num_new_pages * page_size`. - Keep every allocator interface unchanged. Allocators continue to recompute their page count defensively before consuming pages. - Add CPU regression coverage for: - a page-boundary matrix over page sizes 16, 64, and 128; - a simulated `RadixCache` case that verifies a cached prefix survives a zero-new-page extend; - a mixed batch whose exact allocation requires only one new page and only evicts its capacity shortfall. This does not change paged decode accounting, scheduler admission budgeting, the eviction policy, or allocation kernels. ### Open design question The caller now computes the page count for eviction, while allocators recompute it defensively for allocation safety. On the local CPU benchmark below this costs about 9-10 us per paged extend call and avoids changing the allocator API, including out-of-tree implementations. Would maintainers prefer to keep this compatibility-first duplication, or standardize an optional precomputed page-count argument across every allocator? I intentionally did not add allocator capability flags in this draft. ## Accuracy Tests Target regression: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_paged_alloc_extend_eviction.py ``` ```text 3 passed, 15 subtests passed ``` The 15 page-boundary subtests cover page sizes 16, 64, and 128, with cases for reuse within a partial page, exact free capacity, one- and multi-page crossings, and a reused request with no new tokens. The `RadixCache` regression inserts a 64-token evictable prefix as an unrelated reusable victim before running the `prefix_len=63`, `seq_len=64` extend. It verifies that the cache size stays at 64, `free_segment()` is not called, and the full cached prefix still matches after allocation. Adjacent allocator regression: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_paged_alloc_extend_eviction.py \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_swa_alloc_extend_page_estimation.py \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_multi_ended_allocator.py \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hisparse_allocator.py \ -k 'not TestO3FusedAllocBind' ``` ```text 70 passed, 11 deselected, 15 subtests passed ``` `TestO3FusedAllocBind` was excluded locally because its unrelated Triton JIT tests require Python development headers that are not installed on the test host. The changed path is CPU-only and will also run in the registered `base-a-test-cpu` suite. The change does not alter model math or allocator output. The tests assert that the output is preserved and that no new keyword argument is forwarded to the allocator. ## Speed Tests and Profiling `get_num_new_pages()` was measured on an Intel Core Ultra 7 265K with PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, using 9 repeats of 1,000 calls (`page_size=64`): | Batch size | Median per call | | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 9.31 us | | 8 | 9.67 us | | 32 | 9.91 us | | 128 | 10.05 us | The deterministic regression cases show the eviction difference directly: | Case | Previous shortfall | Exact shortfall | | --- | ---: | ---: | | `prefix=63`, `seq=64`, no free capacity | 65 tokens | 0 tokens | | Mixed batch, 32 free tokens | 353 tokens | 32 tokens | No general throughput improvement is claimed. The expected benefit is retaining reusable prefixes under page-level cache pressure. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing API or configuration change.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31891562985](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31891562985)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31891562818](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31891562818)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Fix] Delegate shared-read-ends declarations in wrapper attention backends
signal.text: Follow-up to #34916. Three things: name the read-end concept after what it is, make wrapper backends answer for the child that actually reads, and cut the fence tests down to what they guard. ### `SharedReadBoundary` -> `SharedReadEnds` The values now say where they sit relative to the two init hooks, instead of leaving the reader to infer it: ```python PRE_REPLAY = auto() # After the init_forward_metadata_out_graph IN_REPLAY = auto() # After the init_forward_metadata_in_graph POST_REPLAY = auto() # Metadata snapshot not implemented UNKNOWN = auto() # not audited -> coarse whole-forward fence ``` `POST_REPLAY` is worth calling out: it is not a design state, it marks a backend whose metadata snapshot is incomplete. Naming it that way is what makes the remaining users of it auditable. Also `shared_read_boundary()` -> `shared_read_ends()`, `_resolve_shared_read_boundary` -> `_resolve_shared_read_ends`, and the local in the resolver -> `declared` (the backend's declaration, as distinct from the resolved point the function returns). ### Wrapper backends now delegate the declaration A wrapper drives one or more child backends but inherited the base declaration and answered for itself. Fixed for all four, via a new `SharedReadEnds.max_of` (the record must cover every child, so the latest end wins): | wrapper | | |---|---| | `HybridAttnBackend` | delegates to `_select_backend(mode)` | | `TboAttnBackend` | max over primary + children | | `HybridLinearAttnBackend` | max over `attn_backend_list` | | `MiniMaxHybridAttnBackend` | max over sparse + dense | This is a real fence bug wherever a wrapped child overrides the default. Concretely, `TboAttnBackend` wrapping `DeepseekV4AttnBackend`: the child declares `POST_REPLAY` for non-DSPARK target verify, the wrapper reported `IN_REPLAY`, so the scheduler was released while the child was still reading across graph segments. Behavior is otherwise unchanged -- children that inherit the default all report `IN_REPLAY`, so the aggregate matches what the wrapper returned before. ### Fence tests: 136 -> 80 lines Dropped the `execute()` harness (fake backend, `ShapeKey`, `PPProxyTensors`, `load_batch`, `device_module`) and the three cases built on it -- ~60 lines guarding six lines of `if` wiring. What is left tests the two methods directly: a five-row table over the resolver, and both branches of `_publish_read_done`. The backend stub is now `create_autospec(AttentionBackend, instance=True)` rather than a `SimpleNamespace`. A hand-rolled stub supplies whatever name the caller asks for, so a renamed method leaves a stale call site in the runner green in CI and broken at runtime; spec'd against the real ABC it fails in the test. Not covered anymore: that the pre-replay record lands before `backend.replay()`. That ordering assertion was the only thing needing the full harness. ### Not in this PR - The default stays `IN_REPLAY`. Moving a backend to `PRE_REPLAY` is a per-backend optimization worth one audit each, not a global flip. - `_resolve_shared_read_ends` still answers two questions (does this phase own the publish, and where do the reads end). Splitting the ownership predicate out is the next step. - The `IN_REPLAY -> PRE_REPLAY` fallback demotes to a point earlier than the declared end; `POST_REPLAY` is the sound direction. Left as a TODO in code -- it is only reachable under `--debug-cuda-graph` and on platforms without external-event support, where the barrier is off anyway. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31915127758](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31915127758)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31915127678](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31915127678)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] NEXTN (MTP) + structured output (xgrammar) crashes scheduler on Mamba-hybrid model (Qwen3.5-397B) — TypeError 'NoneType' in prepare_mamba_track_for_verify (sm_100)
signal.text: ## Describe the bug With `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN` enabled on a Mamba-hybrid model (`Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8`), sending a request with **structured output** (`response_format` = `json_schema` or `json_object`) crashes **all TP scheduler ranks** and brings the server down (`/health` 200 → 000). Notably: - The structured output itself is **functionally correct** — for one request the server returns schema-valid JSON, then the scheduler dies immediately after. - Happens **regardless of `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`** (true or false). - **Without** speculative decoding, structured output works fine. **With** NEXTN but **without** structured output, chat / tool-calling / high-concurrency all work fine and stably. This looks adjacent to #26957 (NEXTN + hybrid-SWA + sm_100 crash, fixed 2026-06-09), but is triggered specifically by the **structured-output (grammar) + spec-verify + mamba-track** interaction rather than `trtllm_mha` attention. ## Reproduction Launch (8x B200, sm_100): ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 --tp 8 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --port 30000 ``` Request (crashes the server; `enable_thinking` true or false both crash): ```bash curl http://localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8", "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Extract: John Smith is 42 years old and lives in Seoul. Return JSON."}], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 256, "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}, "response_format": {"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":"person","schema":{ "type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"age":{"type":"integer"},"city":{"type":"string"}}, "required":["name","age","city"],"additionalProperties":false}}} }' ``` ## Observed - Response (when it returns): `{"name":"John Smith","age":42,"city":"Seoul"}` (schema-valid). - Immediately after, all TP ranks log: ``` [TP*] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last): ... File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py", line 1025, in forward_batch_generation File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py", line 1237, in verify File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py", line 318, in eagle_prepare_for_verify File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/spec_utils.py", line 550, in prepare_mamba_track_for_verify TypeError: 'NoneType' object cannot be interpreted as an integer ``` - Server dies; subsequent requests get connection refused. ## Expected Structured output (grammar-constrained decoding) should coexist with NEXTN speculative decoding on Mamba-hybrid models, or at minimum fail the request gracefully without killing the scheduler. ## Environment - SGLang: `0.5.13.post2.dev332+g486ec150d` (main, installed for Qwen3.5 support) - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` (Mamba-hybrid MoE), TP=8 - GPU: NVIDIA B200 (sm_100); torch 2.11+cu13, flashinfer 0.6.12, sgl-kernel 0.4.3 - attention_backend `triton`, moe_runner_backend `flashinfer_trtllm`, `--mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer` ## Workaround Route structured-output requests to a non-speculative endpoint (disable NEXTN for `response_format` json requests). Chat / tool / concurrency on NEXTN are unaffected.

signal.title: HiCache: HiMambaRadixCache crashes with 'Destination indices must be a CUDA tensor' on Qwen3.5/3.6
signal.text: ## Bug: HiCache crashes on hybrid Mamba+Attention models (Qwen3.5-397B, Qwen3.6-27B) ### Environment - SGLang version: latest main (as of 2026-04-29) - Hardware: RTX PRO 6000 (SM120 Blackwell) - Models: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (TP=4), Qwen3.6-27B (TP=1) - Both NVFP4 quantized, FP8 KV cache ### Reproduction Enable `--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 2.0 --hicache-io-backend kernel --hicache-write-policy write_through` on either Qwen3.5-397B or Qwen3.6-27B. The server starts, allocates host memory for both hierarchical KV cache and hierarchical Mamba cache: ``` [TP0] Allocating 14.06 GB host memory for hierarchical KV cache. [TP0] Allocating 12.63 GB host memory for hierarchical Mamba cache (layout=layer_first). ``` CUDA graphs capture successfully. On the first actual inference request, the scheduler crashes: ``` [TP0] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last): RuntimeError: Destination indices must be a CUDA tensor ``` All TP ranks hit the same error simultaneously. The server restarts and crash-loops. ### Root cause (hypothesis) `HiMambaRadixCache` (which is correctly selected for these hybrid models) appears to have an index tensor placement bug in its cache transfer path. During eviction or restore between L1 (GPU) and L2 (host), destination indices are on CPU when the CUDA kernel expects them on GPU. This is distinct from the `"HiRadixCache only supports MHA and MLA yet"` error (which we also hit on DeepSeek-V4-Flash due to its compressed attention, tracked in #23639). The Mamba path is reached correctly via `HiMambaRadixCache`, but the transfer kernel fails. ### Working model for comparison MiniMax-M2.7 (230B, Lightning Attention, no Mamba layers) works perfectly with HiCache. Same flags, same hardware. Cache hit rate climbs to 95% at 18K tokens. This confirms the bug is specific to the Mamba cache path, not HiCache in general. ### What we tested | Model | Attention Type | HiCache Result | |-------|---------------|----------------| | MiniMax-M2.7 (230B) | Lightning Attention | Works, 95% cache hit at 18K tokens | | Qwen3.5-397B | Hybrid Mamba+Attention | Crashes: "Destination indices must be a CUDA tensor" | | Qwen3.6-27B | Hybrid Mamba+Attention | Same crash | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Compressed MLA + SWA | "HiRadixCache only supports MHA and MLA yet" (tracked in #23639) | ### Workaround Disable HiCache (`--enable-hierarchical-cache` removed) for affected models.

signal.title: [Feature] Load Balance Refactor for DP-Attention
signal.text: ### Motivation Current data parallel attention routing and load balance have the following problems: - Confusing naming: In PD mode, the `round_robin` balance method is not round robin. It should be called "follow_bootstrap_room" (see [code](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/88f3de25148d620f10eec3f9c8fdde7b4e695750/python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py#L530)), since it uses bootstrap_room to assign target ranks. - Limited load balancing methods: It leads to load imbalance in many cases. - In PD mode, it only supports "follow_bootstrap_room" method. - In non-PD model, the DataParallelController (DPC) only supports round robin or balancing by number of requests, but does not support balancing by the number of tokens. - Limited compatibility with external routing: we would like to use the the rust router (model gateway) to directly assign dp ranks but it is not supported. ### Tasks 1. Fix confusing names - Introduce a new load balancing method, "follow_bootstrap_room". Move the current [code](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b5d9fc873bf238ff1172b8050dfa1fbb665f0f4d/python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py#L517-L531) to this new method instead of incorrectly reusing "round_robin". - To make things backward compatible, we can change the default value of "--load-balance-method" to "auto" and set it in `ServerArgs:__post_init__` with the following rules: - If it is non-PD, set it to "round_robin". - If it is PD, set P workers to "follow_bootstrap_room" and set D workers to "round_robin". - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/16110 - Remove the balance method "decode_round_robin" and all its related code. It is not useful anymore. Basically revert this PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/15164. - Remove the argument `"--prefill-round-robin-balance"` and its related code. It is very confusing. If we want to do the check. We should let the router do the check. 2. Support methods other than "follow_bootstrap_room" in PD mode. We want to support the following two mode: a) The router directly add prefill and decode dp ranks in `GenerateReqInput`. In this case, DPC just follows the assignment. b) The router does not assign dp ranks and DPC assign prefill ranks. In this case, the decode worker needs an additional communication to know the prefill dp rank. See (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/14726). In this way, we can support flexible balance method in prefill worker. The old behavior falls in the category of (a), since router knows bootstrap_room, it will directly set prefill dp rank in `GenerateReqInput` as `bootstrap_room % dp_size`. 3. DP controller refactors - Unify the naming. Rename `shortest_queue` -> `total_requests`. Rename `minimum_tokens` -> `total_tokens`. These are the two basic methods that balance by the total number of requests or total number of tokens. - Implement both `total_requests` and `total_tokens` correctly in DPC with the piggyback load reporting. Simplify the implementation. For example, this function https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/88f3de25148d620f10eec3f9c8fdde7b4e695750/python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py#L98 is over complicated. We do not need to do ahead-of-time planning. We can simply do the following: a) when we get piggyback load report from a worker, we forcibly update the load of the worker. b). For each new request, we dispatch it to the worker with minimal load and increment the load of that worker by one. - Correctly set the default balance method with the guideline below: - For prefill, we typically use balance by total_tokens or cache aware - For decode, we look at the limiting resources. If KV cache is enough and latency requirement is tight, balance by total_requests (this is the normal case for online serving). If KV cache is very limited, balance by total_tokens. In the future, we might explore cache aware as well. 4. External Scheduling - [x] Support external assigned DP rank with router. - [ ] Support dp-rank aware load balancing with other instance-level load balance strategies, e.g., cache aware. Related Issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/13052

signal.title: [Feature] dLLM performance optimization in prefill and batching
signal.text: ### Checklist - [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation Recently, we did a performance calibration of dLLM efficiency with speculative decoding. The majority of the work is done by Lingxiao Yang @eroship from ZLab@UCSD. In short, we found there is a huge gap of (long prefill) in dLLM and batching with speculative decoding, where the dLLM should be more efficient than speculative decoding because it does not need drafting. #### Why do we compare with the speculative decoding? 1. [similar usage] block dLLM and spec decoding are both accelerations for latency-sensitive tasks; 2. [same complexity] When we control the block size in dLLM and token candidate number in spec decoding, the verification/decode complexity is the same in both cases; 3. [refer to mature implementation] spec decoding is mature in SGLang, and we need to calibrate the long prefill and batching implementation of dLLM with spec decoding based on reason 1&2 above. #### Two optimization opportunities The two important performance optimizations to be done: - [ ] Longer/flexible prefill chunk size. Currently, all prefill and decode blocks share the same chunk size, like 32, which is inefficient in the long prefill case. - [ ] Fine-grained early exit of batching. Now the requests in a batch that end earlier cannot exit the decode chunk before all requests in the batch finish the decoding process of the entire chunk. We open-sourced the code for performance tracking. Lingxiao will share the code link below, as well as the performance gap analysis with evidence in two separate issues: 1. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24645 2. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24646 ### Related resources _No response_

signal.title: [Bug]
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug When launching a prefill server with --enable-prefill-cp (prefill context parallel) for a WNA16-quantized MoE model (e.g., Kimi K2.5), the server crashes during initialization with the following error: NotImplementedError: Runner backend MoeRunnerBackend.MARLIN requires a fused func for a2a backend deepep, but none is registered. Workaround Attempted (Not Working) Adding --moe-a2a-backend none to the launch command does not fix the issue. The flag is silently overridden. After tracing the code, the root cause is in server_args.py (~line 2134): when --enable-prefill-cp is used together with an MLA-based model (e.g., DeepSeek V3 / Kimi K2.5), moe_a2a_backend is unconditionally forced to "deepep", regardless of what the user explicitly sets: # server_args.py if self.enable_prefill_cp and self.use_mla_backend(): ... self.moe_a2a_backend = "deepep" # overrides user's --moe-a2a-backend none This means the user-provided --moe-a2a-backend none has no effect. Root Cause The conflict is between two components: Prefill CP + MLA forces moe_a2a_backend = "deepep" for correctness reasons (in server_args.py). WNA16 quantization (via Compressed Tensors) automatically selects CompressedTensorsWNA16MarlinMoEMethod, which creates MoeRunner(MoeRunnerBackend.MARLIN, ...). In FusedOpPool, the ("deepep", "marlin") combination has no registered fused function (only ("none", "marlin") exists in marlin.py), causing the NotImplementedError. Relevant call stack summary: server_args.py: moe_a2a_backend forced to "deepep" due to --enable-prefill-cp + MLA → compressed_tensors_wNa16_moe.py: creates MoeRunner(MoeRunnerBackend.MARLIN, ...) → runner.py: FusedOpPool.get_fused_func("deepep", "marlin") → None → raise NotImplementedError(...) Either: The ("deepep", "marlin") fused function is registered so that Marlin MoE works with DeepEP all-to-all, or A clear early error is raised stating that WNA16/Marlin quantization is not compatible with --enable-prefill-cp (which requires DeepEP), rather than failing with a cryptic internal error. Suggested Fix Register a @register_fused_func("deepep", "marlin") function in sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/marlin.py that handles DeepEPNormalDispatchOutput (used in prefill/high-throughput mode) and adapts it to call fused_marlin_moe with the pre-dispatched tokens. Alternatively, a short-term fix in server_args.py could detect the Marlin/WNA16 quantization and raise an informative error (or skip the deepep override) when --enable-prefill-cp is used with an incompatible quantization scheme. ### Reproduction NotImplementedError: MoeRunnerBackend.MARLIN requires a fused func for a2a backend deepep when using --enable-prefill-cp with WNA16-quantized MoE model When launching a prefill server with --enable-prefill-cp (prefill context parallel) for a WNA16-quantized MoE model (e.g., Kimi K2.5), --moe-a2a-backend none； --enable-prefill-context-parallel --attention-backend fa3 --attn-cp-size 8 ### Environment Model: Kimi K2.5 (uses DeepseekV3ForCausalLM as language model) Quantization: WNA16 via Compressed Tensors (CompressedTensorsWNA16MarlinMoEMethod) Launch args include: --enable-prefill-cp, --disaggregation-mode prefill SGLang version: (custom build from /sgl-workspace/sglang)

signal.title: gRPC mode: --enable-metrics error message cites wrong servicer version (≥0.5.3 → should be ≥0.5.5); v0.5.13 image ships 0.5.4 and fails to boot
signal.text: ## Summary In gRPC mode, `--enable-metrics` requires `smg-grpc-servicer` to expose the `on_request_manager_ready` hook (that hook is what starts the HTTP sidecar serving `/metrics`). `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/grpc_server.py` guards this, but **the required version it reports is wrong**, and the **released `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.11`/`v0.5.13` images ship a servicer that lacks the hook**, so `--grpc-mode --enable-metrics` raises `RuntimeError` at startup out of the box. ## Bug A — wrong version in the error message + comment `serve_grpc()` in `grpc_server.py` says: ``` raise RuntimeError( "--enable-metrics requires smg-grpc-servicer ≥ 0.5.3 (the version " "that accepts 'on_request_manager_ready'); ..." ) ``` (and the comment above it: "Older smg-grpc-servicer releases (≤ 0.5.2) ... ≥ 0.5.3 ... accepts on_request_manager_ready") This is incorrect. Verified against `smg-grpc-servicer==0.5.4` (the version bundled in the `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.13` image): ```python import inspect from smg_grpc_servicer.sglang.server import serve_grpc print(list(inspect.signature(serve_grpc).parameters)) # -> ['server_args', 'model_info'] print("on_request_manager_ready" in inspect.signature(serve_grpc).parameters) # -> False ``` So 0.5.4 does **not** accept the hook. Empirically the first version that does is **0.5.5** (confirmed working: a `0.5.5` install starts the `:30001` sidecar). A user who follows the error's own advice and installs 0.5.3 or 0.5.4 will still crash. **Fix:** change `≥ 0.5.3` to `≥ 0.5.5` in both the `RuntimeError` message and the comment in `grpc_server.py`. ## Bug B — released images can't serve grpc-mode metrics out of the box `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.13` bundles `smg-grpc-servicer==0.5.4` + `smg-grpc-proto==0.4.9`, so `--grpc-mode --enable-metrics` hits the `RuntimeError` above and the server won't start. Root cause is release timing, not a code decision: - The image's pip layer was built **2026-06-11 ~10:05 UTC** (per `docker history`). - `smg-grpc-servicer 0.5.5` and `smg-grpc-proto 0.4.10` (which 0.5.5 requires, `proto>=0.4.10`) were published **2026-06-11 ~16:10 UTC** — ~6h later. - `pyproject.toml` pins `smg-grpc-servicer>=0.5.0` (newest-wins), so the layer resolved to the newest then-available: 0.5.4 + 0.4.9, which lacks the hook. **Suggested fix:** bump the pin to `smg-grpc-servicer>=0.5.5` (which transitively pulls `smg-grpc-proto>=0.4.10`) and/or rebuild the published image now that those packages exist, so `--grpc-mode --enable-metrics` works out of the box. ## Repro ```bash docker run --rm --entrypoint python3 lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.13 -c \ "import inspect; from smg_grpc_servicer.sglang.server import serve_grpc; \ print(list(inspect.signature(serve_grpc).parameters))" # ['server_args', 'model_info'] <- no on_request_manager_ready # => launch_server --grpc-mode --enable-metrics raises RuntimeError at startup ``` ## Environment - Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.13` (also affects `v0.5.11`) - `smg-grpc-servicer==0.5.4`, `smg-grpc-proto==0.4.9`, `grpcio==1.81.0` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [AMD][CI] Add GPT-OSS perf benchmarks to the ROCm 7.2 nightly
signal.text:
## Motivation GPT-OSS is one of the models in the reported ROCm 7.2 + Triton 3.7 slowdown, and it has no throughput coverage on AMD — DeepSeek-V4 is the only affected model that does. Rebased onto latest `main` to clear the conflict in `nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`, which came from [#34643](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34643) editing the same MI30x GPT-OSS job. Kimi-K3 has been dropped from this PR so it covers GPT-OSS only. ## Modifications Add one benchmark per architecture, each sweeping batch sizes 1/8/16/64 (plus a leading warmup) at ISL 4096 / OSL 512 through `bench_one_batch_server`: | Test | Hardware and precision | Models | |---|---|---| | `test_gpt_oss_perf_mi35x.py` | MI35x (gfx950) TP8, native MXFP4 + AITER | `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, `openai/gpt-oss-120b` | | `test_gpt_oss_perf_amd.py` | MI30x (gfx942) TP8, bf16 conversions | `lmsys/gpt-oss-20b-bf16`, `lmsys/gpt-oss-120b-bf16` | Launch arguments match the corresponding accuracy tests, so a throughput change points at the serving stack rather than at a different recipe. The checkpoints differ per architecture for the same reason the accuracy tests already split them: MI30x does not serve the MXFP4 checkpoints natively, which is why the `lmsys/*-bf16` conversions exist. **Both run as a step on the GPT-OSS accuracy job that already serves the same models**, not as separate jobs: - MI30x → `nightly-accuracy-8-gpu-rocm720` - MI35x → `nightly-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-rocm720` That avoids paying container setup and the weight cache a second time. Because no new jobs are created, the workflow diff is just the two added steps — no `job_select` options and no `check-all-jobs` dependencies change. Also lift the duplicated cost-free AMD markdown renderer into `generate_simple_markdown_report()` in `nightly_bench_utils.py`; both new tests use the same output schema as the existing AMD perf sweeps. The tests report benchmark data and fail on launch or benchmark errors. They intentionally carry no throughput thresholds: there is no nightly history yet from which to set defensible baselines. The numbers below are the first data points toward those baselines. DeepSeek-V4 gating is separate in [#34640](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34640). ## Validation run **[nightly-test-amd-rocm720 run 31850998638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31850998638) — success**, dispatched against this branch: ```bash gh workflow run nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml \ --ref cursor/amd-gpt-oss-kimi-k3-perf-tests-7e6c \ -f job_filter='nightly-accuracy-8-gpu-rocm720,nightly-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-rocm720' \ -f continue_on_error=true ``` The filter selected exactly the two jobs this PR touches and skipped the other 45. All four steps passed, with each new perf step running after its existing accuracy step in the same job: | Job | Accuracy step | Perf step | |---|---|---| | `nightly-accuracy-8-gpu-rocm720` | success, 11.7 min | success, 6.5 min | | `nightly-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-rocm720` | success, 18.4 min | success, 3.9 min | ## Accuracy Tests No model or kernel changes; the new tests reuse existing serving recipes and add no accuracy assertions. Both GPT-OSS accuracy steps still pass in the validation run, unaffected by the added perf step. Static validation completed: - registered-test registry validation, and both suites resolve to exactly one file - workflow YAML parsing, duplicate job-name check, and no stale dispatch option or `check-all-jobs` dependency - Ruff, Black, isort, codespell - no Kimi-K3 reference remains in the AMD tests or this workflow ## Speed Tests and Profiling Measured in the validation run above, at ISL 4096 / OSL 512, TP8. > These are **two independent baselines, not a head-to-head comparison.** The two rows of the matrix differ in both silicon and checkpoint precision — MI35x is gfx950 serving native MXFP4, MI30x is gfx942 serving the bf16 conversions — so each table gates its own architecture over time and the two are not meant to be equal. See the [cross-architecture note](#cross-architecture-gap) below. **MI35x (gfx950), MXFP4** | Model | BS | Latency (s) | Output tok/s | ITL (ms) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `openai/gpt-oss-20b` | 1 | 1.14 | 463.69 | 2.16 | | | 8 | 1.43 | 3148.30 | 2.54 | | | 16 | 1.66 | 5793.03 | 2.76 | | | 64 | 2.82 | 17393.64 | 3.68 | | `openai/gpt-oss-120b` | 1 | 1.65 | 319.90 | 3.13 | | | 8 | 2.06 | 2177.35 | 3.67 | | | 16 | 2.39 | 4040.90 | 3.96 | | | 64 | 4.21 | 11661.29 | 5.49 | **MI30x (gfx942), bf16** | Model | BS | Latency (s) | Output tok/s | ITL (ms) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `lmsys/gpt-oss-20b-bf16` | 1 | 1.61 | 328.27 | 3.05 | | | 8 | 2.25 | 2119.96 | 3.77 | | | 16 | 2.73 | 3889.67 | 4.11 | | | 64 | 5.41 | 11078.14 | 5.78 | | `lmsys/gpt-oss-120b-bf16` | 1 | 2.29 | 230.71 | 4.33 | | | 8 | 3.41 | 1393.54 | 5.74 | | | 16 | 4.72 | 2165.65 | 7.39 | | | 64 | 10.52 | 4837.02 | 13.23 | ### Why the two tables differ The gap is dominated by weight-memory traffic, which the precision split changes directly. Per-GPU weight footprint from the run's `Load weight end` lines: | Model | MI35x (MXFP4) | MI30x (bf16) | Extra traffic on MI30x | |---|---:|---:|---:| | 20b | 2.33 GB | 5.00 GB | 2.15x | | 120b | 11.52 GB | 27.40 GB | 2.38x | Measured MI35x/MI30x output-throughput ratio: | Model | BS 1 | BS 8 | BS 16 | BS 64 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 20b | 1.41x | 1.49x | 1.49x | 1.57x | | 120b | 1.39x | 1.56x | 1.87x | **2.41x** | For 120b at batch 64 the ratio (2.41x) lands almost exactly on the weight-traffic ratio (2.38x), which is what bandwidth-bound decode should do. The smaller 20b model stays further from that bound, so its gap is correspondingly smaller. The remainder is the gfx950-vs-gfx942 generation difference (larger HBM, newer memory subsystem — 274 GB vs 176 GB free after weight load in these runs). ### Added nightly cost The sweeps are short because both models load and serve quickly: | Step | Measured | Added cost | |---|---:|---:| | MI30x perf step | 6.5 min | 0.87 GPU-h | | MI35x perf step | 3.9 min | 0.52 GPU-h | | **Total** | | **≈1.4 GPU-h/night** | Folding into the accuracy jobs rather than creating standalone jobs avoids repeating container setup and dependency install, which cost 9.0 min on MI30x and 6.0 min on MI35x in this run: standalone jobs would have made the same coverage ≈3.4 GPU-h/night. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

signal.title: [Spec] Guard multi-layer EAGLE against diverted dp-attention non-extend batches
signal.text: ## Motivation `MultiLayerEagleWorkerV2.forward_batch_generation` routes on ```python if batch.forward_mode.is_extend() or batch.is_extend_in_batch: ``` `is_extend_in_batch` is the **global** dp-attention stamp (`layers/dp_attention.py`), so a rank whose **local** batch is not an extend can be diverted into the target-prefill branch while the scheduler nulled `input_ids` for the spec iteration. Today that branch forwards the batch straight into `target_worker.forward_batch_generation`: - the staggered-IDLE rank (a peer prefills while this rank has nothing to run — the only non-extend shape the default spec+dp-attention no-mix sync produces here) crashes the target forward on `input_ids=None`; - a NON-empty locally-DECODE batch (only possible when the no-mix sync is skipped via `--speculative-skip-dp-mlp-sync`) would run much further and fail later in `rotate_input_ids` — an anonymous crash with peer ranks already hung in the dp gather. Found while running multi-rank speculative-decoding workloads on a downstream deployment (dp-attention with staggered prefill arrival). ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py` — in the extend branch, before the target forward: 1. **Fail-loud tripwire** for a non-empty locally-non-extend divert: a `RuntimeError` naming the batch shape (`bs`, `forward_mode`), raised before the target forward instead of the later anonymous crash. It sits above the bonus-shape condition so a divert with a `None`/mismatched bonus is caught too. 2. **Staggered-IDLE fill**: for the empty batch, populate `input_ids`/`out_cache_loc` from `spec_info.bonus_tokens` and the `req_to_token` rows (both no-op empty tensors), so the IDLE batch flows through the target forward like any other idle forward instead of carrying `None`s. New unit test `test/registered/unit/spec/test_multi_layer_eagle_divert_guard.py` (CPU CI, `base-a-test-cpu`; white-box `__new__` + SimpleNamespace style like the existing spec unit tests): - non-empty DECODE divert raises the RuntimeError before the fill and before the target forward (with and without a bonus-shaped spec_info); - the staggered-IDLE batch reaches the target forward with empty int64 `input_ids`/`out_cache_loc` (no `None` left for downstream padding helpers); - a genuine local extend reaches the target forward untouched. ## Accuracy Tests No numerics change: the fill only affects empty (IDLE) batches, and the tripwire only turns an existing downstream crash into an immediate, named error. Red/green on the new test: Without the fix (test alone on current main): ``` $ python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/spec/test_multi_layer_eagle_divert_guard.py -q ... E AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'numel' ... FAILED test/registered/unit/spec/test_multi_layer_eagle_divert_guard.py::TestMultiLayerEagleDivertGuard::test_non_empty_decode_divert_fails_loud FAILED test/registered/unit/spec/test_multi_layer_eagle_divert_guard.py::TestMultiLayerEagleDivertGuard::test_non_empty_decode_divert_fails_loud_without_bonus_shape FAILED test/registered/unit/spec/test_multi_layer_eagle_divert_guard.py::TestMultiLayerEagleDivertGuard::test_staggered_idle_fill_noops_into_target_forward 3 failed, 1 passed, 19 warnings in 12.29s ``` (diverted batches reach the target forward with `input_ids=None`; the IDLE batch leaves `None`s behind) With the fix: ``` $ python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/spec/test_multi_layer_eagle_divert_guard.py -q 4 passed, 19 warnings in 16.64s ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not perf-relevant: two host-side checks on the extend branch; the fill runs only for empty (IDLE) diverted batches. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31915335012](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31915335012)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31915334866](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31915334866)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text:
## Motivation Conflict-resolved rebasing of #33919, which went `CONFLICTING` / `DIRTY` against `main`. The original PR is authored by @Lzy17 on a fork branch (`Lzy17:qwen35-recipes`); its commits are preserved here verbatim, with one added merge commit that resolves the conflict. Content and intent are unchanged from #33919 — see that PR for the motivation and the MI355X validation numbers. ### What conflicted Exactly one file: `scripts/ci/slurm/nightly-configs.yaml`. Both sides appended new MI355X entries at the end of the file: - `main` gained the GLM-5.2 wide-EP16 2P1D pair (`glm52-fp4-mi355x-ep16-sglang`, `glm52-fp4-mi355x-ep16-mtp-sglang`) from #34476, which landed after this branch's merge base. - This branch appends the four Qwen3.5 entries (`qwen35-fp4-mi355x-{,mtp-,dp8ep8-,dp8ep8-mtp-}sglang`). Git could not pick a side because the two additions overlap at the same end-of-file anchor. There is no semantic disagreement between them. ## Modifications Resolved as a pure union, GLM-5.2 EP16 first (preserving `main`'s ordering), then the Qwen3.5 block. No other file conflicted: `main` touched only `nightly-configs.yaml` and the two new `glm52/1k1k/2p1d-ep16*.yaml` recipes under `scripts/ci/slurm/` since the merge base, and did not touch `launch_mi355x.sh`. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — CI recipe configuration only, no runtime or model code. The accuracy numbers backing the four recipes are in #33919 (GSM8K `run_eval` on MI355X 2-node 1P1D: 0.976 / 0.973 / 0.971 / 0.973). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. ### Verification of the resolution The resolution was checked mechanically rather than by eye: - **Union is exact.** `diff(resolved, PR-head version)` is precisely `main`'s 32 added lines, and `diff(resolved, main version)` is precisely the PR's 64 added lines — neither side lost or gained anything else. - **Nothing else drifted.** `git diff main HEAD` is the same 6 files / +376 / -5 that GitHub reports for #33919. - **Generated CI matrix is the union.** `generate_matrix.py --runner mi355x` yields 38 entries: 34 from `main` plus the 4 new `qwen35-fp4-1k1k-1p1d*` entries, equivalently 36 from the PR plus the 2 new `glm52-fp4-1k1k-2p1d-ep16*` entries. Nothing lost from either side, and no duplicate matrix names. - **Workflow grouping still succeeds.** `nightly-amd-mi355x-disagg.yml` hard-fails its `setup` job on any entry that matches neither the `-1p1d` (2-node) nor `-2p1d-ep16` (4-node) group. Simulating that step over the merged config leaves zero unmatched entries: 26 in `matrix-2n` (including the four Qwen3.5 recipes) and 12 in `matrix-4n` (including the two new GLM-5.2 EP16 recipes). - **The new launcher knob is inert for existing recipes.** Running the launcher's recipe parser over all 22 `mi355x-fp4` recipes shows every pre-existing one — including `main`'s new `glm52/1k1k/2p1d-ep16*.yaml`, which this branch never saw — resolving to the `few_shot` / 512 defaults, so their behavior is byte-identical. Only the four Qwen3.5 recipes opt into `run_eval` / 2048. - YAML parses, all 40 top-level keys survive with no duplicates, `bash -n` on `launch_mi355x.sh` passes, and `pre-commit run --files` over the changed files passes (notably `check-yaml` and `check-merge-conflict`). ### Note for the author of #33919 This branch is a strict descendant of `c7bb72d` (the head of #33919), so if you would rather keep the conflict fix on your own PR than merge this one, you can fast-forward your branch onto it and close this PR: ```bash git fetch https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git cursor/resolve-conflict-qwen35-recipes-8ece git checkout qwen35-recipes && git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD && git push ``` No force push needed.
