signal.title: [Bug] --enable-eplb + --speculative-algorithm DSPARK crashes during draft CUDA graph capture: on_select_experts scatter_add_ dimension mismatch (layer_idx=None)
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Enabling EPLB together with DSPARK speculative decoding on DeepSeek-V4-Flash crashes all 8 TP ranks simultaneously during **draft-model decode CUDA graph capture**, then crash-loops on restart (container restart policy). Not an OOM — the crash happens with ~43 GB still available per GPU. Traceback (identical every restart, SGLang 0.5.17, all ranks): ``` File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 972, in init_all_cuda_graphs self.draft_worker.init_cuda_graphs() File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py", line 342, in init_cuda_graphs File ".../sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py", line 985, in run_once out = forward(...) File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_dspark.py", line 542, in forward x = self._run_ffn(x, forward_batch) File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_dspark.py", line 549, in _run_ffn y = self._run_moe_ffn_dp_sync(...) File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py", line 1869, in _run_moe_ffn_dp_sync hidden_states = self.mlp(...) File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 983, in forward_normal_dual_stream topk_output = self.topk(...) File ".../sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py", line 2287, in select_experts get_global_expert_distribution_recorder().on_select_experts(...) File ".../sglang/srt/eplb/expert_distribution.py", line 247, in _on_hook getattr(gatherer, hook_name)(layer_idx=self._current_layer_idx.value, **kwargs) File ".../sglang/srt/eplb/expert_distribution.py", line 540, in on_select_experts self._data[layer_idx, :].scatter_add_( RuntimeError: Index tensor must have the same number of dimensions as self tensor Exception: Capture cuda graph failed: Index tensor must have the same number of dimensions as self tensor ``` **Root cause analysis:** - `--enable-eplb` force-activates the expert distribution recorder (mode `stat`) — there is no way to disable it while EPLB is on. - During CUDA graph capture of the DSPARK draft model, the draft's MoE forward path (`deepseek_v4_dspark.py` → `deepseek_v2.py forward_normal_dual_stream` → `select_experts`) reaches `on_select_experts` without a `with_current_layer` context, so `layer_idx` is `None`. - `self._data[None, :]` adds a singleton dimension (becomes 2-D), and `scatter_add_(dim=0, index=..., src=...)` gets a 1-D index → dimension mismatch → RuntimeError inside graph capture → capture fails → scheduler exits → crash loop. This is the same failure mode documented in #25355 for the MegaMoE path (`forward_mega_moe` unwrapped by `with_current_layer`, hook fires with `layer_idx=None`, identical error text), but reached through the **DSPARK draft worker** entry instead of the MegaMoE dispatch path. Verified the `expert_distribution.py` guard is still absent on main as of 2026-08-16. Related prior art on spec-decode × EPLB/recorder incompatibility: #32105 / #32106 (EAGLE + expert-distribution-metrics during draft capture), #34846 (DSpark draft MoE skips expert-location dispatch under EPLB — correctness, acceptance 1.61→3.38 after fix), and the historical Qwen3 MTP+EPLB fixes #16044 / #19812 / #19232. **Workaround:** disable EPLB (keep DSPARK). EPLB cannot be kept because `--expert-distribution-recorder-mode null` is rejected by arg validation (YAML null → string `"None"`, `invalid choice`), and EPLB force-enables the recorder anyway. ### Reproduction Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash (single checkpoint, DSpark head bundled), 8x H20-3e (141 GB, CC 9.0), TP=8 / EP=8. ```yaml # config.yml (launched via: sglang serve --model-path ... --config /scripts/config.yml) tp-size: 8 ep-size: 8 mem-fraction-static: 0.68 page-size: 256 max-running-requests: 8 kv-cache-dtype: fp8_e4m3 attention-backend: dsv4 moe-runner-backend: marlin speculative-algorithm: DSPARK speculative-num-steps: 1 speculative-eagle-topk: 1 speculative-num-draft-tokens: 6 enable-eplb: true # <- toggling this line is the entire repro ep-num-redundant-experts: 8 expert-distribution-recorder-mode: stat # default; also forced by eplb ``` 1. Start the server with the config above → all ranks crash at draft decode graph capture (~6-7 min into init), identical traceback each restart (crash-loop with auto-restart). 2. Comment out `enable-eplb` + `ep-num-redundant-experts` → server starts and serves normally (verified, stable). 3. Crash is independent of `mem-fraction-static` (0.70 and 0.68 both crash) and of redundant-expert count (EPLB alone, without redundant experts, also crashes). ### Environment From `python3 -m sglang.check_env` inside the serving container `lmsysorg/sglang:latest-cu130` (sglang installed at `/sgl-workspace/sglang`): ``` Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA H20-3e GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 9.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.0, V13.0.88 CUDA Driver Version: 580.173.02 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.17 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5 flashinfer_python: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.15.post1+cu130 triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0+cu130 numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.141.1 huggingface_hub: 1.27.0 modelscope: 1.39.1 orjson: 3.11.9 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.0 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.52.1 ```

signal.title: [AMD] DSv4: fuse the qk-norm-rope pair on the MTP target-verify path
signal.text: ## Summary On the DeepSeek-V4 unified-KV path, the fused qk-norm-rope kernel is wired to decode only. MTP **target-verify** falls back to running the same work as two separate launches per layer — `sglang::fused_q_norm_rope` for q and `sglang::fused_norm_rope` for kv — which is 122 launches per verify step across the 61 target layers. This PR routes target-verify through the same fused kernel, **with the cache store left off**. The store half deliberately does not move. Decode is a 1-source consumer: the ring holds everything, so writing it before attention is required. Target-verify is **2-source** — attention reads history from the ring and takes the current chunk as `k`/`v` so the draft tokens stay causally masked against one another. Writing the current chunk into the ring ahead of attention makes those tokens indistinguishable from history, and every draft position then attends to all of them regardless of order. Fusing the store as well drops GSM8K from 0.950 to 0.027 while looking like a ~7% throughput win, because it skips exactly the work correctness depends on. Only the norm+RoPE half is sound, and that is what this PR fuses. ## Modifications - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`** (`MQALayer._forward_prepare`) - `do_fused_store` now also admits `is_target_verify()` when the new gate is on. The kernel is token-indexed (`q`, `kv` and `positions` are all length M), so a verify batch carrying several draft tokens per request is a shape it already handles. - On that path the kernel is called with `swa_cache`/`swa_loc` left as `None`, so it performs q-norm+RoPE and kv-norm+RoPE and stores nothing. `get_unified_swa_loc` is not called at all — it exists solely to address a store this path no longer performs. - `kv` is returned instead of being set to `None`, so the caller's existing contract drives the rest unchanged: `attn_k = kv` gives attention the real current-chunk source, and `save_kv_cache = kv is not None` makes the backend write the ring after attention, exactly as the unfused path did. - `kv` is materialised with `.contiguous()` first: it is a strided slice of `qkv_a`, and the ring store requires a contiguous buffer. The unfused path pays the identical copy inside `_compute_kv_bf16`, so this is parity, not added overhead. - **`python/sglang/srt/environ.py`** — new `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY` (default on). Set to 0 to fall back to the unfused chain on the verify path. Decode, prefill and the non-unified paths are untouched. ### Kernel-level evidence Per target-verify forward, from graphs-off traces segmented by the 61 `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` frames (TP8, 8k/1k, conc 16, rank 0). `fused_q_norm_rope` and `fused_norm_rope` both go to zero and one `_fused_qk_norm_rope_store_kernel` replaces them; no other kernel is added. | layer type | launches/fwd (base → patched) | GPU us/fwd excl. collective | |---|---|---| | CSA (30 layers) | 1920.0 → 1800.0 | 15779 → 15488 (−1.8%) | | HCA (31 layers) | 1526.8 → 1410.5 | 12385 → 12014 (−3.0%) | "excl. collective" is the number to read: `cross_device_reduce` blocks until the slowest rank arrives, so its duration tracks inter-rank skew rather than work this change moves. ## Accuracy Model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`, MI355X (gfx950), TP8. GSM8K, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy. | run | accuracy | invalid | |---|---|---| | baseline (gate 0) | 0.950 | 0.000 | | patched (gate 1) | 0.949 | 0.000 | | patched (gate 1, repeat) | 0.945 | 0.000 | Note this is measured **without** `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`. The throughput harness pins acceptance to the golden AL, which fabricates which draft tokens are accepted — fine for speed, but it would bypass the accept/reject path this change touches. Acceptance here is whatever the draft model earns. ```bash export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton export SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1 export SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1 export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=high # flip this between 0 (baseline) and 1 (patched) export SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 31710 --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --page-size 256 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --max-running-requests 32 --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --backend srt --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 31710 \ --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 \ --max-new-tokens 1024 --temperature 0.0 --parallel 32 ``` ## Performance Same model and hardware. 8k input / 1k output, TP8, steady state (10 waves through a `--max-concurrency` gate). Each cell is the mean of 2 repeats run in `off, on, on, off` order per concurrency, so a monotonic drift over the block shifts both arms equally instead of being credited to the patch. Repeated all-gates-off runs on this node put the noise floor at 0.25% (1σ). | concurrency | output tok/s (base → patched) | uplift | mean TPOT ms | accept len | |---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 332.43 → 341.07 | **+2.60%** | 11.37 → 11.06 | 2.499 → 2.498 | | 8 | 543.73 → 555.57 | **+2.18%** | 13.75 → 13.46 | 2.499 → 2.469 | | 16 | 839.00 → 857.32 | **+2.18%** | 17.98 → 17.57 | 2.499 → 2.507 | | 32 | 1167.14 → 1186.66 | **+1.67%** | 25.79 → 25.34 | 2.482 → 2.508 | Acceptance length is flat across arms, so the uplift is kernel time and not a shift in speculation behaviour. ```bash # same server launch as above, with SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY # flipped 0/1 between arms, plus the throughput harness env: export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=2.49 export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token # CONC in {4, 8, 16, 32}; --max-running-requests/--cuda-graph-max-bs = 2*CONC # capped at 32 on both arms (this image cannot capture a decode graph at bs 48). CONC=16 python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31710 --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 0.8 --num-prompts $((CONC * 10)) \ --max-concurrency $CONC ``` `bench_serving` ignores EOS by default here (it only offers `--disable-ignore-eos`), so every request runs to exactly 1024 output tokens and neither arm can win by generating less. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31901655398](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31901655398)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31901655847](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31901655847)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Native Hunyuan3D image encoders
signal.text: ## Summary - replace the Transformers CLIP and DINOv2 neural modules in the Hunyuan3D Shape conditioner with native SGLang implementations - add a native DINOv2 encoder with packed QKV, tensor-parallel linear layers, explicit checkpoint loading, and layerwise offload support - fix native CLIP vision attention to be non-causal while preserving causal CLIP text attention - make the Hunyuan3D conditioner weight-loading contract explicit and validate complete checkpoints ## Why Hunyuan3D Shape instantiated full Transformers vision models inside an otherwise native pipeline. This bypassed SGLang tensor parallelism and layerwise offload. It also exposed a latent correctness bug in the shared native CLIP implementation: vision attention was configured as causal. ## Validation - `pre-commit run --files` for all changed files - `pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_hunyuan3d_image_encoder.py` - `pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_disagg_roles.py` - DINOv2-Giant checkpoint parity for TP=1 and TP=2 - 40-layer DINOv2 layerwise-offload parity against resident execution For DINOv2-Giant on H100 with Torch SDPA, the 20-run median encoder latency changed from 10.42 ms to 9.68 ms (-7.1%). TP=1 cosine similarity against Transformers was 0.9999989; TP=2 was 0.9999966, with identical outputs across ranks. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #31901159523](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31901159523)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31901159320](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31901159320)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] HiCache host-pool memory check (psutil.virtual_memory().available) does not account for reserved HugePages, causing false "Not enough host memory" failures
signal.text: [Bug] HiCache host-pool memory check (`psutil.virtual_memory().available`) does not account for reserved HugePages, causing false "Not enough host memory" failures ## Checklist - [x] I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version (reproduced against a recent `main` checkout). - [x] Environment info and a minimal reproduction are included below. ## Describe the bug When `vm.nr_hugepages` is configured on the host and `--enable-hierarchical-cache` is used, `HostKVCache.__init__` (in `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/base.py`) can fail to start with: ``` ValueError: Not enough host memory available. Requesting 7.05 GB but only have 2.04 GB free. Please reduce the size of the hierarchical cache. ``` even though the reserved HugePages pool is *completely free* at that moment (`HugePages_Free` == `HugePages_Total`), and even though the very allocation this check is gating will, if it succeeds, be satisfied via a hugetlbfs-backed `mmap` from that same pool — not from general system RAM. The check in question: ```python # python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/base.py (~line 135-146) # Verify there is enough available host memory. host_mem = psutil.virtual_memory() requested_bytes = self.size * self.size_per_token available_bytes = host_mem.available - HICACHE_HOST_MEMORY_RESERVE_BYTES if requested_bytes > available_bytes: raise ValueError( f"Not enough host memory available. Requesting " f"{requested_bytes / 1e9:.2f} GB but only have " f"{available_bytes / 1e9:.2f} GB free. Please reduce the " f"size of the hierarchical cache." ) ``` `psutil.virtual_memory().available` mirrors the kernel's `MemAvailable` in `/proc/meminfo`, which **excludes reserved HugePages by design** (they are not reclaimable general-purpose memory, regardless of whether they're currently allocated). So reserving `N` GB of HugePages reduces `available` by roughly `N` GB, and this check then uses that already-reduced `available` to decide whether there's room for... an allocation that is actually going to be satisfied from the (still fully free) HugePages pool. Net effect: the more HugePages you reserve to make the host KV pool fast, the more likely this pre-flight check is to fail, independent of whether the HugePages pool itself has enough room. ## Root cause confirmation Immediately after this check would pass, the actual allocation path confirms it targets hugetlbfs specifically. When no HugePages are reserved (`vm.nr_hugepages=0`), the same code path logs: ``` Hugepage mmap via libc failed ([Errno 12] Cannot allocate memory); falling back to plain mmap. SGLANG_HUGEPAGE_SIZE=2MB will be ignored. ``` This proves the intended allocation always attempts `MAP_HUGETLB` first, and only falls back to plain pages when hugetlbfs allocation fails — i.e., the code is fully hugepage-aware downstream of the check, just not *in* the check itself. ## Reproduction Hardware: Ryzen 7 9700X, 32 GB DDR5, RTX 5060 Ti 16GB, single node, `--tp 1`. Model launched with `--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 2.0` and varying `--hicache-size`. **1) Baseline, no HugePages reserved:** ``` $ free -h Mem: 30Gi 1.3Gi 16Gi ... 29Gi available HugePages_Total: 0 ``` **2) Reserve HugePages sized to match `--hicache-size 8`, start server — succeeds:** ``` $ sudo sysctl -w vm.nr_hugepages=4096 # 8 GiB $ free -h Mem: 30Gi 9.3Gi 8.4Gi ... 21Gi available HugePages_Total: 4096 HugePages_Free: 4096 ``` Server starts fine with `--hicache-size 8`. After startup: `HugePages_Free: 280` (pool nearly fully consumed, ~7.45 GB used out of 8 GB reserved) — i.e. it *does* use the HugePages successfully when the check passes. **3) Reserve HugePages sized to match `--hicache-size 12`, start server — fails:** ``` $ sudo sysctl -w vm.nr_hugepages=6144 # 12 GiB $ free -h Mem: 30Gi 13Gi 3.8Gi ... 17Gi available HugePages_Total: 6144 HugePages_Free: 6144 # 100% free ``` Server startup fails: ``` Allocating full hierarchical KV host pool: 246016 tokens, 7.05 GB host memory. ValueError: Not enough host memory available. Requesting 7.05 GB but only have 2.04 GB free. ``` Note: `HugePages_Free` was 6144 (fully free, 12 GB available in the hugetlb pool) immediately before this. The "2.04 GB free" clearly does not come from the hugepage pool. **4) Remove the HugePages reservation entirely, same `--hicache-size 12` — succeeds:** ``` $ sudo sysctl -w vm.nr_hugepages=0 $ free -h Mem: 30Gi 1.3Gi 17Gi ... 29Gi available ``` ``` Allocating full hierarchical KV host pool: 246016 tokens, 7.05 GB host memory. Hugepage mmap via libc failed ([Errno 12] Cannot allocate memory); falling back to plain mmap. Allocating swa hierarchical KV host pool: 69056 tokens, 4.95 GB host memory. Hugepage mmap via libc failed ([Errno 12] Cannot allocate memory); falling back to plain mmap. ... The server is fired up and ready to roll! ``` Same total request (12 GB), same machine, same free RAM budget minus the HugePages reservation — succeeds without HugePages, fails with them. ## Expected behavior The pre-flight check should not treat HugePages capacity as unavailable when the allocator is actually going to (attempt to) draw from the HugePages pool. At minimum, when `HugePages_Total > 0`, the check should also consider `HugePages_Free * Hugepagesize` (from `/proc/meminfo`) as usable capacity for this request, e.g. something like: ```python available_bytes = host_mem.available - HICACHE_HOST_MEMORY_RESERVE_BYTES if hugepages_are_configured(): available_bytes += free_hugepage_bytes() # HugePages_Free * Hugepagesize ``` (or equivalently, only apply the `psutil`-based check when the allocation is *not* going to attempt hugetlbfs, and check `HugePages_Free` instead when it is). ## Environment (sglang-env) mario@mario-ia:~$ python3 -m sglang.check_env Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti GPU 0 Compute Capability: 12.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.3, V13.3.73 CUDA Driver Version: 595.71.05 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.17 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5 flashinfer_python: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_cubin: Module Not Found flashinfer_jit_cache: Module Not Found triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0 numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.141.1 huggingface_hub: 1.27.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.39.1 orjson: 3.11.9 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.52.3 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.1 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.13.0 anthropic: 0.122.0 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: 0.11.1 NVIDIA Topology: GPU0 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID GPU0 X 0-15 0 N/A Legend: X = Self SYS = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the SMP interconnect between NUMA nodes (e.g., QPI/UPI) NODE = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the interconnect between PCIe Host Bridges within a NUMA node PHB = Connection traversing PCIe as well as a PCIe Host Bridge (typically the CPU) PXB = Connection traversing multiple PCIe bridges (without traversing the PCIe Host Bridge) PIX = Connection traversing at most a single PCIe bridge NV# = Connection traversing a bonded set of # NVLinks ulimit soft: 1024 ## Additional context This is consistent with documented Linux kernel behavior: `MemAvailable` (and by extension `psutil.virtual_memory().available`) intentionally excludes HugePages, reserved or not, since they are a separate, non-reclaimable memory pool. So this isn't a kernel quirk — it's specifically that the SGLang check doesn't compensate for it when HugePages are configured and about to be used.

signal.title: [AMD] DSv4: fuse compress+norm+rope, emit bpreshuffle scale natively, keep kv_score in bf16
signal.text: ## Motivation On DeepSeek-V4 decode a good part of each attention layer goes to kernels that only move or re-lay-out data rather than compute anything. Three of them run on every layer of every step: 1. On CSA layers (`compress_ratio` 4) compress, norm and rope are three separate launches. Each is 4-8 us, which is small enough that dispatch rather than the work sets the cost. 2. The fp8 quant path writes its scale tensor in one layout and then a second kernel transposes it into the layout the bpreshuffle GEMM actually wants — 152 extra launches per decode step. 3. The compressor takes fp32, so the bf16 `wkv_gate` output is widened by a separate elementwise copy before it can be consumed — 92 extra launches per decode step. None of these carry information the surrounding kernels don't already have, so each can be folded into its neighbour without changing the math. ## Modifications Three independent optimisations, each behind its own env gate. **`SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_COMPRESS_NORM_ROPE`** — new `fused_compress4_norm_rope.cuh` folds compress, norm and rope into a single kernel for CSA layers. The fused kernel maps one token per 64-lane wavefront rather than two; that takes it from 85 to 47 VGPRs and lifts occupancy from 5 to 8 waves/SIMD, which is what makes the fused kernel actually cheaper than the three it replaces instead of merely equal to them. **`SGLANG_OPT_NATIVE_BPRESHUFFLE_SCALE`** — the quant kernel writes the scale tensor directly in the physical layout bpreshuffle wants (column-major in M), so the separate transpose pass is not needed. **`SGLANG_OPT_KV_SCORE_BF16`** — `c4_v2.cuh` and `c128_v2.cuh` gain a `SrcFloat` template parameter, kept separate from the compute dtype so `score_bias` stays fp32. The compressor then widens the `wkv_gate` output as it loads it and the fp32 copy in front of compress is never materialised. `compress_forward()` only widens on the XPU path, and `compressor.py` calls `linear_kv_score` where it previously called `linear_bf16_fp32`. **On the defaults.** All three gates default to on. They are separable on purpose — each can be turned off on its own with `=0` if it regresses a shape I did not measure — but the numbers below are all with the three together, which is the configuration the defaults select. Happy to ship any or all of them off by default instead if maintainers would rather see soak time first. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K, all 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, on the environment below. | Run | Gates | Accuracy | Invalid | |---|---|---|---| | Baseline | all off | 94.7% | 0.000 | | Patched, pass 1 | all on | 94.5% | 0.000 | | Patched, pass 2 | all on | 94.8% | 0.001 | Baseline and patched are the same build on the same image, gates flipped by env var only. The patched arm was run twice because temperature 0 is not bit-deterministic here — batching order moves with arrival timing — so a single number cannot separate a real accuracy change from run-to-run noise. The two patched passes differ from each other by 0.3 points and bracket the baseline, which is the most that can be claimed: no accuracy change is visible above run-to-run noise at this sample size. ```bash MODEL= FUSE=1 NATIVE_SCALE=1 KVBF16=1 \ NUM_QUESTIONS=1319 NUM_SHOTS=5 MAX_NEW_TOKENS=512 PARALLEL=1200 \ bash bench/gsm8k_item4_517.sh # FUSE=0 NATIVE_SCALE=0 KVBF16=0 for baseline ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Environment | | | |---|---| | GPU | 8x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) | | ROCm | 7.2.0 | | Image | `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260812` | | Model | DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 61 layers | | Shape | 8k in / 1k out, `--random-range-ratio 1.0` | Server: ```bash sglang serve --model-path "$MODEL" --port "$PORT" \ --tensor-parallel-size $TP $DP_ARGS \ --trust-remote-code --disable-radix-cache --attention-backend dsv4 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs "$CONC" --max-running-requests "$CONC" \ --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --page-size 256 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --context-length 16384 \ --chunked-prefill-size $((ISL * TP)) \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion --watchdog-timeout 1800 # DP_ARGS for the conc-64 shape: # --dp $TP --enable-dp-attention --enable-prefill-delayer --enable-two-batch-overlap ``` Client: ```bash python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang-oai \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$PORT" --model "$MODEL" \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts "$NUM_PROMPTS" --max-concurrency "$CONC" ``` ### Throughput Each shape is measured A B B A and the pairs averaged, so drift over the sweep cancels instead of being charged to whichever arm happened to run second. | Shape | Baseline (tok/s) | Patched (tok/s) | Gain | |---|---|---|---| | conc 4, TP4 | 174.23, 174.85 -> 174.54 | 180.96, 179.99 -> 180.48 | **+3.40%** | | conc 8, TP4 | 302.63, 302.48 -> 302.56 | 314.70, 314.41 -> 314.56 | **+3.97%** | | conc 64, TP8 + DP8 | 1600.37, 1593.98 -> 1597.17 | 1645.41, 1643.07 -> 1644.24 | **+2.95%** | Within-arm spread is 0.05-0.40% on baseline and 0.09-0.54% on patched, comfortably under the gap between arms, so the gain is not sweep-order drift. ### Profile Decode window, 8k1k conc 64 TP8 + DP8, per layer on rank TP-0: | Per layer | Baseline | Patched | |---|---|---| | CSA kernels | 55 | **48** | | HCA kernels | 43 | **40** | | Elementwise, CSA / HCA | 8x / 6x | **3x / 3x** | | bf16->fp32 copy, CSA / HCA | 2x / 1x | **0x / 0x** | The widening copy that fed compress is gone from both layer types, and the 48 / 40 counts hold on all seven ranks that captured a full decode window. The compress kernels take bf16 directly — the fourth template argument is the source dtype: - CSA `flash_c4_decode_norm_rope<512l, float, float, __hip_bfloat16, float, 0, false, true>` - HCA `flash_c128_decode<512l, float, float, __hip_bfloat16, float, false>` The three elementwise launches left per layer are two same-dtype `direct_copy` (bf16->bf16, fp32->fp32) and one bf16 residual add. None is a dtype conversion and none sits in front of compress. One caveat worth stating: CSA layer time drops 6.1% while HCA is flat at -0.07% even though HCA also loses three kernels. A single five-step profiler window carries a few us of per-layer drift, which is the same order as the effect being measured, so the throughput sweep above rather than this table is the measurement of record. ### Unit tests ```bash python -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_c4_v2.py \ test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_c128_v2.py -q # 110 passed ``` `test_c4_v2.py` and `test_c128_v2.py` are parametrised over a new bf16 source dtype: 55 of the 110 are those new cases. The `SrcFloat` path had no coverage before, and the bf16 arm was confirmed to actually reach the new specialisation (the dispatcher was observed compiling with `dtype_src=torch.bfloat16`) rather than being quietly widened somewhere above the kernel. All four compress specialisations (c4/c128 x fp32/bf16 source) were also checked to compile. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations) — no user-facing surface changed; the three gates are internal env switches. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #31900312254](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31900312254) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #31900312269](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31900312269)

signal.title: Fix dsv4 kl test timeout
signal.text: ## Motivation `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dsv4.py` is killed at 1200s on every scheduled run, most recently https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31849115802. The stage sets no `timeout_per_file`, so `run_suite.py` falls back to its flat 1200s default, which sits below the file's own registered `est_time` of 1500. It is the only registered CUDA test with an `est_time` above that default. Measured with no harness timeout on 4 GPUs and a warm cache: 16 tests pass in 2055s. `est_time` moves to 2400 as well because `compute_partitions.py` packs shards by it, so raising only the per-file timeout would trade the file timeout for a job timeout. Left alone: `--timeout-from-est-time` would have derived 3300s here, but it is gated on the `scheduled` input that `pr-test.yml` and `pr-test-extra.yml` never pass, and passing it would also flip `max-parallel` to 1 for every scheduled stage. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31895383698](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31895383698)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #31895383613](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31895383613)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [LoRA] Add the sgl_lora MoE execution engine with JSON config resolution
signal.text: ## Motivation MoE (expert-weight) LoRA serving in SGLang currently runs through the experimental TRT-LLM path (`--moe-runner-backend experimental_sgl_trtllm` + virtual experts). That path has structural limits: - **Blackwell-only**: the trtllm-gen kernels require SM100/120, so there is no expert-LoRA path at all on Hopper (H200). - **Virtual-expert routing scales with `max_loras_per_batch × num_experts`**, so multi-adapter serving degrades sharply as slot capacity grows. - **No prefill CUDA graphs with LoRA**, and no support for shared-outer adapter factors (gate_up A / down B shared across experts, `expert_dim=1` — the native format of some recent MoE adapters). This PR adds `sgl_lora`: a self-contained MoE-LoRA execution engine selected with `--lora-execution-engine sgl_lora`, built from an exhaustive kernel/fusion/overlap sweep on GB300, B200, and H200 across three models (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Qwen3.5-397B, Inkling-Small; per-expert and shared-outer adapters, ranks 8–64). ## Modifications - **Engine** (`python/sglang/srt/lora/sgl_lora/`): masked expert-major decode path and route-major serial prefill path; per-expert and shared-outer factor layouts; two base-GEMM providers (DeepGEMM, CuTeDSL); side-stream overlap windows for the shared-decode path; capacity-flat routing (cost scales with *active* adapters, not slot capacity). - **JSON config resolution** (`sgl_lora/configs/{gb300,h200,default}.json`): every kernel-family/fusion/overlap/tile decision is data, resolved per (layout, activation, phase, batch shape) through ordered first-match scenario rows with fail-closed validation — a malformed row, unknown plan field, or unknown predicate key aborts startup instead of serving a wrong plan. `SGLANG_SGL_LORA_CONFIG_DIR` points at an override config root (arch JSONs at top level, M-bucketed base-GEMM tile tables under `gemm/`). Every shipped row carries real-model sweep provenance; unknown architectures fall to a conservative serial fallback (`default.json`). - **Prefill CUDA graphs with MoE LoRA** (breakable backend), including graph-stable LoRA workspaces. - **Dense-module gate**: adapter targets are pruned to weight-backed modules at registration, and per-module effective ranks let mixed multi-adapter batches skip dense-LoRA work for adapters that carry no weights for a module (the shared dense kernels in `kernels/ops/gemm` stay byte-identical to upstream — the gate enters as a batch-info view). - **Onboarding tuner** (`benchmark/kernels/lora_moe/tune_lora_config.py`): `--check` (CI-gateable coverage report), `--emit-seed` (serve a new geometry immediately), `--sweep` (e2e-tunes the two geometry-sensitive axes; writes winners back into the seed). - Guards: expert LoRA + DP-attention / elastic-EP / EPLB fail closed at startup (the DP-attention token-axis limitation exists silently in the legacy path today). Scope: bf16 serving path. fp8/nvfp4 qlora support is planned as a follow-up in this PR (the tuner carries a `TODO(quant)` and the config resolver already fails closed on future `quant` predicate keys). Structure note: the first commit is the engine; subsequent commits are review-round changes and will be squashed before undrafting. Two orthogonal fixes found during this work ship separately: `fix/chunked-sgmv-cache-key` (csgmv compile-cache key omits codegen parameters) and `fix/swa-kvpool-v-head-dim` (SWAKVPool lacks `get_v_head_dim`, crashing hybrid-SWA models on the triton attention backend). ## Accuracy Tests - `test/registered/unit/lora/`: 248 passed / 6 skipped (H200), including config-resolution pins, kernel numerics vs an fp32 oracle, byte-identity pins for the decode kernel policy, and prefill graph-vs-eager bit-exactness. - Greedy-decode correctness on real adapters vs the legacy triton reference: per-token logprob deltas at the measured bf16 noise floor (per-expert and shared-outer, all three campaign models). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Protocol: `bench_one_batch_server`, input 4096 / output 1024, bs 1/8/16/32, `max_loras_per_batch=4` distinct adapters, medians after first-pass discard. Baseline = experimental TRT-LLM LoRA path at its best posture (incl. prefill graphs where it can use them). - **Qwen3.5-35B (GB300, TP4)**: prefill +15–19%, decode parity. - **Qwen3.5-397B (B200, TP8)**: prefill +23%, decode −1.2%…+4.5% across bs. - **Inkling-Small (GB300)**: decode +0.5%…+11.9% with the model's shared/routed-expert parallelism active on both engines; prefill +2–5%. - **H200 (fa4 posture)**: the TRT engine cannot run (SM100/120-only kernels); vs the only runnable incumbent (legacy virtual experts on triton fused_moe): decode +1.7%…+19.7%, prefill +1.0–1.5% at bs≥8 (−13% at bs1). - **Prefill CUDA graphs**: 2.5–3.0× prefill throughput vs eager at equal chunking (the incumbent disables prefill graphs under LoRA). - **Multi-adapter**: routing cost is capacity-flat; with 4 distinct adapters/ranks resident, +15–24% prefill and +2–17% decode vs the incumbent. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [DeepEP] Use static FP8 communication for W4AFP8 normal dispatch
signal.text: ## Motivation For W4AFP8 MoE on the DeepEP normal-dispatch path, the dispatcher previously sent BF16 hidden states over the all-to-all and re-quantized them on the receiving side using the checkpoint's static activation scale. This doubles the communication volume (BF16 instead of FP8) and re-does a quantization that the weights were already calibrated against. Since W4AFP8 carries a single static `w13_input_scale` from the checkpoint, we can quantize hidden states to FP8 *before* dispatch and communicate the FP8 payload directly, removing the BF16 transport and the redundant re-quantization. ## Changes - **`token_dispatcher/deepep.py`**: `dispatch()` of the normal dispatcher now accepts an optional `static_scale`. When provided, hidden states are per-tensor quantized to FP8 (`float8_e4m3fn`) with that scale before the all-to-all, so the dispatch payload is FP8 instead of BF16. The low-latency path is left unchanged (it already consumes DeepEP's per-token-group scales). - **`ep_moe/layer.py`**: `DeepEPMoE` computes and forwards the static `w13_input_scale` to `dispatch()` when running a W4AFP8 model on DeepEP. - **`cutlass_w4a8_moe.py`**: `cutlass_w4a8_moe_deepep_normal` now accepts an already-FP8 `gateup_input_pre_reorder` and skips the redundant per-tensor FP8 quantization in that case. - **`quantization/w4afp8.py`**: `W4AFp8MoEMethod` configures the dispatcher's `normal_dispatcher_output_dtype` to `fp8` (instead of `bf16`) for the DeepEP backend, and `postprocess_dispatch` validates that a static FP8 payload (no per-token-group scale) was produced. - **`batch_overlap/two_batch_overlap.py`**: thread `static_scale` through the TBO dispatcher wrapper so the overlap path benefits from the same FP8 dispatch. - **Tests**: extend `test_w4afp8_deepep_dtype.py` and `test_w4afp8_deepep_post_reorder.py` to cover the static-FP8 normal-dispatch path (dtype assertions + post-reorder correctness). ## How it works ``` Before: hidden_states(BF16) --a2a--> per_tensor_quant_fp8 --> W4A8 GEMM After: hidden_states --quant(static_scale)--> FP8 --a2a--> W4A8 GEMM ``` The all-to-all now transmits FP8 (half the bytes of BF16), and the receiver no longer re-quantizes — the static scale used for dispatch is the same one the weights were calibrated with. ## Checklist - [x] Code follows the project style (ruff/black conventions in place). - [x] Existing W4AFP8 + DeepEP unit tests extended for the new path. - [ ] CI (will rely on the project CI run on this PR). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31676535100](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31676535100)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31676534754](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31676534754)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] HF3FS HiCache hits ZeroDivisionError with DeepSeek-V4 logical KV anchor
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ### Symptom DeepSeek-V4 HiCache uses a LogicalHostPool as the primary KV anchor. This pool only manages logical token indices and does not contain physical KV data. When hf3fs is selected as the HiCache storage backend, the backend calculates bytes_per_page=0 from this logical pool and later divides by it during initialization. Therefore, DeepSeek-V4 cannot start with HF3FS L3 storage. Starting sglang with DSV4 and HF3FS will encounter: ``` File "/path/to/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/hf3fs/storage_hf3fs.py", line 220, in __init__ self.num_pages = self.file_size // self.bytes_per_page ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ZeroDivisionError: integer division or modulo by zero ``` The DeepSeek-V4 cookbook currently lists hf3fs as an available L3 backend, but I could not find a DSV4-specific HF3FS test or existing issue covering this problem. ### root cause DeepSeek-V4 creates a LogicalHostPool whose storage-related properties are: ``` self.kv_buffer = None self.size_per_token = 0 def get_ksize_per_token(self): return 0 ``` The storage factory calculates: ``` bytes_per_page = ( mem_pool_host.get_ksize_per_token() * mem_pool_host.page_size ) ``` Therefore, bytes_per_page is zero. `HiCacheHF3FS.__init__()` subsequently executes: ``` self.num_pages = self.file_size // self.bytes_per_page ``` This should result in: ZeroDivisionError: integer division or modulo by zero ### Reproduction Setup HF3FS config json file according to doc https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/hf3fs/docs/deploy_sglang_3fs_multinode.md Start SGLang server like: ``` export SGLANG_HICACHE_HF3FS_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/hf3fs_config.json sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --tp 2 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.92 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32 \ --served-model-name local-dsv4-flash \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-ratio 2 \ --hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct \ --hicache-io-backend direct \ --hicache-storage-backend hf3fs \ --hicache-storage-prefetch-policy wait_complete ``` You will see ``` File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py", line 527, in build_deepseek_v4_hicache_stack cache_controller = HybridCacheController( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py", line 205, in __init__ self.attach_storage_backend( File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py", line 225, in attach_storage_backend super().attach_storage_backend( File "/path/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py", line 475, in attach_storage_backend self.storage_backend = StorageBackendFactory.create_backend( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/backend_factory.py", line 94, in create_backend return cls._create_builtin_backend( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/backend_factory.py", line 183, in _create_builtin_backend return backend_class.from_env_config(bytes_per_page, dtype, storage_config) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/hf3fs/storage_hf3fs.py", line 362, in from_env_config return HiCacheHF3FS( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/path/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/hf3fs/storage_hf3fs.py", line 220, in __init__ self.num_pages = self.file_size // self.bytes_per_page ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ZeroDivisionError: integer division or modulo by zero ``` ### Environment Python: 3.12.3 (main, Mar 23 2026, 19:04:32) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server signal.title: Add --http2-max-concurrent-streams server arg
signal.text: From @happierpig ## Motivation `--enable-http2` runs the ASGI app under Granian, which advertises Granian's built-in `SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS` value. That value is not configurable today, and it is not reported anywhere. A client that pools HTTP/2 connections to an engine needs to know the per-connection stream limit in order to size its own admission control. If it admits more streams than the server advertises, the excess requests queue invisibly inside the client's HTTP/2 transport instead of failing fast at the pool boundary; if it admits fewer, usable connection capacity sits idle. The server should own this value and make it explicit. ## Modifications - Add `--http2-max-concurrent-streams` to `ServerArgs` (default 200). It is validated against the HTTP/2 range (1 to 2^32 - 1) and only takes effect with `--enable-http2`. - Pass it through `_run_granian_server` to Granian's `HTTP2Settings.max_concurrent_streams`. - Add a CPU unit test asserting the configured value reaches Granian, and set an explicit value in the existing HTTP/2 server tests so the flag is exercised end to end on both the single- and multi-tokenizer-worker paths. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no model execution or numerics are affected. ## Benchmarking and Profiling Not applicable — this only changes an HTTP/2 setting advertised at connection setup. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/accuracy_results.html). - [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and would like to remove yourself as a reviewer, please leave a comment with `/unassign`. ## Test plan - `black --check` and `isort --check-only --profile black` pass on all four touched files. - `python3 -m py_compile` passes on all four touched files. - Not run locally: `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_http2_server_config.py` and `test/registered/openai_server/basic/test_http2_server.py`. The development machine used for this port has no `torch`/`granian` installation, so both are left to CI. ## Original commits - `2c8be0057` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31826412107](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31826412107)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31826411909](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31826411909)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [MoE] Add FlashInfer SM90 MXFP4 W4A8 MoE
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang currently supports FlashInfer's SM90 MXFP4 W4A16 CUTLASS MoE path, which was introduced in SGLang #24816 on top of FlashInfer [#3084](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3084). FlashInfer [#3738](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738) adds a different Hopper path that dynamically quantizes activations to FP8 and runs MXFP4-weight x FP8-activation MoE GEMMs using Humming-style pre-MMA E8M0 scale fusion. This PR wires that path into SGLang as an explicit opt-in: ```bash --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 ``` The existing `default` and `bf16` behavior is unchanged. Related work: - SGLang https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24816 - FlashInfer https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738 ### FlashInfer version requirement This integration intentionally targets the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431, where the FC1 and FC2 residual scales are FP32 tensors in local-expert order with shape `[num_local_experts]`. FlashInfer reuses its internal expert permutation to map those scales to routed rows, including global-to-local expert mapping under EP. The original #3738 ABI briefly shipped before being reverted from FlashInfer 0.6.17 by #4411. It required downstream runtimes to construct routed-row residual tensors during every forward. SGLang does not support that older ABI. The new option therefore requires both: - `flashinfer-python >= 0.6.18` - `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` SGLang currently pins FlashInfer 0.6.17. This PR does not change that global pin. With 0.6.17, selecting `fp8` fails immediately with an actionable error, while all existing FlashInfer paths remain compatible. The dependency, cubin, and JIT-cache pins should be upgraded together in a follow-up change. GPU validation for this PR used FlashInfer 0.6.18 built from commit `8044d94bf9acc5369857baf88d28906bb32bf264`, which contains the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431. ## Modifications ### Runtime selection and compatibility - Add `fp8` to `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision`. - Select the new path only for `flashinfer_mxfp4` on SM90. - Keep W4A16 as the default SM90 behavior. - Reject the SM90-specific `fp8` option on SM100 and SM120 to avoid confusing it with their existing MXFP8 activation paths. - Require the corrected FlashInfer 0.6.18+ API instead of accepting the older routed-row residual ABI. - Pass `use_wfp4afp8_humming=True` only when the new path is selected. The keyword is omitted completely for FlashInfer 0.6.17 compatibility. ### Weight preprocessing - Use `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` for both FC1 and FC2 during post-load processing. - Store the folded interleaved weight scales produced by FlashInfer. - Store `residual * 64` as one FP32 value per local expert for FC1 and FC2. - Preserve GPT-OSS gate/up layout conversion and its existing padding rules. - Fill synthetic E8M0 scale padding from an existing scale in the same expert, preventing padding from changing that expert's min/max exponent range. - Support both the GPT-OSS MXFP4 quantization path and the DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 expert path. ### Kernel invocation Construct the five Humming quant-scale slots expected by the corrected FlashInfer API: 1. FC1 folded weight block scales 2. FC1 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation 3. Reserved scalar FC2 activation scale 4. FC2 folded weight block scales 5. FC2 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation The existing TP/EP topology is forwarded to FlashInfer so it can map global expert IDs to the corresponding local residual scale. ### Tests and benchmark - Extend the registered SM90 MXFP4 test suite with: - GPT-OSS preprocessing checks against the FlashInfer helper - five-scale kernel invocation and direct FlashInfer comparison - aligned and non-aligned hidden/intermediate dimensions - padding invariance for per-expert residual scales - EP rank with global expert IDs - DeepSeek-V4 preprocessing - fail-fast behavior on FlashInfer versions before 0.6.18 - Extend the manual SM90 benchmark to compare: - SGLang Marlin W4A16 - FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A16 - FlashInfer Humming W4A8 - Update the server-argument documentation. ## Accuracy Tests GPU correctness and end-to-end smoke testing completed in the following environment: | Component | Version / configuration | | --- | --- | | GPU | 4 x NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), TP=4 | | NVIDIA driver | 590.48.01 | | CUDA toolchain | CUDA 13.0, NVCC 13.0.88 | | Host compiler | GCC 13.3.1 | | PyTorch | 2.13.0+cu130 | | FlashInfer | 0.6.18 (`8044d94bf9acc5369857baf88d28906bb32bf264`) | | sglang-kernel | 0.4.6.post1 | | Model | `/home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` | The registered SM90 MXFP4 suite passed: ```bash python -m pytest \ test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp4_sm90_cutlass.py -v ``` ```text 18 passed, 1 skipped ``` The DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 checkpoint was launched with: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 4 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 \ --enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` All 43 MoE layers completed the FlashInfer SM90 CUTLASS W4A8 weight preprocessing path. SGLang Custom AllReduce remained enabled during startup and inference. The server passed both health and generation checks: ```text GET /health -> HTTP 200 POST /generate -> HTTP 200 Prompt: "The capital of France is" Output: " Paris..." Completion tokens: 16 End-to-end latency: 0.251 s ``` No CUDA error, runtime error, or traceback was observed during model loading, CUDA graph capture, or the generation request. Broader accuracy evaluation and GPT-OSS end-to-end coverage are still required before enabling this path by default. ## Speed Tests and Profiling FlashInfer #3738 reports broad fused-MoE kernel gains on H200, while results on H20 depend more heavily on token count and topology. Those upstream numbers are not sufficient to establish SGLang end-to-end gains. The updated downstream benchmark can be run on H100/H200 with FlashInfer 0.6.18+: ```bash FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \ python test/manual/layers/moe/bench_mxfp4_sm90_kernels.py ``` Results should be collected for decode and prefill token counts and reported as W4A16/W4A8 latency and speedup. End-to-end serving throughput and latency should also be measured before changing the default precision. | GPU | Model shape | Token range | W4A16 | Humming W4A8 | Speedup | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | H100/H200 | GPT-OSS-like | 4-8192 | TODO | TODO | TODO | | H100/H200 | DeepSeek-V4 | decode/prefill | TODO | TODO | TODO | ## Scope and Limitations - The implementation is SM90-only. - It is opt-in and does not change the default W4A16 path. - It targets the corrected per-local-expert API from FlashInfer #4431. - The current `flashinfer_mxfp4` runner is registered for the standard/no-A2A dispatcher. This PR does not add Humming support to DeepEP dispatchers. - A coordinated FlashInfer 0.6.18 dependency update and broader H100/H200 and GPT-OSS validation are required before production enablement. ## Checklist - [ ] Format the code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the repository test conventions. - [x] Update server-argument documentation. - [x] Run the registered tests on an SM90 GPU with FlashInfer 0.6.18. - [x] Add a DeepSeek-V4 end-to-end smoke-test result. - [ ] Add broader accuracy results for GPT-OSS and DeepSeek-V4. - [ ] Add downstream kernel and end-to-end performance results. - [ ] Upgrade the FlashInfer Python, cubin, and JIT-cache pins together in a coordinated follow-up change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31897611111](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31897611111)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31897749451](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31897749451)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Native Pi0.5 SigLIP vision tower
signal.text: ## Summary - extract the existing native SigLIP implementation from Gemma3 into a shared encoder - replace Pi0.5's Hugging Face `PaliGemmaModel` vision tower and runtime attention monkey patch with the native SigLIP/PiGemma composition - preserve both Gemma3 TP packed-QKV weights and Pi0.5 non-TP Transformers checkpoint names - document that the Pi0.5 runtime neural network is fully native ## Why Pi0.5 constructed a Transformers PaliGemma model, deleted its language model, and monkey-patched every SigLIP attention layer after dtype materialization. This left a third-party `nn.Module` in the native runtime and made checkpoint layout, dtype handling, attention selection, and layerwise ownership harder to reason about. The shared native encoder now owns those semantics directly. Transformers remains only for configuration, output dataclasses, and tokenization. ## Validation - remote pre-commit: passed - remote Pi0.5 unit tests: `24 passed` - `lerobot/pi05_base` real checkpoint: strict load passed - old/new real-checkpoint vision features, first-layer prefix K/V, masks, and 2-step actions: bitwise equal, max absolute error `0` - old/new Gemma3 TP SigLIP state-dict and output parity: bitwise equal, max absolute error `0` - H100 single-image SigLIP forward, 50 repeats: median `5.075 ms -> 4.858 ms` (`-4.3%`) The public Python E2E preprocessor could not be run because `google/paligemma-3b-pt-224` requires gated access in the validation environment. The direct policy validation uses the same real checkpoint and covers vision encoding, prefix K/V generation, and action denoising without tokenizer access. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31895887526](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31895887526)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31895901766](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31895901766)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Quantization] Fix GPTQ scheme attachment broken by LinearBase.scheme default
signal.text: ## Summary #29328 added a class-level `scheme = None` to `LinearBase`, which turned GPTQ's `if not hasattr(layer, "scheme")` guard into a no-op — the scheme never gets built and weight creation dies with `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'create_weights'`. Every GPTQ checkpoint fails to load; `test_gptqmodel_dynamic.py` is the only e2e test covering it. Probe becomes `layer.scheme is None`, per the repo's no-defensive-probe rule. That makes the default load-bearing, so it's declared on the other two bases a GPTQ method can be handed (`VocabParallelEmbedding` for a quantized `ParallelLMHead`, `FusedMoE` for gptq_marlin MoE), and `FusedMoE`'s two `hasattr` weight-loader reads flip with it — leaving those would set `method = None` for every unquantized and fp8 MoE layer on reload. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31894414468](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31894414468)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31894414374](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31894414374)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: mmangkad

signal.title: [Bug] Kimi-K3 tool call parser fails ~8x/hour in production: TypeError 'string indices must be integers' and json 'unexpected character'
signal.text: ## Describe the bug Running Kimi-K3 with `--tool-call-parser kimi_k3` in production (agentic coding workload, Claude-Code-style tool loop), the tool call parser raises on a significant fraction of model outputs. Over a 24h window with moderate traffic we counted **~190 parser failures**: - 106x `Tool call parsing error: string indices must be integers` (TypeError — a parsed call is indexed like a dict but is a str) - 84x `Tool call parsing error: unexpected character: line 1 column 1 (char 0)` (json.loads on a non-JSON argument payload) - 1x `Tool call parsing error: Input is a zero-length, empty document` Logged from `serving_chat.py` ("Tool call parsing error") — the request then falls back to returning the raw text instead of a structured `tool_calls` entry, so the client sees a turn without tool calls and the agent loop degrades or retries. ## Environment - SGLang 0.5.17-tree, ROCm (8x MI350X, gfx950), `--tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --enable-strict-thinking`, grammar backend xgrammar - Failures occur both with streaming and non-streaming chat completions ## Analysis `function_call/kimik3_detector.py` extracts calls via `_CALL_RE`/`_ARG_RE` and then: - `json.loads(raw_value)` on each argument value — raises `unexpected character` when the model emits an unquoted/partial value (this is exactly the second error class), and - downstream consumers index `call["name"]`/`call["arguments"]` — the `string indices` TypeError suggests a code path where the parsed call is still a plain string (e.g. malformed/partial `<|open|>call ...` block that the regex only partially matches). ## Expected behavior Malformed tool-call blocks from the model should be handled defensively (skip the malformed call and/or return it as text with a warning), never raise inside the parser. Given Kimi-K3 is explicitly advertised for agentic workloads, hardening this parser has outsized impact — at our traffic every ~7-8 minutes an agent turn silently loses its tool call. ## Reproduction We do not yet have a captured raw failing sample (the error log does not include the payload). We are happy to add debug logging in production and attach concrete failing model outputs if that helps — please tell us the preferred capture point. ## Checklist - [x] Searched existing issues — found tool_call_id-related PRs for kimi-k3 but nothing covering these parser exceptions.
signal.author: stefanskiasan

signal.title: Fix guided decoding for channel-framed reasoning
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #34631. Channel-framed reasoning formats such as Muse Glimmer emit an answer-channel header after the reasoning end marker. Guided decoding currently resumes as soon as `<|eom|>` is accepted, so the JSON grammar constrains the model-written `<|start|>assistant to=user<|message|>` header instead of starting at the answer body. ## Modifications - Add optional detector-declared markers for the channel-header boundary and for identifying another reasoning channel. - Opt Muse Glimmer into the channel-header transition. - Add an intermediate state that leaves channel headers unconstrained and does not feed them to the inner grammar. - Preserve state correctly across `copy()` and speculative rollback, including rollback that spans thinking, channel-header, and generation states. - Add `SGLANG_MAX_CHANNEL_HEADER_TOKENS` (default: 16; negative means unlimited) as a fail-safe that resumes guided decoding when a malformed header never closes. - Keep direct transitions unchanged for all other detectors and for requests without reasoning. - Add 13 off-server unit cases covering answer and repeated-reasoning channels, fail-safe behavior, multi-token markers, direct generation, copy, and rollback. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable to model forward accuracy. The state-machine regression checks pass in an isolated CPU-only harness, including the reproduction's grammar arming boundary and rollback behavior. The repository pytest module cannot be collected on this macOS development host because SGLang imports Triton at package initialization and Triton is not available on macOS. It fails before any test code executes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The change adds only small token-sequence matchers while a detector explicitly waits for a channel header; all existing detectors retain the direct transition. ## Checklist - [x] Formatted the changed files with Black and checked them with Ruff. - [x] Added unit tests for the new behavior and compatibility paths. - [x] Followed the existing reasoning grammar and environment-variable conventions. - [x] Documentation is not required; this is an internal parser boundary and the fail-safe environment variable is documented inline with the existing environment settings. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31673244768](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31673244768)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31673244621](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31673244621)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Inference Support Mamba 2 and 1
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Add SGLang support for the **Mamba family of pure state-space models**, none of which could be served before — they crashed at startup or fell through to attention code paths they don't fit. This PR covers both generations: - **Mamba2 (SSD):** `mistralai/Mamba-Codestral-7B-v0.1` - **Mamba-1 (selective-scan):** `tiiuae/falcon-mamba-7b` / `-instruct`, `state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf`, and the raw `state-spaces/mamba-{130m,790m,2.8b}` checkpoints Root causes addressed: these configs have no `num_attention_heads`/`head_dim`, so shape derivation tripped before any weights loaded; the pure-SSM path routed through the paged decoder KV cache (an SSM keeps none); Mamba2 checkpoints use `backbone.*` names with no `max_position_embeddings`; and the raw state-spaces configs carry no `model_type`/`architectures`, so `AutoConfig` rejected them outright. ## Modifications - **New models:** `Mamba2ForCausalLM` (`models/mamba2.py`), `FalconMambaForCausalLM` (`models/falcon_mamba.py`), `MambaForCausalLM` (`models/mamba.py`) — pre-norm mixer decoder layers, no MLP; weight loaders remap `backbone.* → model.*`, `embeddings/embedding. → embed_tokens`, `norm_f → norm` (Mamba2 also `A_log → A`; Mamba-1 keeps `A_log`). - **New Mamba-1 mixer** (`layers/attention/mamba/mamba1.py`, `MambaMixer1`): causal conv over intermediate channels, `x_proj`/`dt_proj` selection, optional Falcon weightless RMSNorm on `B`/`C`/`dt`. Decode reuses `selective_state_update`; prefill uses a portable per-timestep selective scan (works off-CUDA, e.g. XPU). - **Reuse of the Mamba2 backend for Mamba-1:** express the full-rank Mamba-1 state on the Mamba2 head layout (`num_heads = intermediate_size`, `head_dim = 1`) via `Mamba2StateShape.create_mamba1`, so it rides the existing attention backend and memory pool unchanged. - **Config/wiring (gated, additive):** `AttentionArch.SSM`; `PURE_SSM_ARCHITECTURES` / `PURE_MAMBA1_ARCHITECTURES` with `_is_pure_mamba2` / `_is_pure_mamba1` flags; KV-less handling (`head_dim = 0`) in `model_config.py`; cache-param build in `hybrid_arch.py`; SSM backend selection in `attention_backend_setup.py`; forward-metadata guard in `eager_runner.py`. - **Raw-checkpoint support:** `_try_load_raw_mamba_config` pre-`AutoConfig` hook in `utils/hf_transformers/config.py` builds a `MambaConfig` from the minimal `d_model`/`n_layer`/`ssm_cfg` config. - **Conv dtype fix** for fp32 checkpoints (`SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE` mismatch); CPU unit test for Mamba2 weight remapping; docs entry. All changes are gated behind the SSM arch/flag; existing MLA/MHA models keep their original code paths. ## Accuracy Tests | Model | Task | Metric | SGLang (Intel XPU) | |---|---|---|---| | Mamba-Codestral-7B-v0.1 | gsm8k (1319, 5-shot, greedy) | flexible / strict | 0.4579 / 0.4488 | | falcon-mamba-7b | gsm8k (1319, 5-shot) | flexible / strict | 0.5140 / 0.5095 | | falcon-mamba-7b-instruct | gsm8k (1319, 5-shot, chat) | flexible / strict | 0.5883 / 0.5534 | | state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf | piqa (1000, 5-shot) | acc / acc_norm | 0.649 / 0.637 (≈ published 0.64) | | state-spaces/mamba-130m (raw) | hellaswag (limit-50, 5-shot) | acc / acc_norm | 0.34 / 0.48 | | state-spaces/mamba-790m, 2.8b (raw) | — | greedy generation | coherent | All models load with 0 real skipped params. Stock server commands run unchanged (raw checkpoints need `--tokenizer-path EleutherAI/gpt-neox-20b`, a deployment flag). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Adds new models with no change to existing code paths or their speed. Serving on Intel XPU (2× Arc Pro B60): Mamba-Codestral ~36 concurrent sequences / ~220 tok/s decode (tp-size 2); Falcon-Mamba ~42 / ~200 tok/s (tp-size 1). Pure SSM models report a zero-byte KV cache, so concurrency is bounded by `--max-total-tokens` / Mamba state-cache slots rather than KV memory. Mamba-1 prefill uses a per-token selective scan (no in-tree chunked-scan kernel yet), so prefill throughput is low — a Triton Mamba-1 scan kernel is the natural follow-up. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. signal.title: fix(sgl-kernel): preload CUDA runtime before loading common ops
signal.text: ## Motivation `common_ops.so` resolves its shared-library dependencies while it is dynamically loaded. Preloading `libcudart` afterward cannot prevent an earlier `libcudart.so.*` resolution failure. ## Modifications Preload the CUDA runtime with `RTLD_GLOBAL` before loading the architecture-specific `common_ops` extension. ## Tests - `python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/kernels/aot/python/sgl_kernel/__init__.py` - `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` - `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/kernels/aot/python/sgl_kernel/__init__.py` - Manual smoke test on an NVIDIA A100 CUDA host: applied the same loader-order change to the installed `sgl_kernel` package under `site-packages` and successfully started SGLang. The original `libcudart.so.*` lookup failure was not reproducible on the test host. The change is based on the loader ordering: `common_ops.so` dependency resolution occurs before a subsequent CUDA runtime preload could run. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->pending<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->pending<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix Kimi-K3 media token resolution
signal.text: ## Motivation Kimi-K3 currently takes the `<|media_pad|>` token ID from the checkpoint configuration. When that value is stale or differs from the tokenizer vocabulary, SGLang looks for and expands the wrong token ID, breaking image-placeholder resolution for multimodal requests. The tokenizer is the source of the input IDs used at runtime, so the processor should prefer its vocabulary mapping while retaining the checkpoint value as a compatibility fallback. ## Modifications - Resolve the Kimi-K3 `<|media_pad|>` ID from the processor tokenizer vocabulary during processor initialization. - Fall back to `hf_config.media_placeholder_token_id` when the tokenizer vocabulary does not contain the placeholder. - Emit a startup warning when the tokenizer ID overrides the checkpoint-configured ID. - Propagate the resolved ID through `MultimodalSpecialTokens`, the GPU processor wrapper, and cloned processor workers. - Extend the existing Kimi processor worker test to cover tokenizer/config mismatches and the checkpoint fallback path while preserving Kimi-K2.5 coverage. ## Accuracy Tests No model-level accuracy test was run. The focused CPU regression coverage verifies that the resolved media token ID is shared by the multimodal token contract, the active Kimi-K3 wrapper, and its cloned worker. ```text python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k25.py 36 passed ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The change performs one tokenizer vocabulary lookup during Kimi-K3 processor initialization and does not add work to inference or preprocessing hot paths. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No documentation changes are required for this internal bug fix.) - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
