signal.title: fix(test): stabilize nightly precision regression
signal.text: ## Root cause [`test_nightly_precision_regression`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31501558607/job/94072436800) failed for `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` with TP=8 for two independent harness reasons: 1. The test skipped the remote restore when a self-hosted runner already had `.pt` files under `/tmp/sglang_precision_baselines`. A stale baseline captured replicated layer-entry tensors after FlashInfer fusion failed to initialize, while the target contained TP-partial tensors. Treating both as partial produced the approximately 8x mismatch. The historical initialization failure is tracked by [FlashInfer #3676](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3676) and [SGLang #30875](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/30875), and was mitigated by [SGLang #30580](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30580). 2. After a clean fused refresh, the comparator still observed rank-local BF16 buffers before fused all-reduce and residual RMSNorm. CPU-side reduction of those buffers is not the kernel's semantic output and drifted across runners. Current H200 runs initialize TRTLLM fusion on all eight ranks. This PR keeps fusion enabled and moves the comparison to `self_attn.inputs.hidden_states`, the replicated value consumed by attention after `prepare_attn()`. ## Fix - Always restore a signature-compatible remote baseline, atomically replace local tensors, and include the capture filters, TP size, and fusion backend in the signature. - Compare only the replicated post-fusion attention input. Keep layer-entry captures only as a per-layer/step/rank guard that rejects fusion fallback. - Make ordinary `/rerun-test` read-only. Add a maintainer-only, in-repo H200 refresh path: `/rerun-test --refresh-precision-baseline test/registered/debug_utils/test_nightly_precision_regression.py`. Serving runtime and all-reduce implementation code are unchanged. ## Verification - [Cross-runner Nightly comparator](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31862539092): passed all 33 post-fusion records with `max_rel_diff=0.0`. - [Cleanup-head baseline refresh](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31893911079): fusion initialized on all eight ranks and the guarded refresh passed. - [Cleanup-head read-only comparator](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31894139007): restored the refreshed baseline, passed a non-empty comparison, and did not publish. - All 42 baseline-store unit tests and changed-file pre-commit checks passed. ## Accuracy Tests No model-forward changes. The registered 8-GPU H200 test exercises the actual fused path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable; serving performance is unchanged. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31893841833](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31893841833)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31893841776](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31893841776)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: JustinTong0323

signal.title: fix(bcg): preserve Qwen3-VL DeepStack inputs during replay
signal.text: ## Motivation Prefill breakable CUDA graph (BCG) replay should preserve the same model semantics as eager execution. Qwen3-VL passes intermediate visual features through `input_deepstack_embeds` and adds them at selected language-model layers. However, BCG did not copy this request-specific tensor into a stable graph input slot. As a result, normal BCG execution behaved like an explicit zero-DeepStack run rather than eager execution. Requests still completed successfully, making this a silent correctness issue. ## Reproduction Environment: - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct` - Revision: `0c351dd01ed87e9c1b53cbc748cba10e6187ff3b` - GPU: NVIDIA H200 - Dtype: BF16 - Decoding: greedy, `max_new_tokens=20` - Input: deterministic RGB vertical-stripe image The GPU test harness temporarily enabled Qwen3-VL for BCG testing. The experiment compares four arms: 1. `eager_normal` 2. `eager_zero_deepstack` 3. `bcg_normal` 4. `bcg_zero_deepstack` The zero-DeepStack arms replace `input_deepstack_embeds` with zeros immediately before the language-model forward call. Each result is formatted as: ```text (common_prefix_length, all_token_ids_equal, maximum_absolute_logprob_difference) ``` | Comparison | Before fix | After fix | |---|---:|---:| | `bcg_normal` vs `eager_normal` | `(7, False, 1.154)` | `(15, True, 0.071)` | | `bcg_normal` vs `bcg_zero_deepstack` | `(20, True, 0.000)` | `(7, False, 1.148)` | | `bcg_zero_deepstack` vs `eager_zero_deepstack` | `(20, True, 0.066)` | `(20, True, 0.066)` | | `eager_zero_deepstack` vs `eager_normal` | `(7, False, 1.138)` | `unchanged` | Before the fix, `bcg_normal` was identical to `bcg_zero_deepstack` and diverged from `eager_normal`. After the fix, `bcg_normal` matches `eager_normal` at the token level and correctly diverges from `bcg_zero_deepstack`. The zero-DeepStack control remains unchanged. Instrumentation also confirmed that `input_deepstack_embeds` was present and non-zero at the language-model entry before replay. The RGB image is used only as a deterministic semantic-equivalence test, not as a visual-quality benchmark. ## Modifications - Add an explicit `supports_bcg_deepstack_replay` capability to Qwen3-VL. - Add an optional stable `input_deepstack_embeds` buffer and graph slot. - Allocate the slot only for multimodal models that opt in and have a non-zero DeepStack width. - Pass the stable slot during BCG capture so the DeepStack additions are included in the graph. - Copy the request-specific DeepStack tensor into the slot before replay. - Clear missing and padded regions to prevent stale data from previous requests. - Fail closed when a non-empty DeepStack tensor does not fit the captured slot, instead of replaying with a zeroed slot. - Add unit tests for capability gating, buffer allocation, slot registration, inactive model paths, and the per-replay slot lifecycle. Absence (`None` or an empty tensor) clears the slot silently; a non-empty tensor with a mismatched shape, dtype, or device raises rather than silently downgrading the request to zero-DeepStack semantics. `input_embeds` cannot be reused because DeepStack has a different shape and is consumed at selected intermediate language-model layers. Current Qwen3.5 checkpoints have no active DeepStack embeddings, so the new replay path remains inactive for them. The BCG allowlist is unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests ```bash pytest \ test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_deepstack_replay_slot.py \ test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py \ test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py \ test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner_helpers.py ``` Result: ```text 63 passed, 24 warnings, 8 subtests passed in 10.13s ``` This includes 16 new tests and 47 existing adjacent tests. The GPU four-arm validation results are shown in the Reproduction section. ## Speed Tests and Profiling This is a correctness fix, not a speed optimization. Models that do not activate DeepStack replay do not allocate the new buffer or perform the replay copy. signal.title: Fix Whisper transcription for audio over 30 seconds
signal.text: ## Summary Whisper's feature extractor pads or truncates input to its fixed 3000-mel-frame (30-second) encoder window, so `/v1/audio/transcriptions` silently drops everything after 30 seconds when the serving layer sends a long file as one generation. This change: - splits long Whisper audio into contiguous chunks of at most 30 seconds; - places each seam at the quietest 100 ms RMS window within the final second of the chunk, matching the former vLLM speech-to-text behavior; - runs non-streaming chunks concurrently and stitches results in audio order; - streams chunks sequentially with one final finish frame; - offsets `verbose_json` segment timestamps by each chunk's start time; - preserves fused language auto-detection and reports the first chunk's detected language; - gates chunking through the transcription adapter, so Qwen3-ASR and other adapters remain unchanged. Each chunk receives an independent sampling-parameter dictionary because the multimodal processor consumes transcription-only keys while preparing decoder prompts. ## Validation - Added CPU unit coverage for energy-aware split points, contiguity, maximum duration, waveform preservation, short-audio behavior, ordered stitching, chunk failures and aborts, streaming, fused auto-detection, spaceless scripts, and verbose timestamp offsets. - Added GPU endpoint coverage using a 40-second clip whose speech begins after Whisper's 30-second encoder window: JSON transcription, `verbose_json` timestamps past 30 seconds, and streaming. - The audio splitter tests pass locally (5 tests). - Changed Python files pass AST, isort, Ruff, Black, codespell, CI registry, merge-conflict, and private-key checks; `compileall` and `git diff --check` pass. - Live validation with `openai/whisper-large-v3` on a 57.06-second file produced the complete transcript, including segments after 30 seconds, with one streaming stop frame. Split points and explicit-language output matched vLLM 0.11.0. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31868247356](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31868247356)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31868247211](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31868247211)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: shenxiul

signal.title: [AMD] Enable gfx1250 Support
signal.text: ## Motivation AMD gfx1250 is a new GPU architecture that differs substantially from the existing gfx95x and gfx942 targets SGLang already supports. Several components require gfx1250-specific paths due to architectural differences: - **No MFMA/WMMA FP4 scale instructions** (`V_WMMA_SCALE_F32_32X16X128_F4`): the existing CK/ASM `fused_moe` and fp4 dense GEMM paths produce garbage or crash. - **Triton `tl.dot(fp8, fp8)` miscompiles** for contraction dim ≥ 128 on gfx1250 (verified correct at K=64, broken at K≥128), requiring bf16 upcasting in the MLA attention Triton kernels. - **`llvm.amdgcn.raw.buffer.*` buffer instructions are absent** on RDNA4 (gfx12): the `quick_all_reduce` kernel would fail to compile. - **aiter CK-backed kernels (rope, QK RMSNorm, etc.) do not build** against the gfx1250 ROCm 7.15 image's composable_kernel. - **TileLang CK-backed buffer addressing does not compile** on gfx1250, blocking the Sinkhorn/MHC path. - **`num_stages > 1` Triton pipelines miscompile** on gfx1250, causing NaN in block-FP8 matmuls. - **ROCm SDK is pip-installed** (not at `/opt/rocm`) on this new image, requiring build and runtime path fixups for AITER, TileLang, MORI, and SGLang itself. This PR brings up gfx1250 support for DSv4, DSR1, and GPT-OSS-120B models with MXFP4/FP8 quantization. ## Modifications ### Infrastructure & Docker (`docker/rocm.Dockerfile`, `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh`, `python/pyproject_other.toml`) - Added a new `gfx1250-rocm7_15` Docker build stage starting from `ubuntu:24.04` with pip-installed ROCm 7.15 SDK, PyTorch 2.11, and Triton 3.7. Includes path and symlink workarounds for a pip-based (non-`/opt/rocm`) ROCm SDK. - Added `GPU_ARCH_LIST_ARG` build-arg and made `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH` configurable; per-arch `TRITON_COMMIT_DEFAULT` env vars. - Added gfx1250-specific AITER build path (`ENABLE_CK=0`, pip `--no-build-isolation`) and MORI build path using `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` for the ROCm SDK. - Added gfx1250-aware TileLang `ROCM_PATH` override during CMake build. - Updated Triton rebuild logic to preserve the installed version string (workaround for ROCm 7.15 / [rocm-systems#7643](https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/issues/7643)). - Renamed `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION` → `SGLANG_VERSION` to avoid leaking SGLang's nightly version into AITER's version. - Added `compressed-tensors==0.16.0` pin to `runtime_common` (supports torch ≥ 2.10) and dropped the old per-`srt_hip` `==0.15.0` pin. - CI install script: ROCm-version-aware AITER rebuild (`pip --no-build-isolation` for ROCm ≥ 7.15), MORI `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` fix, and MORI commit extraction validation. ### Core utility (`python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py`) - Added `is_gfx1250_supported()` (cached) to detect AMD RDNA4 by `gcnArchName`. - Extended `mxfp_supported()` to include `"gfx1250"`. ### sgl-kernel (`sgl-kernel/setup_rocm.py`, `sgl-kernel/csrc/allreduce/quick_all_reduce_base.h`) - Added `gfx1250` to the allowed arch list in `setup_rocm.py`; gfx1250 shares the `E4M3` FP8 type and the 128KB dynamic smem budget with gfx950. - Guarded `llvm.amdgcn.raw.buffer.load/store.v4i32` declarations behind `#if !defined(__gfx1250__)`, providing stub no-ops for RDNA4 where those intrinsics don't exist. ### Attention kernels (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/`) - **`decode_attention.py`**: Do not downcast `q` to `fp8` before the QK dot; instead upcast K to `q`'s dtype (`bf16`) for the dot product, avoiding the gfx1250 fp8 dot bug at K≥128. Also keep softmax weights `p` in fp32 for the P·V accumulation (recovers GSM8K accuracy ~0.82 → ~0.92 on gfx1250 R1). - **`extend_attention.py`**: Same fp8 upcast fix and fp32 P·V fix for the prefill extend/unified kernels. - **`dsv4/unified_kv_kernels/paged_decode.py`**: On gfx1250, dispatch DSv4 sparse decode attention to `aiter.ops.triton.attention.pa_decode_sparse.pa_decode_sparse` (the triton path) instead of the custom Triton implementation. - **`dsv4/unified_kv_kernels/paged_prefill.py`**: Disable the OPUS (gfx950 ASM) prefill path on gfx1250. ### MoE gate JIT kernel (`python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/moe/moe_fused_gate.cuh`) - Widened `__shfl_down_sync` mask from `0xFFFFFFFF` to a 64-bit `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFULL` on gfx1250 (which requires a 64-bit sync mask), while staying 32-bit on all other arches. ### Layernorm (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/layernorm/mhc.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py`) - On gfx1250, use aiter's Triton RMSNorm and `rmsnorm2d_fwd_with_add` instead of the CK-backed aiter equivalents (which do not build). - Added pure-torch (`_hc_split_sinkhorn_torch`) and Triton (`_hc_split_sinkhorn_triton`) implementations of the Sinkhorn MHC kernel, dispatched on gfx1250 since TileLang's CK-backed addressing does not compile there. ### Quantization – FP8 (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`) - **`fp8_kernel.py`**: Added `_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_gfx1250`, a gfx1250-specific block-FP8 matmul that: (1) upcasts fp8 operands to bf16 before `tl.dot`, (2) uses only `num_stages=1` (no SW pipelining), and (3) avoids modulo-wrap index tricks that miscompile on gfx1250. Selected automatically when `_is_gfx1250` is set. - **`fp8_utils.py`**: Force `_use_aiter = False` on gfx1250 (CK/MFMA-dependent aiter quant/GEMM kernels cannot run), directing gfx1250 to the pure-Triton block-FP8 path. Extended `triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` to accept pre-quantized `(input, input_scale)` from gfx1250's fused quant ops (skipping re-quantization). - **`fp8.py`**: On gfx1250, use `moe_shuffle_scale` (n32k4 layout) instead of the gfx950 `shuffle_scale` (e8m0 layout) for FP8 MoE weight scales. Respect the `AITER_FORCE_A8W4` flag to select the triton a8w4 kernel shuffle layout. ### Quantization – MXFP4 Quark schemes (`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/`) - **`quark_w4a4_mxfp4.py`**: On gfx1250 with `AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1`, dequantize FP4 weights to bf16 at load time (since no dense fp4 GEMM is available) and run a plain bf16 linear forward. Includes a pure-Python MXFP4 e2m1 → bf16 dequantization LUT. - **`quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py`**: On gfx1250, use `moe_shuffle_scale` (n32k4 layout) for W4A4 MoE weight scales (instead of `e8m0_shuffle`). Shuffle weights with the (16,16) aiter layout when `AITER_FORCE_A8W4` is set. - **`quark_w4a8_mxfp4_moe.py`**: Added a dedicated gfx1250 W4A8 MoE path (`_use_gfx1250_w4a8`): bypasses the aiter CK/ASM fused_moe entirely; uses aiter's triton `moe_gemm_a8w4` kernel with a contraction-major, gate/up-interleaved, unshuffled weight layout. Weight preparation (`_process_weights_gfx1250`) and forward (`aiter_w4a8_gfx1250_forward` in new file `aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe.py`) are implemented separately from the gfx950 path. ### New file: `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe.py` - Implements MXFP4 W4A8 GPT-OSS MoE forward for gfx1250 via `moe_gemm_a8w4`: routing, manual activation gather (in-kernel TDM gather disabled on gfx1250), static-FP8 downcast, two-GEMM (gate_up + down) execution with fused SwiGLU, and scatter back to token order. ### RoPE (`python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py`) - Fall back from aiter's CK rope kernels to SGLang's native rope on gfx1250 (aiter rope does not build on this arch). ### Communicator / fused quant (`python/sglang/srt/layers/communicator.py`) - On gfx1250, use `fused_rms_fp8_group_quant` (triton, group_size=hidden_size = per-token) instead of aiter's CK `rmsnorm_quant` / `add_rmsnorm_quant` kernels. ### Sampler (`python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py`) - Disable aiter's greedy sample kernel on gfx1250 (not supported), falling back to `torch.argmax`. ### Capture mode (`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_utils/capture_mode.py`) - Disable `torch.compile` during CUDA graph capture on gfx1250 (compilation + capture together triggers issues on this arch). ### MLA attention (`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py`, new `triton_qk_rmsnorm.py`) - On gfx1250 (`AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1`), substitute the aiter `fused_qk_rmsnorm` (CK-backed, doesn't build) with a self-contained Triton RMSNorm or pure-torch fallback from the new `triton_qk_rmsnorm.py`. - Fixed the RoPE skip condition to check membership in `FORWARD_ABSORB_CORE_ATTENTION_BACKENDS` (not a string equality check), preventing an incorrect empty-K bug on non-aiter backends. ### DSv4 decoder layer (`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`, `deepseek_common/utils.py`, `amd/deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py`) - Extended all `_is_gfx95_supported` guards that gate MXFP4 fused quant, MQA q/k-norm, post-attention layernorm fused rmsnorm, and the fused MHC post/pre path to also include `_is_gfx1250_supported`. - On gfx1250, the fused MHC path is enabled by `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE` alone (no TileLang dependency), and the aiter Triton `try_fused_hc_post_pre` is used at all token batch sizes (no M-threshold cap, since there is no TileLang fallback). - gfx1250 does not skip the post-layernorm step after the Triton MHC kernel (since `norm_fused=False` for the aiter path). ### C4 attention indexer (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py`) - Added `_use_torch_fn` guard so the `SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH` env var correctly prevents the 1D c4sl unsqueeze on gfx1250. ### Server args (`python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`) - Track `_mem_fraction_static_set_by_user`: when the user explicitly sets `--mem-fraction-static`, skip the automatic 0.85 scaling for `aiter` backend with long contexts (instead, emit a warning so the user knows what is happening). ## Accuracy Tests Passed E2E accuracy tests of DSv4, DSR1, and GPT-OSS-120B. GPT-OSS-120B > AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8/ --trust-remote-code --tp 1 --prefill-attention-backend triton --decode-attention-backend aiter --max-running-requests 1024 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --disable-radix-cache --page-size 64 DSR1 > ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 AITER_GROUPED_FORCE_SPLIT_K1=1 SGLANG_MOE_SHUFFLE_GFX1250=1 ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=NONE SGLANG_AITER_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=0 SGLANG_AITER_MLA_PERSIST=0 SGLANG_INT4_WEIGHT=0 SGLANG_MOE_PADDING=1 SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1 SGLANG_ROCM_FUSED_DECODE_MLA=0 SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=1 AITER_GROUPED_CONTIGUOUS_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=16 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --trust-remote-code --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --attention-backend triton --max-running-requests 128 --kv-cache-dtype auto --page-size 64 DSv4-Flash > SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 AITER_GROUPED_CONTIGUOUS_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=16 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=max SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0 SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=0 SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE=0 ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_GROUPED_FORCE_SPLIT_K1=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --trust-remote-code --tp 1 --attention-backend dsv4 --page-size 256 --mem-fraction-static 0.60 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --disable-shared-experts-fusion --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --cuda-graph-max-bs 256 --max-running-requests 256 --disable-radix-cache --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 ## signal.title: [Diffusion] Native SANA-WM stage-2 refiner stack
signal.text: ## Summary - replace the SANA-WM stage-2 Diffusers/HF runtime modules with native SGLang refiner, connector, and text-only Gemma-3 implementations - route nested refiner components through the unified component loaders and support layerwise offload for `transformer_2`, `text_encoder_2`, and `connectors` - remove duplicate batch/streaming Diffusers forward paths, preserve streaming KV behavior behind explicit model APIs, and document the native runtime/residency behavior ## Details - loads the released audiovisual LTX-2 checkpoint into a video-only 48-layer refiner while treating only the known audio/AV branches as intentionally unused - avoids materializing the unused 416M-parameter Gemma-3 vision tower - keeps Diffusers/Transformers checkpoint compatibility and the existing tokenizer path - fixes the packed/5D refiner output contract and keeps timestep scaling owned by the native model - removes the low-signal warning listing 2295 expected unused audio/AV checkpoint keys while preserving warnings for unknown keys ## Validation - `pre-commit run --files ...` - remote H100: `103 passed` for SANA-WM native/config tests and FSDP loader tests - released SANA-WM checkpoint, BF16 math SDPA: - Gemma-3: all 49 hidden states bitwise identical to HF on the runtime-valid 128-token path; signal.title: [Fix] Stream prose between and after DSML tool calls
signal.text:
## Motivation The DSML streaming path only recovers the text in front of the **first** tool call. #34458 fixed that lead and left a note in the code saying the rest is still missing: ```python # Only recovered for the first call: the DSML guard above never releases a # buffer that still holds a marker, so later prose stays buffered. ``` Content is lost two different ways after that first call: - **Between two calls — dropped.** Consuming the second invoke sets `self._buffer = current_text[invoke_match.end():]`, advancing straight past the text in front of it. - **After the last call — stranded.** The section closer keeps `potentially_dsml` true for the rest of the turn, so the guard at the top never releases the buffer, and nothing flushes it at end of turn. Reproduced against `main` (`DeepSeekV4Detector`, one call, then prose, then a second call): ``` normal_text = '' buffer left = '
</｜DSML｜tool_calls>' ``` The prose never reaches the client. Both paths are DSML-specific; the pythonic detector already streams this text, and `test_parse_streaming_multiple_tool_calls` asserts it does. Two further problems surfaced in review, both fixed here: - **A turn that ends inside an invoke repeated its lead and leaked markup.** Only a completed call advances the buffer, so an invoke cut short leaves its lead in there after it has already been emitted, and `finish()` released it a second time — along with the half-written tag and its partial JSON, since `_strip_section_markers` only removes tags that finished arriving. That shape is what a length-capped or aborted generation looks like, and it was a regression against `main` on both counts. - **`detect_and_parse` disagreed with the streaming path.** The one-shot path drops everything between and after the sections — precisely the text this PR recovers for streaming — so the same generation read differently depending on `stream=`. ## Modifications **Streaming** - Collect the lead text for every call instead of only the first, guarded on `current_tool_name_sent` so an invoke spanning several deltas cannot re-emit its lead, and drop it from the buffer as soon as it is emitted so nothing can release it again. - Flush the residual buffer once nothing left in it parses as a call. - Hold back a suffix that could still grow into a marker, plus a trailing newline run, since newlines indent DSML tags and emitting one before its tag arrives is not something a later delta can take back. - `finish()` separates the two things it can be holding: a fragment kept back for a marker that never came was ordinary text all along and is owed to the client, whereas a buffer the turn stopped inside of is markup by then and is dropped. **One-shot** - `detect_and_parse` walks the sections as match objects and appends the text between and after them. - A partial opening tag no longer reaches the client as content: `text.find(bot_token)` never saw it, so a turn cut off mid-tag returned the tag verbatim. Pre-existing on `main`. **Shared** - Both paths trim a gap the same way. The call sat on its own line, so a gap's leading whitespace collapses to the one line break the call was standing on, plus whatever follows the last newline in it — that belongs to the line the prose resumes on, and dropping it takes the indent off a code line and stops a list item starting its line. It collapses to nothing only when no text has been emitted yet, where the turn opened with the call and there is nothing on the other side to separate from, and it is left alone when it holds no newline at all, where the call was inline. Trailing layout goes wherever another section follows and can claim the whitespace as its indent; the last gap ends the turn, so its trailing newlines are the model's own. - On the streaming side that trim spans deltas, so it is tracked on the instance rather than applied to each chunk in isolation — a newline in the middle of the prose has to survive. ## Accuracy Test The two paths now agree, so the tests assert exactly that: streamed `normal_text` and merged calls equal `detect_and_parse`, over 15 turn shapes at chunk sizes down to one character per delta, and over every prefix of a turn for the cut-short case (text only there — streaming a cut-off call is what the incremental protocol is for, while the one-shot path has no complete section to report). That invariant subsumes the per-chunk substring checks it replaces, and is what surfaced the whitespace differences fixed here. Checked more widely offline than the committed tests run: 16 shapes across both detectors at 26 chunkings, and 6152 truncation prefixes at 7 chunkings — no divergence, no markup in `normal_text`, no chunk-dependent output, and the buffer drained at end of turn every time. One deliberate departure from `main`: the preamble is trimmed with `rstrip()` rather than `removesuffix("

")`. The separator now comes from the far side of the call, so leaving one behind here too opens a blank line the model never wrote. Both paths change together. With the trims equal on either side of a call, the first call no longer needs a rule of its own. The joined text is asserted directly as well as through the comparison. It has to be: the streaming and one-shot paths agreed with each other on every shape below while both were dropping the line break, so the invariant alone is blind to it. | turn | content | | --- | --- | | `'Let me look it up.

' + call + '
It is sunny in SF.'` | `'Let me look it up.
It is sunny in SF.'` | | `'我查一下。

' + call + '
旧金山是晴天。'` | `'我查一下。
旧金山是晴天。'` | | `call + '
And now the other one:
' + call + '
Done.'` | `'And now the other one:
Done.'` | | `'Here you go:

' + call + '
- SF: sunny
- LA: hot
'` | `'Here you go:
- SF: sunny
- LA: hot
'` | | `'Result:
' + call + '
 x = True
'` | `'Result:
 x = True
'` | ## Checklist - Each new case fails on the code it guards against and passes on the fix: 36 and 600 failing subtests against the pre-fix detector, 25 against the one before the line break was kept. The 8 pre-existing cases kept in the file pass either way. - `test_deepseekv4_detector.py`: 12 tests, 0 failures. - `test_function_call_parser.py`: 205 tests, 0 failures, identical before and after this change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #31892090181](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31892090181)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #31892090039](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31892090039)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Align MiniMax H3 request RNG with reference
signal.text: ## Summary - use one request-local CPU generator for MiniMax H3 noise - preserve the reference draw order: visual conditions, target video tensor, then target audio rows - precompute condition noise before denoising instead of re-seeding per modality or condition - keep the existing H3-only scope so other diffusion consistency trajectories are unchanged ## Why The previous implementation independently re-seeded video, audio, and condition streams. For T2VA this made the target audio latent diverge immediately; because H3 jointly attends over video and audio rows, video output also drifted. The new contract follows the official Diffusers MiniMax H3 implementation from huggingface/diffusers#14355. ## Validation - focused MiniMax H3 numerical contract: 5 passed on H100 devbox - pre-commit: passed on the exact remote checkout - standard 2-GPU H100 E2E: 1 passed in 176.29s (47.50s generation, 22.5 GiB peak GPU memory) - official GT workflow: [run 31890047128](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890047128) succeeded - ci-data GT commit: [81ca8f18](https://github.com/sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion/commit/81ca8f18d485df4e4bac9a5a40c5b4666f0fa57f) - NVIDIA PR CI: [run 31890556920](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890556920) succeeded The GT follow-up is intentionally limited to the affected MiniMax H3 H100 T2VA frames. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31890556920](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890556920)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31890556799](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890556799)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] DSPARK silently corrupts identifiers on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, making speculative decoding unsafe
signal.text:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug

Summary

On DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, SGLang’s DSPARK speculative decoding silently introduces single-character corruptions into identifiers supplied verbatim in the prompt:

kimi-k3 → kimi-kw nova-x7 → nova-7 apollo-n9 → apollo-n11

The same server, weights, prompts, and launch configuration—with only speculative decoding disabled—produces zero such corruptions across thousands of grounded identifier tokens.

The corruption rate increases with the DSPARK verify-window width:

--speculative-dspark-block-size | speculative_num_draft_tokens | Temp 0 | Temp 1 -- | -- | -- | -- 6 | 7 | 1.03% | 0.82% 5 | 6 | 0.32% | 0.77% 1 | 2 | 0.00% | 0.00% Speculation disabled | — | 0.00% | 0.00%

Aggregated across both block_size=1 runs:

  • Temperature 0: 0 / 4561
  • Temperature 1: 0 / 3701

Using the rule of three, the corresponding approximate 95% upper bounds are:

  • Temperature 0: <0.066%
  • Temperature 1: <0.081%

This contrasts with the 1.03% observed rate at block_size=6, temperature 0.

Examples of corrupted identifiers

Malformed forms observed at block_size=6, temperature 0:

kimi-kw -> kimi-k3 (x5) kimi-k2 -> kimi-k3 (x3) kimi-k7 -> kimi-k3 (x2) apollo-n11 -> apollo-n9 (x2) nova-12 -> nova-x7 (x2) wq-7f2e -> wq-7f2b (x2) kimi-kw2 -> kimi-k3 kimi-v2 -> kimi-k3 kimi-k11 -> kimi-k3 apollo-n12 -> apollo-n9 nova-7 -> nova-x7 nova-v7 -> nova-x7 wq-7f2e2 -> wq-7f2b

These are not malformed responses or obvious decoding failures. They are plausible-looking, single-character-wrong identifiers embedded in otherwise normal output.

Expected behavior

At temperature 0, DSPARK should emit the same greedy token sequence as the target model without speculative decoding.

A draft token should only be committed if it matches the corresponding target prediction. On mismatch, DSPARK should emit the target prediction instead.

Therefore, enabling DSPARK should not change grounded identifiers from:

kimi-k3

to:

kimi-kw

when the non-speculative target forward selects the correct token.

Actual behavior

With multi-position DSPARK verification enabled:

  • Grounded identifiers are silently corrupted.
  • The issue reproduces at temperature 0.
  • The issue requires or is strongly amplified by heterogeneous concurrent batching.
  • The rate increases with verify-window width.
  • No request error or warning is produced.
  • The finish reason remains normal.
  • Disabling speculation eliminates the corruption.
  • Reducing DSPARK to block_size=1 eliminates the corruption.

Hypotheses investigated and ruled out

1. Lossy accept/verify rule

This does not appear to be the cause.

Both accept_greedy and accept_greedy_triton in:

sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/dspark/dspark_accept.py

delegate to compute_dflash_correct_drafts_and_bonus in:

sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py

The relevant logic is:

matches = candidates[:, 1:] == target_predict[:, :-1] correct_len = matches.to(torch.int32).cumprod(dim=1).sum(dim=1) bonus = target_predict[torch.arange(bs, ...), correct_len]

Every committed token should therefore be either:

  1. An accepted draft token that compared equal to target_predict; or
  2. The bonus token, which is taken directly from target_predict.

A mismatching draft token should not be able to leak into the output.

This implies that the corrupted emitted tokens are likely themselves present in target_predict. In other words, the target verify forward appears to be producing incorrect logits or incorrect token alignment.

2. Ragged verify-window misalignment

accept_greedy performs:

torch.argmax(target_logits, dim=-1).view( bs, verify_num_draft_tokens )

A dense reshape could misalign tokens if requests had different verify lengths.

However, SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE defaults to static. In static mode, resolve_ragged_verify_layout returns None, and verify lengths are uniform.

Therefore, the rectangular reshape is expected to be valid for this reproduction.

3. Numerical noise or batch-shape-dependent reductions

We tested three separate interventions. Each was verified to engage, and none removed the corruption.

FP32 LM head

Enabled:

--enable-fp32-lm-head

Engagement was confirmed empirically:

  • Before the change, 65.5% of recorded margins fell on the 0.25 BF16 grid.
  • After the change, 0% did.
  • There were zero exact ties across 34,420 records.

The typo rate did not improve.

Deterministic FP32 MoE reduction

We forced:

use_atomic_add = False

so the already-passed:

use_fp32_reduce = True

would engage.

In:

sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_wna16_marlin.py

the FP32 temporary buffer is allocated only under:

if use_fp32_reduce and not use_atomic_add:

This provides a structural confirmation that the path was active.

The observed rates remained approximately:

  • Temperature 0: 1.03%
  • Temperature 1: 0.82%

Tie epsilon on sampled accept path

Adding a tie epsilon to the sampled acceptance path had no effect.

More generally, an identifier repeated verbatim several times in the prompt should usually be a high-margin prediction. Low-order numerical noise would not be expected to repeatedly transform such identifiers into plausible alternatives.

The non-speculative control also varies in free-form prose between temperature-0 runs—likely due to prefix-cache or chunked-prefill effects—but it never corrupts a grounded identifier.

4. Draft/target gamma mismatch

The CLI can override the draft checkpoint’s declared gamma with only a warning:

DSpark gamma mismatch: using gamma=6 (from speculative_num_draft_tokens=7) but draft config block_size=5.

This occurs in:

sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_config.py

The draft module itself obtains gamma from the checkpoint:

self.gamma = int(dspark_config.resolve_gamma(...))

in:

sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_dspark.py

This means the draft module and worker may disagree about the verify-window width.

However, running with block_size=5:

  • Makes the configured values agree
  • Removes the warning
  • Still reproduces the bug

Observed rates at block_size=5 were:

  • Temperature 0: 0.32%
  • Temperature 1: 0.77%

Therefore, the gamma mismatch is not the root cause of this corruption, although the silent override may be worth hardening as a separate issue.

5. Draft-side kernels

SGLANG_DSPARK_FAST_KERNEL only gates the draft forward.

Under a correct speculative verification rule, draft quality may affect acceptance and performance, but it should not affect temperature-0 correctness. Incorrect draft tokens should be rejected in favor of the target prediction.

Therefore, a draft-only kernel failure does not explain committed token corruption unless there is also a target-verification or alignment bug.

Suspected fault area

The following is a hypothesis, not yet a verified root cause.

Given that:

  1. The accept rule appears to emit only target_predict;
  2. The corruption reproduces at temperature 0;
  3. The corruption disappears at a two-position verify window;
  4. The rate generally increases with verify-window width;
  5. Multiple numerical-determinism interventions had no effect; and
  6. The issue depends on concurrent heterogeneous batching,

the likely fault is in the target verify forward for multi-position DSPARK verification, especially for in-block positions t >= 1.

Potential areas include:

  • Intra-block causal masking
  • Position-ID construction or indexing
  • KV-cache placement for draft positions
  • Request-to-token mapping under heterogeneous batching
  • CUDA graph replay metadata for TARGET_VERIFY
  • Batch-slot reuse or stale per-request metadata
  • dsv4 attention behavior during multi-token verification

The current evidence suggests the target verification pass is computing incorrect logits or associating correct logits with the wrong request/position.

We have not yet isolated the specific kernel or metadata transition.

Suggested next diagnostics

A useful first datapoint would be:

--speculative-dspark-block-size 2

This would help distinguish between:

  • Failure beginning at the first genuinely multi-position verify step; and
  • Error probability accumulating with larger verify windows.

Other useful comparisons may include:

  1. DSPARK with CUDA graphs disabled.
  2. DSPARK with the hierarchical cache disabled.
  3. DSPARK with radix cache and chunked prefill disabled.
  4. An alternate attention backend, if DeepSeek-V4-Flash supports one.
  5. Capturing target_predict before acceptance and comparing it against independent one-token target forwards.
  6. Logging request IDs, verify positions, position IDs, and KV locations for the first divergent token.

Workaround

Both of the following avoid the observed corruption:

Option 1: Disable speculative decoding

This is the safest workaround.

Option 2: Use block_size=1

--speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 1

This produced zero true typos across:

  • 4,561 grounded identifiers at temperature 0
  • 3,701 grounded identifiers at temperature 1

However, this sacrifices most of the speculative speedup, so it is a mitigation rather than a practical fix.

Until the multi-position verification issue is resolved, DSPARK should not be used with DeepSeek-V4-Flash for workloads where exact token reproduction matters.

Reproduction notes

DeepGEMM JIT warmup

Changing:

--speculative-dspark-block-size

changes num_tokens_per_req and invalidates the DeepGEMM JIT shape cache.

The first launch after changing this value may compile approximately 16,000 shapes and exceed a 3,600-second readiness budget. If the process is killed during warmup, it may look like an unrelated startup failure.

Please allow additional warmup time when changing the block size.

Log probabilities unavailable

DSPARK currently rejects:

"return_logprob": true

with:

DFLASH speculative decoding does not support return_logprob yet

Therefore, per-token target margins cannot currently be collected over HTTP on the affected speculative arm.

Severity

This is a silent data-corruption issue, not only a quality or performance regression.

The generated response is well-formed, and the corrupted identifier often looks plausible. Downstream systems therefore have no reliable way to distinguish the incorrect value from an intended value.

For DeepSeek-V4-Flash, this makes multi-position DSPARK speculative decoding unsafe for exact-identifier and tool-use workloads.

### Reproduction

Reproduction

The corruption usually requires concurrent, heterogeneous batching. A single request in isolation may not reproduce it. The script below sends four byte-identical target requests and four variable-length distractor requests per round.

1. Launch the affected DSPARK configuration

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <deepseek-v4-flash-0731> \ --tp 4 \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 6 \ --max-running-requests 16 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16

2. Save the reproduction script

Save the following code as dspark_typo_repro.py:

#!/usr/bin/env python3 """Concurrency typo probe for one model and temperature.""" import collections import concurrent.futures import json import os import re import time import urllib.error import urllib.request MODEL = os.environ["TEST_MODEL"] TEMP = float(os.environ.get("TEST_TEMP", "0")) ROUNDS = int(os.environ.get("TEST_ROUNDS", "30")) BASE = os.environ.get("TEST_BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:30000") URL = f"{BASE}/v1/chat/completions" IDS = [ "kimi-k3", "nova-x7", "atlas-j9", "wq-7f2b", "zeta-r1", "apollo-n9", ] CTX = " ".join( f"event{i}=ok latency={i % 37}ms owner=team{i % 9}" for i in range(350) ) PROMPT = ( f"Analyze this deployment history and write a 6-section operational report. " f"{CTX}\n" f"Canonical identifiers: {', '.join(IDS)}. " "Include a table and prose recap. " "Use every identifier at least four times, always verbatim; " "do not invent or normalize identifiers." ) RX = re.compile(r"[a-z][a-z0-9]*-[a-z0-9]+", re.I) def lev(a, b): prev = list(range(len(b) + 1)) for i, x in enumerate(a, 1): cur = [i] for j, y in enumerate(b, 1): cur.append( min( cur[-1] + 1, prev[j] + 1, prev[j - 1] + (x != y), ) ) prev = cur return prev[-1] def ask(prompt=PROMPT, max_tokens=700, retries=5): body = json.dumps( { "model": MODEL, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], "max_tokens": max_tokens, "temperature": TEMP, "top_p": 1.0, } ).encode() for n in range(retries): request = urllib.request.Request( URL, data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, ) try: with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=300) as response: result = json.load(response) return result["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] or "" except urllib.error.HTTPError as error: if error.code not in (429, 503) or n + 1 == retries: raise time.sleep(0.3 * (n + 1)) raise RuntimeError("retries exhausted") wrong = collections.Counter() truncations = collections.Counter() error_types = collections.Counter() exact = 0 grounded = 0 responses = 0 errors = 0 typo_responses = 0 started = time.time() with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool: for rnd in range(ROUNDS): futures = [pool.submit(ask) for _ in range(4)] # Variable-length distractors perturb server-side batch composition. for j in range(4): length = 50 + ((rnd * 67 + j * 97) % 500) distractor = "Summarize: " + " ".join( f"word{k}" for k in range(length) ) futures.append(pool.submit(ask, distractor, 128)) for future in futures[:4]: try: text = future.result() responses += 1 except Exception as error: errors += 1 error_types[type(error).__name__] += 1 continue response_has_typo = False for token in ( match.lower().rstrip(".,;:") for match in RX.findall(text) ): if token in IDS: exact += 1 grounded += 1 continue distance, target = min( (lev(token, identifier), identifier) for identifier in IDS ) if distance <= 2: grounded += 1 if any(identifier.startswith(token) for identifier in IDS): # Prefixes are output-limit truncations, not typos. truncations[(token, target, distance)] += 1 else: wrong[(token, target, distance)] += 1 response_has_typo = True typo_responses += response_has_typo for future in futures[4:]: try: future.result() except Exception: pass print( f"MODEL={MODEL} TEMP={TEMP} rounds={ROUNDS} " f"responses={responses} errors={errors} " f"errtypes={dict(error_types)} " f"elapsed={time.time() - started:.1f}s" ) print( f"grounded_ids={grounded} exact={exact} " f"true_typos={sum(wrong.values())} " f"typo_responses={typo_responses} " f"rate={(sum(wrong.values()) / grounded if grounded else 0):.4%} " f"truncations={sum(truncations.values())}" ) print("typo_forms:", dict(wrong.most_common(20)) or "NONE")

A true typo is a token with Levenshtein distance 1–2 from a canonical identifier that is not a prefix of one. Prefixes are counted separately as output-limit truncations.

3. Run the reproduction at temperature 0

TEST_MODEL=<served-model-name> \ TEST_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:30000 \ TEST_TEMP=0 \ TEST_ROUNDS=30 \ python3 -u dspark_typo_repro.py

4. Repeat at temperature 1

TEST_MODEL=<served-model-name> \ TEST_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:30000 \ TEST_TEMP=1 \ TEST_ROUNDS=30 \ python3 -u dspark_typo_repro.py

5. Run the non-speculative control

Relaunch the server with all --speculative-* flags removed while leaving every other launch argument unchanged. Repeat both commands above. This control produced zero true typos.

6. Test the block-size workaround

Relaunch DSPARK with a block size of 1: 

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <deepseek-v4-flash-0731> \ --tp 4 \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 1 \ --max-running-requests 16 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16

Repeat the temperature-0 and temperature-1 tests. This configuration also produced zero true typos.

Expected result

At temperature 0, DSPARK should produce the same greedy token sequence as non-speculative decoding. All identifiers supplied verbatim in the prompt should be emitted without modification.

Observed result

With --speculative-dspark-block-size 6, the output silently contains plausible single-character corruptions such as: 

kimi-k3 -> kimi-kw nova-x7 -> nova-7 apollo-n9 -> apollo-n11 wq-7f2b -> wq-7f2e

In one temperature-0 run, 23 of 2,224 grounded identifiers were corrupted (1.0342%), affecting 15 of 120 target responses. The same test produced zero corruptions with speculative decoding disabled and with DSPARK block size 1.

Reproduction note

Changing --speculative-dspark-block-size changes num_tokens_per_req and may invalidate the DeepGEMM JIT shape cache. The first launch after changing the block size can require a long recompilation warmup. Allow enough startup time to prevent the server from being killed before it becomes ready.

### Environment Run this **inside the same Python environment/container used to launch the affected SGLang server**: ```bash python3 -m sglang.check_env 2>&1 | tee sglang_check_env.txt ``` Then paste the **complete command output verbatim** into that field, preferably wrapped as: ```text ``` Do not substitute the manually listed environment details; the maintainers explicitly require the actual `check_env` output.

signal.title: [AMD] Avoid padded Q for unified DSV4 prefill
signal.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek V4 TP prefill currently allocates a decode-oriented 64-head padded Q tensor, then passes the local-head slice to the unified-KV attention backend. At TP=8 that slice has 16 heads and is noncontiguous, so the OPUS wrapper materializes it with `q.contiguous()` before launching the kernel. The 64-head layout is useful for the FlashMLA sparse decode specialization, but unified-KV extend/prefill does not require it. ## Modifications - evaluate the unified-KV gate once per `MQALayer.forward` call - skip TP head padding for unified-KV extend modes and write Q directly in contiguous local-head layout - retain the existing 64-head padded layout for decode - retain existing behavior for non-unified backends - add real `MQALayer.forward` control-flow tests for unified prefill, decode, fallback, multi-stream, and prefill-CP routing ## Accuracy Tests The focused test runs through the real `MQALayer.forward` control flow and verifies: - unified EXTEND, MIXED, TARGET_VERIFY, and SPLIT_PREFILL use contiguous local-head Q - unified DECODE retains 64-head padding - non-unified modes retain the previous layout - HIP multi-stream and prefill-CP paths preserve the intended decision Result: `4 tests passed` in the official ROCm MI355X image after rebasing onto current `main`. Static validation also passed: Ruff (`F401,F821,UP037`), `py_compile`, registered-test validation, and `git diff --check`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling At the production sparse-prefill shape, the OPUS wrapper-to-kernel delta was 43.5-44.7 us per call across three runs. That delta includes wrapper dispatch and argument handling, so it is an upper bound on the removable contiguous-copy cost, not a model-level or TTFT result. ## Model E2E (MI355X, TP8 / DP1) The branch was rebased onto current `main` (`ab9e7abad`; parent `c87a2ced1`) and tested in the pinned ROCm image on 8 x MI355X. Both arms used unified-KV DSV4 attention, TP8/DP1, chunked prefill 8,192, OSL=1, distinct uncached token sequences, one warmup, and repeated scored requests. - 8K: baseline median **318.23 ms**, candidate **315.29 ms** (**0.93%** improvement); all five output tokens matched. - 64K first sandwich: baseline median **2,790.31 ms**, candidate **2,771.56 ms** (**0.68%** improvement); all five output tokens matched. Candidate had one server-side **11.90 s** outlier, so the five-sample P90/mean regressed despite the steady-state median gain. - 64K candidate follow-up: ten fresh uncached prompts, median **2,772.25 ms**, P90 **2,782.55 ms**, range **2,765.25-2,808.13 ms**, zero retractions; the outlier did not reproduce. - 64K A2/B with the same ten fresh prompt indices: baseline median/P90/mean **2,793.65 / 2,795.65 / 2,793.33 ms**; candidate **2,772.25 / 2,782.55 / 2,775.21 ms**, improving **0.77% / 0.47% / 0.65%**. All ten output tokens matched; neither arm had an outlier above 2x its median. - Baseline A1 -> A2 drift on the original five prompt indices was **0.30%** at the median (A2 slower), below the candidate's steady-state improvement. The result is a small steady-state E2E win, not the larger wrapper-level upper bound. The isolated 11.90 s event is retained as a tail-risk observation; it did not reproduce in either ten-request arm and is not attributed to this Q-layout change. ## Checklist - [x] Add focused unit tests - [x] Preserve decode and non-unified behavior - [x] Provide accuracy and operator profiling evidence - [x] Complete model E2E and graph-capture validation - [ ] Documentation update (not needed for this internal layout change) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31890497031](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890497031)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31890496542](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890496542)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.author: mmangkad

signal.title: SGLang scale-down number of processes.
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang's upstream elastic-EP supports **scale-up** (adding ranks) and **fault recovery** (recovering a rank that crashed), but not runtime **scale-down** (retiring live ranks from a serving deployment). This PR adds a Mooncake-native scale-down path, layered on top of upstream's existing elastic-EP infrastructure, and stabilizes end-to-end shrink + grow flows against Mooncake C++'s runtime constraints. The design principle is simple: at launch, allocate `--max-ep-size` ranks and immediately **pre-shrink** to the operator's desired starting size. Every subsequent scale-up is then treated as a *grow-into-retired-slot* operation via upstream's v1 recovery path, and every scale-down is a retirement of a contiguous suffix of live ranks. This unifies scale-up and scale-down under one contract (the `active_ranks` bitmask), keeps the mask size stable across the lifetime of the deployment, and lets us reuse upstream's `maybe_recover_ep_ranks` machinery unchanged. ## What this PR adds ### 1. Scale-down finite state machine (new) `ElasticEPStateManager` gains a scale-down phase graph: ``` serving ──POST /scale_elastic_ep(target<current)──▶ waiting_for_retire │ ▼ drain (admission gate; drain in-flight batches) │ ▼ flip_mask (survivors clear active_ranks[retiree]; retirees run local Mooncake quiesce + os._exit(0)) │ ▼ reconfig (Mooncake update_ep_member; broadcast_global_expert_location_metadata) │ ▼ local_cleanup (rearm EPLB, reset expert distribution recorder) │ ▼ serving_shrunk ``` Driver lives in `python/sglang/srt/elastic_ep/scale_down_state.py` (new) with per-tick callbacks (`on_prepare` / `on_flip_mask` / `on_reconfig` / `on_exit`) implemented on `ModelRunner`. The scheduler + tokenizer manager gate new admissions on the phase. ### 2. NIXL retire barrier (new) A TCPStore-backed elected-leader epoch derivation coordinates the `flip_mask` transition across the surviving cohort. Handles rank-drift, arrival-counter rollback, catch-up busy-polling, and the same-tick DRAIN fold. Full implementation in `python/sglang/srt/elastic_ep/elastic_ep.py::nixl_retire_barrier_{post,check,consume}`. ### 3. Two-cycle Mooncake retire primitive (new) `try_retire_ranks(retirees)` fences via `cuda.synchronize()`, clears `active_ranks[retiree]=0` on every launch-time PG, calls `mooncake_ep.update_ep_member(WORLD, active_ranks)`, and awaits a completion barrier. Retirees separately execute `_retire_and_exit(...)` which quiesces Mooncake buffers and calls `os._exit(0)` — deliberately *not* `sys.exit(0)`, so we avoid pytest atexit hooks that would re-enter the Mooncake destructor and hang. ### 4. Grow-into-retired-slot via v1 recovery (new integration) When the operator POSTs `/scale_elastic_ep` with `target > effective_ep_size`, the scheduler now populates `ElasticEPStateManager.pending_recover_ranks` from `active_ranks == 0` slots, and `maybe_join_ep_ranks` routes through upstream's `try_recover_ranks` + `_finalize_scale_recover` instead of `try_admit_scale_ranks`. Retired slots stay in the Mooncake peer table for exactly this reason, so no new joiner subprocess needs to negotiate a wider WORLD. The joiner subprocess (`server_args.ep_join_mode="recover"` + non-zero `ep_join_rank_offset`) initializes elastic-EP state via `ModelRunner.__init__` before `initialize()`, gets its `active_ranks` mask flipped ON, and syncs the random seed from the survivor cohort via TCPStore (paired write in `_finalize_scale_recover`, `is_source=True`). ### 5. Runtime stabilization - **`retire_barrier_consume` skips `Work.wait()` when the TCPStore counter confirms all ranks posted** — Mooncake's async collective can hang here asymmetrically after retiree exit; the counter is the authoritative signal. - **Same-tick DRAIN fold**: `scale_down_state.py` no longer returns to the scheduler between DRAIN-posted and DRAIN-consumed on the same tick, avoiding a 30s stall in the NIXL a2a barrier. - **TCPStore initialization for Mooncake WORLD**: `_create_global_tcp_store` runs unconditionally when elastic-EP is enabled (previously NIXL-only), so the elected-leader epoch works uniformly. - **`_finalize_scale_up` writes `self.dp_size = target_size`**: `update_dp_attention_post_scale` only updates module globals; downstream consumers reading `ModelRunner.dp_size` (DP-attention-aware kernels, DPC-side elasticity accounting) would otherwise see the stale launch value. - **`maybe_join_ep_ranks` silent-skips on `has_scaled` when `pending_size is None`**: upstream's original called `fail_recovery` which sets `scale_phase="recovery_unsupported"` and blocks every subsequent scale request. Our design needs scale-up and scale-down to remain requestable after any prior scale, so we return silently. - **Local timeout check** (per-rank `time.monotonic()` on `pending_since`) instead of upstream's `dist.all_reduce(WORLD, MAX)`: our WORLD may include `os._exit(0)`'d retirees whose Mooncake slot has not yet reconnected, and NCCL/Gloo would deadlock waiting for peers that will never respond. ### 6. Test coverage (new) - **Manual end-to-end** (`test/manual/ep/test_mooncake_scale_down.py`, 3.7k lines): MC01–MC14 cover single-node + multi-node scale-down and grow-back on both NIXL and Mooncake a2a backends. MC06 uses deterministic inference (`--enable-deterministic-inference` + fixed seed + serial GSM8K + KV-cache flush between rounds) and asserts byte-identical scores across three post-shrink rounds. MC11 is intentionally skipped (Mooncake C++ `join_group(WORLD)` deadlock on join-then-shrink is a separate upstream issue). MC13 (shrink-below-primary after append) is env-gated behind `SGLANG_MC13_FORCE_RUN` as a compatibility valve for older container images; on the default nightly (Mooncake 0.3.12+) MC13 passes. - **Unit tests** (`test/srt/unit/elastic_ep/`, new): FSM transitions, boot-guard rejections (max-ep-size / initial-size / recover-only-with-mooncake), wiring between `ElasticEPStateManager` ↔ scheduler ↔ tokenizer manager. ### 7. Runtime environment - Default container in sweep scripts: nightly ≥ 2026-07-29 (bakes Mooncake 0.3.12.post1, which resizes P2PProxy peer arrays dynamically). Older containers still work for MC01–MC12/MC14 but need `SGLANG_MC13_FORCE_RUN=0` (the default) to skip MC13. ## Design constraints worth calling out for reviewers **Mooncake P2PProxy peer arrays.** In Mooncake versions before 0.3.12 the peer arrays were fixed-width at construction time. Our pre-shrink pattern (allocate at `--max-ep-size`, immediately retire down to the operator's desired starting size, grow back into retired slots) neatly sidestepped that constraint. Mooncake 0.3.12+ resizes these arrays dynamically (kvcache-ai/Mooncake#2623), so the constraint no longer applies at runtime — but we keep the pre-shrink design because it also gives us a stable `active_ranks` mask size, keeps every scale-up on the same code path (upstream's recovery path), and lets us keep retired slots addressable in the Mooncake peer table for future refill. **Asymmetric `Work.wait()` on Mooncake WORLD backend.** Some ranks return instantly from `handle.wait()`, others hang for 30s+. On NIXL this doesn't matter (all ranks tick at the same rate), but on Mooncake a2a it corrupts subsequent C++ collectives (`EPBuffer.update_ep_member` hangs). We ship a NIXL-first design; Mooncake a2a scale-down carries this documented limitation and is out of scope for this PR. **Fault recovery + scale coexistence.** Upstream's original `maybe_join_ep_ranks` calls `fail_recovery` when a runtime recovery attempt is detected on a scaled cohort, permanently blocking every subsequent scales. Our design supports iterative shrink/grow cycles, so we return silently on that path and preserve the ability to request future scales. ## Test plan - [x] Unit tests (`test/srt/unit/elastic_ep/`): FSM transitions, boot-guard rejections, and admission-gate wiring. - [x] Full MC01–MC14 × 5 baseline sweep on NIXL a2a: **PASS**. - [x] MC01 smoke on the layered-port rebase: **PASS** (GSM8K parity 62.50% → 61.72%, within 10% tol). - [x] MC06 deterministic smoke: byte-identical scores across all three post-shrink rounds. - [x] All 11 commits pass `python3 -m py_compile` at every snapshot. ## Commit-by-commit walkthrough (11 commits) Rebased on top of `sgl-project/sglang:main` as of 2026-07-31. Each commit passes tests standalone. | # | Commit | Summary | |---|---|---| | 1 | `e38192f08e` | **Layer scale-down on top of upstream elastic-EP.** New `scale_down_state.py`, `try_retire_ranks`, retire barrier, FSM entry points on `ModelRunner`, scheduler + tokenizer-manager admission gates, `pending_recover_ranks` plumbing, `is_ep_offset_joiner` predicate. | | 2 | `b2197ff6d1` | Unit + manual test coverage (MC01–MC12, unit tests). | | 3 | `f9e7d340b6` | Stabilize scale-down on NIXL a2a: retire barrier busy-poll, TCPStore epoch derivation, arrival-counter rollback handling. | | 4 | `9d55cf89e8` | Fix recover-mode joiner MoE storage sizing (joiner slot count from `ep_join_rank_offset + tp_size`, not `elastic_ep_initial_size`, to support partial regrow). | | 5 | `4085745e18` | Wire scale-down FSM + partial-recovery grow-back through `maybe_join_ep_ranks`. | | 6 | `3f74440ec6` | MC14 (`4→3→5` shrink-recover-then-append) + skipped MC13 regression trigger. | | 7 | `6f7c2cd19d` | Env-gate MC13 on Mooncake ≥ 0.3.12 P2PProxy fix. | | 8 | `19b9fa11e2` | Harden scale-down FSM: same-tick DRAIN fold, backend-conditional `Work.wait()` skip, TCPStore for Mooncake WORLD, `_finalize_scale_up::dp_size`, local timeout in `maybe_join_ep_ranks`. | | 9 | `078bf87c26` | Pre-PR cleanup: barrier arrival-counter leak, dedup, doc drift. | | 10 | `0c12260b21` | Dedup `ModelRunner` methods after layered port; **reorder methods to match upstream order** (reviewer-friendly diff shape, drops 603 lines of `git diff` phantom-move noise). | | 11 | `8ec48f0cae` | Make MC06 deterministic: exact-equality across post-shrink rounds via `--enable-deterministic-inference` + `--random-seed 42` + serial GSM8K + KV-cache flush between rounds. | ## Diff shape 29 files changed; net `+9,731 / -236`. Two files carry most of the surface: - `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py`: `+1507 / -123` after the reorder in commit 10. All upstream methods stay at their upstream line numbers; new scale-down/retire methods append at the class tail as a clean additive block. - `python/sglang/srt/elastic_ep/elastic_ep.py`: `+1559 / -33`. Mostly honest additions (NIXL retire barrier, retire primitives, FSM state). Other notable: - `python/sglang/srt/elastic_ep/scale_down_state.py`: new file, 677 lines (FSM driver). - `test/manual/ep/test_mooncake_scale_down.py`: new file, 3,716 lines (MC01–MC14). - `test/srt/unit/elastic_ep/*.py`: 3 new unit test files. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [x] Provide test results (5-round baseline sweep + smoke tests, itemized above). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31890380942](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890380942)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31890380863](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890380863)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Observability] Trace DP controller delivery stalls
signal.text: ## Summary - make the existing `--enable-request-time-stats-logging` flag propagate API, DP-controller, scheduler-receive, queue, and prefill timestamps to response metadata - keep timestamp IPC propagation disabled by default - log synchronous DP-controller worker sends exceeding 100 ms with target rank, request ID, and duration - add one-hop/two-hop clock-rebasing and controller logging tests ## Motivation A hot DP8 c64 sequence reproduced round medians of 1.112 s, 7.972 s, and 1.116 s. The slow round spent about 6.230 s after API dispatch completed but before scheduler receive; scheduler processing itself was about 0.006 ms. The first two requests arrived immediately and the remaining 62 reached all eight ranks together, pointing at the single-threaded DP-controller delivery boundary. This PR adds opt-in evidence for the next occurrence; it does not claim to fix the intermittent stall. ## Validation - 18 DP-controller dispatch tests: pass - 4 request-time serialization/rebasing tests: pass - exact repository Ruff rules (`F401,F821,UP037`): pass - isort 7.0.0: pass - live DP8 responses contain the expected scheduler timestamp fields when enabled - default DPC serialization omits the additional fields <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31890249739](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890249739)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31890249753](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890249753)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Fix ROCm FP8 DP gather quantization
signal.text: ## Summary - route ordinary ROCm row-major FP8 group quantization through the existing in-file Triton kernel - write directly into caller-owned quantized/scales outputs with the requested gfx950 E4M3 range - add an AMD JIT-kernel CI regression for group-128 `[4, 7168]` quantization ## Root cause The ROCm DP FP8-gather path reached a CUDA-only JIT wrapper that is not imported on HIP. Importing it is not sufficient: it compiles `cuda_fp8.h`, while the pinned `sgl_kernel` wheel also lacks the AOT v2 op. The local Triton kernel is the supported dependency-free fallback for the plain row-major case. Unsupported UE8M0/fused/masked/column-major combinations fail explicitly. ## Validation - focused gfx950 numerical regression: pass - AMD CI registration: `jit-kernel-unit-test-amd` - full DeepSeek-V4-Pro DP8/EP8/TP8 service reaches healthy state with `SGLANG_ENABLE_DP_GATHER_FP8=1` - three stable c64 1K-to-1 rounds have balanced DP routing and zero retractions ## Performance note This fixes the crash, but does not enable FP8 gather by default. In the tested DSV4 workload, FP8 wire gather regressed median/P99 TTFT by 8.33%/14.05% versus the same Gatherv bundle, so the environment gate should remain disabled pending a better communication decomposition. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31890246697](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890246697)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31890246560](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890246560)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text:
# Support LingBot-Video MoE: image-to-video, text-to-image, refiner, and prompt rewriting ## Motivation The initial LingBot-Video MoE 30B-A3B port covered text-to-video. The released checkpoint also ships refiner weights and supports image-to-video and text-to-image, so a deployment today exercises only part of what the model can do. This PR closes that gap. Related issue: #32336 Upstream PR: #32341 ## Design One pipeline serves every task. `task_type` becomes `TI2V`, which makes the input image optional, so the request decides: `image_path` gives image-to-video, omitting it gives text-to-video, `num_frames=1` gives a still. The checkpoint leaves little choice here — `model_index.json` declares a single pipeline class and the registry resolves a single config, so a second class would be unreachable without an extra CLI flag on every image-to-video request. Conditioning uses the frame twice: as visual context for the Qwen3-VL encoder, and as a clean latent pinned to the head of the diffusion latent and rewritten after every scheduler step. The DiT forward signature is untouched. The refiner is the one part behind an explicit `--pipeline-class-name LingBotVideoRefinerPipeline`, since doubling resident DiT weights is a deployment decision rather than a per-request one. It loads from the checkpoint's `refiner/` subfolder by redirecting only the weight path, so the component keeps its `transformer_2` identity and still resolves the transformer loader. Its second pass rebuilds text conditioning without vision tokens because the refiner DiT has no image-conditioning path, drives both posterior samples and the noise draw from one seeded generator, and rejects single-frame requests. Prompt rewriting runs as a stage against an externally served vision language model over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, rather than pulling another 27B model into the diffusion worker. Set `rewriter_url` and free-text prompts get expanded and mapped to JSON in two turns; structured captions pass through untouched, and leaving the URL unset skips the stage. ## Verification Checked against the reference diffusers implementation on the same hardware, checkpoint, seed, and parameters. Cross-GPU comparison is not meaningful for this model — identical code and seed on an H100 and a 5090 produce visibly different motion — so every comparison below is same-hardware. ### Prompts and inputs The DiT consumes a structured JSON caption rather than a plain sentence, so the prompt below is the caption itself. Every run in this section uses seed 42 and the same caption for its task, so a reviewer can reproduce any clip from the served model. ```bash sglang serve --model-path robbyant/lingbot-video-moe-30b-a3b --num-gpus 1 ```

Reference numbers come from its own denoising-loop timer and exclude text encoding and VAE decode. Base pass, 320x192, 121 frames: | Runtime | Hardware | s/step | Denoise | Decode | Text encode | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | sglang T2V | H100 80GB | 0.700 | 28.0 s | 0.96 s | 0.13 s | | sglang TI2V | H100 80GB | 0.705 | 28.2 s | 0.96 s | 0.19 s | | reference T2V | H100 80GB | 0.95 | 38 s | -- | -- | | reference TI2V | H100 80GB | 0.95 | 38 s | -- | -- | | sglang T2V | 5090 32GB, dit layerwise offload | 2.122 | 84.9 s | 0.96 s | 0.12 s | | sglang TI2V | 5090 32GB, dit layerwise offload | 2.122 | 84.9 s | 0.97 s | 0.19 s | Text to image, 832x480, single frame: | Runtime | Hardware | s/step | Denoise | Decode | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | sglang | H100 80GB | 0.198 | 7.9 s | 0.06 s | | reference | H100 80GB | 0.30 | 12 s | -- | | sglang | 5090 32GB, dit layerwise offload | 2.122 | 84.9 s | 0.22 s | Across 16 requests all three tasks land on the same 2.122 s/step on the 5090, because layerwise offload streams the whole DiT from host memory every step and the loop is bound by that transfer rather than by sequence length: a single 832x480 frame carries 1560 tokens against 7440 for the 121-frame clip and still costs the same. On H100 without offload the three tasks separate as expected, 0.700 / 0.705 / 0.198. Refiner, 49 frames, 8 refiner steps, t_thresh 0.85, sigma tail 2: | Runtime | Hardware | Refiner res | Base denoise | Upscale | Refine s/step | Refine total | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | sglang | H100 80GB, offload | 1920x1088 | 87.2 s | 5.8 s | 20.18 | 163.2 s | | sglang | 5090 32GB, offload | 640x384 | 86.5 s | 1.2 s | 2.17 | 17.6 s | | reference | H100 80GB, 8-way FSDP | 1920x1088 | 121 s | -- | -- | 210 s | Both sglang refiner rows keep layerwise offload on so the two DiTs share one card, which is why their base denoise sits near the 5090 figure rather than the 28 s an H100 reaches without offload. Refiner cost then tracks the refiner resolution rather than the hardware: 1920x1088 is 8.5x the pixels of 640x384 and costs 9.3x per step. signal.title: [XPU][Diffusion] Enable MiniMax H3 on XPU platforms
signal.text: This PR adds key changes to cover the enabling for Minimax H3 model specific on XPU platforms, including - Mapping to XPU attention backend with optimized kernel from sgl-kernel-xpu - Necessary device dispatching/autocast codes - Runtime XPU memory D2H/H2D fix Tested serving pipelines include: - TP + layer_wise offload for both encoder/dit/vae ( similar as cookbook on cuda 5090: https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3#3-serve-minimax-h3, but preferring no offload (only encoder) when device memory is enough, i.e., x4 or x8) Next plans (as follow-up PRs, for further optimizations). - Apply more fusions (like QKnorm_RoPE and silu_and_mul, to be on par with cuda fusion pathes) - More serving pipelines/parallelism to be explored and evaluated. - XPU FA backend with non-contiguous support Tested example: - T2VA example from cookbook: https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3#4-generate-video-and-audio Result: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09e086a7-95ae-489b-bb9b-5e48553eca91 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31766407552](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31766407552)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31766407402](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31766407402)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
