signal.title: [kernel] Add opt-in deterministic CuTe-DSL DSA top-k backend (--dsa-topk-backend cutedsl)
signal.text: # [kernel] Opt-in deterministic CuTe-DSL DSA top-k backend (`--dsa-topk-backend cutedsl`) Adds an opt-in, bitwise-deterministic top-k backend for the DSA/lightning-indexer selection stage, implemented in CuTe DSL (SM90/SM100). This description is self-contained: it folds in the earlier thread discussion (tie semantics, 0.0-plateau structure, topk_v2 safety data) and the scan-emit output-stage optimization added after the initial review round. ## Problem The DSA indexer scores are `sum_h w_h * relu(q_h . k_h)` (see `fp8_index`), so every key whose head-dots are all non-positive lands on **exactly 0.0**: real indexer rows carry a large exact-0.0 tie plateau — structural to the ReLU-sum architecture, not a fixture artifact (distribution study: [evidence comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31115#issuecomment-4966578547)). Whenever a row's k-th boundary falls inside that plateau (`nnz(row) < k`, common for mid-length rows), the boundary tie set is huge, and the default `sgl_kernel.fast_topk_v2`: 1. **Selects a different index set run to run.** Winners are emitted in smem-atomic arrival order and boundary ties resolve by arrival order: on tie-heavy inputs we measured 21–25/25 replays returning *distinct index sets* (noisy sibling stream; harness in the evidence comment). Same request, same weights — different attended tokens. 2. **Can drop strictly-positive candidates.** On the ReLU-shaped fixture (L=16384, ~1640 nonzero < k=2048) a strictly-positive candidate was replaced by a 0.0 one in 1/256 rows — the #17747 overflow-drop mode, which also bites systematically in narrow-value-range regimes (#17747, #15041 family). 3. **Short rows take a separate, score-blind fill path.** When a row has fewer candidates than `topk` the kernel emits an identity-style fill without reading scores — set-correct, but yet another slot-order regime; combined with (1), the output is not byte-reproducible in any regime. Practical impact: identical requests are not replayable (debugging), RL rollouts against a served model are not bitwise-reproducible, and the drift enters at *token selection*, where seeding cannot recover it. (2) is a correctness defect independent of determinism. All data is synthetic and reproducible; no proprietary captures involved. ## Solution `--dsa-topk-backend cutedsl` — a single-kernel CuTe DSL selector (one CTA per row), opt-in with zero default behavior change: - **Bitwise determinism, always.** Output is a pure function of the input: histogram atomics are commutative adds; staging atomics only permute buffers that feed order-independent histograms or a canonical index sort. 30/30 replays bitwise-identical under a noisy sibling stream on every input class tested (tie plateaus, quantized, narrow-range, -inf windows, degenerate rows). - **Exact top-k with a defined tie policy**: smallest-index selection at the k-th boundary (radix select over `~idx`); no candidate is ever dropped — threshold-bin overflow falls back to full-row rescans (identical result, slower) instead of silently skipping (#17747). - **Canonical output order: ascending index**, front-packed, -1 padded. The kernel has two shape-selected output stages — an ordered ballot+block-scan **scan-emit** pass and an **index-sort** collect — that emit the *identical* canonical output bit-for-bit (asserted directly in tests); an internal heuristic picks the faster one per shape. Ascending order is gather-friendly for the downstream page-table fetch. No sglang consumer depends on any slot order (the default backend's order is arrival-nondeterministic; we audited every consumer of the top-k tensor — all are element-wise `-1`-masked gathers, mask-based compactions, or permutation-invariant attention). - **Performance**: the scan-emit stage (new in this revision) removes the bitonic sort from the hot path where it dominated. vs the first revision of this backend: up to **3.8x faster** on prefill-scale grids and 1.2–2x on mid-band decode shapes, and no measured band regresses beyond noise (the sort stage is retained exactly where it wins). vs the default radix kernel the picture is now honest and mixed rather than uniformly behind: **faster on realistic (0.0-plateau) prefill-scale rows at L<=4k (1.33x)**, near-parity at small-L decode and dense prefill (0.81–0.94x), while **radix stays 2–4x faster at mid/long L** — see the table. ### Performance (B200, fp32 scores, CUDA-graph replay timing, per-call µs) `relu` = realistic indexer-shaped scores (exact-0.0 plateau, the distribution the DSA indexer actually produces); `randn` = dense distinct scores. "prev rev" = this backend before the scan-emit stage; "radix" = `sgl_kernel.fast_topk_v2` (default, nondeterministic); "fi/fi-det" = `flashinfer.top_k` with `deterministic=False/True`. k=2048 (production DSA config). | scores | rows | L | cutedsl | prev rev | radix | fi | fi-det | radix/cutedsl | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | relu | 64 | 4096 | 12.9 | 22.7 | 11.1 | 8.8 | 23.8 | 0.86x | | relu | 64 | 16384 | 36.3 | 43.2 | 15.8 | 18.1 | 40.1 | 0.44x | | relu | 64 | 131072 | 137.0 | 137.1 | 54.2 | 25.9 | 57.0 | 0.40x | | relu | 256 | 16384 | 76.5 | 93.9 | 25.4 | 39.9 | 73.7 | 0.33x | | relu | 512 | 65536 | 199.0 | 199.8 | 87.3 | 98.5 | 143.3 | 0.44x | | relu | 2048 | 4096 | 74.7 | 202.5 | 99.5 | 85.6 | 257.1 | **1.33x** | | relu | 2048 | 16384 | 358.2 | 482.1 | 166.2 | 272.3 | 500.0 | 0.46x | | relu | 8192 | 4096 | 305.0 | 805.4 | 406.8 | 339.2 | 1015.6 | **1.33x** | | relu | 8192 | 8192 | 673.7 | 1223.3 | 483.8 | 538.7 | 1348.3 | 0.72x | | relu | 8192 | 16384 | 1319.5 | 1829.7 | 646.2 | 1057.5 | 1979.7 | 0.49x | | randn | 64 | 4096 | 8.4 | 17.2 | 6.8 | 6.8 | 18.7 | 0.81x | | randn | 64 | 16384 | 27.1 | 32.4 | 13.7 | 14.6 | 25.5 | 0.51x | | randn | 256 | 16384 | 57.2 | 82.6 | 20.5 | 20.5 | 45.5 | 0.36x | | randn | 2048 | 4096 | 43.3 | 162.8 | 40.7 | 55.9 | 158.3 | 0.94x | | randn | 8192 | 4096 | 190.8 | 656.2 | 163.1 | 221.1 | 617.2 | 0.85x | | randn | 8192 | 8192 | 386.4 | 811.5 | 303.9 | 329.9 | 855.0 | 0.79x | | randn | 2048 | 65536 | 1374.1 | 1378.9 | 330.6 | 469.9 | 540.5 | 0.24x | Honest summary of the bands: - Tie-plateau (realistic) prefill-scale rows at L<=4096: **cutedsl beats the default radix kernel** (1.33x) — big tie sets are exactly where arrival-order kernels also thrash. - Small-L decode and dense prefill at L<=8192: near-parity (0.72–0.94x). - Mid/long L (>=16k) at small/mid batch: **radix remains 2–4x faster**; flashinfer's multi-CTA-per-row split dominates everyone at L>=64k low batch. If you need bitwise determinism there, this backend still costs only low-hundreds of µs absolute. - vs `flashinfer.top_k(deterministic=True)`: cutedsl is faster on most shapes tested (up to 3.4x at prefill scale), slower at long-L low-batch. (Note also the flashinfer deterministic mode documents reproducibility, not a smallest-index tie policy, and its unfused sglang integration adds a masking pass.) Numbers are average per-call µs over 30 CUDA-graph replays of a 10-call graph (eager warmup excluded); full-length rows; harness reproducible from the test fixtures. ### Scope / envelope - Opt-in only; zero default behavior change (`sgl-kernel` remains the default). - SM90+ with `nvidia-cutlass-dsl`; fp32 scores; `topk <= 4096`, `L < 2^24`, `B*L`, `B*topk < 2^31` — enforced with actionable errors; `supports()` gates call sites. - Like the `torch` backend, currently requires `SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK=false` (the fused paged/ragged transform paths keep their existing backends). - CUDA-graph safe: compile and first-touch allocations refuse graph capture with a clear eager-warmup message; compile cache is device-keyed, compilation serialized. - NaN ordering documented (deterministic bitwise total order; DSA indexer logits are NaN-free). `SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_CUTEDSL_SURVCAP` / `SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_CUTEDSL_STAGE` are validated perf-only overrides — results are bit-identical for any legal value. ## Review guide - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/cutedsl_topk.py` — the kernel (single file; module docstring is the full algorithm spec) - `dsa_topk_backend.py` + `server_args.py` — dispatch/choice registration only (+13 lines) - `test/registered/jit/test_cutedsl_topk.py` — 16 registered tests: tie-robust exact-contract checks (selected score multiset bitwise vs reference, smallest-index k-th-boundary tie subset asserted directly, canonical ascending order, -1 tail packing), determinism replays covering both output stages, bit-identity between the two output stages, the SURV_CAP overflow fallback (forced, checked bit-identical), envelope/env-override error contracts, CUDA-graph capture/replay, empty/edge shapes - Evidence for the Problem section: [score-distribution + topk_v2 tie-safety study](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31115#issuecomment-4966578547) (synthetic, reproducible, includes a harness you can run on live captures) History note: the branch is squashed into 3 logical commits (kernel / dispatch / tests); the pre-review hardening from the earlier 48bce24 push (input-contract enforcement, CUDA-graph guards, seed-stable tests) is retained in full. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #29393610563](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29393610563)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #29393610429](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29393610429)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [BugFix][DSA] Harden top-k v1/v2 kernels against negative padded seq_lens
signal.text: ## Motivation Related to #25574 (`topk_transform_512_v2` illegal memory access on SM100 under DP-attention). We set out to reproduce and fix that issue on B200 (SM100) and found the following: 1. **The code quoted in #25574 no longer exists.** #26788 rewrote `topk_v2.cuh`; the old `topk_fused_transform` SMALL/TRIVIAL early-return branches are gone, and the rewritten fused small-batch kernel already has cluster-uniform fall-through control flow. Note the branch condition is per-`blockIdx.x` and all 8 blocks of a cluster share `blockIdx.x`, so even in the old kernel every block of a cluster took the same branch — there was never a *divergent* cluster barrier (`compute-sanitizer --tool synccheck` on the pre-#26788 kernel reports 0 errors, and 24k+ stress iterations over mixed TRIVIAL/SMALL/LARGE batches, eager + CUDA-graph replay, never faulted on B200). The B300-specific crash could not be reproduced at kernel level on B200, and its proposed patch (#25575) targets the deleted code. 2. **What does reproduce — deterministically, at current `main` — is the negative-`seq_lens` crash class.** Negative per-row lengths (DP-padded / idle-companion rows; #30378 observed `-4` from GLM 5.2 MTP draft-extend metadata, and DP-attention idle rows are the same class) are read through unsigned conversions in **both** top-k kernels and become ~4e9-token rows: - v1 (`topk_v1.cuh`): illegal memory access for **any** negative length (notably, the `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=0` fallback is equally exposed); - v2 (`topk_v2.cuh`): illegal memory access (e.g. `-1048576`, on every dispatch shape: fused small-batch cluster, persistent pool, streaming) or — worse — a **silently garbage top-k row** (`-1`/`-4`, where the unsigned chunk arithmetic happens to wrap to a zero-length chunk and `handle_tie` pads the row with bogus indices). #30378 clamped two DSA triton *producers* caller-side, but the kernels stay exposed to every other caller — e.g. the DSv4 DP-attention path (`dsv4/metadata.py` feeds `c4_seq_lens` to `plan_topk_v2` unclamped). ## Modifications Per review feedback, negative lengths are handled with **signed comparisons** (no arithmetic clamp) so a negative row takes the documented trivial all-`(-1)` "no tokens" path -- every non-negative candidate index compares `>= -1`, so none qualifies: - `topk_v1.cuh`: `seq_len` stays `int32_t`; the signed trivial dispatch (`seq_len <= (int32_t)kTopK`) routes negative rows into `naive_transform`, whose fill comparison is signed; the radix path casts to `uint32_t` only after the `> kTopK` guard proves the value positive; - `topk_v2.cuh`: a signed `is_trivial()` (`(int32_t)seq_len <= (int32_t)topk`) used by the main and fused small-batch kernels; `trivial_transform`'s per-element comparison is signed; - `topk_v2.cuh` `topk_plan` (parameter type fixed to `const int32_t*` to match the tensor dtype): the threshold-count loop compares signed against the candidate thresholds (all int32-exact); the pool-compaction predicate proves a row positive (signed) before the unsigned threshold compare, so negative rows are never routed to the persistent pool as ~4e9-token items while a full-uint32 `static_cluster_threshold` keeps its meaning. Python docstrings updated (producers should still clamp to 0 themselves; the kernel no longer turns a producer bug into an illegal address or silent corruption). Cost is unchanged -- paired timing below. New tests: `test_topk_v2_negative_lengths` (8 configs x k in {512, 2048}, one config per dispatch shape: level 0/1/2, fused small-batch cluster with `-1`/`-4`/`-1048576`, persistent pool), `test_topk_v2_plan_negative_lengths` (pins the plan kernel's counting loop via a candidate-cap-boundary distribution and the plan metadata, plus a full-uint32 static-threshold boundary check), and `test_topk_v1_negative_lengths`. Output buffers are poison-prefilled; each test asserts negative rows come back all-`(-1)` (both `out` and `raw`) and non-negative rows in the same batch still match `torch.topk`. ## Accuracy Tests On B200 (CUDA 13.3), before this patch (current `main`): - `[40000]*16 + [-1048576, 400]` (streaming), `[131072, 9000, 9000, -1048576]` (fused cluster), `[131072]*20 + [400]*10 + [-1048576]` (persistent pool): `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` — deterministic; - `[131072, 9000, 9000, -4]` / `[..., -1]`: padded row returns 512 garbage indices (silent corruption); - v1 with `[9000, 9000, 9000, -4]`: illegal memory access; - on the pre-#26788 kernel (the code #25574 was filed against), `[131072, 9000, 9000, -4]` reproduces the exact reported failure signature (illegal address surfacing at the fused-kernel launch). After this patch: - all of the above complete, negative rows = all `(-1)`; - full registered suite `test/registered/jit/deepseek_v4/test_topk_v2.py`: **262 passed** (244 pre-existing + 18 new); - stress: 14 scenarios (branch mixes, batch-15 boundary, zero rows, negative rows) x eager + CUDA-graph replay: pass; - `compute-sanitizer` memcheck + synccheck on negative-row and mixed-branch cluster scenarios: 0 errors. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Paired A/B timing (median of 5x50 launches, 4 interleaved rounds, B200), `main` vs this PR, us/launch: | shape (batch x seq) | dispatch | main | this PR | |---|---|---:|---:| | 128 x 8192 | level 0 (Register2) | 5.41-5.72 | 5.24-5.45 | | 64 x 16384 | level 1 (Register4) | 6.19-6.37 | 6.20-6.24 | | 100 x 65536 | level 2 (Streaming) | 13.85-14.16 | 13.84-13.86 | | 8 x 131072 | fused small-batch cluster | 10.82-10.96 | 10.80-10.83 | | 64 x 131072 | persistent pool + main | 23.95-24.06 | 24.07-24.10 | | 4 x 9000 | decode-like level 1 | 5.07-5.09 | 5.04-5.09 | All deltas within run-to-run noise on a shared machine. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #29328239541](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29328239541)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #29328239210](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29328239210)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [VLM] Reuse cached Kimi-K3 embeddings before preprocessing
signal.text: ## Summary Stacked on #34404; review `fd40b11ac0cb0..63cf4f894c57c` for the PR-3-only diff. - acquires per-image embedding-cache leases on the request's final DP route before processor dispatch, and omits features only when every required TP rank has pinned the same entries - transfers lease ownership to the admitted request; consume, cancel, abort, flush, timeout, and internal retry paths release pins safely - moves EPD metadata and local/global embedding lookup before decode/processor/ViT through a model-declared, per-modality capability; K3 is the first adapter, with multi-image partial hits and deduplication - preserves CPU, CUDA IPC, and CUDA VMM compatibility; featureless references do not allocate IPC/VMM proxies or a new fixed HBM pool - adds low-cardinality identity, preprocess phase, embedding acquire, skipped-stage, occupancy, eviction, and single-flight metrics - adds typed Protocol/resolver interfaces instead of model-name branches or `getattr` probing, plus the canonical `VLM preprocessing and caching` guide and concise API, EPD, model-support, new-model, server-argument, and K3 Cookbook references ## Correctness and failure behavior - false hits are prevented in three stages: a type-preserving artifact identity covers exact media plus processor configuration; a full feature identity binds it to the processor-output hash; embedding lookup uses a compact 64-bit key but requires exact feature-identity equality - identity matching is symmetric: an identity-less request cannot match a strong entry, and inserting either identity kind replaces an unpinned entry of the other kind instead of inheriting it - K3 namespaces Radix prefix KV by the ordered full feature identities, so two media items whose legacy pad sentinels collide after the 30-bit reduction still cannot share language-model KV; a partial identity list is rejected rather than creating an incomplete namespace - same path/URL with changed bytes, processor/backend/config/per-image option changes, and tensor/PIL metadata changes cannot reuse an artifact; unsupported identity values are rejected - leases atomically pin cache entries against eviction and become request-owned after scheduler admission - partial TP hits and expired leases retry internally through the feature-carrying path - feature-hash mismatch clears the stale processor artifact and rejects reuse - K3 EPD carries feature identities alongside image sizes and grids to the language server, so reconstructed items use the same embedding and Radix identity checks as normal serving - K3 Mooncake/global embedding-cache entries are keyed by the full feature identity; a caller-provided global-cache key is combined with, rather than substituted for, that identity - caller-provided legacy `mm_hashes` changes only the router/pad sentinel; K3 stores its processor-derived embedding key separately, so a caller hash cannot redirect lease admission, embedding lookup, or cache write-back - untrusted identity still reads and verifies actual media bytes; only `--trust-mm-content-hashes` lets a metadata hit skip the source read - cache flush, model update, shutdown, cancellation, and timeout clear their preprocess state and outstanding leases `--trust-mm-content-hashes` is the explicit correctness boundary: a trusted hot hit does not read the source, so a stale or incorrect caller hash can return a stale artifact. Without that flag, SGLang verifies caller hashes against the actual media snapshot and rejects mismatches. In other words, false hits are fail-closed under the default configuration. A 64-bit embedding-key collision only selects a candidate and still requires the full SHA-256 feature identity to match; a 30-bit pad collision is isolated by the full-identity Radix namespace; mutable paths and URLs are re-read and re-hashed. The only intentional exception is trusted-hash mode, where correctness is explicitly delegated to the caller. ## Normal-serving performance Full real-weight Kimi-K3 (`1.56 TB`), 2 nodes x 4 NVIDIA GB300, TP8, commit `25eae3c909d7`. Each cell is the median of 3 runs over 32 conversations x 8 turns. The same image set is resent on every turn; random images are seeded from 512x512 through 2048x2048. Both sides use the same 4096 MiB lazy embedding-cache cap and auto CUDA VMM/FABRIC feature transport. The only A/B switch is K3 auto versus `--mm-preprocess-cache-size-mb 0`. Four random images, concurrency 32, 16 output tokens: | Request rate | Output tok/s off -> on | Median TTFT off -> on | Median E2E off -> on | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 53.29 -> 100.14 (+87.9%) | 5846 -> 1122 ms (-80.8%) | 6364 -> 1479 ms (-76.8%) | | 4 | 53.83 -> 109.46 (+103.3%) | 6128 -> 1148 ms (-81.3%) | 6721 -> 1482 ms (-78.0%) | | 8 | 55.53 -> 107.57 (+93.7%) | 5830 -> 1174 ms (-79.9%) | 6294 -> 1502 ms (-76.1%) | | inf | 54.33 -> 106.05 (+95.2%) | 5973 -> 1133 ms (-81.0%) | 6366 -> 1479 ms (-76.8%) | The `inf` A/B was repeated on the same physical nodes. Cache-on duration fell from 75.39 s to 38.62 s. Median hot-turn TTFT fell from 5956 to 1147 ms (-80.8%). The first cold turn did not regress (19307 -> 15830 ms at saturated concurrency). Representative matrix: | Case | Output tok/s off -> on | Median TTFT off -> on | Median TPOT off -> on | |---|---:|---:|---:| | 4 random images, c1, o16 | 21.20 -> 29.90 (+41.0%) | 501 -> 297 ms | 12.12 -> 10.89 ms | | 4 random images, c8, o16 | 44.58 -> 80.69 (+81.0%) | 1874 -> 639 ms | 15.07 -> 13.67 ms | | 1 fixed image, c32, o16 | 197.22 -> 283.14 (+43.6%) | 1702 -> 976 ms | 21.10 -> 19.60 ms | | 4 fixed images, rate 8, c8, o16 | 59.47 -> 98.01 (+64.8%) | 1471 -> 623 ms | 14.75 -> 13.47 ms | | 4 random images, rate 8, c32, o128 | 305.14 -> 488.26 (+60.0%) | 6287 -> 1404 ms | 33.86 -> 30.49 ms | The measured 128 cold images produced 896 metadata and embedding hits. All 896 hot images skipped processor work, feature transport, and ViT. Aggregate preprocess-stage time fell from 194.28 s to 24.56 s (-87.4%). The CPU cache held 128 entries / 62,692 bytes with no eviction. Peak HBM was 257,304 MiB cache-on versus 265,202 MiB cache-off (~7.7 GiB lower); there is no new fixed HBM reservation. The environment's auto FlashInfer MXFP4 TRT-LLM Gen SiTU MoE path hung after one run, so both sides pin Marlin. These numbers establish the cache A/B, not the best possible production absolute throughput. `--enable-symm-mem` was accepted but K3 disabled it for decode-graph correctness. No EPD runtime benchmark is claimed in this PR; EPD is covered by the code and unit tests only in this round. ## Validation - changed-file pre-commit, Python compile, registered-test validation, Cookbook validation, and Mintlify link/build checks: pass - final stacked Linux suite on both GB300 nodes: 170 passed + 5 subtests per node; the latest focused false-hit/K3 suite is 143 passed + 5 subtests and covers forced 64-bit embedding-key collision, forced 30-bit pad collision, identity downgrade, caller router-hash override, partial-identity rejection, mutable path, processor-output change, EPD identity propagation, and strong global-cache keys - strict full-real-weight normal-serving matrix compares prompt/output token IDs, messages, finish reasons, and usage across cold/hot paths; it covers one/two/duplicate/reordered images, partial hits, cross input forms, mutable paths, caller-hash rejection, concurrent single-flight, and `n=2` - the latest full-real-weight 2-node GB300 rerun passes all 11 normal-serving identity cases; a Native `/generate` adversarial check also proves that changing `mm_hashes` for the same image still skips processor/transport/ViT, while two different images forced to share the same `mm_hashes` value perform a cold miss before only the true repeat becomes hot - 0 request errors across the full normal-serving matrix; input/output usage lengths stay aligned ## Stack 1. #34398 — content identity, API, bounded LRU, and single-flight infrastructure 2. #34404 — typed K3 per-image artifacts and ordinary/EPD identity plumbing 3. this PR — scheduler lease, early EPD reuse, metrics, documentation, and benchmark <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->_Not run yet_<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:warning: **Not run on latest push** -- push again to dispatch.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] DSA sparse-MLA prefill silently computes no attention at all for a single extend > 65535 tokens (trtllm-gen gridDim.z limit is still unguarded on the non-DP path)
signal.text: ## TL;DR `gridDim.z` overflow in trtllm-gen sparse MLA (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3125) is still reachable from sglang, and still silent. On SM100, any **single unchunked extend of more than 65535 tokens** on the DSA `prefill=trtllm` path launches **zero** attention kernels, leaves the attention output tensor **uninitialized**, raises **no** Python exception, and returns garbage. `bench_one_batch` hits this by construction for `--input-len > 65535`. The onset is exact: **65535 tokens works, 65536 does not.** ### Relation to existing reports (please read before closing as duplicate) | prior art | state | why this report is not covered by it | |---|---|---| | flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3125 — "trtllm-gen attention error on large batch size" | closed 2026-04-21, **no fix commit** | Correctly diagnosed the root cause. Maintainer proposed "just raise an error"; that was never implemented. `fmhaKernels.cuh` still has a bare `int numCtasZ = params.mBatchSize;` and `cuErrCheck` still only `fprintf`s. | | sgl-project/sglang#29453 — GLM-5.2 NVFP4 DP4 long-context crash | closed 2026-06-27, **no code fix** | Same root cause, but reported via a *downstream* symptom (invalid sampling probabilities) under **DP attention**, and closed after the reporter worked around it with `--chunked-prefill-size`. No guard landed. | | sgl-project/sglang#29522 — "Guard Blackwell TRT-LLM prefill chunk size" | **closed, not merged** | The only guard attempt. It capped `chunked_prefill_size` / `get_max_chunk_capacity()` in `server_args.py` + `forward_batch_deepseek_mha_mixin.py` — i.e. **server config only**, gated on `enable_dp_attention`. It would not have covered the direct-ModelRunner path (`bench_one_batch`, `dp_size=1`) at all, and it never landed anyway. | | flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3238 — `cum_seq_lens_q` for trtllm-gen MLA | merged 2026-06-24 | This is the structural cure (stop flattening tokens into the batch dim), but sglang has **not adopted it**: `dsa_backend.py:3242` still does `q_all.view(batch_size, 1, num_heads, head_dim)`. | **New in this report:** (a) the fault is reachable with `dp_size=1` on the plain ModelRunner path, which no proposed guard covered; (b) an exact one-token onset bisection (65535 vs 65536); (c) direct proof of *silent corruption* — a sentinel-filled `out` tensor comes back untouched — rather than an inferred downstream symptom; (d) profiler proof that `0` of `num_layers` attention kernels run, so `bench_one_batch` silently reports **falsely fast** long-context prefill numbers. Also worth noting: sglang already guards this exact hardware limit elsewhere — `python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py:298` gates a fused kernel on `query.shape[0] < 65535`, and `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/mamba_slot_fused.py:133` comments "gridDim.y/z cap at 65535". The DSA attention path has no such check. ## Environment | | | |---|---| | GPU | NVIDIA B200 (SM100), driver 590.48.01 | | sglang | `18107e38d266a98f59a8e3c766f8ddaf9b723ded` (main, 2026-08-14) | | flashinfer-python | 0.6.17 | | sglang-kernel | 0.4.6.post1 | | torch | 2.13.0 / Python 3.12.3 | | resolved backends | `Set DSA backends for fp8_e4m3 KV Cache: prefill=trtllm, decode=trtllm.` | `prefill=trtllm` here is the **auto-selected default** for fp8 KV on SM100 — no `--dsa-prefill-backend` flag was passed. (`enable_auto_select_prefill_impl` at `dsa_backend.py:350` is only true when the resolved impl is literally `flashmla_auto`, so the `flashmla_sparse`/`flashmla_kv` rewrite in `set_dsa_prefill_impl` does not apply here.) Reproduced on two models and two TP degrees: a 78-layer DSA MLA model at TP8, and a 47-layer `DeepseekV32ForCausalLM` fp8 checkpoint (`index_topk=2048`) at TP2. TP degree is irrelevant — the overflowing dimension is the token/pseudo-batch dimension, which TP does not shard. Note `SGLANG_DSA_PREFILL_DENSE_ATTN_KV_LEN_THRESHOLD` defaults to **2048** (`python/sglang/srt/environ.py:1375`), so both 32768 and 131072 take the same MLA path — the difference in behaviour is purely the 65535 overflow, not an MHA/MLA path switch. ## Minimal reproducer (no model, no sglang, ~30 s) Same FlashInfer entry point sglang calls, with a sentinel-filled `out` so "did the kernel run?" is directly observable: ```python import sys, torch, flashinfer B = int(sys.argv[1]) # pseudo-batch == number of query tokens NH, TOPK, KVL, ROPE, HD = 16, 2048, 512, 64, 576 PAGE, PAGES, SENT = 64, 8192, -31337.0 kv = torch.zeros(PAGES, 1, PAGE, HD, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device="cuda") ws = torch.empty(256 << 20, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda") q = torch.zeros(B, 1, NH, HD, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device="cuda") bt = torch.zeros(B, 1, TOPK, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") sl = torch.full((B,), TOPK, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") out = torch.full((B, 1, NH, KVL), SENT, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") flashinfer.decode.trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla( query=q, kv_cache=kv, workspace_buffer=ws, qk_nope_head_dim=KVL, kv_lora_rank=KVL, qk_rope_head_dim=ROPE, block_tables=bt, seq_lens=sl, max_seq_len=TOPK, sparse_mla_top_k=TOPK, out=out, bmm1_scale=1.0, backend="trtllm-gen", ) torch.cuda.synchronize() print(f"B={B} out_untouched={(out == SENT).all().item()}") ``` | pseudo-batch `B` (= `gridDim.z`) | output written? | stderr `CUDA Error` lines | Python exception | |---|---|---|---| | 1024 / 32768 / 65534 | yes | 0 | none | | **65535** | **yes** | 0 | none | | **65536** | **NO — 100 % of `out` still holds the sentinel** | 1 | **none** | | 65537 / 98304 / 131072 | NO | 1 | none | The only symptom is one stderr line per failed launch: ``` CUDA Error: CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE .../flashinfer/data/include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaKernels.cuh 388 ``` ## End-to-end reproducer ```bash python -m sglang.bench_one_batch \ --model-path <DeepSeek-V3.2-style DSA checkpoint> \ --tp-size 2 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --disable-cuda-graph \ --batch-size 1 --input-len 32768 65535 65536 --output-len 8 ``` `bench_one_batch` drives the ModelRunner directly, so each `--input-len` is **one unchunked extend** and `dp_size == 1`. Result on a 47-layer `DeepseekV32ForCausalLM` fp8 checkpoint at TP2: | `--input-len` | prefill latency | prefill throughput | swallowed launch errors | |---|---|---|---| | 32768 | 0.710 s | 46 167 tok/s | 0 | | **65535** | **2.195 s** | 29 853 tok/s | **0** | | **65536** | **1.222 s** | **53 614 tok/s** | **94 = 47 layers x 2 ranks** | One extra token makes the prefill **1.80x faster** (2.195 s -> 1.222 s), because 44 % of the work (all of attention) silently disappears. The error count is exactly `num_layers x tp_size`: one failed launch per layer per rank, and precisely zero below the threshold. **On this model the run did not crash at all** — it completed all 8 decode steps and printed benchmark numbers. On the 78-layer TP8 model the same condition instead ended in `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` at `model_runner.synchronize()`. So the observable outcome ranges from "wrong answers, no diagnostics" to "delayed IMA", depending on the model. Through the HTTP server the same thing happens with `--chunked-prefill-size -1` (documented at `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py:7225` as "keeps a request in a single forward") or any `--chunked-prefill-size > 65535`, plus a request longer than 65535 tokens. Auto-selected chunk sizes (2048-16384 by GPU class) keep default servers below the threshold. ## Observed vs expected torch-profiler GPU trace, rank 0, 78-layer model, single extend: | run | attention kernels | attention time | total kernel time | |---|---|---|---| | direct runner, extend 32768 | **78** `fmhaSm100fKernel_QkvE4m3O...TokenSparse...` (= `num_layers`) | 425.58 ms | 1192.20 ms | | direct runner, extend 131072 | **0** — the whole attention bucket is absent | 0 ms | 4079.30 ms | | HTTP server, 131072 chunked at 16384 | **624** (= 8 chunks x 78 layers) | 1755.94 ms | 5986.66 ms | Arithmetic check: the correct chunked run spends `5986.66 - 1755.94 = 4230.72 ms` outside attention; the broken unchunked run's **entire** runtime is 4079.30 ms — 3.6 % apart, leaving no room for any attention work. So `bench_one_batch` above 64K does not merely crash later, it reports a prefill that is ~30 % too fast. Everything *around* attention still runs at 131072 — the sparse indexer (`deep_gemm::sm100_mqa_logits`), top-k selection (`topk_transform_prefill_kernel`) and the KV write (`set_mla_kv_buffer_kernel`, 78 launches) are all present. Only the attention kernel is missing, so nothing upstream signals a problem. **Expected**: either `num_layers` attention kernels, or a loud failure. Never a normal return with an unwritten output tensor. ## Root cause Prefill reuses the *decode* kernel by turning every query token into its own batch entry. `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa_backend.py` @ `18107e38`: * `:1905` — extend with `dsa_impl == "trtllm" and not self.use_mha` -> `_forward_trtllm(..., is_prefill=True)` * `:3201` — `transform_index_page_table_prefill(..., output_num_tokens=q.shape[0])` -> one row **per query token** * `:3230` — `batch_size = page_table_1.shape[0]` -> number of extend tokens * `:3242` — `q = q_all.view(batch_size, 1, num_heads, head_dim)` * `:3256` — `flashinfer.decode.trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla(..., backend="trtllm-gen")` flashinfer 0.6.17, `include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaKernels.cuh`: * `:516` — `int numCtasZ = params.mBatchSize;` * `:640` — `ctaLaunchParams.mNumCtasZ = numCtasZ;` * `:413` — `launch_config.gridDimZ = ctaLaunchParams.mNumCtasZ;` * `:388` — `cuErrCheck(cuLaunchKernelEx(&launch_config, func, kernelParamsList, nullptr));` CUDA's maximum `gridDim.z` is 65535, so `batch_size >= 65536` makes `cuLaunchKernelEx` return `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE`. That return value is then discarded — `include/flashinfer/trtllm/common.h`: ```cpp :44 inline void cuErrCheck_(CUresult stat, char const* file, int line) { :45 if (stat != CUDA_SUCCESS) { :46 char const* msg = nullptr; :47 cuGetErrorName(stat, &msg); :48 fprintf(stderr, "CUDA Error: %s %s %d\n", msg, file, line); // prints, then returns :49 } :50 } ``` A launch-configuration error is also **not** a sticky context error, so nothing downstream notices either — until corrupted values eventually produce an out-of-range index and the IMA. ## Suggested fixes 1. **sglang, smallest useful change**: in `_forward_trtllm`'s `is_prefill` branch, split the call into `ceil(batch_size / 65535)` launches, or at minimum `raise` when `batch_size > 65535` so the failure is loud. This is the only fix that also protects `bench_one_batch` / `dp_size=1`. 2. **sglang, structural**: adopt `cum_seq_lens_q` (flashinfer#3238, merged) so prefill stops flattening tokens into the batch dimension. 3. **FlashInfer**: implement what was agreed in #3125 — `FLASHINFER_CHECK(numCtasZ <= 65535, ...)`, and make `cuErrCheck` raise rather than `fprintf`, so no trtllm-gen launch failure can ever be silent again. Happy to send the sglang-side PR (1) and a companion FlashInfer PR (3) if maintainers agree on the preferred shape. ## Note on the test environment The FlashInfer install carries one local, build-only deviation from the 0.6.17 release: in `fmhaKernels.cuh`, three `#if CUDA_VERSION >= 13030` guards (lines 134/150/167) were extended with `&& defined(FLASHINFER_ENABLE_RUBIN_OVERSIZED_SMEM)` so the file compiles against a CUDA header set lacking `CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_SHARED_MEMORY_MODE`. Those blocks only handle SM107 (Rubin) oversized shared memory and are dead code on SM100; they cannot affect grid configuration.

signal.title: --profile-by-stage with speculative decoding: profiler never stops on decode batches (TARGET_VERIFY counted as prefill); deferred stop + synchronous trace export freeze the server for ~25 s inside later unrelated requests
signal.text: **Environment** - sglang @ 18107e38 (main, 2026-08-14), TP8 on 8x B200, torch 2.13.0 - a DeepSeek-V3.2-style DSA model (MLA, fp8 KV cache; auto-selected DSA backends prefill=trtllm/decode=trtllm) + EAGLE/MTP draft (`--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`) **What happened** Benchmarking with `sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server --profile --profile-by-stage --profile-steps 50` on a bs=1 shape, then immediately running a *clean* (unprofiled) bs=32/32K measurement, the clean run's TTFT inflated from ~39.7 s to 65.4 s (+65%). Server log shows a 25 s gap mid-prefill bracketed by `Stop profiling-EXTEND...` → `Profiling done. Traces are saved to ...`; the 16384-token prefill batch spanning the gap reports ~623 tok/s (26 s). py-spy during the gap shows the TP0 scheduler MainThread in `run_batch -> _profile_batch_predicate -> _stop_profile -> torch.profiler.export_chrome_trace -> gzip write` with GPUs idle. The exported trace is 242 MB (8 ranks). **Root cause** 1. `ForwardMode.is_prefill()`/`is_extend()` include `TARGET_VERIFY` while `is_decode()` matches only `DECODE` (python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py). Under speculative decoding every decode-step batch is TARGET_VERIFY, so `_profile_batch_predicate` (python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/profiler_manager.py) counts verify batches on the *prefill* counter and the DECODE stage can never stop on decode batches. The armed session survives the profiling client and stops ~`num_steps` batches later — inside whichever request happens to be running (in our case, the next benchmark's prefill). 2. `_stop_profile` calls `torch_profiler.export_chrome_trace()` synchronously inside `run_batch` on the scheduler main thread, freezing all serving for the export duration (25 s here). 3. `sglang/profiler.py` documents that the `/start_profile` reply comes "when all steps are processed and files are generated", which is not true with `profile_by_stage` (arming only), so `one_batch_server` proceeds while tracing is still live. **Expected** (a) by-stage counters treat TARGET_VERIFY as decode (e.g. `is_decode() or is_target_verify()`), so stages terminate within the profiled request; (b) trace export moved off the scheduler event loop (or at least a warning that `/stop_profile` stalls serving for the export duration); (c) fix the profiler.py doc claim / actually await flush. **Repro** (deterministic, ~30 min): launch TP8 spec-decode server; run `one_batch_server --batch-size 1 --input-len 32768 --output-len 64 --skip-warmup --profile --profile-activities GPU --profile-steps 50 --profile-by-stage`; immediately run `one_batch_server --batch-size 32 --input-len 32768 --output-len 64` (clean). Clean run TTFT ~65 s vs ~40 s without the preceding profiled run. The stall lands at the same batch position every time (token usage 0.69, 22 running reqs in our shape).

signal.title: [NPU] Support DeepSeek-V4 DSpark and refactor DSV4 cache management
signal.text: ## Motivation This PR adds NPU support for DeepSeek-V4 DSpark speculative decoding. It also consolidates the DSV4 NPU cache and memory-pool implementation and includes several small execution-path optimizations. ## Summary of changes ### 1. DeepSeek-V4 DSpark support on NPU - Add ModelSlim W4A8/W8A8 DSpark checkpoint loading with NPU-specific weight remapping while preserving the existing CUDA loading path. - Support checkpoint-local embedding/LM head handling and QuaRot-compatible weights. - Inject target-model hidden states into the three-stage draft model and maintain the draft model's independent SWA KV cache. - Build the DSV4 sparse-attention and compressor metadata required by draft forward and target verification, including SWA/C4/C128 page tables, compressor state, sequence metadata, and block-noncausal sparse indices. - Support NPU graph capture/replay for draft decode and target verify, including per-replay metadata refresh and DP-attention idle-rank handling. - Integrate DSpark with DP attention, expert parallelism, DeepEP, and Prefill/Decode disaggregation. - Transfer and reconstruct both target-model DSV4 state and draft-model SWA KV state in disaggregated serving. ### 2. DSV4 NPU cache and memory-pool refactor The cache and memory-pool cleanup is consolidated in commit [`0d5167e`](https://github.com/2044145178/sglang/commit/0d5167ecb79e73e26bb9f3dbc6179a496a11415c). - Consolidate address ownership and lifecycle management for full/SWA/C4/C128 KV buffers and compressor state, while keeping their physical storage separate. - Simplify the DSV4 allocator, common hooks, and NPU memory-pool implementation by reusing common full/SWA address mappings and ring-state paths. - Introduce a per-request C128 physical-page sidecar and a dedicated radix-cache component for retaining and restoring complete C128 page groups. - Align DSV4 KV metadata and compressor-state handling across cache allocation, request-to-token pools, radix- cache handling, and P/D transfer. - Remove duplicated allocation, request-table, and bookkeeping logic, and clarify allocation/free responsibilities across normal and disaggregated serving. ### 3. Small optimizations and compatibility fixes - Add NPU multi-stream preparation for Q/KV, indexer projections, and compressor work with explicit event dependencies. - Use NPU fused RMSNorm and rotary-position-embedding paths where applicable. - Refresh graph-owned DSV4 metadata in place and use the current speculative forward's verify width when constructing runtime metadata. - Improve ModelSlim quantized DSpark mapping and shared-expert compatibility. - Keep NPU-specific model loading, rotary, quantization, and attention behavior behind platform/model guards so CUDA and other speculative paths remain unchanged. ## Accuracy Accuracy was evaluated on the complete GPQA-Diamond dataset. | Method | Dataset | Samples | Accuracy | |---|---:|---:|---:| | DSpark on NPU | GPQA-Diamond | 198 | **0.894** | This validates the complete NPU DSpark path, including quantized draft-model loading, target-hidden injection, target verification, acceptance, and KV commit. ## Validation - [x] W4A8/W8A8 DSpark checkpoint loading - [x] Target hidden-state injection and three-stage draft forward - [x] Draft SWA attention and target verification - [x] Acceptance, bonus-token handling, and KV commit - [x] NPU graph capture and replay - [x] DP attention, expert parallelism, and DeepEP - [x] Prefill/Decode disaggregation - [x] GPQA-Diamond accuracy evaluation ## Notes NPU compact/ragged verify is not enabled in this PR. The validated path uses static DSpark target verification; ragged DSV4 attention and compressor metadata support will be handled separately. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31876732400](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31876732400)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31876732262](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31876732262)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Fix H3 swap PEFT SwiGLU lora_B halves when loading FFN Lora
signal.text: ## Motivation MiniMax-H3 fuses SwiGLU `gate` / `up` into one `(28672, 5376)` matrix. The two official layouts store that fused tensor with opposite row order: - diffusers / LightX2V: `ff.net.0.proj` = `[up; gate]` - sglang native: `mlp.fc1` = `[gate; up]` Loading a LightX2V LoRA already renames `ff.net.0.proj` → `mlp.fc1`, but does not swap `lora_B` rows. Shapes match and nothing errors, so the FFN adapter is applied with the two halves reversed. Attention LoRA is unaffected. The two layouts are defined by the `forward` implementations: diffusers [`SwiGLU`](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/v0.37.0/src/diffusers/models/activations.py#L143-L146) (`ff.net.0.proj`): ```python hidden_states, gate = hidden_states.chunk(2, dim=-1) return hidden_states * self.activation(gate) # [up; gate] ``` sglang [`_silu_mul`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3.py#L271-L272) (`mlp.fc1`): ```python gate, up = hidden.chunk(2, dim=-1) return F.silu(gate) * up # [gate; up] ``` The MiniMax-H3 repo ships the same DiT twice, which confirms the row-order mismatch is in the official weights, not a sglang-only convention: - `FL2VA/transformer/` → `blocks.N.mlp.fc1.weight` (what sglang loads) - `transformer/` → `transformer_blocks.N.ff.net.0.proj.weight` (what LightX2V trains against) | tensor | as-is | after swapping the two 14336-row halves | |---|---|---| | fused FFN `fc1` / `ff.net.0.proj` (52 / 52 blocks) | 0 exact | **52 / 52 exact** | | `fc2` / `ff.net.2` | exact | n/a | They are the same model: native fused `qkv_proj` is bit-identical to diffusers `to_q/to_k/to_v` after the documented per-head `[q,k,v]` pack. LightX2V's own two exports of the same adapter repeat the same signature: | | as-is | swapped | |---|---|---| | `fc1` `lora_A` (50 / 50) | exact | n/a | | `fc1` `lora_B` (50 / 50) | 0 exact | **50 / 50 exact** | | `fc2` `lora_B` (50 / 50) | exact | n/a | `lora_A` lives on the input side, so it does not need a row swap. ## Modifications Swap the two 14336-row halves of `lora_B` only on the `ff.net.0.proj.lora_B` → `mlp.fc1.lora_B` path in `load_lora_adapter`. Leave `lora_A` and `fc2` unchanged. Native fused `mlp.fc1` keys and other models' `ff.net.0.proj` (e.g. Flux) do not match both sides of the guard, so they are not rewritten. ## Accuracy Tests Prompt: `A cat walking on a sunny beach, gentle waves.` Config: MiniMax-H3 FL2VA + `lightx2v/Minimax-h3-Turbo` (`minimax_h3_fl2v_turbo_4step_v0.1.safetensors`), 1344×768 / 5 s, `seed=1101`, `lora_scale=0.0625`, `flow_shift=12`, `audio_flow_shift=3`, one H200. Same LoRA, 4-step and 8-step, before vs after this change. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37ee7943-0d37-462a-96c3-fc2be88fca26 Before the fix the fur is smeared; after the fix hair, face, and eyes resolve. Audio RMS also rises (4-step 0.0063 → 0.0097, 8-step 0.0067 → 0.0129). Latency and peak memory are unchanged. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31880164198](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31880164198)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31880164099](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31880164099)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: perf: overlap Qwen shared expert with DeepEP routed experts
signal.text: ## Motivation For Qwen MoE models using CUDA and DeepEP, the shared expert currently runs on the default stream before the routed-expert path. This serializes two independent computations and leaves an available alternate stream unused. This PR adds an opt-in path that overlaps the Qwen shared expert with routed-expert/DeepEP execution. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP` (default: `false`). - When enabled on CUDA, enqueue the shared expert on `alt_stream`, execute the routed-expert path on the current stream, and wait on an event immediately before accumulating the shared output. - Preserve allocator and breakable-CUDA-graph safety by recording the shared output on its producing stream and placing the event wait before an eager graph break. - Document the new environment variable. ## Accuracy Tests Tested commit `38f714d28e1fa01ae5b1ce38ce576373b8293722`, based on upstream main `0c072235f44fce4b89e594c2d3348e4f48e774b8`, with a clean source tree. Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 8x GB300, FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, TP8/DP8/EP8, NEXTN draft length 6, DeepEP low-latency mode, 200 GSM8K examples, 5 shots, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, and top-k 20. The run used natural NEXTN acceptance. | Metric | Result | Gate | |---|---:|---:| | GSM8K score | **0.990** (200/200) | >= 0.95 | | Request-weighted mean accepted length | **4.6102** (1,379 decode-log rows; request weight 11,625) | > 3.3 | | Evaluation latency | 95.646 s | -- | | Evaluation output throughput | 5,621.1 token/s | -- | All eight ranks completed target verify CUDA graph capture, followed by draft decode and draft extend graph capture. The job completed successfully with exit code 0. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The performance A/B exercised the same overlap mechanism on the benchmark stack before this upstream-main port. The upstream-main commit listed in the accuracy section was validated separately through CUDA graph capture and GSM8K. The end-to-end A/B comparison used the same configuration and differed only in the job name and `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP=true`. Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 24x GB300 disaggregated serving (four TP4/DP4/EP4 prefill replicas and one TP8/DP8/EP8 decode replica), FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, NEXTN draft length 6, concurrency 896, fixed accepted length 4.8, and a 3,600-second AgentX replay. | AIPerf metric | Disabled | Enabled | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Total token throughput | 2,649,331.82 token/s | 2,705,912.48 token/s | **+2.14%** | | Output token throughput | 25,466.20 token/s | 26,000.99 token/s | **+2.10%** | | Request throughput | 27.980 request/s | 28.516 request/s | **+1.91%** | | Mean inter-token latency | 18.220 ms | 17.623 ms | **-3.28%** | | Theoretical prefix-cache hit | 95.433% | 95.452% | +0.020 pp | These are end-to-end AIPerf results without profiler instrumentation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). The GPU-only stream path is covered by the end-to-end graph-capture and accuracy tests above. - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Diffusion] Validate MiniMax-H3 quality=high on B300
signal.text: ## 0x0. What this PR does Video generation does not need distillation, a different solver, or model surgery to get fast. Keep the weights and the math untouched, be rigorous about *computing less*, and MiniMax-H3 goes from 41.19 s to 11.16 s for a 5-second 1344x768 clip with audio on 8x B300 — with the quality argument written down, gated, and byte-reproducible. Concretely, this PR: - admits the strict 8x B300 TP1/Ulysses8 deployment for MiniMax-H3 request-scoped `quality="high"` - gives each validated deployment its own audited Cache-DiT schedule: 4xH200 keeps the conservative `(4, 0.04, 1)`; **8xB300 ships `(4, 0.08, 3)`**, selected by a parameter sweep on the sglang-native prompt set and gated on LPIPS plus a consecutive-frame temporal review - makes Sol-Attn dense guard steps use the platform-selected FlashAttention implementation (FA4 on Blackwell) and preserves packed-document boundaries on sparse steps - lets the common BCG fail-closed path run before H3 arms Cache-DiT input preservation - documents the protocol, limitations, results, and comparison figure in the cookbook ![MiniMax-H3 B300 quality and latency comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/16f604256169b1e9889a3ab4f297883f3f84c15d/docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/assets/minimax-h3-b300-quality-high.png) ## 0x1. Results first Hardware: 8x NVIDIA B300 SXM6 (SM103). Workload: MiniMax-H3 FL2VA T2VA, 1344x768, 124 frames @24 fps, 50 sigma points, video/audio flow shifts 12/3, sglang-native prompts (cookbook example + two benchmark presets), seeds 0/1/2. Latency is the median of three requests after one warmup. This air-cooled node sits on its 1100 W power cap and its sustained-clock regime drifts intraday (~20% on step time), so only same-session ratios are comparable — every row below was measured back-to-back in one session: | Arm | Median latency | Speedup vs Diffusers | LPIPS mean / max vs SGLang lossless | Decision | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | Diffusers BF16 dense + Ulysses8 | 41.19 s | 1.00x | 0.347 / 0.465 | baseline | | SGLang lossless | 23.03 s | 1.79x | 0.000 / 0.000 | exact default | | SGLang `quality="high"` Cache-DiT (4, 0.04, 1) | 16.45 s | 2.50x | 0.101 / 0.129 | superseded on B300 | | SGLang `quality="high"` Cache-DiT (4, 0.08, 3) | **11.16 s** | **3.69x** | 0.293 / 0.399 | **admitted** | The admitted path is 2.06x faster than SGLang lossless, and its LPIPS distance (0.293 / 0.399) sits below the distance that already separates the two reference implementations from each other (0.347 / 0.465). Side-by-side frames match the lossless output in content, staging, and lighting on all three prompts. ## 0x2. Where the speedup comes from The 0.08 residual threshold works as an adaptive brake: it sleeps on easy content and forces full computation the moment the trajectory drifts, leaving 21 of 49 full video-tower steps on this prompt set. The conservative 0.04 is too sensitive here (33 full steps on the same prompt, 16.45 s). The consecutive-cache cap barely binds at this threshold — cap 1 at the same threshold is strictly slower at equal quality (11.60 s, LPIPS 0.289 / 0.401) — so cap 3 is used. The schedule is deterministic: fresh server launches on the real `quality="high"` code path reproduce the audited sweep outputs byte-for-byte (md5-verified on all three prompts), so the quality gate transfers exactly to the shipped code. Measured on top of the admitted schedule but not enabled here: SubBlock sparse attention (#34148) composes with Cache-DiT, keeps passing the gate (10.37 s), and passed a 6/6 production-style serving validation on six unseen prompts; its blk64 kernel needs the SM103 scheduling fix now upstream at flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4533, and a rarer intermittent hang is still being rooted out before it can default. NVFP4 was evaluated and rejected (LPIPS 0.53+ under the same-seed gate even MLP-only, for at most 6% latency). ## 0x3. Sweep and rejected candidates Every line below was measured, not guessed: - threshold 0.04 with cap 1 (the H200 schedule): 33 full steps, 16.45 s — superseded - wider thresholds: 0.24 never triggers the brake and reaches LPIPS max 0.596 — rejected - cache cap 4: LPIPS max 0.53+ — rejected - warmup 3: no end-to-end win, quality drops — rejected - cached audio tower: audio drift leaks into the video tower through the dual-tower bridge — rejected - TaylorSeer order 1: no measurable gain — rejected - `--minimax-h3-adaln-online` with Cache-DiT: corrupted outputs — disqualified - generic Sol-Attn on SM103: slower than dense cuDNN-SDPA — rejected - FA4 attention backend: 4-15% slower per kernel than cuDNN-SDPA at H3 shapes, end-to-end tie — not adopted ## 0x4. Quality protocol Two gates, both must pass. Gate one: frame-aligned LPIPS (AlexNet) at 1 fps against the bit-exact SGLang lossless output — LPIPS measures same-seed trajectory drift, not absolute quality, so the yardstick is stated explicitly: the two reference implementations already sit 0.347 / 0.465 apart, and drift below that line is treated as insignificant. Gate two: human review of consecutive 4 fps frames against a temporal-artifact taxonomy (flicker, coherence, boundaries, mosaic/static regions, ghosting, broken motion, major blur). ## 0x5. Reproducibility and validation - benchmark source rebased onto `41cd5a718`; Diffusers baseline `bb56997d4`, BF16 eager dense, lossless ContextParallel Ulysses8 only - `PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_minimax_h3_admission.py python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_sol_attn_backend.py` -> `25 passed, 1 skipped` on the current head - pre-commit hooks pass on every changed file - fresh-launch byte-exact smoke on 8x B300: three prompts, md5 match against the audited sweep outputs, no environment overrides ## 0x6. Risk and rollback The high-quality admission stays fail-closed to the exact B300 device name/capability, topology, task, shape, schedule, flow shifts, eager mode, and native dense attention. The per-deployment schedule map only distinguishes between already-admitted profiles; H200 behavior is unchanged. Removing the B300 deployment branch restores the previous H200-only admission without touching the lossless default. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31791932740](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31791932740)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31791932453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31791932453)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix Python packaging shadowing in DeepEP wheel builds
signal.text: ## Summary - mount the DeepEP packaging overlay at `/sgl-deep-ep-packaging` instead of `/packaging` - update the in-container build command to use the non-conflicting path ## Root cause The packaging overlay contains an `__init__.py` and was mounted at `/packaging`. Because the wheel container runs from `/`, that directory shadowed the installed Python `packaging` distribution. The CUDA 13 build therefore completed compilation and `auditwheel repair`, but failed during `python -m wheel pack` with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'packaging.version'`. ## Validation - `bash -n scripts/build_sgl_deepep.sh` passed - pre-commit hooks passed for the build script - [CUDA 13 build-only workflow run 31878507917](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31878507917) passed all 8 combinations: Python 3.10-3.13 on x86_64 and aarch64 - all 8 jobs completed extension compilation, `auditwheel repair`, and PyPI wheel repacking; publishing jobs were disabled and skipped <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31879509955](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31879509955)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31879509783](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31879509783)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Apply latest DeepEP branch
signal.text: ## Summary - configure `NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH` before CUDA DeepEP low-latency buffer initialization - enforce `max(existing value, 1024, 2 * (num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank + 1))` - preserve larger user-provided values and leave NPU and normal DeepEP paths unchanged - force reinstall `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.30.7` in CUDA 13 CI and the main CUDA 13 image; CUDA 12 remains unchanged - add CPU unit coverage for the default, dynamic minimum, user override, and buffer initialization path ## Motivation DeepEP v2 requires NCCL Gin from NCCL 2.30.7 and an NVSHMEM QP depth of at least twice the low-latency dispatch capacity plus two. For the DeepSeek V4 configuration with 1024 dispatch tokens per rank, the required QP depth is 2050, which is larger than NVSHMEM default of 1024. ## Validation - SGLang pre-commit hooks passed for all changed files - CI dependency script passes shell syntax validation - mocked CUDA-major checks confirm CUDA 13 installs `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.30.7 --force-reinstall --no-deps` and CUDA 12 skips it - CPU unit tests: 6 passed - CPU import fallback without a `deep_ep.Buffer` symbol: passed - GB300, four GPUs, with `NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH` explicitly unset: `TestDSV4FlashFP4B200Balanced` passed all 9 tests in 165.585 seconds - GSM8K score: 0.965 - average speculative accept length: 1.9488 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31879293640](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31879293640)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31879293489](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31879293489)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.author: mickqian

signal.title: [DSA] Add an arch-independent torch paged-MQA-logits backend with a fused Triton fast path
signal.text: ### Problem The DSA indexer's paged-MQA-logits kernel has no backend that runs outside the current three: - **DEEPGEMM** (the `auto` default): compiled C++ `Unsupported architecture` assert on SM120/SM121; DeepGEMM upstream declined SM12x support (deepgemm PR #318). - **CUTEDSL**: gated behind `is_sm100_supported()`, and structurally SM100-only — `_setup_mma` uses `tcgen05.MmaF8F6F4Op`, a datacenter-Blackwell ISA op that does not exist on consumer Blackwell. - **AITER**: ROCm. So every DSA model (DeepSeek-V3.2 family, GLM `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) crashes on its first decode step on SM120/SM121 (DGX Spark GB10, RTX PRO Blackwell). The dsv4 path already solved this exact problem for DeepSeek-V4 (`fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch_sm120`, #24692), but the generic `dsa/dsa_indexer.py` path has no equivalent. ### Changes 1. **New backend value `torch`** in `DSAPagedMQALogitsBackend` + `--dsa-paged-mqa-logits-backend torch`. Opt-in only, NOT selected by `auto` — archs where DeepGEMM/CuteDSL work are unaffected. 2. **New module `dsa/torch_paged_mqa_logits.py`**: a vectorized, cuda-graph-safe (no `.item()`, no data-dependent control flow) pure-torch implementation for the generic DSA path. It discards the DeepGEMM schedule metadata (the torch path does no SM-tiled scheduling), so the eager `get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata()` call sites in `dsa_backend.py::init_forward_metadata` and the graph-replay refresh helper are skipped for this backend. 3. **Dispatch in `dsa_indexer.py::_get_topk_paged`**: pure pass-through for all modes this function serves (decode / target_verify / draft_extend_v2). No reshaping is needed: q/weights are already sliced per token, verify seqlens come from `get_seqlens_expanded()` (per-token), and `init_forward_metadata` already `repeat_interleave`s the page table to per-token rows for the multi-token modes. 4. **Fused Triton fast path `dsa/triton_paged_mqa_logits.py`** (env `SGLANG_DSA_INDEXER_TRITON`, registered in `environ.py`, default on; falls back to torch when triton is unavailable or `num_heads < 16`): one program per (token, 64-token KV page), static launch grid over the full page-table width (cuda-graph-safe) with per-block early exit on the true `seq_lens[b]` read at replay time; fused fp8 load + inline-scale dequant + q·k dot + relu + weighted head-sum, no fp32 HBM intermediates. Motivation: under cuda-graph the page-table width is a capture-time constant and the pure-torch kernel pays the full width every step — measured 1.476 ms/layer-call at width 131072 regardless of the true seq len; the Triton kernel is numerically equivalent and 0.024 ms at the same shape (61x). ### Evidence Live-validated on a 4× DGX Spark (GB10, SM121) cluster serving `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` (504B REAP cut, NVFP4, TP4): decode/prefill/target-verify/draft-extend all healthy, MTP/NEXTN accept length ~2.1, GSM8K 2-shot n=20 conc 8 = 85% with 0 errors/restarts. ### Tests `test/registered/kernels/test_dsa_paged_mqa_logits.py` (modeled on `test_sm120_paged_mqa_logits.py` from #24692; `register_cuda_ci`, runs on any CUDA GPU — no SM12x hardware required): torch vs loopy reference, Triton vs torch equivalence incl. identical `-inf` masks, both KV dtype views (uint8 / float8_e4m3fn), variable per-batch seq_lens, per-token expanded verify shapes (next_n >= 2) incl. a regression test that double-expanding the page table is caught by the shape assert, cuda-graph capture + replay incl. a seq-len change between capture and replay, and the `num_heads < 16` fallback guard. **17/17 pass on GB10 (SM121).** ### Notes - Companion PR (the attention side for SM12x): the sparse-MLA routing PR — neither alone boots DSA on consumer Blackwell; they are independent to review/merge. - The kernel hardcodes the DSA index-cache layout (head_dim 128, 64-token pages, per-page `[64*128 fp8][64*4 fp32 scales]`) and asserts it with descriptive messages. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31878923014](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31878923014)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31878922990](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31878922990)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Support prefill-side pipeline parallelism with EAGLE under PD disaggregation
signal.text: # Support prefill-side pipeline parallelism with EAGLE under PD disaggregation Lets a PD prefill engine run `--pp-size > 1` together with EAGLE/EAGLE3 speculative decoding. The two were mutually exclusive; the assert is narrowed to allow the combination on a PD prefill engine only (decode stays pure TP, and only the pipeline-aware EAGLE/EAGLE3 v2 worker is admitted). Validated on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B across two 8-GPU nodes, gsm8k 1319 questions at concurrency 128: | prefill | KV transfer path | accuracy | throughput | |---|---|---|---| | `pp=1 × tp=8` + EAGLE | `send_kvcache` | 0.961 | 4127 tok/s | | `pp=2 × tp=4` + EAGLE | `send_kvcache_slice` | 0.961 | 3501 tok/s | | `pp=8 × tp=1` + EAGLE | `send_kvcache_slice` | 0.961 | 3127 tok/s | | `pp=2 × tp=4`, no spec | `send_kvcache_slice` | 0.960 | 2503 tok/s | Accuracy-equivalence re-validation on two 4-GPU GB300 nodes (prefill `pp=2 × tp=2` + EAGLE on one node, decode `tp=4` on the other, mooncake MNNVL KV transfer), this branch rebased onto current main: | eval | vanilla main `tp=4` + EAGLE | this branch, PD `pp=2 × tp=2` prefill + EAGLE | |---|---|---| | AIME 2026, repeat 4 | 80.00% ± 4.71 (pass@4 96.67%) | 79.17% ± 4.19 (pass@4 93.33%) | | AIME 2026, repeat 16 | 80.83% ± 4.94 (SEM 1.24, pass@16 96.67%) | 80.62% ± 7.91 (SEM 1.98, pass@16 96.67%) | | gsm8k 200q, thinking | -- | 0.99 (4338 tok/s) | repeat-16 gap is 1 sample in 480, well inside the noise band; failure profiles (truncations, answer-extraction misses, wrong answers) are identical across configurations. The branch also computes a balanced PP layer partition automatically for hybrid models (`Auto PP layer partition: [31, 29]` here), leaving the two stages ~2 GiB apart in GPU memory with no `SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION` set. --- ## The draft lives on the last stage only The EAGLE draft needs the target's last-layer hidden states and the sampled token, which exist only on the last pipeline stage: ```python self._hosts_draft = get_pp_group().is_last_rank self._draft_worker = EagleDraftWorker(...) if self._hosts_draft else None ``` The split is at `EagleDraftWorker`, not at `EAGLEWorkerV2`: every rank keeps an `EAGLEWorkerV2`, so the scheduler's dispatch and `run_batch` stay rank-uniform. A rank without a draft runs the target, returns its proxy tensors, and stops. ### Memory impact The last stage carries the draft's weights *and* a full-size draft KV pool. Qwen3.5-397B at `pp=8 × tp=1` (60 layers, `full_attention_interval=4` ⇒ 15 full-attention layers, default split `7,7,7,7,8,8,8,8`): | stage | full-attn layers | weights | KV pool | GPU used | |---|---|---|---|---| | PP0 | 1 | 88.6 GB | 36.7 GB | 58.6% | | PP1–3 | 2 | 86.6 GB | 73.5 GB | 68.0% | | PP4–6 | 2 | 98.9 GB | 73.5 GB | 74.5% | | **PP7** | 2 **+ draft 1** | 100.8 + **16.1** GB | **110.2 GB** | **92.6%** | Three factors stack on the last rank: the split is by *total* layers while KV cost tracks *full-attention* layers, the total layer count is itself uneven, and the draft sits on top. Spread is **1.58×**; since `max_total_num_tokens` is MIN-synced across stages, the tightest rank caps everyone and **27.7% of cluster memory is idle**. ### Mitigation: manual repartition Effective full-attention layers are `15 + 1 (draft) = 16` over 8 stages, so each stage should hold 2 and the last stage 1 target layer plus the draft. Full-attention layers occur every 4 layers, so the smallest contiguous range holding two is 8, fixing the partition uniquely: ``` SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=8,8,8,8,8,8,8,4 ``` | | default | repartitioned | |---|---|---| | KV pool per stage | 36.7 / 73.5 / **110.2** GB | **40.2 GB on all eight** | | GPU spread | 1.58× | 1.29× | | tightest rank | 92.6% | 62.6% | | `max_total_num_tokens` | 16,949,376 | **21,099,648 (+24.5%)** | PP0 now binds and is already at the structural minimum, so this is optimal under the contiguous-range constraint. The residual 0.85% is the embedding (measured 1.83 GB gap vs 1.90 GB embedding), which cannot move off stage 0. --- ## Changes to EAGLE So a rank can hold an `EAGLEWorkerV2` with no draft inside it and still behave like a plain target worker. - **Proxy tensors** — `EAGLEWorkerV2.forward_batch_generation` takes `pp_proxy_tensors` and passes it to the target worker. The speculative branch in `run_batch` previously dropped it. - **Guards for a missing draft** — the draft KV pool accessor dereferenced the inner `EagleDraftWorker` unconditionally and crashed on every non-last stage; it now returns `None` there (carried by `primary_draft_kv_pool` after the main merge), which is also what the transfer path wants. The adaptive controller is built only where the draft is. - **Half-shared embed/head** — the target's embedding is on the first stage and its lm_head on the last, so a draft on the last stage receives only one of them. `set_embed_and_head` replaced both unconditionally and crashed in `vocab_parallel_embedding` on `None`; it now keeps what the draft loaded for the missing half. - **Result-shape guards** — `copy_to_cpu` is gated on the existing `has_sampled_token_ids`, as the non-speculative branch already was. `FutureMap`'s lazy init keyed `need_topk` on the algorithm alone while `need_hidden_states` also checked the payload; both now check it. - **Shared hidden-state spec** — the PD wire schema needs the draft's hidden width and dtype on ranks with no draft runner, so the helper is split into a config-only core with the runner entry point delegating to it. - **Static slot height under graph capture** — a captured prefill graph hands the draft model its padded static token slot while the target's hidden states arrive at the chunk's real height; the draft now places the real rows into a same-height slot instead of slicing, since the padding rows are never read downstream. ## Changes to PP mechanics - **Draft parallel state** — the draft is one layer and never spans stages, but the model reads `get_pp_group()` in `__init__`, so a draft on a non-first stage turns its embedding into `PPMissingLayer`. Added `_SELF_PP`, a single-member pipeline group per rank, and `patch_pipeline_parallel_group` mirroring the existing `patch_tensor_parallel_group`. `new_group` is collective, so all `world_size` groups are created by every rank. `ps` also needs `pp_size=1`, not just `pp_rank=0`, or `model_runner`'s `support_pp` assert fires first; the same omission is fixed in five sibling spec workers. - **No collectives on last-stage-only paths** — two WORLD collectives would have hung with the draft on a subset of ranks: the pre-model-load memory probe in `bootstrap.py` (the draft reuses the target's `memory_pool_config`, so its own value feeds nothing) and the random seed broadcast (the target's seed is now injected). - **Output ring carries the draft proposal** — every rank consumes the result rebuilt from the output ring, including the last stage, which receives its own output after a full loop. The rebuilt result had no `next_draft_input`, so `topk_p` / `topk_index` / `hidden_states` are relayed and the proposal is rebuilt and rebound to `batch.spec_info`. Cost is `bs × hidden × 2B` per hop per micro-batch. - **Device tensors on the ring** — the speculative branch D2H-copied `next_token_ids` before the ring send, so the relayed tensor reached `FutureMap.stash` on the host while the buffers stayed on device. Under PP that copy is wasted and destructive, so it is gated on `pp_size == 1`. - **Partition env vs. the draft** — `SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION` is process-global, so the `pp_size=1` draft read the target's list and rejected it for the wrong length. `get_pp_indices` now ignores the list when `pp_size == 1`. Prerequisite for any custom partition under PP + spec. - **Linear-state budget was charged model-wide** — `mamba_cache_per_req` counts every linear layer while the pools are built from the stage-local slice, a 7.5× over-charge at `pp_size=8` on a 45-linear-layer model, so `pp=8` with `--max-running-requests 512` failed to start. Now billed at the largest per-stage share so every rank derives the same pool without a collective (landed via #33666, carried here). Independent of speculative decoding. ## Changes to PD disaggregation - **Hybrid-linear KV transfer under PP** (also in #33457, independent of EAGLE) — a hybrid-linear pool stores KV only for its full-attention layers, but `prefill_start_layer` came from `pool.start_layer`, a global index that also counts linear layers, while the decode peer's pointer list is dense over full-attention layers. Translated to a full-attention-relative offset, and layer-id pairing is now preferred whenever both peers publish ids. - **Draft KV buffers get their own layer ids** — `kv_layer_ids` must cover every entry in `kv_data_ptrs`, but the draft buffers appended after the target's had none, so both peers suppressed the list and fell back to positional slicing, which slices the wrong layers under `pp_size > 1`. The draft pool's ids are remapped into a reserved band above the target's layer range; both peers derive it from the same draft config. `send_kvcache_slice` also learns to pair by layer id, since the flat pointer list is no longer `[K block, V block]` once draft entries are appended. - **Staging path pairs slots, not pointer entries** — the staging gather lays out `[all K layers, all V layers]`, which stops matching `kv_data_ptrs` order once draft KV buffers are appended, so layers would land in the wrong staging slots. Both peers now register per-slot layer ids (`slot_layer_ids`, a new trailing wire field with fallback to `kv_layer_ids` for older peers, via `build_staging_slot_metadata`), and `send_kvcache_staged` pairs source and destination slots by id under PP. --- ## Automatic layer partition for hybrid models The manual repartition above is now computed for hybrid linear/full-attention models: a contiguous-range DP minimizes the heaviest stage's estimated bytes — per-layer weights, KV pool cost scaled to a reference token capacity, mamba state cost scaled to a reference slot count, endpoint extras (embedding / lm_head), and the last stage's draft overhead (weights, its own embedding copy, full-size draft KV pool). It is a pure function of the shared configs, so every rank derives the identical partition with no collective (the same pattern as the mamba pool's max-stage billing). Engagement is deliberately narrow: `pp_size > 1`, hybrid model, no `SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION` (the env still wins, and `pp_size == 1` draft workers never read it). Uniform models keep the even split. ## Not covered - The automatic layer partitioner covers hybrid linear/full-attention models; other models keep the even split and may still want `SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION` by hand. - Failure containment on the last stage: an exception in draft extend still escapes `run_batch`. - `send_kvcache_slice` has no unit test — it needs a real transfer engine, unlike `_send_kvcache_generic`. - Only the mooncake slice path was changed; nixl's equivalent is unverified. - Head-sliced transfer now rejects non-uniform KV item lengths instead of mis-computing addresses, tightening a pre-existing assumption. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31878835861](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31878835861)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31878835706](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31878835706)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
